title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試録序
國家以經術得人之盛垂百八
十餘年矧我
皇上中興昌運文武徵才功施
社稷猶足多者乃歲壬子又大比
福建巡按御史曾佩寔司監
臨焉乃率稽
===
制典貞肅矩度事事惟謹維時御
史趙孔昭適被
命當代未及至佩乃豫僉謀諸清
戎御史沈寵暨藩臬諸臣左
布政使岑萬等用聘儒官列
司校藝時則以教諭文暨黃
宏主考試教授簡嚴莫遺賢
punctuated:
福建鄉試録序

國家以經術得人之盛，垂百八十餘年。矧我皇上中興昌運，文武徵才，功施社稷，猶足多者。乃歲壬子，又大比。福建巡按御史曾佩寔司監臨焉，乃率稽制典，貞肅矩度，事事惟謹。維時御史趙孔昭適被命當代，未及至，佩乃豫僉謀諸清戎御史沈寵暨藩臬諸臣、左布政使岑萬等，用聘儒官，列司校藝。時則以教諭文暨、黃宏主考試，教授簡嚴、莫遺賢、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

For some hundred and eighty years, the dynasty has flourished in securing worthy men through classical learning. How much more is there to praise now, when our Emperor has renewed the dynasty’s flourishing fortunes, recruiting men of civil and military talent whose achievements benefit the altars of soil and grain. In the renzi year [1552], the triennial Provincial Examination was again held. Zeng Pei, Regional Inspecting Censor for Fujian, served as Supervising Official. He accordingly consulted the established regulations, maintained strict and upright standards, and exercised care in every matter.

At that time, Censor Zhao Kongzhao had just received orders to replace him but had not yet arrived. Pei therefore consulted in advance with Shen Chong, the Censor charged with military reorganization, and the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, including Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Cen Wan. They engaged educational officials and assigned them to evaluate the candidates’ compositions. County School Instructors Wen Ji and Huang Hong served as Examiners; Prefectural School Professors Jian Yan and Mo Yixian …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
學正彭標敎諭鄺夢琰冀藎
臣安憲張邦禮龍慶雲羅見
麟爲同考試提調則右布政
使朱鴻漸右參政丁以忠監
試則按察使范欽僉事黎澄
百執事咸備乃齋惕一心如
期鑰院矢諸神明祈得眞才
===
仰副我
皇上作人盛心内外規畫旣飭乃
合提學副使朱衡所簡士三
千有奇三試之得中式九十
人遵
制額也錄名氏倂文以
獻旣竣事咸謂得人文乃作而
punctuated: 學正彭標、敎諭鄺夢琰、冀藎臣、安憲、張邦禮、龍慶雲、羅見麟爲同考試。提調則右布政使朱鴻漸、右參政丁以忠，監試則按察使范欽、僉事黎澄。百執事咸備，乃齋惕一心，如期鑰院，矢諸神明，祈得眞才，仰副我皇上作人盛心。内外規畫旣飭，乃合提學副使朱衡所簡士三千有奇，三試之，得中式九十人，遵制額也。錄名氏倂文以獻。旣竣事，咸謂得人，文乃作而
translation_en:
… Peng Biao, a subprefectural school instructor, and Kuang Mengyan, Ji Jinchen, An Xian, Zhang Bangli, Long Qingyun, and Luo Jianlin, county school instructors, served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Zhu Hongjian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Ding Yizhong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner. Supervision of the examination fell to Fan Qin, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Li Cheng, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. With all functionaries in place, they purified themselves and united their minds in reverent vigilance. On the appointed date, they locked the examination compound, swore before the spirits, and prayed to obtain truly talented men, thereby fulfilling His Majesty’s earnest desire to nurture worthy men.

Once arrangements within and outside the compound had been put in order, they assembled the more than three thousand candidates selected by Zhu Heng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant. They examined them in three sessions and selected ninety successful candidates, in accordance with the prescribed quota. They recorded their names together with their essays for presentation to the throne. When the work was finished, all agreed that worthy men had been obtained. Wen then rose to …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
言曰猗歟休哉其
聖化之徵乎詩不云乎周王壽考
遐不作人又不云乎勉勉我
王綱紀四方蓋非綱紀無以
成作人之功非壽考無以運
勉勉之化恭惟我
皇上致理作人已逾三紀于茲
道久化成所謂壽考作人不於
今日欣逢哉夫天之生材也毓靈
者地際會者時振作裁成者
化閩東南隩區也介在山海
間諦見其山崇巒削壁巉巖
嵯峩厥色蒼蒼厥氣沃沃端
若拱峙若立無幻形無晦象
banxin: 八閩鄉試錄前序 二
punctuated: 言曰：「猗歟休哉！其聖化之徵乎？詩不云乎：『周王壽考，遐不作人。』又不云乎：『勉勉我王，綱紀四方。』蓋非綱紀，無以成作人之功；非壽考，無以運勉勉之化。恭惟我皇上致理作人，已逾三紀于茲，道久化成，所謂壽考作人，不於今日欣逢哉？夫天之生材也，毓靈者地，際會者時，振作裁成者化。閩，東南隩區也，介在山海間。諦見其山，崇巒削壁，巉巖嵯峩，厥色蒼蒼，厥氣沃沃，端若拱，峙若立，無幻形，無晦象。
translation_en: …and said: “Ah, how splendid! Is this not evidence of the sage emperor’s transforming influence? Does not the Book of Odes say, ‘May the king of Zhou enjoy long life; how could he fail to nurture men of talent?’ And does it not also say, ‘Diligently our king orders and regulates the four quarters’? Without such ordering and regulation, the work of nurturing talent cannot be accomplished; without longevity, this diligent transforming influence cannot be sustained. We reverently reflect that our emperor has brought about good government and nurtured talent for more than three twelve-year cycles now. His Way has endured, and its transforming work has reached fruition. Are we not fortunate today to encounter what is meant by longevity and the nurturing of talent? When Heaven brings forth talent, the land nurtures its spiritual potency, the age provides the occasion for its emergence, and transforming influence rouses and shapes it. Min [Fujian] is a secluded region of the southeast, situated between mountains and sea. Look closely at its mountains: lofty peaks and sheer cliffs, steep and towering rocks; their color is deep green, their vital energy abundant. Dignified, they seem to bow with hands clasped; lofty, they seem to stand erect. Their forms are never illusory, their appearance never obscured. …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
維岳降神閩其有焉又見夫
海也瀦之百川洩之尾閭狂
瀾滔滔漫瀰萬頃不盈不虛
故觀海者難爲水南越之大
觀以之地靈則人傑况際此
唐虞亨嘉之會濟之
聖化振德之功久之以
===
敬一漸漬之澤則人文丕著又當
何如天下皆爾豈獨閩焉已
哉是故羅之科目試之經術
若不足盡天下士然自
列聖以來迄
今道德功業文章宗工鉅儒所以
彌綸參賛者世不乏人而後
punctuated: 維岳降神，閩其有焉。又見夫海也，瀦之百川，洩之尾閭，狂瀾滔滔，漫瀰萬頃，不盈不虛。故觀海者難爲水，南越之大觀以之。地靈則人傑，况際此唐虞亨嘉之會，濟之聖化振德之功，久之以敬一漸漬之澤，則人文丕著，又當何如？天下皆爾，豈獨閩焉已哉！是故羅之科目，試之經術，若不足盡天下士。然自列聖以來，迄今，道德、功業、文章，宗工鉅儒，所以彌綸參賛者，世不乏人，而後
translation_en:
…“The lofty mountains send down their divine spirits”: Fujian surely has its share of this. Consider also the sea: the hundred rivers fill it, and the Tail Sluice drains it; its mighty billows surge, spreading over ten thousand qing, yet it neither overflows nor runs dry. Thus, for one who has beheld the sea, other waters scarcely count as water; through it, Nanyue has its grand spectacle [?]. Where the land is numinous, its people are outstanding. How much more so when they encounter this auspicious age of flourishing prosperity, like that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, aided by the achievements of the sage emperor’s transforming influence in invigorating virtue, and long steeped in the beneficence of “reverent single-mindedness.” How splendid, then, must the flowering of human culture be! This is so throughout the realm; how could it be confined to Fujian alone?

Therefore, gathering men through the examination system and testing them in classical learning might seem insufficient to encompass all the realm’s scholars. Yet from the successive sage emperors down to the present, every generation has had eminent masters and great Confucian scholars distinguished in moral virtue, meritorious achievement, and literary composition—men who bring comprehensive order and assist in the work of transformation. Only then …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
知我
國家經術取人之典超往古獨
隆其得人之盛獨羨今爲尤
烈也夫人
天地之紀也山川之秀也而徵之
文者又治化之象也是故文
等盡得取三試之士之文而
===
覽之于疏通不泥者見其才
于脉絡粲然者見其智于冲
乎虛恢乎有容蘊涵不露者
見其量于嚴以正峭以拔挺
乎不蝓鏘鏘乎若金石聲者
見其節於是又喟然嘆曰美
哉矯乎渢渢乎澤澤乎眞人
punctuated: 知我國家經術取人之典，超往古獨隆，其得人之盛，獨羨今爲尤烈也。夫人，天地之紀也，山川之秀也；而徵之文者，又治化之象也。是故文等盡得取三試之士之文而覽之：于疏通不泥者見其才，于脉絡粲然者見其智，于冲乎虛、恢乎有容、蘊涵不露者見其量，于嚴以正、峭以拔、挺乎不蝓、鏘鏘乎若金石聲者見其節。於是又喟然嘆曰：「美哉！矯乎！渢渢乎！澤澤乎！眞人
translation_en: …one realizes that our dynasty’s institution of selecting men through mastery of the Classics surpasses antiquity in its singular eminence, and that its abundant success in obtaining worthy men is especially remarkable today [?]. Human beings are the ordering threads of Heaven and Earth and the finest essence of mountains and rivers; what finds expression in their writing is also an image of government and moral transformation. Thus we, Wen and the others, were able to obtain and read all the writings of the candidates from the three examination sessions. In writing that flowed freely without becoming bogged down, we saw their talent; in clearly articulated connections, their intelligence; in unassuming openness, expansive receptiveness, and depth held without display, their capacity; in stern rectitude, lofty distinction, upright firmness [?], and resonance like the sound of metal and stone, their integrity. Thereupon we sighed in admiration once more, saying: “How beautiful! How soaring! How rich in resonance! How lustrous! Truly human…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
文也哉蘊之爲道德行之爲
功業發揮之爲文章閩之人
文始信不獨古昔盛而已謂
非曰海岳之孕泄也誣乎今
夫南山之石巖巖然有節之
道焉中流之柱琅琅然疏達
以應有才之道焉若納百川
===
而無不容者有量之道焉若
虛明鑒照流動不滓者有智
之道焉合是而毓靈于人斯
弘毅合德任重器也剛大竝
用配義功也虛直應物中正
道也則夫秉衷履正知方達
權靜以定躁廣以去隘明以
punctuated: 文也哉！蘊之爲道德，行之爲功業，發揮之爲文章。閩之人文，始信不獨古昔盛而已。謂非曰海岳之孕泄也，誣乎？今夫南山之石，巖巖然，有節之道焉；中流之柱，琅琅然，疏達以應，有才之道焉；若納百川而無不容者，有量之道焉；若虛明鑒照，流動不滓者，有智之道焉。合是而毓靈于人，斯弘毅合德，任重器也；剛大竝用，配義功也；虛直應物，中正道也。則夫秉衷履正，知方達權，靜以定躁，廣以去隘，明以
translation_en: …truly the flowering of human culture! Stored within, it becomes moral virtue; put into practice, it becomes achievement; expressed fully, it becomes literary composition. Now we can indeed believe that the human culture of Min flourished not only in antiquity. Would it not be false to deny that this is what the seas and mountains have nurtured and brought forth [?]? Consider the rocks of the southern mountain: towering and rugged, they embody integrity. The pillar in midstream, ringing clear and responding freely, embodies talent. That which receives the hundred rivers and accommodates them all embodies breadth of capacity. That which is empty and luminous, reflecting like a mirror, flowing without sediment, embodies wisdom. When these qualities combine to nurture spiritual excellence in people, breadth of mind and firmness of purpose unite in virtue, making a vessel capable of bearing great responsibilities; strength and greatness work together, producing achievements consonant with righteousness; openness and uprightness respond to things, constituting the Way of centrality and rectitude. Thus, holding fast to one's innate moral nature and walking uprightly, knowing fixed principles and understanding judicious adaptation, using stillness to settle agitation, breadth to dispel narrowness, and illumination to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
疏窒皆文之昭也化之著也
而文武之眞才咸可胥此焉
出矣豈直曰抱藝多士濟濟
然已乎哉于是見我
聖人綱紀作人之化博以厚矣高
以明矣悠久無疆矣其眞謂
與
天無極者乎堯曰放勳光被四表
格于上下禹告成功聲敎訖
于四海於戲此我
國家經術得人于是益盛而爲
我
社稷永賴其有旣哉是舉也提督
軍務右副都御史張烜遹觀
punctuated:
疏窒，皆文之昭也，化之著也，而文武之眞才咸可胥此焉出矣。豈直曰抱藝多士濟濟然已乎哉？于是見我聖人綱紀作人之化，博以厚矣，高以明矣，悠久無疆矣。其眞謂與天無極者乎！堯曰：「放勳，光被四表，格于上下。」禹告成功，聲敎訖于四海。於戲！此我國家經術得人，于是益盛，而爲我社稷永賴，其有旣哉！
是舉也，提督軍務右副都御史張烜遹觀
translation_en:
…clear away obstructions: all these manifest the brilliance of culture and the visible effects of transformation. Genuine talents in both civil and military affairs can all emerge from this. Could it amount merely to an impressive gathering of many scholars possessed of accomplishments? Here we see that our sage sovereign’s transforming influence, ordering society and nurturing men of talent, is broad and profound, lofty and luminous, enduring and boundless. May it truly be called as limitless as Heaven! Of Yao it was said: “His achievements were vast; his radiance reached the four outer bounds and extended above and below.” Yu reported the completion of his work, and his civilizing influence reached throughout the Four Seas. Ah! Our state’s recruitment of worthy men through classical learning thus flourishes ever more greatly. Will there ever be an end to the lasting support this provides for our altars of soil and grain?
For this examination, Zhang Xuan, Superintendent of Military Affairs and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, proceeded to observe …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
厥成左叅政汪宗元按察副
使汪俅馮璋僉事張恕汪垍
均範理於外行都司都指揮
僉事張漴署都指揮僉事顧
邦重代都指揮田耕事綜撥
軍士焉副使萬虞愷左叅議
熊洛都指揮范德榮行都司
===
都指揮僉事劉敕皆預期入
賀右布政使曾鈞談愷按察使
王昺左叅政王璣左叅議吳
源俱後先以遷秩行先是刑
部郎中陸穩以訊錄至工部
郎中張祥戶部郎中周載皆
以督賦至咸事事境內樂觀
punctuated: 厥成。左叅政汪宗元、按察副使汪俅、馮璋、僉事張恕、汪垍，均範理於外。行都司都指揮僉事張漴、署都指揮僉事顧邦重，代都指揮田耕事，綜撥軍士焉。副使萬虞愷、左叅議熊洛、都指揮范德榮、行都司都指揮僉事劉敕，皆預期入賀。右布政使曾鈞、談愷、按察使王昺、左叅政王璣、左叅議吳源，俱後先以遷秩行。先是，刑部郎中陸穩以訊錄至，工部郎中張祥、戶部郎中周載皆以督賦至，咸事事境內，樂觀
translation_en:
…its completion. Wang Zongyuan, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Wang Qiu and Feng Zhang, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Zhang Shu and Wang Ji, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, all supervised arrangements outside [？]. Zhang Chong, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner of the Branch Regional Military Commission, and Gu Bangzhong, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, took over the duties of Regional Military Commissioner Tian Geng and coordinated the deployment of soldiers. Wan Yukai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Xiong Luo, Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left; Fan Derong, Regional Military Commissioner; and Liu Chi, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner of the Branch Regional Military Commission, all came to offer congratulations before the appointed date.

Zeng Jun and Tan Kai, Provincial Administration Commissioners of the Right; Wang Bing, Surveillance Commissioner; Wang Ji, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; and Wu Yuan, Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left, had departed at various times upon promotion. Earlier, Lu Wen, a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, had arrived to interrogate prisoners and review their cases. Zhang Xiang, a bureau director in the Ministry of Works, and Zhou Zai, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, had both arrived to supervise tax collection. All were attending to official business within the province and were delighted to witness …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人才之盛者亦例得書云
山東兗州府東平州平陰縣
儒學教諭朱文謹序
punctuated:
人才之盛者，亦例得書云。
山東兗州府東平州平陰縣儒學教諭朱文謹序。
translation_en:
…the flourishing of talent likewise have their names recorded here in accordance with customary practice.
Preface by Zhu Wenjin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Pingyin County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史曾佩〔德甫江西臨川縣人辛丑進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使朱鴻漸〔于磐直隸吳縣人辛巳進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右參政丁以忠〔崇義江西新建縣人戊戌進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使范欽〔堯卿浙江鄞縣人壬辰進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司僉事黎澄〔本靜江西樂平縣人丁未進士〕
===
考試官
山東兗州府東平州平陰縣儒學教諭朱文〔質卿直隸上元縣人庚子貢士〕
廣西梧州府蒼梧縣儒學教諭黃宏〔括元廣東順德縣人癸卯貢士〕
同考試官
直隸永平府儒學教授簡嚴〔臨可廣西馬平縣人丁酉貢士〕
湖廣武昌府儒學教授莫遺賢〔堯卿廣西蒼梧縣人辛卯貢士〕
河南開封府鄭州儒學學正彭標〔元表廣東順德縣人庚子貢士〕
浙江寧波府定海縣儒學教諭鄺夢琰〔均房廣東南海縣人戊子貢士〕
直隸廣平府曲周縣儒學教諭冀藎臣〔子忠山西榆次縣人庚子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試

監臨官：
巡按福建監察御史曾佩〔德甫，江西臨川縣人，辛丑進士〕。

提調官：
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使朱鴻漸〔于磐，直隸吳縣人，辛巳進士〕。
福建等處承宣布政使司右參政丁以忠〔崇義，江西新建縣人，戊戌進士〕。

監試官：
福建等處提刑按察司按察使范欽〔堯卿，浙江鄞縣人，壬辰進士〕。
福建等處提刑按察司僉事黎澄〔本靜，江西樂平縣人，丁未進士〕。

考試官：

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之教誠則明矣
明則誠矣
堯舜之道孝弟而已矣
易
文明以健中正而應君子正也唯君子爲
能通天下之志
===
聖人感人心而天下和平
易簡之善配至德
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
慎厥身脩思永惇敘九族庶明勵翼邇可
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。
自誠明謂之性，自明誠謂之教；誠則明矣，明則誠矣。
堯舜之道，孝弟而已矣。

易
文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子爲能通天下之志。
聖人感人心而天下和平。
易簡之善配至德。
昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
慎厥身，脩思永，惇敘九族，庶明勵翼，邇可
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The Master skillfully guides people forward step by step. He broadens me through learning and restrains me through ritual propriety.

To attain understanding through sincerity is called nature; to attain sincerity through understanding is called instruction. With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.

The Way of Yao and Shun consists simply in filial devotion and respect for elder brothers.

Book of Changes
Cultured and enlightened, yet strong; central and correct, and finding a response: this is the correctness of the noble man. Only the noble man can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.

The sage moves people's hearts, and all under Heaven attain harmony and peace.

The goodness of ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.

When the sages of old made the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang; the Way of Earth as yielding and firm; and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They brought together the Three Powers and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. Distinguishing yin and yang and using yielding and firm alternately, they made the six positions of the Changes form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents
Be watchful over your own person; cultivate yourself with thoughts for the distant future. Generously maintain the proper order among the nine degrees of kinship, and let the many enlightened men exert themselves in assisting you. What is near can …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
遠在茲
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
六三德一曰正直二曰剛克三曰柔克平
康正直彊弗友剛克燮友柔克沉潛剛
克高明柔克
我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷歷
年
詩
===
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除
俾爾多益以莫不庶
倬彼雲漢為章于天周王壽考遐不作人
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四
方
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕公
punctuated:
遠在茲。
若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。
六、三德：一曰正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。平康，正直；彊弗友，剛克；燮友，柔克；沉潛，剛克；高明，柔克。
我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷年。

詩
赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
天保定爾，亦孔之固。俾爾單厚，何福不除？俾爾多益，以莫不庶。
倬彼雲漢，為章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？
追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王。

春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕公
translation_en:
…reaching far rests in this.

If you were working metal, I would use you as a whetstone; if crossing a great river, I would use you as a boat and oars; if the year brought a great drought, I would use you as copious rain.

Sixth, the three virtues: the first is uprightness, the second is government through firmness, and the third is government through gentleness. In peace and tranquility, use uprightness; with the forceful and uncompliant, use firmness; with the harmonious and compliant, use gentleness. With the reserved and retiring, use firmness; with the high-minded and brilliant, use gentleness.

We have received Heaven’s mandate. May we fully equal the years of the Xia and not fall short of the years of the Yin.

Book of Odes

Valiant are the warriors, the trusted hearts of dukes and lords.

Heaven protects and establishes you, making you truly secure. It grants you abundant bounty: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you ever greater increase, so that nothing fails to flourish.

Brilliant is that River of Clouds, the Milky Way, forming a pattern in the heavens. The king of Zhou enjoys long life: does he not nurture worthy men?

Carved and polished is his adornment; gold and jade are his substance. Tirelessly our king orders and governs the four quarters.

None dares fail to come with offerings; none dares fail to come to acknowledge the king.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang〕 The duke…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕
季子來歸〔閔公元年〕公子慶父出奔莒〔閔〕
〔公二年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷 齊人來
歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
叔孫得臣會晉人宋人陳人衛人鄭人伐
沈沈潰〔文公三年〕
吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕夏曹公
孫會自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
===
禮記
善教者使人繼其志其言也約而達微而
臧罕譬而喻可謂繼志矣
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
仁者仁此者也禮者履此者也義者宜此
者也信者信此者也强者强此者也
punctuated:
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
季子來歸。〔閔公元年〕公子慶父出奔莒。〔閔〕〔公二年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔定公十年〕
叔孫得臣會晉人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人伐沈，沈潰。〔文公三年〕
吳子使札來聘。〔襄公二十有九年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕
禮記
善教者使人繼其志，其言也約而達，微而臧，罕譬而喻，可謂繼志矣。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。如此，則四海之內合敬同愛矣。
仁者，仁此者也；禮者，履此者也；義者，宜此者也；信者，信此者也；强者，强此者也。
translation_en:
…met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to invade Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
Jizi returned to Lu. 〔First year of Duke Min.〕 Prince Qingfu fled to Ju. 〔Second year of Duke Min; the annotation is split in the original.〕 In summer, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The people of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Shusun Dechen joined men of Jin, Song, Chen, Wei, and Zheng in attacking Shen. Shen collapsed. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕
The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit to Lu. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
A good teacher enables others to carry on his purpose. His words are concise yet clear, subtle yet excellent; he uses few illustrations yet makes himself understood. This may be called enabling others to carry on his purpose.
Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares their ordered rhythms. Through harmony, the myriad things retain their proper natures; through order, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the visible realm there are ritual and music; in the unseen realm there are ghosts and spirits. Thus, all within the Four Seas unite in reverence and share in love.
The benevolent are those who practice benevolence in this; the ritually proper are those who put this into practice; the righteous are those who act fittingly in this; the trustworthy are those who remain faithful to this; the strong are those who exert themselves in this.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄

translation_en:
…The gentleman diligently pursues these two things and stands facing south as ruler; thus all under Heaven enjoys great peace.

Second Session

Discourse: “The gentleman acts, and for generations his actions become the Way for all under Heaven.”

One question from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor ordering the highest ministers, ministers, and grandees to observe the monthly ordinances of the four seasons. Second year of Yangshuo [23 BCE].
Compose a Tang proclamation additionally appointing Fang Xuanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Thirteenth year of Zhenguan [639].
Compose a memorial of thanks from the assembled officials upon being bestowed with Memorials of Eminent Ministers through the Ages (Lidai mingchen zouyi). Fourteenth year of Yongle [1416].

Five legal judgments:
A colleague acting for another in adjudicating cases and signing case documents.
Discarding or destroying utensils, property, crops, and the like.
Marriages involving Mongols and Semu people.
Prohibiting persons previously convicted from serving in the palace guard.
False accusations leading to military exile or forced relocation.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第叁場
策五道
問古帝王所以建極敷錫保乂流衍者非
可襲取為之也稽諸堯舜三代典謨訓
誥具有明徵漢以下英君誼辟其所建
立與所表章非不欲法於天下傳之後
世以垂休光然端本善則之要槩乎未
之有聞此所以治安小康視光明俊偉
之業不侔殆亦有由然者我
===
太祖高皇帝
龍飛淮甸汛掃胡元肇建開闢以來所未有
之勳業其
嘉言善行神謀懿範見於日曆之所序載
聖政記之所頌述者既詳且明不知盡能揄揚
否抑此外别有可言者與我
皇上受
天明命丕振
中興即位以來功德並懋所以經緯天地而
punctuated:
第叁場
策五道
問：古帝王所以建極敷錫、保乂流衍者，非可襲取為之也。稽諸堯舜三代典謨訓誥，具有明徵。漢以下，英君誼辟，其所建立與所表章，非不欲法於天下、傳之後世，以垂休光。然端本善則之要，槩乎未之有聞。此所以治安小康，視光明俊偉之業不侔，殆亦有由然者。我太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，汛掃胡元，肇建開闢以來所未有之勳業。其嘉言善行、神謀懿範，見於日曆之所序載、聖政記之所頌述者，既詳且明，不知盡能揄揚否？抑此外别有可言者與？我皇上受天明命，丕振中興。即位以來，功德並懋，所以經緯天地而
translation_en:
Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The means by which the ancient emperors and kings established the supreme standard and extended its blessings, secured orderly rule, and transmitted its benefits to posterity could not be achieved merely through imitation. Clear evidence is found in the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations concerning Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties. From the Han onward, illustrious rulers and righteous sovereigns, in what they established and what they promoted, certainly wished to provide models for all under Heaven and transmit them to later generations, leaving behind a glorious legacy. Yet of the essentials of setting the foundations right and perfecting standards, scarcely anything was heard. There must surely have been reasons why their peace and modest prosperity did not equal those radiant and magnificent achievements.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao rose like a dragon in the Huai region, swept away the non-Han Yuan rulers, and founded an enterprise unprecedented since the beginning of the world. His excellent words and good deeds, inspired plans and admirable examples are recorded in the Daily Calendar and celebrated in the Record of Sagely Government, both fully and clearly. But have these accounts adequately extolled them all? Or is there more to be said beyond them?

Our reigning Emperor received Heaven’s luminous mandate and vigorously brought about a restoration. Since his accession, his achievements and virtue have both flourished; the means by which he orders Heaven and Earth and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
昭回日月者誠足以克紹
烈祖而超出百王之上不知於日曆
聖政記諸書有脗合否抑淵源之地別有所自
與諸士子佩服
聖訓蓋已有年果能陳其梗槩而探其本原矣
乎實有司者之所願聞
問同律脩禮肇自舜典而五禮六樂之載
在周禮者尤悉焉自秦滅典籍至漢復
重明經惟樂書遂廢不講學者不過取
===
周官宗伯一篇與二戴所記誦習之而
已然以班固藝文志攷之是禮經非樂
也彼樂自為六家今散佚不傳矣夫六
經之道如四時相須以成歲乃自漢以
來缺大樂而不求學者亦安之不復疑
豈理也哉宋時和胡阮李范馬劉楊諸
賢之議終不能以相一而其說亦可得
而聞歟迨至蔡元定旁搜冥契積之累
年著為律呂新書文公稱其明白淵深
punctuated:
昭回日月者，誠足以克紹烈祖，而超出百王之上。不知於《日曆》《聖政記》諸書有脗合否？抑淵源之地，別有所自與？諸士子佩服聖訓，蓋已有年，果能陳其梗槩而探其本原矣乎？實有司者之所願聞。

問：同律脩禮，肇自《舜典》，而五禮六樂之載在《周禮》者尤悉焉。自秦滅典籍，至漢復重明經，惟樂書遂廢不講。學者不過取《周官》宗伯一篇與二戴所記，誦習之而已。然以班固《藝文志》攷之，是禮經，非樂也。彼樂自為六家，今散佚不傳矣。夫六經之道，如四時相須以成歲，乃自漢以來缺大樂而不求，學者亦安之，不復疑，豈理也哉？宋時，和、胡、阮、李、范、馬、劉、楊諸賢之議，終不能以相一，而其說亦可得而聞歟？迨至蔡元定，旁搜冥契，積之累年，著為《律呂新書》，文公稱其明白淵深
translation_en:
…and illuminate the sun and moon are truly sufficient to carry forward the legacy of the illustrious founding ancestor and surpass the hundred kings. We wonder whether these accord with such works as the Daily Calendar and the Record of Sagely Governance, or whether their underlying source lies elsewhere. You candidates have reverently embraced the imperial teachings for years. Can you indeed set forth their broad outlines and probe their origins? This is what the officials responsible earnestly wish to hear.

Question: The harmonization of pitch standards and the cultivation of ritual first appear in the Canon of Shun; the account of the five rites and six musical traditions in the Rites of Zhou is especially comprehensive. After the Qin destroyed the canonical writings, the Han again placed weight on elucidating the classics. Only the writings on music fell into neglect and ceased to be studied. Scholars merely took the section on the Minister of Rites in the Offices of Zhou, together with the records of the two Dai, and recited and studied them. Yet, examined against Ban Gu’s Treatise on Literature, these are ritual classics, not writings on music. Music itself comprised six bibliographical entries, which are now scattered and lost, no longer transmitted. The Way embodied in the Six Classics is like the four seasons, which depend upon one another to complete the year. Yet since the Han, the great music has been missing, and no one has sought to recover it; scholars too have accepted this and no longer question it. How can this be reasonable? During the Song, the views of the worthies He, Hu, Ruan, Li, Fan, Ma, Liu, and Yang ultimately could not be reconciled. May we nevertheless hear an account of their theories? Later, Cai Yuanding searched widely and attained profound insight, accumulating his findings over many years and composing the New Book on Pitch Standards. Lord Wen praised it as clear and profound…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
縝密通暢不爲牽合附會之談元定開
產也今其書具在諸士子固甞誦說而
講求之可悉言其指要歟抑別有其說
歟夫追韶濩之正聲變鄭衞之餘習使
移風易俗不爲虛語必如之何而可
問氏族之學其來久矣三代以前氏族分
而爲二氏以別貴賤也而曰姓可呼爲
氏氏不可呼爲姓者何歟姓以別婚姻
也而氏曰姓不同姓曰氏不同者何歟
===
司馬子長劉知幾良吏也而於姬旦姬
伯猶且昧焉則玆學湮晦可知矣以紀
傳所睹記者漢有官譜氏族篇萬姓譜
魏立九品置中正晉宋以後有百家譜
百官譜姓苑官氏志至唐則尤盛矣氏
族志大唐姓系錄衣冠開元永泰諸譜
而又有韻略韻譜姓纂姓解不知果有
裨於世教否乎參之三代之法抑或有
同歟乃所稱三十二類四聲複姓之說
punctuated:
縝密通暢，不爲牽合附會之談。元定開產也，今其書具在，諸士子固甞誦說而講求之，可悉言其指要歟？抑別有其說歟？夫追韶濩之正聲，變鄭衞之餘習，使移風易俗不爲虛語，必如之何而可？
問：氏族之學，其來久矣。三代以前，氏族分而爲二。氏以別貴賤也，而曰姓可呼爲氏，氏不可呼爲姓者，何歟？姓以別婚姻也，而氏曰姓不同，姓曰氏不同者，何歟？司馬子長、劉知幾，良吏也，而於姬旦、姬伯猶且昧焉，則玆學湮晦可知矣。以紀傳所睹記者，漢有《官譜》《氏族篇》《萬姓譜》；魏立九品，置中正；晉宋以後，有《百家譜》《百官譜》《姓苑》《官氏志》；至唐則尤盛矣：《氏族志》《大唐姓系錄》，衣冠、開元、永泰諸譜，而又有《韻略》《韻譜》《姓纂》《姓解》。不知果有裨於世教否乎？參之三代之法，抑或有同歟？乃所稱三十二類、四聲複姓之說
translation_en:
…closely reasoned and lucid, without strained connections or contrived interpretations. Yuanding was a native of Kai[?]. His book survives in full today, and you candidates have surely recited, expounded, and studied it. Can you explain its essential purport fully? Or do you have other views? How must one proceed to recover the correct sounds of the Shao and Hu music, transform the lingering musical habits of Zheng and Wei, and ensure that reforming manners and changing customs are more than empty words?
Question: The study of clans and lineages has a long history. Before the Three Dynasties, clan and lineage designations were divided into two categories [?]. Clan names (shi) distinguished noble from humble. Why, then, is it said that a surname (xing) may be called a clan name, but a clan name may not be called a surname? Surnames distinguished those eligible to intermarry. Why, then, does the text speak of clan names as “surnames differing,” and surnames as “clan names differing” [?]? Sima Zichang and Liu Zhiji were able officials [?], yet even they were unclear about Ji Dan and Ji Bo. From this one can see how this field of learning had fallen into obscurity. Among the works recorded in annals and biographies, the Han had Genealogies of Officials, Chapters on Clans and Lineages, and Genealogies of the Myriad Surnames. The Wei established the nine ranks and appointed Rectifiers. From the Jin and Song onward there were Genealogies of the Hundred Families, Genealogies of the Hundred Officials, Garden of Surnames, and Treatise on Official Clans. In the Tang this scholarship flourished especially: there were the Treatise on Clans and Lineages and Record of Surname Lineages of the Great Tang; the genealogies of official families and those of the Kaiyuan and Yongtai eras; and also the Outline Arranged by Rhymes, Genealogies Arranged by Rhymes, Compilation of Surnames, and Explanations of Surnames. Did these actually contribute to the moral instruction of society? Compared with the methods of the Three Dynasties, might they have something in common? As for the accounts of the so-called thirty-two categories and compound surnames arranged under the four tones…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
抑又何歟玆欲俾千餘年湮源斷緒之
典燦然在目親上尊祖而安民定志之
道係焉諸士子講之素矣其何以復我
問人有言道勝者文不難而自至文與道
果有二乎六經無文法而天地之至文
歸之孔子曰文不在玆乎子貢稱夫子
之文章可得而聞其所言者何文也戰
國時以操術以騁辨以工言以作賦馳
驟於文苑者不知其幾也可指其人而
===
言之歟漢最盛矣賈陸董劉班馬其著
者嚴徐鄒枚司馬王楊之徒呟議小言
互相雄長抑豈盡無其實耶不然則響
隨人徂何以流傳至今也周情孔思詞
臻其妙然其論古人直以屈孟馬楊爲
一等是不免裂文與道而二之治出於
一之說似矣而其言曰我所謂文必與
道俱不識其文果澤於道耶夫上下數
千年間蓋所稱能文之士如斯而已而
punctuated:
抑又何歟？玆欲俾千餘年湮源斷緒之典燦然在目，親上尊祖而安民定志之道係焉。諸士子講之素矣，其何以復我？
問：人有言：「道勝者，文不難而自至。」文與道果有二乎？六經無文法，而天地之至文歸之。孔子曰：「文不在玆乎？」子貢稱：「夫子之文章，可得而聞。」其所言者何文也？戰國時，以操術，以騁辨，以工言，以作賦，馳驟於文苑者，不知其幾也。可指其人而言之歟？漢最盛矣，賈、陸、董、劉、班、馬，其著者；嚴、徐、鄒、枚、司馬、王、楊之徒，呟議小言，互相雄長，抑豈盡無其實耶？不然，則響隨人徂，何以流傳至今也？「周情孔思，詞臻其妙」，然其論古人，直以屈、孟、馬、楊爲一等，是不免裂文與道而二之。「治出於一」之說似矣，而其言曰：「我所謂文，必與道俱。」不識其文果澤於道耶？夫上下數千年間，蓋所稱能文之士如斯而已，而
translation_en:
…what, moreover, were these? We now wish to bring clearly before our eyes the institutions whose origins have been obscured and whose continuity has been broken for more than a thousand years. On these depends the way of cherishing superiors and honoring ancestors, bringing peace to the people and stability to their aspirations. You candidates have long studied these matters: how will you answer me?
Question: Someone has said, “For one in whom the Way prevails, literary accomplishment comes of itself without difficulty.” Are literature and the Way truly two separate things? The Six Classics have no rules of composition, yet to them belongs the finest writing between Heaven and Earth. Confucius said, “Does not this culture reside here in me?” Zigong said, “The Master’s cultural accomplishments can be heard about.” What did they mean by this word wen? During the Warring States period, countless men ranged through the literary world, practicing arts of persuasion, displaying their powers of disputation, crafting fine speech, or composing rhapsodies. Can you identify these men and discuss them? Literature flourished most abundantly under the Han. Jia, Lu, Dong, Liu, Ban, and Ma were its prominent figures. Men such as Yan, Xu, Zou, Mei, Sima, Wang, and Yang competed for supremacy in their discussions and minor writings [?]. Could they all have been devoid of substance? Otherwise, their echoes would have faded with their deaths: how could their writings have survived to this day? “With the feelings of the Duke of Zhou and the thought of Confucius, his diction attained their subtle excellence.” Yet, in his assessment of the ancients, he simply placed Qu, Meng, Ma, and Yang in a single rank. This inevitably splits literature from the Way and makes them two separate things. The proposition that “government issued from a single source” seems right; yet he said, “What I call literature must always accompany the Way.” I wonder whether his writing was indeed enriched by the Way. Across several thousand years, it would seem that those acclaimed as accomplished writers amount only to men such as these, and yet…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
或謂宋之文不如唐唐不如漢漢不如
三代豈世變趨下而文亦因之乎不然
於數家之外將别有其人乎幸爲我折
衷其說
問聖人不言兵與利而容民畜衆聚人理
財自易發之然則屯田榷鹽亦經國之
要務也如屯金城而臨羌畏服屯斜谷
而百姓安堵屯襄陽而墾田八百行於
內地者足國安民行於外地者寫邊實
===
===
塞似得寓兵於農之意矣管仲舉之而
齊國富強劉晏舉之而饟祿充裕盛度
舉之而公私咸賴取於海池者利足經
國取於井地者澤足濟民似因天地自
然之利矣行之於古輒有成效今閩之
要害皆有屯田居則爲農出則爲兵立
法非不善也而久則弊生遂失初制謂
之兵歟則非荷戈之士謂之民歟則非
授田之戶因屯興田不爲無實之虛文
punctuated:
或謂宋之文不如唐，唐不如漢，漢不如三代，豈世變趨下而文亦因之乎？不然，於數家之外，將别有其人乎？幸爲我折衷其說。

問：聖人不言兵與利，而容民畜衆、聚人理財，自《易》發之。然則屯田榷鹽，亦經國之要務也。如屯金城而臨羌畏服，屯斜谷而百姓安堵，屯襄陽而墾田八百，行於內地者足國安民，行於外地者寫邊實塞，似得寓兵於農之意矣。管仲舉之而齊國富強，劉晏舉之而饟祿充裕，盛度舉之而公私咸賴。取於海池者，利足經國；取於井地者，澤足濟民，似因天地自然之利矣。行之於古，輒有成效。今閩之要害皆有屯田，居則爲農，出則爲兵，立法非不善也，而久則弊生，遂失初制。謂之兵歟，則非荷戈之士；謂之民歟，則非授田之戶。因屯興田，不爲無實之虛文
translation_en:
…Some say that the prose of the Song does not equal that of the Tang, that Tang prose does not equal Han prose, and that Han prose does not equal that of the Three Dynasties. Could it be that, as the times declined, prose followed suit? If not, might there be other writers beyond the several masters mentioned? Please weigh these views and offer me a balanced judgment.

Question: The sages did not speak of warfare and profit, yet accommodating the people and nourishing the multitude, gathering the people and managing wealth, were principles set forth in the Book of Changes. Thus military agricultural colonies and the salt monopoly are also essential affairs of statecraft. When agricultural colonies were established at Jincheng, Linqiang submitted in fear; when they were established at Xiegu, the common people lived securely; when they were established at Xiangyang, eight hundred [?] of farmland were reclaimed. Within the interior, these colonies enriched the state and secured the people; beyond it, they relieved the frontier [?] and strengthened the border defenses. This seems to have fulfilled the intention of embedding soldiers among farmers. Guan Zhong implemented the salt monopoly, and the state of Qi became wealthy and powerful; Liu Yan implemented it, and provisions and official salaries were amply supplied; Sheng Du implemented it, and both public and private interests benefited. Salt obtained from the seas and salt ponds yielded profits sufficient to sustain the state; salt obtained from wells brought benefits sufficient to support the people. This seems to have made use of the natural resources of Heaven and Earth. When these measures were implemented in antiquity, they consistently produced results.

Today, all the strategic locations in Fujian have military agricultural colonies. At home the men farm; when mobilized, they serve as soldiers. The regulations establishing this system were certainly sound, but over time abuses arose, and its original arrangements were lost. If we call these men soldiers, they are not men who bear arms; if we call them commoners, they are not households allotted farmland. Developing farmland through military colonies—does this not amount to an empty form without substance…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣乎閩之瀕海利於鹵鹽司之以官鬻
之以商生財非無道也而久則蠹生因
之極敝謂利在官歟則公無羨餘之積
謂利在商歟則市有折閱之憂計口稅
鹽不爲無名之征求乎今欲祛其弊端
得古人立法之意使公私並受其利抱
竒諸士必有能處之者
punctuated: 矣乎？閩之瀕海，利於鹵鹽，司之以官，鬻之以商，生財非無道也。而久則蠹生，因之極敝。謂利在官歟，則公無羨餘之積；謂利在商歟，則市有折閱之憂。計口稅鹽，不爲無名之征求乎？今欲祛其弊端，得古人立法之意，使公私並受其利，抱竒諸士必有能處之者。
translation_en: …has it not? Coastal Fujian enjoys the benefits of salt production from brine. Officials administer it, and merchants sell it: there is certainly a means of generating revenue. Over time, however, abuses have arisen, bringing the system into extreme disrepair. If the profits are said to accrue to the government, public funds have no accumulated surplus; if they are said to accrue to the merchants, those in the market face the prospect of selling at a loss. Does taxing salt according to the number of persons not amount to an exaction without legitimate grounds? We now wish to eliminate these abuses and recover the intent behind the institutions established by the ancients, so that public and private interests alike may benefit. Among you gentlemen of exceptional ability, there must surely be those who can devise a solution.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
黃星耀
同考試官教諭張批夫子平日教人不出乎此
惟顏子能體之子亦善體顏子者
同考試官教諭龔批此作渾然成章得博約致
一之旨錄之
考試官教諭黃批善發聖賢授受之蘊者
===
考試官教諭朱批典雅莊重
大賢嘆聖人之善教必述教之所以善焉夫文
以啓知禮以約行學之序也知博約之序則知
所以入道矣聖教所以爲善乎此顏子學旣
有得因嘆聖道之高妙而及其教也蓋曰不可
幾及者聖人之道固非示人以遠矣所可循者
聖人之教蓋確然示人以易矣何也夫道有所
由入强之則難功有所當加悖之則拂吾夫子
之教人也因其材而不强人以難能循其序亦
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。」

黃星耀

同考試官教諭張批：「夫子平日教人，不出乎此。惟顏子能體之，子亦善體顏子者。」

同考試官教諭龔批：「此作渾然成章，得博約致一之旨，錄之。」

考試官教諭黃批：「善發聖賢授受之蘊者。」

考試官教諭朱批：「典雅莊重。」

大賢嘆聖人之善教，必述教之所以善焉。夫文以啓知，禮以約行，學之序也。知博約之序，則知所以入道矣。聖教所以爲善乎？此顏子學旣有得，因嘆聖道之高妙而及其教也。蓋曰：不可幾及者，聖人之道，固非示人以遠矣；所可循者，聖人之教，蓋確然示人以易矣。何也？夫道有所由入，强之則難；功有所當加，悖之則拂。吾夫子之教人也，因其材而不强人以難能，循其序亦
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The Master guides people skillfully, step by step. He broadens me through cultural learning and restrains me through ritual propriety.”

Huang Xingyao

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The Master’s everyday teaching never went beyond this. Only Master Yan could fully embody it; you, too, are adept at embodying Master Yan’s understanding.”

Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor, comments: “This composition forms a seamless whole and grasps the purport of bringing breadth of learning and restraint into unity. Include it.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Skillfully reveals the profound meaning of what was transmitted from sage to worthy.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classically elegant, dignified, and weighty.”

When the great worthy praises the sage’s skill in teaching, he must explain what makes that teaching excellent. Cultural learning opens up understanding, while ritual propriety restrains conduct: this is the proper sequence of learning. Knowing the sequence of broadening and restraining, one knows how to enter the Way. Is this why the sage’s teaching is excellent? Here, Master Yan, having already gained something through study, marvels at the loftiness and subtlety of the sage’s Way and consequently speaks of his teaching. In effect, he says: What seems beyond reach is the sage’s Way, yet the sage certainly does not present people with something remote. What can be followed is the sage’s teaching, which assuredly presents people with something accessible. Why is this? There is a route by which one enters the Way; forcing entry makes it difficult. There are points at which effort should be applied; acting contrary to them brings obstruction. In teaching people, our Master proceeds according to their capacities and does not force them to accomplish what is beyond their ability; he follows the proper sequence and also …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
不雜施而不遜何循循善誘如之蓋文以載道
非博知或失則隘矣夫子懼我之未博無以會
道之散殊也而先我以此焉使之或遠稽於文
獻之徵或廣求於事物之故學而知之多識於
前言往行以畜其德也默而識之知周於窮理
盡性求至于命也此則見聞博而所以豫吾入
道之基者在此不有夫子孰知文之當博也如
此哉禮以會道非約行或失則肆矣夫子懼我
之未約無以協道之中正也而繼我以此焉使
===
之或考祥於視履之旋或致審於用動之則範
我于皇極之門隨事觀理率履而不越也飭我
於嘉會之地因物察則範圍而不過也此則中
正履而所以要吾踐道之歸者在此不有夫子
又孰知禮之當約也如此哉夫先之文以始其
知則博文者致知之不可以已者也繼之禮以
約其行則約禮者力行之不可以已者也功以
漸加教有定序此夫子之教所以爲善而回之
由教而入亦因是庶幾矣乎雖然二者之教固
punctuated: 不雜施而不遜，何循循善誘如之！蓋文以載道，非博知，或失則隘矣。夫子懼我之未博，無以會道之散殊也，而先我以此焉。使之或遠稽於文獻之徵，或廣求於事物之故，學而知之，多識於前言往行以畜其德也；默而識之，知周於窮理盡性，求至于命也。此則見聞博，而所以豫吾入道之基者在此。不有夫子，孰知文之當博也如此哉！禮以會道，非約行，或失則肆矣。夫子懼我之未約，無以協道之中正也，而繼我以此焉。使之或考祥於視履之旋，或致審於用動之則，範我于皇極之門，隨事觀理，率履而不越也；飭我於嘉會之地，因物察則，範圍而不過也。此則中正履，而所以要吾踐道之歸者在此。不有夫子，又孰知禮之當約也如此哉！夫先之文以始其知，則博文者致知之不可以已者也；繼之禮以約其行，則約禮者力行之不可以已者也。功以漸加，教有定序，此夫子之教所以爲善，而回之由教而入，亦因是庶幾矣乎！雖然，二者之教固
translation_en:
…nor does he impart instruction indiscriminately and out of sequence. What could equal such orderly and skillful guidance! For cultural learning carries the Way. Unless knowledge is broadened, any failing will lead to narrowness. The Master fears that, while my learning remains insufficiently broad, I will have no means of comprehending the Way in its diverse manifestations; therefore he leads me first through cultural learning. He has me investigate the distant past through the testimony of texts and worthy men, or inquire widely into the reasons underlying affairs and things. By learning, I come to know, acquiring extensive knowledge of the words and deeds of earlier people so as to nurture my virtue. Silently retaining what I learn, I extend my understanding through fathoming principle and fully realizing human nature, seeking thereby to reach an understanding of Heaven’s mandate. Thus my experience and learning become broad: herein lies the foundation he prepares for my entry into the Way. Without the Master, who would know that cultural learning must be broadened in this manner!

Ritual brings the Way together. Unless conduct is restrained, any failing will lead to license. The Master fears that, while I remain insufficiently restrained, I will have no means of conforming to the Way’s centrality and correctness; therefore he guides me next through ritual. He has me examine auspicious signs by reviewing the course of my conduct, or scrutinize the standards governing action. He disciplines me at the gate of the August Ultimate, so that I observe principle in each affair and follow proper conduct without transgression. He orders my conduct in the realm where excellence comes together, so that I discern standards in things and remain within their bounds without excess. Thus I tread the path of centrality and correctness: herein lies the means by which he secures the ultimate direction of my practice of the Way. Without the Master, who, again, would know that one must be restrained through ritual in this manner!

He first uses cultural learning to initiate understanding: broadening one’s cultural learning thus means never ceasing to extend knowledge. He follows this with ritual to restrain conduct: restraint through ritual thus means never ceasing to practice earnestly. Effort increases gradually, and instruction follows a fixed sequence. This is what makes the Master’s teaching excellent; and is it not through this that I, Hui, may come close to entering the Way by following his instruction? Nevertheless, instruction in these two things certainly…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
有先後之序其實功則合一而亦相因者也蓋
博文者博禮之文也而非粗也約禮者約文之
禮也而非隱也夫博約之功卽精一之訓雖聖
賢道學之傳率不外是此固入道心法也要之
博者博此者也約者約此者也過此以往其曾
子一貫之唯顏子心齋坐忘之後乎噫豈惟顏
曾哉進如堯舜道統執中之傳謂非精一之功
基之也不可
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之敎誠則明矣
===
明則誠矣
王墀
同考試官敎諭羅 批 誠明處說得明盡未有如
此篇者
同考試官敎諭龍 批 天人之辨直截得明使學
者有下手處
考試官敎諭黃 批 是有得於誠明之學者
考試官敎諭朱 批 發揮精切
中庸別言性敎之異而必要其同也夫性命於
punctuated:
有先後之序，其實功則合一，而亦相因者也。蓋博文者，博禮之文也，而非粗也；約禮者，約文之禮也，而非隱也。夫博約之功，卽精一之訓，雖聖賢道學之傳，率不外是。此固入道心法也。要之，博者博此者也，約者約此者也。過此以往，其曾子一貫之唯、顏子心齋坐忘之後乎？噫！豈惟顏曾哉？進如堯舜道統執中之傳，謂非精一之功基之也，不可。
自誠明謂之性，自明誠謂之敎；誠則明矣，明則誠矣。
王墀
同考試官敎諭羅批：誠明處說得明盡，未有如此篇者。
同考試官敎諭龍批：天人之辨，直截得明，使學者有下手處。
考試官敎諭黃批：是有得於誠明之學者。
考試官敎諭朱批：發揮精切。
中庸別言性敎之異，而必要其同也。夫性命於
translation_en:
…have an order of precedence, yet in their actual practice they form a unity and also depend upon one another. Broad learning in cultural forms means learning broadly the cultural forms of ritual propriety; it is not superficial. Restraining oneself through ritual propriety means bringing oneself within the bounds of the ritual propriety embodied in cultural forms; it is not something obscure. The work of broad learning and self-restraint is precisely the teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. Even the transmission of the learning of the Way among sages and worthies generally does not go beyond this. This is indeed the method of cultivating the mind by which one enters the Way. In essence, broad learning means learning broadly this very thing, and self-restraint means restraining oneself by this very thing. To advance beyond this—would that be the stage after Master Zeng’s assent to the teaching of the single thread running through all, and Master Yan’s fasting of the mind and sitting in forgetfulness? Ah! Why speak only of Yan and Zeng? Going further, even in the transmission of holding fast to the Mean within the succession of the Way from Yao and Shun, one cannot deny that the work of refinement and single-mindedness laid its foundation.

“To proceed from sincerity to understanding is called nature; to proceed from understanding to sincerity is called instruction. With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.”

Wang Chi 王墀

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “No essay has explained sincerity and understanding as clearly and fully as this one.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: “The distinction between Heaven and human agency is made clear and direct, giving learners a place to begin their efforts.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Here is someone who has gained an understanding of the learning of sincerity and understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The exposition is precise and incisive.”

The Doctrine of the Mean speaks separately of the difference between nature and instruction, yet necessarily seeks their unity. Now, nature is ordained by…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天敎立於人若異矣然由敎入性以人盡天何
嘗不歸於同哉此子思子發明誠明之義者至
矣若謂天人之不能無判者分也而其未始有
間者理也于其分則等異于其理則歸同何也
理備於我精以粹矣至純而無所於雜夫是之
謂誠知發於我靈以瑩矣至照而無所於遺夫
是之謂明夫由誠而明者言之是乃原於帝降
之衷非假人力至者剛柔立本洗心退藏於密
自可酬酢而佑神也易簡成能齋戒神明其德
===
自能知來而藏往也非性而何夫由明而誠者
言之是乃本於吾學之力非由人性生者窮理
盡性見天則於會通之餘冒天下之道也下學
上達合天德於研幾之後立天下之有也非敎
而何此聖賢所由以分似若區以別者然而道
原於一理終歸于同爾蓋誠而明者天人合一
者也德無不實明無不照無所爲而然也明而
誠者以人合天者也先明乎善後實其善必俟
勉而至也誠之至者固無不照矣未至於誠者
punctuated: 天，敎立於人，若異矣。然由敎入性，以人盡天，何嘗不歸於同哉？此子思子發明誠明之義者至矣。若謂天人之不能無判者，分也；而其未始有間者，理也。于其分則等異，于其理則歸同，何也？理備於我，精以粹矣，至純而無所於雜，夫是之謂誠。知發於我，靈以瑩矣，至照而無所於遺，夫是之謂明。夫由誠而明者言之，是乃原於帝降之衷，非假人力至者。剛柔立本，洗心退藏於密，自可酬酢而佑神也；易簡成能，齋戒神明其德，自能知來而藏往也。非性而何？夫由明而誠者言之，是乃本於吾學之力，非由人性生者。窮理盡性，見天則於會通之餘，冒天下之道也；下學上達，合天德於研幾之後，立天下之有也。非敎而何？此聖賢所由以分，似若區以別者。然而道原於一，理終歸于同爾。蓋誠而明者，天人合一者也，德無不實，明無不照，無所爲而然也。明而誠者，以人合天者也，先明乎善，後實其善，必俟勉而至也。誠之至者，固無不照矣；未至於誠者
translation_en:
…Heaven, while teaching is established by human beings: they seem different. Yet through teaching one enters into one’s nature, and through human effort fully realizes Heaven. How could they fail to converge in unity? Master Zisi’s elucidation of the meaning of sincerity and understanding is thus consummate. The necessary distinction between Heaven and humanity concerns their respective allotments; their never having been separate concerns principle. In their allotments they differ in degree, but in principle they converge in unity. Why is this? Principle is fully present within me, refined and pure, utterly unmixed: this is what is called sincerity. Knowing issues from within me, numinous and luminous, illuminating everything without omission: this is what is called understanding.

Speaking of proceeding from sincerity to understanding, this originates in the inner moral norm bestowed by the Lord on High; it is not attained through human effort. With the firm and yielding establishing the foundation, one cleanses the heart and withdraws into hidden profundity; one can then naturally respond to affairs and assist the spiritual powers. With ease and simplicity bringing capacities to fruition, one purifies oneself through fasting and makes one’s virtue spiritually luminous; one can then naturally know what is to come and preserve what has passed. What could this be but nature? Speaking of proceeding from understanding to sincerity, this is grounded in the effort of one’s learning; it does not arise spontaneously from human nature. By investigating principle exhaustively and fully realizing one’s nature, one perceives Heaven’s norms after comprehending their interconnections, thereby encompassing the Way of all under Heaven. By learning what is below and penetrating what is above, one accords with Heaven’s virtue after examining the incipient workings of things, thereby establishing all that exists under Heaven. What could this be but teaching?

This is the basis for distinguishing sages from worthies, as though they belonged to separate categories. Yet the Way originates in unity, and principle ultimately converges in sameness. Those who proceed from sincerity to understanding unite Heaven and humanity as one: their virtue is wholly genuine and their understanding illuminates everything; this is so without deliberate effort. Those who proceed from understanding to sincerity bring humanity into accord with Heaven: first they understand goodness, and then they make that goodness real. They must exert themselves to attain it. Those whose sincerity is consummate assuredly leave nothing unilluminated; those who have not yet attained sincerity…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
先之格致之功而誠正豫焉精義入神其寂然
者可以見誠之源也德之實者固無不明矣尚
歉於實者殆乎問學之道而德性尊焉大心體
物其澄然者可以見誠之立也謂非明亦可以
至於誠哉是知性教之分聖賢之等也明誠之
同安勉之歸也思誠君子其當知所從事也乎
雖然首言性道教此獨言性教不及道者何也
噫道固在其中也誠明謂者率此性而天道者
也明誠謂者率此性而人道者也天人雖殊其
===
歸實一而已大抵由教者固當知善反矣性之
者奈何亦曰不可無盡性之功焉聖人定之中
正仁義而立人極此則道自我行教自我立而
性自我盡矣故曰惟至誠爲能盡性
堯舜之道孝弟而已矣
廖雲鵬
同考試官教諭安批堯舜無窮事業只自孝弟
中推出來此作發揚得盡非用心於內者不能道
同考試官教諭鄺批是寧志於作聖者不徒以
punctuated:
先之格致之功，而誠正豫焉。精義入神，其寂然者，可以見誠之源也。德之實者，固無不明矣；尚歉於實者，殆乎問學之道，而德性尊焉。大心體物，其澄然者，可以見誠之立也。謂非明亦可以至於誠哉？是知性教之分，聖賢之等也；明誠之同，安勉之歸也。思誠君子，其當知所從事也乎！雖然，首言性道教，此獨言性教，不及道者，何也？噫！道固在其中也。誠明謂者，率此性而天道者也；明誠謂者，率此性而人道者也。天人雖殊，其歸實一而已。大抵由教者，固當知善反矣；性之者，奈何？亦曰不可無盡性之功焉。聖人定之中正仁義而立人極，此則道自我行，教自我立，而性自我盡矣。故曰：「惟至誠爲能盡性。」
堯舜之道，孝弟而已矣。
廖雲鵬
同考試官教諭安批：「堯舜無窮事業，只自孝弟中推出來。此作發揚得盡，非用心於內者不能道。」
同考試官教諭鄺批：「是寧志於作聖者，不徒以
translation_en:
…first undertake the work of investigating things and extending knowledge, and making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind are already involved therein. By refining understanding of principles and entering into the spiritual, one can perceive the source of sincerity in that stillness. Those whose virtue is substantial are certainly never without understanding. Those still deficient in substance pursue the path of inquiry and learning [?], thereby honoring their virtuous nature. By enlarging the mind to embody all things, one can perceive the establishment of sincerity in that clarity. Can one claim that sincerity can also be attained without understanding? Thus we know that the distinction between nature and teaching marks the different levels of sage and worthy; the unity of understanding and sincerity is the common destination of those who attain it effortlessly and those who strive. Surely the gentleman intent upon sincerity should know where to direct his efforts!
Nevertheless, the opening speaks of nature, the Way, and teaching, whereas this passage speaks only of nature and teaching without mentioning the Way. Why is this? Ah! The Way is already contained within them. What is called proceeding from sincerity to understanding is following this nature as the Way of Heaven; what is called proceeding from understanding to sincerity is following this nature as the human Way. Though Heaven and humanity differ, their ultimate destination is truly one. Generally, those who proceed through teaching must know how properly to return to their nature. But what of those who possess it by nature? They, too, cannot dispense with the work of fully realizing their nature. The sage establishes centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, thereby setting the ultimate standard for humanity. Thus the Way is practiced through oneself, teaching is established through oneself, and one's nature is fully realized through oneself. Hence it is said: “Only utmost sincerity can fully realize one's nature.”
“The Way of Yao and Shun is simply filial piety and fraternal respect.”
Liao Yunpeng
Comment by Associate Examiner An, Instructor: “The boundless achievements of Yao and Shun were developed entirely from filial piety and fraternal respect. This composition brings out their significance exhaustively. No one who had not devoted himself to inward cultivation could have expressed this.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
文而已
考試官教諭黃批文有思致有體認殆無愧
於士矣
考試官教諭朱批精鬯
大賢言二聖之道不外率性之常而已夫性分
常道莫先孝弟也堯舜所以爲聖不過率此性
已爾聖脩之功何俟他求哉此孟子曉曹交意
蓋如此今夫道不遠人而遠人爲之者失之離
性外無聖而外性求之者幾於罔何則堯大聖
===
人也後世無及焉以放勳則天觀堯堯若有異
行也而不知堯之爲道亦惟從事於此性矣舜
大聖人也後世無及焉以重華協帝觀舜舜若
有絕德也而不知舜之爲道外性亦非所有事
矣親親爲仁吾性之孝形焉夫人同此性則同
此孝而堯舜固亦同夫人爾敬長爲義吾性之
弟著焉夫人同此性則同此弟而堯舜則亦與
人同爾蓋孝弟也者不慮而知吾性良知也堯
舜雖生知亦不過率孝弟之良知以爲知外此
punctuated:
文而已。
考試官教諭黃批：文有思致，有體認，殆無愧於士矣。
考試官教諭朱批：精鬯。
大賢言二聖之道，不外率性之常而已。夫性分常道，莫先孝弟也。堯舜所以爲聖，不過率此性已爾。聖脩之功，何俟他求哉？此孟子曉曹交意，蓋如此。今夫道不遠人，而遠人爲之者，失之離；性外無聖，而外性求之者，幾於罔。何則？堯，大聖人也，後世無及焉。以放勳則天觀堯，堯若有異行也，而不知堯之爲道，亦惟從事於此性矣。舜，大聖人也，後世無及焉。以重華協帝觀舜，舜若有絕德也，而不知舜之爲道，外性亦非所有事矣。親親爲仁，吾性之孝形焉。夫人同此性，則同此孝，而堯舜固亦同夫人爾。敬長爲義，吾性之弟著焉。夫人同此性，則同此弟，而堯舜則亦與人同爾。蓋孝弟也者，不慮而知，吾性良知也。堯舜雖生知，亦不過率孝弟之良知以爲知，外此
translation_en:
…literary composition alone.
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The composition displays thoughtful insight and personal understanding; its author is surely worthy of being called a scholar.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Refined and lucid.”
The great worthy says that the Way of the two sages consists simply in following the constant principles of human nature. Among the constant principles inherent in our nature, none takes precedence over filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. What made Yao and Shun sages was nothing more than following this nature. Why should the work of cultivating sagehood require seeking elsewhere? Such, broadly, was Mencius’s intention in enlightening Cao Jiao. Now, the Way is not far from people; those who pursue it far from people err by separating themselves from it. There is no sagehood outside human nature; those who seek it outside that nature come close to delusion. Why is this so? Yao was a great sage whom no one in later ages could equal. If we consider Yao in terms of his far-reaching achievements and his taking Heaven as his model, he seems to have possessed extraordinary conduct. Yet this overlooks the fact that Yao’s practice of the Way consisted solely in attending to this nature. Shun was a great sage whom no one in later ages could equal. If we consider Shun in terms of his renewed brilliance and his accord with the emperor Yao, he seems to have possessed peerless virtue. Yet this overlooks the fact that, in practicing the Way, Shun likewise concerned himself with nothing outside human nature. Loving one’s parents constitutes benevolence: in this, the filial devotion of our nature takes form. Everyone shares this nature and therefore shares this filial devotion; Yao and Shun were certainly no different from everyone else in this respect. Respecting one’s elders constitutes righteousness: in this, our nature’s respect for elder brothers becomes manifest. Everyone shares this nature and therefore shares this fraternal respect; Yao and Shun were likewise the same as other people in this respect. For filial devotion and fraternal respect are known without deliberation: they are the innate knowledge of our nature. Although Yao and Shun possessed knowledge from birth, their knowing consisted simply in following the innate knowledge of filial devotion and fraternal respect. Beyond this…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
良知而有所知非性之知也何庸心焉不學而
能吾性良能也堯舜雖安行亦不過率孝弟之
良能以爲能外此良能而有所能非性之能也
何致力焉本之民彝之常而寓聖脩之極其在
堯也猶夫舜也觀其自親睦以至昭明協和皆
舉此措之爾舍孝弟之外無堯矣堯亦更能外
此而他有所爲乎始之烝民之則而極作聖之
功其在舜也猶夫堯也觀其自克諧以至慎徽
風動皆推此運之爾舍孝弟之外無舜矣舜又
===
===
安能遠此而更有所加乎故曰而已矣者眞見
孝弟之足以盡堯舜而求堯舜之道者固不必
遠有所慕矣知此則知湯之所以爲湯文之所
以爲文亦非外性分有他道者昧此而泥於形
體之較不亦陋也與大抵堯舜聖之至者也孝
弟性之至者也蓋性分之中萬善咸備一孝弟
立而萬善固從之矣故始于家邦而終于四海
雖施諸後世而無朝夕者由此其選也若夫遠
人爲道外性求聖者其弊也離且罔又何怪哉
punctuated: 良知而有所知，非性之知也，何庸心焉？不學而能，吾性良能也。堯舜雖安行，亦不過率孝弟之良能以爲能。外此良能而有所能，非性之能也，何致力焉？本之民彝之常，而寓聖脩之極，其在堯也猶夫舜也。觀其自親睦以至昭明協和，皆舉此措之爾。舍孝弟之外無堯矣，堯亦更能外此而他有所爲乎？始之烝民之則，而極作聖之功，其在舜也猶夫堯也。觀其自克諧以至慎徽風動，皆推此運之爾。舍孝弟之外無舜矣，舜又安能遠此而更有所加乎？故曰「而已矣」者，眞見孝弟之足以盡堯舜，而求堯舜之道者固不必遠有所慕矣。知此，則知湯之所以爲湯、文之所以爲文，亦非外性分有他道者。昧此而泥於形體之較，不亦陋也與？大抵堯舜，聖之至者也；孝弟，性之至者也。蓋性分之中，萬善咸備，一孝弟立，而萬善固從之矣。故始于家邦而終于四海，雖施諸後世而無朝夕者，由此其選也。若夫遠人爲道、外性求聖者，其弊也離且罔，又何怪哉？
translation_en:
…to know something outside this innate moral knowledge is not knowledge belonging to our nature. Why expend thought on it? What we can do without learning is the innate capacity of our nature. Although Yao and Shun acted effortlessly, their capacity consisted simply in following their innate capacity for filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. To possess some capacity outside this innate capacity is not a capacity belonging to our nature. Why expend effort on it? Grounding himself in the constant norms of human relationships and embodying the utmost cultivation of the sage, Yao was just like Shun. Consider how he proceeded from bringing his kin into affectionate harmony to making virtue manifest and bringing all into concord: all this was simply putting these virtues into practice. Apart from filial devotion and brotherly respect, there is no Yao. Could Yao have gone beyond these and done something else? Beginning with the norms of the common people and bringing the work of becoming a sage to its culmination, Shun was just like Yao. Consider how he proceeded from achieving harmony in his family to carefully making the cardinal relationships flourish and transforming others as the wind moves them: all this was simply extending and exercising these virtues. Apart from filial devotion and brotherly respect, there is no Shun. How, then, could Shun have gone beyond these and added anything further?

Thus, the words “nothing more” express a true understanding that filial devotion and brotherly respect suffice to encompass all that Yao and Shun were. Those seeking the Way of Yao and Shun need not direct their admiration toward anything remote. Understanding this, one understands that what made Tang Tang, and King Wen King Wen, likewise involved no other Way outside their endowed nature. Is it not narrow-minded to miss this and become fixated on comparisons of bodily stature? Yao and Shun represent the utmost in sagehood; filial devotion and brotherly respect represent the utmost in our nature. Within our endowed nature, all goodness is fully present. Once filial devotion and brotherly respect are established, all goodness naturally follows. Thus, beginning with the family and state and extending throughout the realm, their influence reaches even later generations, without distinction of morning or evening; this is the source of their preeminence [?]. As for those who pursue a Way remote from human beings and seek sagehood outside human nature, their errors lead to estrangement and delusion. What is surprising about that?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
然則有志堯舜之道者如何曰近而取足吾性
分中則蕩蕩巍巍眞堯舜者固自在也
易
文明以健中正而應君子正也唯君子爲
能通天下之志
王徽猷
同考試官敎諭鄺批措詞典雅說理精到可卜
其爲佳士無疑
同考試官敎授簡批發揮大同之道詳盡非平
===
日正己應物者不能作
考試官敎諭黃批理明詞則
考試官敎諭朱批腴而暢
彖傳本卦以釋同人之貞而推其爲大同之道
也蓋天下无正外之同也而君子之所以大同
於天下者胥此矣與人同者而可以不之務乎
今夫同人之道審乎公私邪正之間而已矣卦
之爲同本非不足於公者而文王必重以利貞
之戒夫固欲人擇其正也是故必有明辨之智
punctuated:
然則有志堯舜之道者如何？曰：近而取足吾性分中，則蕩蕩巍巍，眞堯舜者固自在也。

易
文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子爲能通天下之志。
王徽猷

同考試官敎諭鄺批：措詞典雅，說理精到，可卜其爲佳士無疑。
同考試官敎授簡批：發揮大同之道詳盡，非平日正己應物者不能作。
考試官敎諭黃批：理明詞則。
考試官敎諭朱批：腴而暢。

彖傳本卦以釋同人之貞，而推其爲大同之道也。蓋天下无正外之同也，而君子之所以大同於天下者胥此矣。與人同者而可以不之務乎？今夫同人之道，審乎公私邪正之間而已矣。卦之爲同，本非不足於公者，而文王必重以利貞之戒，夫固欲人擇其正也。是故必有明辨之智
translation_en:
What, then, should those who aspire to the Way of Yao and Shun do? The answer is: seek nearby, finding sufficiency within our own endowed nature; then, vast and lofty, what truly made Yao and Shun who they were is already present within us.

Book of Changes
“Possessing cultivated clarity together with strength, central and correct yet responsive: this is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.”
Wang Huiyou

Comment by Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor: “The diction is classically elegant, and the exposition of principle precise and thorough. One can predict without doubt that he will prove an excellent scholar.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jian, Professor: “He expounds the Way of Great Unity thoroughly and fully. Only someone who habitually rectifies himself and responds appropriately to affairs could have written this.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The reasoning is clear and the language conforms to proper standards.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Rich and flowing.”

The Commentary on the Judgments draws upon this hexagram to explain the correctness of Fellowship with Others (Tongren), and extends its implications to establish the Way of Great Unity. For there is no fellowship under Heaven apart from correctness; this is the foundation upon which the gentleman achieves great unity with all under Heaven. Can those who seek fellowship with others neglect to attend to it? Now, the Way of Fellowship with Others consists simply in discerning the distinction between public-mindedness and private interest, between deviance and correctness. The fellowship represented by this hexagram is certainly not deficient in public-mindedness; nevertheless, King Wen insisted on adding the admonition, “It is beneficial to be correct.” His intention was surely that people should choose what is correct. Thus one must possess the wisdom to discriminate clearly…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也而後能審於所同而此卦之德則文明以健
者也夫其健也而出於文明也則是可否之辨
預持於翕受之初而諂瀆之幾不昧於泛交之
際其在同人固有求同理而不求同俗者矣必
有中正之守也而後能慎於所從而此卦之體
則中正而應者也夫其應也而本於中正也則
是所挾持者大而不舍己以徇人所篤棐者忠
而非自卑以求幸其事是君固有相知以心而
相濟以道者矣此固君子之正而同人之所尚
焉者也如此而不有以通天下之志邪蓋天下
无正外之理而同人以正則盡乎理矣理之所
在勢固不得而限之天下无正外之心而同人
以正則得其心矣心之所在跡又不得而拘之
故自其同之見於處物也不必其可者與之而
後以為同也雖其不可者拒之而天下亦不病
其為隘自其同之見於事君也不必其美者將
順之而後以為同也雖其過焉匡救之而天下
亦不病其為拂信乎天下之志唯君子為能通
punctuated: 也，而後能審於所同。而此卦之德，則文明以健者也。夫其健也而出於文明也，則是可否之辨，預持於翕受之初；而諂瀆之幾，不昧於泛交之際。其在同人，固有求同理而不求同俗者矣。必有中正之守也，而後能慎於所從。而此卦之體，則中正而應者也。夫其應也而本於中正也，則是所挾持者大，而不舍己以徇人；所篤棐者忠，而非自卑以求幸。其事是君，固有相知以心而相濟以道者矣。此固君子之正，而同人之所尚焉者也。如此，而不有以通天下之志邪？蓋天下无正外之理，而同人以正，則盡乎理矣。理之所在，勢固不得而限之。天下无正外之心，而同人以正，則得其心矣。心之所在，跡又不得而拘之。故自其同之見於處物也，不必其可者與之而後以為同也；雖其不可者拒之，而天下亦不病其為隘。自其同之見於事君也，不必其美者將順之而後以為同也；雖其過焉匡救之，而天下亦不病其為拂。信乎，天下之志，唯君子為能通
translation_en:
…only then can one discern carefully with whom to unite. The virtue of this hexagram is inner illumination joined with strength. Since its strength issues from illumination, the distinction between what is acceptable and unacceptable is already maintained when one first welcomes others, and the incipient signs of flattery and disrespect do not escape notice amid wide-ranging associations. In fellowship with others, one thus seeks agreement in principle rather than conformity to prevailing customs. Only with steadfast adherence to centrality and correctness can one exercise care in choosing whom to follow. The structure of this hexagram is central and correct, with a corresponding response. Since this response is rooted in centrality and correctness, what one upholds is great, and one does not abandon oneself to comply with others; the devoted assistance one offers is loyal [?], rather than self-abasement to seek favor. In serving this ruler, there is thus mutual understanding through the heart and mutual assistance through the Way. This is indeed the correctness of the noble man, and what Fellowship with Others (Tongren) esteems. Could such conduct fail to bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communion?

There is no principle under Heaven outside correctness; by uniting with others through correctness, one therefore fully realizes principle. Wherever principle resides, circumstances cannot limit it. There is no heart under Heaven outside correctness; by uniting with others through correctness, one therefore wins their hearts. Wherever the heart inclines, outward forms likewise cannot constrain it. Thus, when such fellowship manifests itself in dealing with others, one need not assent to what is acceptable before this can count as fellowship. Even when one rejects what is unacceptable, all under Heaven will not fault one for narrowness. When such fellowship manifests itself in serving the ruler, one need not support and advance his good actions before this can count as fellowship. Even when one corrects and remedies his errors, all under Heaven will not fault one for opposition. Truly, only the noble man can bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communion…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之而大同之道亦惟於至正得之耳苟或不擇
可否而一於同則反爲同之累矣而亦何所於
利哉故君子不爲苟同非好異也必天下之是
已則非矣不徇人以同非惡同也必天下之同
已則異矣推之三仁不能易其心而禹稷顏回
可以易其地皆是物也而况與人同者可以弗
之由乎嗚呼公私邪正之辨學易者可以深長
思矣
易簡之善配至德
===
郭培之
同考試官教諭龍批製詞朗潤析理精深非
惟秀雅可愛亦足占其體認之學
同考試官教諭安批易道配人事處講得透
徹必爲用意密造理深之士
考試官教諭黃批詞理俱到
考試官教諭朱批敷贍精當
大傳擬易理於人心之德而易之廣大徵矣蓋
人心易理其道本相通也以易簡之善而配之
punctuated:
之，而大同之道亦惟於至正得之耳。苟或不擇可否而一於同，則反爲同之累矣，而亦何所於利哉？故君子不爲苟同，非好異也；必天下之是已，則非矣。不徇人以同，非惡同也；必天下之同已，則異矣。推之，三仁不能易其心，而禹稷顏回可以易其地，皆是物也。而况與人同者，可以弗之由乎？嗚呼！公私邪正之辨，學易者可以深長思矣。
易簡之善配至德
郭培之
同考試官教諭龍批：製詞朗潤，析理精深。非惟秀雅可愛，亦足占其體認之學。
同考試官教諭安批：易道配人事處，講得透徹，必爲用意密、造理深之士。
考試官教諭黃批：詞理俱到。
考試官教諭朱批：敷贍精當。
大傳擬易理於人心之德，而易之廣大徵矣。蓋人心易理，其道本相通也。以易簡之善而配之
translation_en:
…them, and the way of great concord can likewise be attained only through utmost rectitude. If one fails to distinguish what is acceptable from what is not and seeks agreement alone, this instead becomes an impediment to concord. What benefit could there be in that? Thus the gentleman does not agree indiscriminately, but this is not because he delights in dissent. To insist that everyone under Heaven approve of oneself would itself be wrong [?]. He does not follow others merely to agree with them, but this is not because he dislikes concord. To insist that everyone under Heaven agree with oneself would itself create discord [?]. Extending this reasoning, the three humane men could not change their convictions, while Yu, Ji, and Yan Hui could have exchanged places: all exemplify this same principle. How, then, could someone seeking concord with others fail to follow it? Alas! Those who study the Book of Changes should ponder deeply and at length the distinction between public-mindedness and selfishness, between the deviant and the upright.
The Goodness of Ease and Simplicity Matches Supreme Virtue
Guo Peizhi
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor, comments: “The diction is lucid and polished, and the analysis of principle precise and profound. It is not merely elegant and pleasing; it also affords evidence of his learning through personal understanding and realization.”
Associate Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The correspondence between the Way of the Changes and human affairs is explained thoroughly. He must be a scholar meticulous in his thinking and profound in his attainment of principle.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Both diction and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Ample in exposition, precise and apt.”
The Great Commentary compares the principles of the Changes to the virtue of the human heart, thereby demonstrating the vastness and greatness of the Changes. For the human heart and the principles of the Changes are fundamentally interconnected in their Way. Taking the goodness of ease and simplicity and matching it with…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
至德夫何間然之有哉此可見易之廣大也大
傳之意若謂易之爲書也推其廣大之由固天
地以爲本論其廣大之實則天人以爲配是故
不但參諸造化而推之人事亦有脗合焉者矣
何則乾一而實確然示人易者也易之卦爻而
屬乎陽者其善不同同歸於易矣夫坤二而虛
隤然示人簡者也易之卦爻而屬乎陰者其善
不同同歸於簡矣實理昭於法象而善有成名
至道顯於卦爻而用无定在孰不曰此易簡之
===
在書者耳而何以配人之至德也殊不知人之
生也天命之性雖全體而不偏而健順之德則
隨感而異用故廓然太公而一私不撓人有健
之德也而易之言易者與之合焉蓋德行恒易
是亦天下之至健者爲之也而易與人非有二
矣怡然順理而一物无累人有順之德也而易
之言簡者與之準焉蓋德行恒簡亦惟天下之
至順者能之也而理與書合于一矣故默會乎
法象之表則易簡者健順之良能也健順者易
punctuated: 至德，夫何間然之有哉？此可見易之廣大也。大傳之意若謂：易之爲書也，推其廣大之由，固天地以爲本；論其廣大之實，則天人以爲配。是故不但參諸造化，而推之人事，亦有脗合焉者矣。何則？乾一而實，確然示人易者也。易之卦爻而屬乎陽者，其善不同，同歸於易矣。夫坤二而虛，隤然示人簡者也。易之卦爻而屬乎陰者，其善不同，同歸於簡矣。實理昭於法象，而善有成名；至道顯於卦爻，而用无定在。孰不曰：「此易簡之在書者耳，而何以配人之至德也？」殊不知人之生也，天命之性雖全體而不偏，而健順之德則隨感而異用。故廓然太公而一私不撓，人有健之德也，而易之言易者與之合焉。蓋德行恒易，是亦天下之至健者爲之也，而易與人非有二矣。怡然順理而一物无累，人有順之德也，而易之言簡者與之準焉。蓋德行恒簡，亦惟天下之至順者能之也，而理與書合于一矣。故默會乎法象之表，則易簡者健順之良能也，健順者易
translation_en:
…supreme virtue—what discrepancy could there be? Here one can see the vastness and greatness of the Changes. The meaning of the Great Commentary seems to be this: tracing the source of the vastness and greatness of the Changes as a book, one takes Heaven and Earth as its foundation; discussing the substance of that vastness and greatness, one takes Heaven and humanity as its counterparts. Thus it accords not only with the workings of creation: extended to human affairs, it also finds correspondences there.

Why is this? Qian is one and solid; firmly it manifests ease to people. The hexagrams and lines of the Changes that belong to yang differ in their excellences, yet all converge upon ease. Kun is two and hollow; yielding, it manifests simplicity to people. The hexagrams and lines of the Changes that belong to yin differ in their excellences, yet all converge upon simplicity. Substantial principle shines forth in patterns and images, and its excellence acquires established names; the supreme Way appears in hexagrams and lines, yet its operation has no fixed locus. Who would not say, “These are merely ease and simplicity as they exist in the book. How can they correspond to supreme human virtue?”

Such a person fails to understand that, when human beings are born, although the nature conferred by Heaven is complete and without partiality, the virtues of vigor and compliance operate differently in response to what moves them. Thus, when people are expansive and wholly impartial [?], undisturbed by a single selfish thought, they possess the virtue of vigor; and what the Changes calls ease accords with this. For constancy in ease in virtuous conduct is something accomplished by those of utmost vigor in the world: the Changes and humanity are not two separate things. When people joyfully follow principle, unencumbered by a single thing, they possess the virtue of compliance; and what the Changes calls simplicity corresponds to this. For constancy in simplicity in virtuous conduct is likewise something attainable only by those of utmost compliance in the world: principle and the book unite as one. Thus, apprehending silently what lies beyond patterns and images, one finds that ease and simplicity are the innate capacities of vigor and compliance, while vigor and compliance are ease…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
簡之成德也至德非妙於有而易簡非隱於无
矣其用相發而其理有不足以相當也哉神明
於卦爻之內則易本陰陽之理以為書也人會
陰陽之理以成德也人固天地之心而易亦性
命之奧矣其理相通而其善有不足以相配也
哉由是觀之而易之廣大見矣雖然易書固該
乎人道而人心實備乎易理者也聖人心涵太
極全體動靜而以其理示之易故易作而聖人
之心極昭焉此易簡之所自來也吾人之心孰
===
不有太極乎而往往以自私用智累之所以卒
畔于易也是故易知易從之訓聖人首發於傳
而此復以其相配言之若曰易簡吾心所本有
也而易特與之配焉耳然則自喪其良而不知
求配於易者可不為之動心乎
書
愼厥身脩思永惇敘九族庶明勵翼邇可
遠在茲
黃休泰
punctuated:
簡之成德也。至德非妙於有，而易簡非隱於无矣。其用相發，而其理有不足以相當也哉？神明於卦爻之內，則易本陰陽之理以為書也，人會陰陽之理以成德也。人固天地之心，而易亦性命之奧矣。其理相通，而其善有不足以相配也哉？由是觀之，而易之廣大見矣。雖然，易書固該乎人道，而人心實備乎易理者也。聖人心涵太極，全體動靜，而以其理示之易，故易作而聖人之心極昭焉。此易簡之所自來也。吾人之心孰不有太極乎？而往往以自私用智累之，所以卒畔于易也。是故易知易從之訓，聖人首發於傳，而此復以其相配言之，若曰：「易簡，吾心所本有也，而易特與之配焉耳。」然則自喪其良，而不知求配於易者，可不為之動心乎？

書

愼厥身脩，思永，惇敘九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠在茲。

黃休泰
translation_en:
…simplicity brought to perfected virtue. Supreme virtue does not exercise its subtle power solely in what exists, nor are ease and simplicity concealed in nonbeing. Their operations bring one another forth: could their principles fail to correspond? When one apprehends the spiritual illumination within the hexagrams and their lines, one sees that the Changes takes the principles of yin and yang as the basis of its text, while human beings comprehend those principles to perfect their virtue. Human beings are indeed the heart of Heaven and Earth, and the Changes contains the mysteries of human nature and destiny. Their principles interpenetrate: could their goodness fail to match? Viewed in this way, the breadth and greatness of the Changes become apparent.

Nevertheless, although the Changes encompasses the human Way, the human heart itself fully possesses the principles of the Changes. The sage’s heart embraces the Supreme Ultimate and fully embodies activity and stillness, displaying their principles in the Changes. Thus, when the Changes was composed, the sage’s heart became supremely manifest. This is the source of ease and simplicity. Which of our hearts does not possess the Supreme Ultimate? Yet we frequently burden it with selfishness and contrived cleverness, and thus ultimately depart from the Changes. Therefore, the sage first set forth in the Commentary the teaching concerning what is easy to know and easy to follow, and here again speaks of their correspondence, as if to say: “Ease and simplicity are inherent in our hearts; the Changes merely corresponds to them.” Can those who themselves forfeit their innate goodness and do not know to seek correspondence with the Changes fail to be stirred by this?

Book of Documents

“Be mindful of cultivating your person; think of the enduring consequences. Bring the nine degrees of kinship into cordial order, and let the many enlightened men exert themselves in assisting you. Whether what is near can reach afar depends on this.”

Huang Xiutai

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭張批此題似易實難作者不掇
陳言則聘浮詞理渾涵而文醇雅者僅見此篇
同考試官敎授莫批融貫心理思致悠揚疏通知
遠之學不當如是耶取之
考試官敎諭黃批莊重有體
考試官敎諭朱批峻潔
人君知所以脩德則其化大行矣夫君身萬化
之原也德脩于上而天下國家之化有不裕如
矣乎臯陶陳謨而廣之也蓋謂人君之治求之
===
於外者拂而難反之于已者順而易所謂迪德
謨明者亦惟於身焉取之誠使其逸欲是戒敬
脩其可願之善而發號施令之必臧兢業自持
率循於罔愆之度而出入起居之必欽然猶謀
慮深長不以小成而自安言而思世為天下法
也志意高遠不以近利而自狃行而思世為天
下則也以此迪德則脩身之外無餘理而思永
之外無餘心吾見氣機感動而道化流行由之
而家焉此心同也此理同也具文以合愛懽然
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭張批：此題似易實難，作者不掇陳言，則聘浮詞。理渾涵而文醇雅者，僅見此篇。
同考試官敎授莫批：融貫心理，思致悠揚，疏通知遠之學，不當如是耶？取之。
考試官敎諭黃批：莊重有體。
考試官敎諭朱批：峻潔。
人君知所以脩德，則其化大行矣。夫君身，萬化之原也。德脩于上，而天下國家之化有不裕如矣乎？臯陶陳謨而廣之也，蓋謂人君之治，求之於外者拂而難，反之于已者順而易。所謂迪德謨明者，亦惟於身焉取之。誠使其逸欲是戒，敬脩其可願之善，而發號施令之必臧；兢業自持，率循於罔愆之度，而出入起居之必欽。然猶謀慮深長，不以小成而自安，言而思世為天下法也；志意高遠，不以近利而自狃，行而思世為天下則也。以此迪德，則脩身之外無餘理，而思永之外無餘心。吾見氣機感動，而道化流行。由之而家焉，此心同也，此理同也，具文以合愛，懽然
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “This topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Writers either piece together stale sayings or deploy empty phrases [?]. Only in this essay have I found principles comprehensively encompassed and prose pure and elegant.”
Associate Examiner Mo, Professor, comments: “It integrates the mind and principle throughout, and its thought unfolds with sustained resonance. Should not learning that brings penetrating understanding and knowledge of what is distant be like this? Accept it.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Grave and dignified, with proper form.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Lofty and limpid.”
When a ruler understands how to cultivate virtue, his transforming influence spreads far and wide. The ruler’s person is the source of all transformation. If virtue is cultivated above, how could the transformation of all under Heaven, the state, and the family fail to proceed abundantly and with ease? Gao Yao set forth his counsels and elaborated upon this. His meaning was that, in a ruler’s governance, seeking externally meets resistance and difficulty, whereas turning back upon oneself proceeds smoothly and easily. What is called practicing virtue and being discerning in counsel is likewise to be sought only within oneself. Let him truly guard against indolence and desire, reverently cultivate the goodness worthy of aspiration, and ensure that his proclamations and commands are good. Let him maintain himself in vigilance, follow standards that admit no error, and ensure reverence in going out and coming in, rising and resting. Yet his deliberations must also be profound and far-reaching: he must not rest content with minor achievements, but, when speaking, consider how his words may serve for generations as a model for all under Heaven. His aspirations must be lofty and far-reaching: he must not become habituated to immediate advantage, but, when acting, consider how his conduct may serve for generations as a standard for all under Heaven. If he practices virtue in this way, no principle lies outside self-cultivation, and no concern lies outside taking thought for the long term. I see the vital impulses stirring in response, and the transforming influence of the Way spreading freely. Extend this to the family: this mind is shared, and this principle is shared. Establish ceremonial forms to unite them in affection, joyfully …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
情意之浹洽殊事以合敬沛然恩義之流通觀
于其家而家無不齊也是不由于脩身乎由之
而國焉此心同也此理同也百僚師師奮庸以
熙帝載庶官濟濟祗慎以亮天工觀于其國而
國無不治也是又不本于脩身乎又由家國而
之天下焉此心同也此理同也舉此加彼有不
疾而速之機篤近舉遠有不行而至之妙萬邦
之協和皆俊德之所昭宣四方之風動皆惠迪
之所衣被觀于天下而天下無不平也又豈能
===
外于此身之脩耶夫脩身則迪德之實可見而
其化蓋不止于謨明弼諧而已非吾君之所當
務歟嗟乎是說也天德王道一以貫之者也其
要在于兢業萬幾蓋幾者動之微善惡之所由
分也察微知著圖大於細而檢身之功益以邃
密其于治也何有此臯陶所以尤致意於終篇
也堯舜執中要不外是序道統者而謂臯陶見
而知之有以哉
我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷歷
punctuated:
情意之浹洽；殊事以合敬，沛然恩義之流通。觀于其家，而家無不齊也，是不由于脩身乎？由之而國焉，此心同也，此理同也。百僚師師，奮庸以熙帝載；庶官濟濟，祗慎以亮天工。觀于其國，而國無不治也，是又不本于脩身乎？又由家國而之天下焉，此心同也，此理同也。舉此加彼，有不疾而速之機；篤近舉遠，有不行而至之妙。萬邦之協和，皆俊德之所昭宣；四方之風動，皆惠迪之所衣被。觀于天下，而天下無不平也，又豈能外于此身之脩耶？夫脩身，則迪德之實可見，而其化蓋不止于謨明弼諧而已，非吾君之所當務歟？嗟乎！是說也，天德王道，一以貫之者也。其要在于兢業萬幾，蓋幾者，動之微，善惡之所由分也。察微知著，圖大於細，而檢身之功益以邃密，其于治也何有？此臯陶所以尤致意於終篇也。堯舜執中，要不外是。序道統者，而謂臯陶見而知之，有以哉！

我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷
translation_en:
…feelings become thoroughly harmonious; through distinct duties, they unite in reverence, and kindness and righteousness flow abundantly. Observe his family: it is fully ordered. Does this not proceed from cultivating oneself? Extend this to the state: the mind is the same, and the principle is the same. The hundred officials emulate one another, exerting themselves in service to advance the sovereign’s undertakings; the assembled officers, reverent and cautious, assist in Heaven’s work. Observe his state: it is fully governed. Is this not likewise rooted in cultivating oneself? Extend this further, from family and state to all under Heaven: the mind is the same, and the principle is the same. Applying here what has been achieved there brings about swiftness without haste; attending earnestly to what is near and extending it to what is distant achieves arrival without movement. The concord of the myriad states is entirely the manifestation of illustrious virtue; the transformation of the four quarters, as though stirred by the wind, is entirely the encompassing influence of following the Way. Observe all under Heaven: everything is at peace. How could this lie outside the cultivation of one’s own person?

Through self-cultivation, the substance of putting virtue into practice becomes visible, and its transforming influence surely extends beyond enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance. Is this not what our ruler should strive for? Ah! This teaching runs through Heaven’s virtue and the kingly Way as a single thread. Its essential point is to attend with vigilant care to the myriad incipient movements of affairs. Such incipient movements are the subtle beginnings of action, where good and evil diverge. By discerning the subtle, one knows what will become manifest; by attending to small details, one plans for great things. As the work of examining oneself becomes ever more profound and exact, what difficulty can governing present? This is why Gao Yao gave particular attention to this at the close of the chapter. Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the Mean ultimately amounts to nothing beyond this. Those who trace the succession of the Way have reason to say that Gao Yao knew it through seeing it firsthand!

“I have received Heaven’s mandate. May our years greatly match those of the Xia, and may we not fall short of the Yin’s length of…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
年
蔣龍
同考試官教諭張批說君臣同心祈命詞不繁
璅意自明達可以爲文矣
同考試官教授莫批語緒和平想見當時氣象
經義之優者
考試官教諭黃批體裁渾雄
考試官教諭朱批典暢
大臣欲君臣期有周受命之永兼乎二代焉甚
===
矣天命之難諶也然則欲兼二代之永命者不
有望于君臣之相成哉召公陳誥于王而深致
意于此也蓋曰天命之簡畀無常上下之責任
則一我之欲其勤恤者豈有他哉亦相期於無
窮而已誠以我周之命文考之所誕膺締造亦
艱難矣玆欲其中土之乂克配上帝有以衍統
緒於昌明武王之所迪有積累亦憂勤矣玆欲
其初服之愼克享天心有以垂曆數於悠久遠
而稽之於夏歷年四百何其祚之靈長也然祚
punctuated:
年。

蔣龍。

同考試官教諭張批：說君臣同心祈命，詞不繁璅，意自明達，可以爲文矣。

同考試官教授莫批：語緒和平，想見當時氣象，經義之優者。

考試官教諭黃批：體裁渾雄。

考試官教諭朱批：典暢。

大臣欲君臣期有周受命之永，兼乎二代焉。甚矣，天命之難諶也！然則欲兼二代之永命者，不有望于君臣之相成哉？召公陳誥于王而深致意于此也。蓋曰：天命之簡畀無常，上下之責任則一。我之欲其勤恤者，豈有他哉？亦相期於無窮而已。誠以我周之命，文考之所誕膺，締造亦艱難矣。玆欲其中土之乂，克配上帝，有以衍統緒於昌明；武王之所迪有，積累亦憂勤矣。玆欲其初服之愼，克享天心，有以垂曆數於悠久。遠而稽之於夏，歷年四百，何其祚之靈長也！然祚
translation_en:
…years.

Jiang Long 蔣龍.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It explains how ruler and ministers unite their hearts in praying for the Mandate. The wording is neither verbose nor fussy, and the meaning is naturally clear and accessible. This is worthy essay writing.”

Associate Examiner Mo, Professor, comments: “The flow of language is harmonious and even, allowing one to imagine the atmosphere of that time. An outstanding exposition of the Classics.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The composition is integrated and powerful.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classically elegant and fluent.”

The great minister wished ruler and ministers to aspire to a duration of Zhou’s Heaven-granted Mandate that would encompass those of the two preceding dynasties. How very difficult it is to rely upon Heaven’s Mandate!
