If they wished for a lasting Mandate encompassing the durations of both dynasties, must they not have placed their hopes in ruler and ministers supporting one another? When the Duke of Shao presented his announcement to the king, he gave this matter profound attention. His meaning was this: Heaven’s selection and bestowal of its Mandate are not constant, but the responsibility of those above and below is one. Could I have any other purpose in wishing them to be diligent and solicitous? It is simply that we should together aspire to an endless future.

Indeed, the Mandate of our Zhou was grandly received by our deceased cultured father, King Wen; founding the dynasty was arduous indeed. Now we wish that, through good government of the central lands, we may worthily match the Lord on High and extend the dynastic succession in flourishing splendor. What King Wu came to possess likewise resulted from an accumulation of anxious toil. Now we wish that, through care at the beginning of the reign, we may win Heaven’s favor and transmit the allotted years of rule far into the future. Looking far back to examine Xia, we find that it lasted four hundred years. How enduring was its blessed dynastic fortune! Yet that fortune…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
于有夏亦可以祚于有周將申命而用休近而
觀之於殷歷年六百何其慶之綿延也然慶於
有殷亦可以慶于有周將眷命而用懋並乎夏
而又克兼乎殷天之祐也無已吾受之也亦無
已宜君宜王得以紹休于先烈矣同乎殷而又
克兼乎夏帝之畀也無疆吾承之也亦無疆克
長克君得以媲美于前代矣雖曰周命維新安
知其久而不渝也上下勤恤正以迓滋至之休
可諉曰我周受命止如夏而已乎雖曰多方誕
===
受安保其遠而不替也君臣同心正以凝單厚
之福可諉曰我周受命止如殷而已乎吁召公
之欲君臣祈天永命如此可謂深切著明者矣
雖然帝天之命主于民心而敬德又所以誠小
民故曰王其疾敬德又曰欲王以小民受天永
命人君以德誠民則至和熏烝天心感孚歷年
久長可以馴致宜乎召公反覆致意也厥後成
王爲周令主而卜世卜年皆過其曆然後知老
成謀國之慮非偶然者噫其斯以爲召公歟
punctuated:
于有夏，亦可以祚于有周，將申命而用休。近而觀之於殷，歷年六百，何其慶之綿延也！然慶於有殷，亦可以慶于有周，將眷命而用懋。並乎夏而又克兼乎殷，天之祐也無已，吾受之也亦無已；宜君宜王，得以紹休于先烈矣。同乎殷而又克兼乎夏，帝之畀也無疆，吾承之也亦無疆；克長克君，得以媲美于前代矣。雖曰周命維新，安知其久而不渝也？上下勤恤，正以迓滋至之休，可諉曰我周受命止如夏而已乎？雖曰多方誕受，安保其遠而不替也？君臣同心，正以凝單厚之福，可諉曰我周受命止如殷而已乎？吁！召公之欲君臣祈天永命如此，可謂深切著明者矣。

雖然，帝天之命主于民心，而敬德又所以誠小民。故曰：「王其疾敬德。」又曰：「欲王以小民受天永命。」人君以德誠民，則至和熏烝，天心感孚，歷年久長，可以馴致。宜乎召公反覆致意也！厥後成王爲周令主，而卜世卜年皆過其曆，然後知老成謀國之慮非偶然者。噫！其斯以爲召公歟？
translation_en:
…upon the Xia could likewise confer blessings upon the Zhou, renewing the mandate and bestowing favor. Looking to the more recent Yin, whose rule lasted six hundred years, how enduring were its blessings! Yet the power that blessed the Yin could likewise bless the Zhou, favoring it with the mandate and fostering its flourishing. Equaling the Xia and also encompassing the span of the Yin, Heaven’s protection would be unceasing, and our reception of it likewise unceasing. Worthy to be lords and kings, we could carry forward the glory of our forebears’ achievements. Equaling the Yin and also encompassing the span of the Xia, the Supreme Lord’s gifts would be boundless, and our inheritance of them likewise boundless. Capable of leading and ruling, we could rival the excellence of former dynasties. Although it is said, “Zhou’s mandate is newly bestowed,” how can we know that it will endure without change? Those above and below must labor diligently and be watchful, precisely to welcome blessings arriving in ever greater abundance. Could we evade this responsibility by saying that our Zhou’s receipt of the mandate need only last as long as the Xia’s? Although it is said, “The many regions have amply received [the mandate],” how can we ensure that it will continue far into the future without decline? Ruler and ministers must be of one mind, precisely to secure abundant blessings. Could we evade this responsibility by saying that our Zhou’s receipt of the mandate need only last as long as the Yin’s? Ah! Such was the Duke of Shao’s desire that ruler and ministers should pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate. His intent may indeed be called profound, earnest, and clearly expressed.

Nevertheless, the mandate of the Supreme Lord, Heaven, rests upon the people’s hearts, and reverence for virtue is also the means of winning the sincere allegiance of the common people. Thus he said, “Let the king make haste to revere virtue.” He also said, “I desire that the king, through the common people, receive Heaven’s enduring mandate.” If a ruler wins the people’s sincere allegiance through virtue, perfect harmony will spread its influence, and Heaven’s heart will be moved and respond in trust. A long duration of rule can thereby gradually be attained. It was fitting that the Duke of Shao should repeatedly emphasize this concern! Subsequently, King Cheng became an excellent ruler of Zhou, and the dynasty’s duration exceeded the allotted span of both generations and years foretold by divination. Only then do we understand that the seasoned elder’s deliberations for the state were no casual matter. Ah! Was this not what made him the Duke of Shao?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
詩
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除
俾爾多益以莫不庶
陳聯芳
同考試官教諭龔批題語若重復而其中自有
脉絡此作體貼得精可以式矣
同考試官學正彭批詞意渾成而且有倫得作
詩之義
考試官教諭黃批是能發揚忠愛之情者
===
考試官教諭朱批典雅
臣子託天眷君之至而錫福無所不備焉蓋百
順之謂備福莫大焉詩人之祝其君者以之忠
愛之情可見矣且天保臣子有愛君無巳之心
故託諸祝頌以致其願望之私若曰吾人受君
之恩渥矣莫知其所以報者亦惟望諸天耳天
之所以眷吾君者何如降鑒不遠所以扶持而
安全之者益篤其仁愛之心使之滿而不溢高
而不危將以奠之磐石之固而承藉之基恃以
punctuated:
詩

天保定爾，亦孔之固。俾爾單厚，何福不除？俾爾多益，以莫不庶。

陳聯芳

同考試官教諭龔批：題語若重復，而其中自有脉絡。此作體貼得精，可以式矣。

同考試官學正彭批：詞意渾成，而且有倫，得作詩之義。

考試官教諭黃批：是能發揚忠愛之情者。

考試官教諭朱批：典雅。

臣子託天眷君之至，而錫福無所不備焉。蓋百順之謂備，福莫大焉。詩人之祝其君者以之，忠愛之情可見矣。且天保，臣子有愛君無巳之心，故託諸祝頌，以致其願望之私。若曰：吾人受君之恩渥矣，莫知其所以報者，亦惟望諸天耳。天之所以眷吾君者何如？降鑒不遠，所以扶持而安全之者，益篤其仁愛之心，使之滿而不溢，高而不危，將以奠之磐石之固，而承藉之基恃以
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Heaven protects and establishes you, with exceeding firmness. It causes your blessings to be wholly abundant: what blessing does it not bestow? It causes you to receive ever greater increase, so that nothing is lacking in abundance.”

Chen Lianfang

Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor, comments: “The wording of the topic seems repetitive, yet it has its own connected progression. This essay grasps it with precision and may serve as a model.”

Associate Examiner Peng, Director of Studies, comments: “Its language and meaning form a seamless whole and are orderly as well. It captures the intent behind the composition of the ode.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “This succeeds in giving full expression to feelings of loyalty and love.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

The subject gives expression through Heaven to the utmost solicitude for his ruler, with blessings bestowed that lack nothing. All things proceeding favorably constitute completeness; no good fortune is greater than this. The poet invokes this in blessing his ruler, making his feelings of loyalty and love apparent. Now, in “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao), the subject has an unceasing love for his ruler. He therefore entrusts it to words of blessing and praise, expressing his heartfelt hopes. It is as though he said: “We have received our ruler’s generous favor. Knowing no way to repay it, we can only look to Heaven. How does Heaven show solicitude for our ruler? Its downward gaze is never far away. In supporting him and keeping him safe, it makes its benevolent love ever more profound, allowing him to be full without overflowing and exalted without peril. It will establish him with the firmness of a great rock, so that the foundation supporting him may be relied upon to…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
無恐矣臨下有赫所以保右而申命之者益隆
其眷顧之私使之身其用康國其用寧將以措
之泰山之安而帝位之履賴以不疚矣所以保
定之者何其固耶蓋使爾之受福也與時俱積
旣斂之而盡厚矣然厚薄之勢相乗者也所受
者一或不繼則厚者有時而薄非福之全也其
必有秩之祜黙運夫循環之端前之所錫方除
其舊而後之所繼已布其新翕受有無方之益
而美利獲厚終之慶是所以成其盡厚者益不
===
可窮矣又何有不除乎又使爾之受福也日進
無疆旣集之而多益矣然損益之機相形者也
所受者一有不繼則益者有時而損非福之備
也其必多助之至引之爲盛大之休在此者惟
見其有餘而在彼者非見其不足天心篤栽培
之理而造化無多取之忌是所以成其多益者
愈不可紀矣又何有不庶乎至是則吾君諸福
之物爲始備而吾人願望之私亦庶乎少慰矣
大抵人君之所奉若者天道也則其所以欽承
punctuated:
無恐矣。臨下有赫，所以保右而申命之者，益隆其眷顧之私，使之身其用康，國其用寧，將以措之泰山之安，而帝位之履賴以不疚矣。所以保定之者何其固耶！蓋使爾之受福也，與時俱積，旣斂之而盡厚矣。然厚薄之勢相乗者也，所受者一或不繼，則厚者有時而薄，非福之全也。其必有秩之祜，黙運夫循環之端，前之所錫方除其舊，而後之所繼已布其新，翕受有無方之益，而美利獲厚終之慶，是所以成其盡厚者益不可窮矣。又何有不除乎？又使爾之受福也，日進無疆，旣集之而多益矣。然損益之機相形者也，所受者一有不繼，則益者有時而損，非福之備也。其必多助之至，引之爲盛大之休，在此者惟見其有餘，而在彼者非見其不足。天心篤栽培之理，而造化無多取之忌，是所以成其多益者愈不可紀矣。又何有不庶乎？至是，則吾君諸福之物爲始備，而吾人願望之私亦庶乎少慰矣。
大抵人君之所奉若者天道也，則其所以欽承
translation_en:
…without fear. Heaven looks down in its radiant majesty; in protecting him and renewing its mandate, it deepens its particular care for him, bringing well-being to his person and peace to his state. It will establish him in security like that of Mount Tai, so that his occupancy of the imperial throne may remain free from affliction. How firm is the protection by which Heaven secures him! It causes the blessings you receive to accumulate with time: gathered together, they have already attained the fullest abundance. Yet abundance and scarcity succeed one another. Should the blessings received ever cease to continue, abundance will sometimes become scarcity; this would not be the fullness of blessing. There must therefore be blessings bestowed in due succession, silently setting the cycle in motion. Just as the earlier gifts shed their old forms, those that follow have already spread anew. In receiving them all together, one gains increase without limit, and these benefits bring the joy of abundance enduring to the end. Thus, what brings their abundance to fullness becomes ever more inexhaustible. How, then, could they fail to be renewed?
It also causes the blessings you receive to increase daily without bound: assembled together, they have already brought manifold increase. Yet the workings of decrease and increase manifest themselves in relation to one another. Should the blessings received ever cease to continue, increase will sometimes turn to decrease; this would not be the completeness of blessing. The utmost abundance of assistance must therefore extend them into blessings of magnificent scope. Here one sees only a surplus, while elsewhere no insufficiency appears. Heaven's purpose steadfastly follows the principle of nurturing growth, and the workings of creation impose no prohibition on receiving abundantly. Thus, what produces this manifold increase becomes ever more beyond reckoning. How, then, could the blessings fail to be numerous? Only at this point do all the blessings of our ruler become complete, and our own heartfelt hopes may perhaps find some small consolation.
In general, what a ruler reverently follows is the Way of Heaven; thus, that which he reverently receives…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之者亦惟天之明命而已天保臣子必備言其
天福之隆得無侈乎噫雖其願望之深媚愛之
至其從諷諫矣乎故召公卷阿之告必本於壽
考福祿之盛而書以斂時五福爲武王告蓋欲
履其盛者思以保其終而以克負荷者當自得
之於言意之表此固詩人之意也其得告君之
體可與言忠愛者與
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽考遐不作人
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四
===
方
黃星耀
同考試官教諭龔批作人綱紀之義發揮殆
盡錄之
同考試官學正彭批此必有得於
聖化者可與言詩矣
考試官教諭黃批渾然成章可誦
考試官教諭朱批文有典則
詩人兩興美聖人之德自其化人統人者言之
punctuated:
之者，亦惟天之明命而已。《天保》，臣子必備言其天福之隆，得無侈乎？噫！雖其願望之深，媚愛之至，其從諷諫矣乎？故召公《卷阿》之告，必本於壽考福祿之盛，而《書》以斂時五福爲武王告。蓋欲履其盛者思以保其終，而以克負荷者當自得之於言意之表。此固詩人之意也，其得告君之體，可與言忠愛者與？
倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
黃星耀
同考試官教諭龔批：作人綱紀之義，發揮殆盡，錄之。
同考試官學正彭批：此必有得於聖化者，可與言詩矣。
考試官教諭黃批：渾然成章，可誦。
考試官教諭朱批：文有典則。
詩人兩興，美聖人之德，自其化人統人者言之
translation_en:
…in reverently receiving it, he need only follow Heaven’s luminous mandate. In “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao), the minister fully describes the abundance of Heaven’s blessings upon his ruler: is this not extravagant? Ah! Though his hopes are profound and his affectionate devotion utmost, does he thereby offer indirect admonition [?]? Thus the Duke of Shao’s counsel in “Winding Hills” (Juan a) necessarily takes as its basis the fullness of longevity, blessings, and emoluments; and the Book of Documents counsels King Wu to gather these five blessings. The intention is that one enjoying such abundance should consider how to preserve it to the end, while one capable of bearing the burden should himself grasp what lies beyond the words and their expressed meaning. This, indeed, is the poet’s intent. Having mastered the proper manner of addressing a ruler, may he not be counted among those with whom one can discuss loyalty and affection?
Vast is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in the heavens. The king of Zhou is long-lived: how could he fail to nurture men of worth? Chisel and polish his pattern; make gold and jade his substance. Diligently our king gives order to the four quarters.
Huang Xingyao.
Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor in a county Confucian school, comments: “The meanings of nurturing men of worth and giving order are expounded almost exhaustively. Include this essay.”
Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “This must be someone who has gained an understanding of the sage’s transforming influence. One may discuss the Odes with him.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor in a county Confucian school, comments: “The composition forms a seamless whole and is worthy of recitation.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor in a county Confucian school, comments: “The writing follows classical standards.”
Through two evocative comparisons, the poet praises the sage’s virtue, speaking of it in terms of his transforming and governing the people…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也蓋德者治化之本也周王之德久而且純其
能振作綱紀天下也宜哉此詩人所以歌咏之
也其託興之意若曰在天皆成象也惟玆有取
於雲漢之爲章焉其懸象也倬然其甚大其著
明也煥乎其有章在天之文於斯爲至矣况我
文王之德之久不足以成天下之化乎蓋民風
之所尚恒視乎所感之淺深也我周王至德之
所感召而必得其壽皇天之所眷命而多歷年
所是壽考也者所以運敎思於無窮者也故在
===
上者鼓舞作興有以神其機於無間而在下者
敏德遷善有以翼其進於日新大以成大小以
成小而一代人文之運於是乎開之矣聖人之
所以化人者蓋有所自如此在物皆有文質也
惟玆有取於文質之至者焉追琢以爲章而盡
人之巧也金玉以爲相而渾乎天成也在物之
理於是爲至矣况我文王之德之純而不足以
維天下之治乎蓋人心之所向恒視乎君德之
純貳也惟我周王持自强不息之心而恒以一
punctuated:
也。蓋德者，治化之本也。周王之德，久而且純，其能振作綱紀天下也，宜哉！此詩人所以歌咏之也。其託興之意若曰：在天皆成象也，惟玆有取於雲漢之爲章焉。其懸象也，倬然其甚大；其著明也，煥乎其有章。在天之文，於斯爲至矣。况我文王之德之久，不足以成天下之化乎？蓋民風之所尚，恒視乎所感之淺深也。我周王至德之所感召，而必得其壽；皇天之所眷命，而多歷年所。是壽考也者，所以運敎思於無窮者也。故在上者鼓舞作興，有以神其機於無間；而在下者敏德遷善，有以翼其進於日新。大以成大，小以成小，而一代人文之運，於是乎開之矣。聖人之所以化人者，蓋有所自如此。
在物皆有文質也，惟玆有取於文質之至者焉。追琢以爲章，而盡人之巧也；金玉以爲相，而渾乎天成也。在物之理，於是爲至矣。况我文王之德之純，而不足以維天下之治乎？蓋人心之所向，恒視乎君德之純貳也。惟我周王持自强不息之心，而恒以一
translation_en:
…so it is. Virtue is the foundation of government and moral transformation. The virtue of the king of Zhou was both enduring and pure: how fitting that he could rouse the people and order all under Heaven! This is why the poet sang his praises. The meaning conveyed through his evocative imagery is as follows: everything in Heaven forms a celestial configuration, but here he singles out the patterned brilliance of the Milky Way. Suspended in the sky, it is lofty and immense; shining forth, it is radiant in its pattern. Here celestial beauty reaches its utmost. How, then, could the enduring virtue of our King Wen fail to bring about the moral transformation of all under Heaven? What the people esteem in their customs always depends on how deeply they have been moved. Through the response evoked by his consummate virtue, our king of Zhou was assured of longevity; favored and commissioned by August Heaven, he lived through many years. This longevity enabled him to exercise his purpose of instruction without end. Thus those above inspired and encouraged the people, giving the workings of transformation an unfailingly wondrous efficacy; those below diligently cultivated virtue and turned toward goodness, furthering their progress through daily renewal. Those of great capacity achieved greatness, and those of lesser capacity achieved what lay within their scope. Thus began an era of cultural flourishing. Such was the source from which the sage’s transformation of the people proceeded.
All things possess both outward refinement and underlying substance, but here the poet singles out those in which refinement and substance reach perfection. Carving and polishing produce patterns, exhausting the resources of human skill; metal and jade provide the substance, whole and complete as though fashioned by Heaven. Here the principles embodied in things reach their utmost. How, then, could the purity of our King Wen’s virtue fail to sustain order throughout all under Heaven? The direction in which people’s hearts turn always depends on whether their ruler’s virtue is pure or divided. Our king of Zhou maintained a resolve to strengthen himself without ceasing, and was ever constant in one…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
德操憂勤惕若之念而健以體天是勉勉也者
所以運王道於無外者也是故在上者勵精明
作有以握其機於至一而在下者範圍曲成有
以萃其渙於大同綱則常張紀則常理而天下
一統之盛於是乎基之矣聖人之所以治人者
蓋有所本又如此矣是則舉天下而皆在於綱
紀敎化之中則髦士之趨六師之及其所得於
此者多矣文王之德之盛不亦徵諸是哉抑觀
周道之昌自文王要其成盛德大業後世無以
===
加矣而要其所以自得則自敬始故曰敬止曰
勉勉曰亹亹此純亦不已也惟不已故敎化之
所以成綱紀之所由布而周之興也勃焉自此
而執競之武王勉敬之成王因之以為祈天永
命之基皆此道也故古今致盛治而為天下後
世之所不可幾及者未嘗不自敬得之豈但文
王為然
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳莊公十有五年公
punctuated:
德，操憂勤惕若之念，而健以體天，是勉勉也者，所以運王道於無外者也。是故在上者勵精明作，有以握其機於至一；而在下者範圍曲成，有以萃其渙於大同。綱則常張，紀則常理，而天下一統之盛於是乎基之矣。聖人之所以治人者，蓋有所本，又如此矣。是則舉天下而皆在於綱紀敎化之中，則髦士之趨、六師之及，其所得於此者多矣。文王之德之盛，不亦徵諸是哉？抑觀周道之昌，自文王要其成，盛德大業，後世無以加矣。而要其所以自得，則自敬始。故曰「敬止」，曰「勉勉」，曰「亹亹」，此純亦不已也。惟不已，故敎化之所以成、綱紀之所由布，而周之興也勃焉。自此而執競之武王、勉敬之成王，因之以為祈天永命之基，皆此道也。故古今致盛治，而為天下後世之所不可幾及者，未嘗不自敬得之，豈但文王為然？

春秋

秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。莊公十有五年。公
translation_en:
…virtue, holding fast to thoughts of anxious diligence and vigilance, and embodying Heaven through vigorous action. Such unflagging effort is what extends the kingly Way everywhere, leaving nothing outside it. Thus those above apply themselves wholeheartedly and act with understanding, grasping the pivotal workings of government in perfect unity; those below order all things and bring each to fulfillment, gathering what is scattered into great concord. The guiding principles remain firmly established, and the ordering rules remain well regulated: here are laid the foundations for the flourishing unity of all under Heaven. Such, too, is the foundation upon which the sage governs people. When the whole world is thus encompassed within these principles, rules, and moral instruction, both the endeavors of outstanding scholars and the reach of the six armies owe much to them. Is not the greatness of King Wen’s virtue demonstrated by this? Moreover, consider the flourishing of the Way of Zhou, beginning with King Wen. Judged by its accomplishment, its abundant virtue and great achievements could not be surpassed by later generations. Yet if we examine how he himself attained it, it began with reverence. Hence the expressions “abiding in reverence,” “unflagging in effort,” and “untiring”: this purity, too, was unceasing. Precisely because it was unceasing, moral instruction was accomplished, principles and rules were propagated, and Zhou rose with vigor. Thereafter, King Wu, “steadfast and strong,” and King Cheng, “diligent in reverence,” followed this as the foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. All followed this same Way. Thus, throughout antiquity and later times, those who achieved flourishing government beyond the reach of anyone in the world or in subsequent generations invariably attained it through reverence. How could this have been true of King Wen alone?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Zhu attacked Ni.” The fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.

“The duke …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘僖公四年
林貞相
同考試官教諭羅批齊桓主盟而敢專征他尚
何責焉詞嚴義正無踰此作
考試官教諭黃批得正名本意
考試官教諭朱批簡嚴
春秋兩紀兵事有序外君主兵而見其罪有序
伯主專征而見其罪夫諸侯不得主兵伯主不
===
得專征皆分之所在也郕與楚之伐也而春秋
烏可逭其罪哉且嘗攷周官而知有周之所以
制兵矣天子以一人而莅萬邦故有用天下諸
侯以討不庭焉未聞諸侯而主諸侯之兵也方
伯以六服而承天子故有奉天子明命以討不
庭焉未聞方伯而專方伯之兵也春秋而降周
制不存列國用兵恒隨時之所變以為上下蓋
自霸圖之未成也而權無所統則以諸侯而自
用其兵有如宋桓之伐郕郕附庸之小邦伐之
punctuated:
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。僖公四年。
林貞相。
同考試官教諭羅批：齊桓主盟而敢專征，他尚何責焉？詞嚴義正，無踰此作。
考試官教諭黃批：得正名本意。
考試官教諭朱批：簡嚴。
春秋兩紀兵事，有序外君主兵而見其罪，有序伯主專征而見其罪。夫諸侯不得主兵，伯主不得專征，皆分之所在也。郕與楚之伐也，而春秋烏可逭其罪哉？且嘗攷周官，而知有周之所以制兵矣。天子以一人而莅萬邦，故有用天下諸侯以討不庭焉，未聞諸侯而主諸侯之兵也。方伯以六服而承天子，故有奉天子明命以討不庭焉，未聞方伯而專方伯之兵也。春秋而降，周制不存，列國用兵，恒隨時之所變以為上下。蓋自霸圖之未成也，而權無所統，則以諸侯而自用其兵。有如宋桓之伐郕，郕附庸之小邦，伐之
translation_en:
…met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to invade Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. Fourth year of Duke Xi.
Lin Zhenxiang.
Associate Examiner Luo, an Instructor, comments: “Duke Huan of Qi presided over the covenant yet dared to undertake punitive expeditions on his own authority. What further reproach need be made of others? Stern in language and correct in principle, no composition surpasses this one.”
Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: “Grasps the original intent of the rectification of names.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Concise and rigorous.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records two military operations: in one, it recounts how rulers of other states commanded troops and thereby reveals their guilt; in the other, it recounts how the hegemon undertook a punitive expedition on his own authority and thereby reveals his guilt. That the feudal lords may not command military operations, and that the hegemon may not undertake punitive expeditions on his own authority, are both matters of their allotted station. In the attacks upon Cheng [?] and Chu, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals let their guilt go unpunished?
I have examined the Offices of Zhou and thereby learned how the Zhou regulated military affairs. The Son of Heaven, as the sole sovereign, presided over the myriad states; thus he could employ the feudal lords of All-under-Heaven to chastise those who failed to render submission at court. Never have I heard that a feudal lord could command the troops of the other feudal lords. The regional chief served the Son of Heaven through the six zones of service; thus he could carry out the Son of Heaven’s explicit command to chastise those who failed to render submission at court. Never have I heard that a regional chief could exercise independent authority over the troops under his charge.
From the Spring and Autumn period onward, the Zhou institutions no longer endured. The various states deployed troops, continually expanding or restricting their actions as circumstances changed. Before hegemonic rule had been established, authority had no unifying center, and feudal lords consequently employed their troops on their own initiative. Such was Duke Huan of Song’s attack upon Cheng [?—the examination passage names Ni]. Cheng was a small dependent state; to attack it…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
非也然而宋人所以伐之者一出於已而未甞
有王朝司馬之與聞牙璋無起旅之文虎符無
興兵之制狥其所私而威福自便人臣懷靖共
之心者不為此矣不然則彝黼九章之器宋之
所以承先王也是皆所以尊王章勵臣節而桓
之專恣至此何有一念本原之思乎春秋於郕
之伐也而以宋為主兵主兵豈諸侯事哉而桓
之罪自明矣迨覇圖之巳就也而權有所歸則
以方伯而奔徴其兵有如齊桓之伐楚楚憑陵
===
之大邦伐之宜也然而齊桓所以伐之者一專
於已而未甞有王朝司馬之錫命在庭無弓矢
之賜在廟無鈇鉞之頒犯其所禁而匡合是圖
人臣懷畏抑之心者不為此矣不然則五侯九
伯之命齊之所以承先王也是正所以尊王靈
肅侯度而桓之專擅至此何甞一念冠履之思
乎春秋於楚之伐也而以齊為專征專征豈方
伯事哉而桓公之罪又明矣雖然宋之伐郕不
足論也齊之圖覇功也安中夏攘外夷無衆以
punctuated:
非也。然而宋人所以伐之者，一出於已，而未甞有王朝司馬之與聞。牙璋無起旅之文，虎符無興兵之制，狥其所私而威福自便，人臣懷靖共之心者不為此矣。不然，則彝黼九章之器，宋之所以承先王也，是皆所以尊王章、勵臣節，而桓之專恣至此，何有一念本原之思乎？《春秋》於郕之伐也，而以宋為主兵。主兵豈諸侯事哉？而桓之罪自明矣。
迨覇圖之巳就也，而權有所歸，則以方伯而奔徴其兵，有如齊桓之伐楚。楚憑陵之大邦，伐之宜也。然而齊桓所以伐之者，一專於已，而未甞有王朝司馬之錫命。在庭無弓矢之賜，在廟無鈇鉞之頒，犯其所禁而匡合是圖，人臣懷畏抑之心者不為此矣。不然，則五侯九伯之命，齊之所以承先王也，是正所以尊王靈、肅侯度，而桓之專擅至此，何甞一念冠履之思乎？《春秋》於楚之伐也，而以齊為專征。專征豈方伯事哉？而桓公之罪又明矣。
雖然，宋之伐郕不足論也，齊之圖覇，功也。安中夏，攘外夷，無衆以
translation_en:
…was wrong. Yet Song’s attack proceeded entirely on its own initiative, without the royal court’s Minister of War having any knowledge of it. There was no written authorization accompanying a toothed jade tablet to mobilize troops, nor any command conveyed by a tiger tally to raise an army. Pursuing private interests, Song exercised punishment and reward at its own discretion. A subject who cherished loyal and respectful service would not have acted thus. Otherwise, consider the ritual vessels and regalia with axe patterns and nine emblems through which Song inherited the legacy of the former kings: all served to honor royal institutions and strengthen a subject’s integrity. Yet Duke Huan’s arbitrary self-indulgence reached such a point! Did he give even a moment’s thought to their foundations? In its account of the attack on Cheng, the Spring and Autumn Annals treats Song as taking the initiative in warfare. Is initiating warfare the business of a regional lord? Duke Huan’s guilt is thus self-evident.
Once the project of hegemony had been accomplished and authority had a center, a regional overlord could urgently levy troops, as when Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu. Chu was a great state that bullied others, and attacking it was appropriate. Yet Duke Huan of Qi undertook the attack entirely on his own authority, without receiving a command from the royal court’s Minister of War. No bows and arrows were bestowed at court, nor were battle-axes conferred in the ancestral temple. He violated the prohibitions binding him while seeking to set the realm in order and unite its lords. A subject who cherished reverence and restraint would not have acted thus. Otherwise, consider the mandate over the five ranks of lords and the nine regional chiefs through which Qi inherited the legacy of the former kings: its very purpose was to honor royal majesty and uphold the rules governing regional lords. Yet Duke Huan’s usurpation of authority reached such a point! Did he ever give a moment’s thought to the proper ordering of cap and shoes—that is, superior and subordinate? In its account of the attack on Chu, the Spring and Autumn Annals treats Qi as undertaking a punitive expedition on its own authority. Is undertaking such an expedition the business of a regional overlord? Duke Huan’s guilt is again clear.
Nevertheless, Song’s attack on Cheng scarcely merits discussion; Qi’s pursuit of hegemony was an achievement. It brought peace to the central Chinese lands and repelled the outer barbarians, [the wording 無衆以 is unclear] [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
尊王爲名而陘亭之師徵王貢問王祭焉此尊
王至大也舉天下至大之名而不能仗天下之
大義以大分臨之宜楚之能爲辭也夫苟知春
秋之法諸侯無專兵方伯無專征舉天下之大
而唯一人之命是從天下可大定矣吁此春秋
所以爲經世也
吳子使札來聘〔襄公二十有九年〕夏曹公
孫會自鄫出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
陳奎
同考試官教諭羅批會傳成文長於褒貶者
考試官教諭黃批開闔有法
考試官教諭朱批莊重
===
春秋以過中貶辭國之賢以世類進去國之士
此見季札爲賢者之過故責之備公孫會爲賢
者之後故善之長也其春秋因事褒貶之教乎
且札吳之公子也聞樂知德吾嘗聞其賢矣賢
而特書春秋之法經於札之來聘獨以名紀者
何蓋君子遇變而能通故道行而無弊札之在
punctuated:
尊王爲名，而陘亭之師徵王貢、問王祭焉，此尊王至大也。舉天下至大之名，而不能仗天下之大義，以大分臨之，宜楚之能爲辭也。夫苟知春秋之法，諸侯無專兵，方伯無專征，舉天下之大而唯一人之命是從，天下可大定矣。吁！此春秋所以爲經世也。
「吳子使札來聘。」〔襄公二十有九年〕「夏，曹公孫會自鄫出奔宋。」〔昭公二十年〕
陳奎
同考試官教諭羅批：「會傳成文，長於褒貶者。」
考試官教諭黃批：「開闔有法。」
考試官教諭朱批：「莊重。」
春秋以過中貶辭國之賢，以世類進去國之士。此見季札爲賢者之過，故責之備；公孫會爲賢者之後，故善之長也。其春秋因事褒貶之教乎！且札，吳之公子也，聞樂知德，吾嘗聞其賢矣。賢而特書，春秋之法。經於札之來聘，獨以名紀者何？蓋君子遇變而能通，故道行而無弊。札之在
translation_en:
…taking “honoring the king” as their cause. Yet the army at Xingting demanded the tribute owed to the king and inquired about the royal sacrifices: these were matters of the utmost importance in honoring the king. To invoke the greatest cause under Heaven, yet fail to uphold the great righteousness of all under Heaven and confront Chu with the supreme distinction between ruler and subject—it is no wonder that Chu could offer a rebuttal. If only the rules of the Spring and Autumn Annals were understood—that regional lords may not mobilize troops on their own authority, and regional overlords may not undertake punitive campaigns on their own authority—then all the vast realm would obey the commands of the one sovereign alone, and all under Heaven could attain lasting order. Ah! This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals serves to order the world.
“The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit to our court.” 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang〕 “In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zeng to Song.” 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao〕
Chen Kui.
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “He brings the commentaries together into a coherent essay and excels at praise and censure.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The unfolding and drawing together of the argument are methodical.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Dignified and weighty.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals censures a worthy man who declined rulership for going beyond the mean, while commending a gentleman who left his state on account of his lineage. This shows that Ji Zha committed the error characteristic of a worthy man, and therefore the Annals held him to a standard of completeness; Gongsun Hui was descended from a worthy man, and therefore it commended his strengths. Is this not the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals, which assigns praise and censure according to the circumstances?
Now Zha was a prince of Wu. Hearing music, he could discern the virtue it expressed; I have heard of his worthiness. To single out worthy men for special mention is the rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, when recording Zha’s diplomatic visit, does the Classic record him simply by his personal name? A gentleman can adapt when he encounters changing circumstances; thus the Way is put into practice without harmful consequences. As for Zha’s position in…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
吳非猶泰伯之於周夷齊之於孤竹也札非壽
夢之所賢者乎使札也承父兄之志以慰其付
託之重則邦其永孚於休胡乃徇狷介之節而
昧大中之道效匹夫之爲而陷賢智之過則延
陵之逃不免爲於陵之操而專諸之禍兆矣噫
以札而非賢也則固無足責矣札而誠賢也其
可使之有過中之行也哉故因其來聘而特以
名稱所謂責賢之備者以此若會者曹之大夫
也待放而奔是亦人臣之常耳常事不書亦春
===
秋之法經於會之出奔賢以公孫者何蓋君子
節立而不毀故名遠而彌光曹之有子臧猶唐
之有巢許虞之有務光也會非子臧之後裔乎
使會也懷利祿之榮有忝於箕裘之紹則世德
弗能作求今也自鄭而待深得察罪之宜賜玦
而奔尤協去國之禮則守道不失適光於守節
無求而甘棠之愛永矣噫以會而匪臧也則亦
無足錄矣會而有臧也其可使之泯滅無聞也
哉故因其出奔而特稱公孫所謂善善之長者
punctuated: 吳，非猶泰伯之於周、夷齊之於孤竹也。札非壽夢之所賢者乎？使札也承父兄之志，以慰其付託之重，則邦其永孚於休。胡乃徇狷介之節，而昧大中之道，效匹夫之爲，而陷賢智之過？則延陵之逃，不免爲於陵之操，而專諸之禍兆矣。噫！以札而非賢也，則固無足責矣；札而誠賢也，其可使之有過中之行也哉？故因其來聘而特以名稱，所謂責賢之備者以此。若會者，曹之大夫也。待放而奔，是亦人臣之常耳。常事不書，亦春秋之法。經於會之出奔，賢以公孫者何？蓋君子節立而不毀，故名遠而彌光。曹之有子臧，猶唐之有巢許、虞之有務光也。會非子臧之後裔乎？使會也懷利祿之榮，有忝於箕裘之紹，則世德弗能作求。今也自鄭而待，深得察罪之宜；賜玦而奔，尤協去國之禮。則守道不失，適光於守節無求，而甘棠之愛永矣。噫！以會而匪臧也，則亦無足錄矣；會而有臧也，其可使之泯滅無聞也哉？故因其出奔而特稱公孫，所謂善善之長者
translation_en:
…in Wu was not like that of Taibo in Zhou, or of Boyi and Shuqi in Guzhu. Was not Ji Zha the one whom Shoumeng regarded as worthy? Had Zha fulfilled the intentions of his father and elder brothers, thereby honoring the weighty trust they had placed in him, the state would surely have enjoyed lasting well-being. Why, then, did he cling to a scrupulously aloof integrity while failing to understand the great Way of the mean, imitate the conduct of a private individual, and fall into the error of the worthy and wise who go too far? Thus the flight of the lord of Yanling inevitably became like the rigid scrupulousness of Chen Zhongzi of Yuling, and the seeds of the calamity wrought by Zhuan Zhu were sown. Alas! Had Zha not been worthy, there would certainly have been no reason to reproach him. But if Zha was truly worthy, could conduct that exceeded the mean be allowed in him? Thus, when recording his diplomatic visit, the Annals specifically calls him by his personal name. This is what is meant by demanding completeness of the worthy.

As for Hui, he was a grand master of Cao. To await dismissal and then flee was merely the ordinary conduct of a minister. Not to record ordinary events is also a rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, when the Classic records Hui’s flight, does it honor him with the designation “ducal grandson”? Once a gentleman’s integrity is established and remains unbroken, his reputation travels far and grows ever more illustrious. Cao’s possession of Zizang was like Tang’s possession of Chao Fu and Xu You, or Yu’s possession of Wu Guang. Was not Hui a descendant of Zizang? Had Hui cherished the glory of wealth and office, disgracing the inheritance of his forebears, he could not have carried forward their hereditary virtue. As it was, he waited from Zheng [?], fully observing what was proper in awaiting scrutiny of his offense; on being given a jade ring with a gap, he fled, conforming still more closely to the rites for leaving one’s state. By holding to the Way without deviation, he fittingly brought luster to the integrity of one who sought nothing for himself, perpetuating the affection commemorated by the sweet pear tree. Alas! Had Hui lacked goodness, there would likewise have been nothing worth recording. But since Hui possessed goodness, could he be allowed to disappear into oblivion, unheard of? Thus, when recording his flight, the Annals specifically calls him “ducal grandson.” This is what is meant by extending the honoring of goodness across generations…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
以此是則均一辭國也在季札則責諸其身在
子臧則錄諸其後聖人豈有厚薄於其間哉無
亦以中道防之耳雖然臧固無議矣札其可少
乎當勢利喧豗之時而能砥礪名節誠足以廉
頑立懦觀其掛劔示信退師全名其所見者甚
定也豈與利疚勢回盛衰改節者比哉使國人
能成其志則亦可以垂名於不替矣惜乎所值
之非不得以遂其附於子臧之志也然則君子
責人固所當備而取人尤可不恕也哉
===
禮記
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
楊棐
同考試官敎諭羅批聖人心通天地故禮序樂
和功用隆懋此作根極理要而辭復昌達錄之以式
考試官敎諭黃批精醇明鬯非苟作者
punctuated:
以此。是則均一辭國也，在季札則責諸其身，在子臧則錄諸其後，聖人豈有厚薄於其間哉？無亦以中道防之耳。雖然，臧固無議矣，札其可少乎？當勢利喧豗之時，而能砥礪名節，誠足以廉頑立懦。觀其掛劔示信，退師全名，其所見者甚定也，豈與利疚勢回、盛衰改節者比哉？使國人能成其志，則亦可以垂名於不替矣。惜乎所值之非，不得以遂其附於子臧之志也。然則君子責人固所當備，而取人尤可不恕也哉？

禮記
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。如此，則四海之內合敬同愛矣。
楊棐
同考試官敎諭羅批：「聖人心通天地，故禮序樂和，功用隆懋。此作根極理要，而辭復昌達，錄之以式。」
考試官敎諭黃批：「精醇明鬯，非苟作者。」
translation_en:
…for this reason. Thus, although both alike declined a state, in Ji Zha’s case the sage demanded accountability of the man himself, whereas in Zizang’s case he recorded merit in his descendant. Could the sage have favored one over the other? Surely he was merely using the mean to guard against excess. Nevertheless, although Zizang is beyond reproach, can Zha be belittled? Amid the clamor for power and profit, he tempered his reputation and integrity: this was indeed enough to make the avaricious incorruptible and give the timid resolve. Consider how he hung up his sword to demonstrate trustworthiness and withdrew his army to preserve his good name. His convictions were firmly settled. How could he be compared with those corrupted by profit and swayed by power, who change their principles as fortunes rise and fall? Had the people of his state enabled him to fulfill his purpose, he too could have left an enduring name. Regrettably, the adverse circumstances he encountered prevented him from fulfilling his ambition to emulate Zizang. Thus, although a gentleman should demand completeness of others, when recognizing their merits, can he above all fail to exercise sympathetic understanding?

Record of Rites
“Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares their ordered distinctions. Through harmony, the myriad things retain their proper place; through ordered distinctions, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the manifest realm there are ritual and music; in the hidden realm there are ghosts and spirits. In this way, all within the Four Seas unite in reverence and share in love.”

Yang Fei
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The sage’s mind communicates with Heaven and Earth; hence ritual establishes order and music brings harmony, and their efficacy is great and abundant. This composition probes to the root of essential principles, while its language is also flourishing and fluent. It is recorded here to serve as a model.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Refined and pure, lucid and fully expressive: this is no carelessly composed work.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭朱批整雅
論禮樂之成功合造化而感人心也蓋聖人之
禮樂與天地相為流通者也則其感人心也豈
容已哉且夫不觀禮樂之功用極其隆無以見
聖人之制作極其善何以言之樂一也謂之大
樂者和之至而非徒假於聲容之末者也欣喜
歡愛之情脗合乎絪縕化醇之妙即天地自然
之和焉禮一也謂之大禮者序之至而非徒事
乎器數之煩者也親疎貴賤之制默契乎高下
===
散殊之理即天地自然之節焉夫惟其和之同
也故能以和召和昭宣化育而百物為之咸若
無或失者矣夫惟其節之同也故能以序賛序
節事天地而百神為之受職無弗享者矣是則
禮樂鬼神其致一也自其明而在聖人之制作
言之則有禮樂禮樂者有迹之鬼神也自其幽
而在天地之功用言之則有鬼神鬼神者無形
之禮樂也其合造化如此是天地且弗違而況
於人乎吾見大禮之所感召興起其退讓之風
punctuated:
考試官教諭朱批：整雅。

論禮樂之成功，合造化而感人心也。蓋聖人之禮樂，與天地相為流通者也，則其感人心也，豈容已哉？且夫不觀禮樂之功用極其隆，無以見聖人之制作極其善。何以言之？樂一也，謂之大樂者，和之至，而非徒假於聲容之末者也。欣喜歡愛之情，脗合乎絪縕化醇之妙，即天地自然之和焉。禮一也，謂之大禮者，序之至，而非徒事乎器數之煩者也。親疎貴賤之制，默契乎高下散殊之理，即天地自然之節焉。夫惟其和之同也，故能以和召和，昭宣化育，而百物為之咸若，無或失者矣。夫惟其節之同也，故能以序賛序，節事天地，而百神為之受職，無弗享者矣。是則禮樂鬼神，其致一也。自其明而在聖人之制作言之，則有禮樂，禮樂者，有迹之鬼神也；自其幽而在天地之功用言之，則有鬼神，鬼神者，無形之禮樂也。其合造化如此，是天地且弗違，而況於人乎？吾見大禮之所感召，興起其退讓之風
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: Orderly and elegant.

In discussing the consummate achievement of rites and music, we find that they accord with the transformations of nature and move human hearts. The sage’s rites and music communicate freely with Heaven and Earth; how, then, could their influence on human hearts be restrained? Unless we behold the utmost grandeur of their efficacy, we cannot perceive the utmost excellence of the sage’s institutions. How can this be explained? Music is one, yet what is called great music is harmony brought to perfection, not merely something dependent on the superficial features of sound and outward display. The feelings of joy, delight, affection, and love accord perfectly with the wondrous intermingling of cosmic forces through which things are transformed and brought to fullness: this is the spontaneous harmony of Heaven and Earth. Rites are one, yet what are called great rites are order brought to perfection, not merely attention to the intricacies of ritual vessels and prescribed numbers. The regulations distinguishing close from distant kin and noble from humble accord tacitly with the principle by which things stand high or low and are distributed in their diversity: this is the spontaneous measure of Heaven and Earth. Precisely because their harmony is the same, they can summon harmony through harmony and manifest the work of transformation and nurture, so that all things conform and none falls out of place. Precisely because their measure is the same, they can assist order through order and regulate service to Heaven and Earth, so that the myriad spirits assume their offices and none fails to receive the offerings. Thus rites, music, and the spirits have a single ultimate purport. Viewed in their manifest aspect, embodied in the sage’s institutions, there are rites and music: rites and music are spirits with perceptible traces. Viewed in their hidden aspect, embodied in the workings of Heaven and Earth, there are spirits: spirits are rites and music without visible form. Such is their accord with the transformations of nature. Even Heaven and Earth do not run counter to them; how much less would human beings? I see how the influence of great rites calls forth a spirit of modest deference…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
四海雖大莫不有序有等而相接一於敬矣大
樂之所潛孚敦尚其仁厚之俗四海雖遠莫不
和親和順而相與一於愛矣由是言之禮樂成
功之大自有不可誣者謂非達天德之聖人其
孰能當之雖然要之皆出於吾心耳蓋聖人之
心與天地本同一理其始也法天地以為禮樂
終則以禮樂而賛天地至於天地官萬物育則
其功化之極固有不期然而然者故曰吾之心
正則天地之心亦正吾之氣順則天地之氣亦
===
順兩間之妙用莫有出於此心之外者此其所
以與天地叅也嗚呼先王之道禮樂可謂盛矣
君子力此二者以南面而立夫是以天下
太平也
李遇春
同考試官教諭羅批由身達治天人合一之學
正如此發明透徹無踰此作
考試官教諭黃批峻潔得體
考試官教諭朱批淵朗
punctuated:
四海雖大，莫不有序有等，而相接一於敬矣。大樂之所潛孚，敦尚其仁厚之俗，四海雖遠，莫不和親和順，而相與一於愛矣。由是言之，禮樂成功之大，自有不可誣者。謂非達天德之聖人，其孰能當之？雖然，要之皆出於吾心耳。蓋聖人之心與天地本同一理，其始也，法天地以為禮樂；終則以禮樂而賛天地。至於天地官、萬物育，則其功化之極，固有不期然而然者。故曰：「吾之心正，則天地之心亦正；吾之氣順，則天地之氣亦順。」兩間之妙用，莫有出於此心之外者，此其所以與天地叅也。嗚呼！先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣！君子力此二者，以南面而立，夫是以天下太平也。

李遇春

同考試官教諭羅批：由身達治，天人合一之學，正如此。發明透徹，無踰此作。

考試官教諭黃批：峻潔得體。

考試官教諭朱批：淵朗。
translation_en:
…Though the realm within the Four Seas is vast, all observe order and distinctions of rank, and their dealings with one another are united in reverence. Wherever great music silently wins people’s trust, it strengthens their esteem for humane and generous customs. Though the Four Seas extend far, all live in harmony, affection, and concord, and their relations with one another are united in love. Viewed in this light, the greatness of what rites and music accomplish is undeniable. Who but a sage who has attained Heaven’s virtue could be equal to this? Nevertheless, in the final reckoning, all of it issues from our own heart. For the sage’s heart and Heaven and Earth fundamentally share one principle. At first, he models rites and music on Heaven and Earth; ultimately, through rites and music, he assists Heaven and Earth. When Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices [?] and the myriad things are nurtured, the culmination of his transformative achievement comes about naturally, without being deliberately sought. Thus it is said: “When my heart is rectified, the heart of Heaven and Earth is likewise rectified; when my vital force flows harmoniously, the vital force of Heaven and Earth likewise flows harmoniously.” None of the wondrous operations between Heaven and Earth lies outside this heart. This is how the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Ah! In the Way of the former kings, rites and music may indeed be called magnificent! The gentleman exerts himself in these two things and takes his place facing south as ruler; thereby all under Heaven enjoys great peace.

Li Yuchun

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “Proceeding from the cultivation of oneself to government: this is precisely the learning that unites Heaven and humanity. Its exposition is penetrating and thorough; no essay surpasses this one.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Lofty and lucid, and appropriate in form.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Profound and clear.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
君子以禮樂而爲治則天下化成矣夫禮樂出
於吾身致治之本也君子舉而措諸天下而有
不化成者哉夫子告子張問政至此謂夫禮樂
之道其用雖達諸天下而其本不外於吾身是
故君子蓋甞言而履之矣匪以自淑也舉而施
之於有政吾身之序達之爲天下之序蓋甞行
而樂之矣匪以自豫也推而見之於臨民吾身
之和達之爲天下之和向明蒞治之餘有以立
大中至正之矩出乎身者加乎民者也正位凝
===
命之際有以妙體信達順之機發乎邇者見乎
遠者也是雖無心於天下之化也然禮達而分
自定作則自我也人莫不順其則聲敎所及自
四達而不悖樂行而民鄕方建極於上也下莫
不歸其極德化所被殆充周而不窮篤恭之妙
徵至治於有象内外寧謐之休可坐而致矣而
天下之人有不得其所者乎平中之盛昭大化
於無爲遠近乂安之治不勞而定矣而天下之
事有不得其理者乎此天下之治必以有本而
punctuated: 君子以禮樂而爲治，則天下化成矣。夫禮樂出於吾身，致治之本也。君子舉而措諸天下，而有不化成者哉？夫子告子張問政，至此謂夫禮樂之道，其用雖達諸天下，而其本不外於吾身。是故君子蓋甞言而履之矣，匪以自淑也，舉而施之於有政；吾身之序，達之爲天下之序。蓋甞行而樂之矣，匪以自豫也，推而見之於臨民；吾身之和，達之爲天下之和。向明蒞治之餘，有以立大中至正之矩，出乎身者，加乎民者也；正位凝命之際，有以妙體信達順之機，發乎邇者，見乎遠者也。是雖無心於天下之化也，然禮達而分自定，作則自我也，人莫不順其則，聲敎所及，自四達而不悖；樂行而民鄕方，建極於上也，下莫不歸其極，德化所被，殆充周而不窮。篤恭之妙，徵至治於有象，内外寧謐之休，可坐而致矣，而天下之人有不得其所者乎？平中之盛，昭大化於無爲，遠近乂安之治，不勞而定矣，而天下之事有不得其理者乎？此天下之治必以有本而
translation_en:
When the gentleman governs through ritual and music, all under Heaven are transformed and brought to fulfillment. Ritual and music issue from one’s own person and are the foundation of good government. When the gentleman puts them into practice throughout all under Heaven, how could transformation fail to be accomplished? At this point in his reply to Zizhang’s question about government, the Master means that, although the operation of the Way of ritual and music extends throughout all under Heaven, its foundation lies nowhere beyond one’s own person.

Thus the gentleman has spoken of it and put it into practice, not merely to improve himself, but to apply it in government: the order within his own person is extended to become order throughout all under Heaven. He has practiced it and found joy in it, not merely for his own delight, but to make it manifest in governing the people: the harmony within his own person is extended to become harmony throughout all under Heaven. As he faces the light and attends to government, he establishes the standard of supreme centrality and utmost correctness. What issues from his person is brought to bear upon the people. As he takes his proper position and secures Heaven’s mandate, he gives subtle effect to the workings of embodying trustworthiness and extending harmony. What originates close at hand becomes manifest far away.

Although he has no deliberate intention of transforming all under Heaven, when ritual extends its reach, distinctions settle into place of themselves. The standard originates with him, and everyone follows it; wherever his moral instruction reaches, it naturally spreads in all directions without encountering resistance. When music is practiced, the people turn toward the proper course. He establishes the supreme standard above, and everyone below turns to it; wherever his transforming virtue reaches, it spreads fully and without limit.

The subtle efficacy of earnest reverence manifests perfect government in visible forms. The blessings of peace and tranquility within and without can be attained while he remains seated: could anyone under Heaven then fail to find a proper place? The fullness of balanced centrality reveals great transformation through nonaction. Order and peace, far and near, are secured without toil: could any affair under Heaven then fail to accord with its proper principle? Thus, government throughout all under Heaven must have a foundation upon which …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
立也爲政者烏可不知所從事哉抑此卽王天
下之道力此者德也南面者位也有其德有其
位而致天下之治無難矣是之謂天德王道聖
人履中正而樂和平之明驗也匪獨告子張爲
然他日語爲邦之問斟酌四代禮樂則夫子之
爲政可槩見者如此苟得邦家綏來動和之化
固其所必致也哉故曰作禮樂者必聖人在天
子之位
第貳場
===
論
君子動而世爲天下道
林茂勛
同考試官學正彭批士人輒事套括以炫藝能
要於理道無當此作根究本始開闔無端如入武庫而
百物森具閱良驥而牝牡北羣空雄偉奇雋於是徵矣
同考試官教授莫批文章多技惟在主理而澤
氣思致淵深詞華鬯茂者僅見此篇人共退避三舍乎
考試官教諭黃批格高詞古學博氣昌讀之
punctuated:
立也。爲政者烏可不知所從事哉？抑此卽王天下之道，力此者德也，南面者位也。有其德，有其位，而致天下之治無難矣。是之謂天德王道，聖人履中正而樂和平之明驗也。匪獨告子張爲然，他日語爲邦之問，斟酌四代禮樂，則夫子之爲政可槩見者如此。苟得邦家，綏來動和之化，固其所必致也哉！故曰：「作禮樂者，必聖人在天子之位。」

第貳場

論

君子動而世爲天下道

林茂勛

同考試官學正彭批：士人輒事套括，以炫藝能，要於理道無當。此作根究本始，開闔無端，如入武庫而百物森具，閱良驥而牝牡北羣空，雄偉奇雋於是徵矣。

同考試官教授莫批：文章多技，惟在主理而澤。氣思致淵深，詞華鬯茂者，僅見此篇。人共退避三舍乎？

考試官教諭黃批：格高詞古，學博氣昌，讀之
translation_en:
…is established. How could those who govern fail to know where to direct their efforts? This, moreover, is precisely the way to rule all under Heaven as king. Virtue supplies the strength for this; facing south signifies the sovereign’s position. Possessing both that virtue and that position, one can bring order to all under Heaven without difficulty. This is what is called heavenly virtue and the kingly Way: clear evidence that the sage treads the path of centrality and correctness and delights in harmony and peace. Nor was this true only of what he told Zizhang. On another occasion, answering a question about governing a state, he weighed the rites and music of the four dynasties. From this one can broadly discern how the Master would govern. Were he to obtain a state or domain, he would surely bring about a transforming influence that comforts the people, draws them to him, inspires them, and brings them into harmony. Thus it is said: “The maker of rites and music must be a sage occupying the position of the Son of Heaven.”

Second Session

Discourse

“When the gentleman acts, he becomes the Way for all under Heaven for generations.”

Lin Maoxun

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor: Scholars habitually employ stock formulas to show off their literary abilities, yet these ultimately have no bearing on principle and the Way. This composition investigates the very roots and beginnings; its unfolding and gathering are inexhaustibly varied. It is like entering an arsenal and finding every kind of weapon arrayed in profusion, or inspecting a fine steed and finding the northern herds emptied of mares and stallions [?]. Here its grandeur, power, originality, and distinction are demonstrated.

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Professor: Literary composition involves many skills, but the essential thing is to take principle as its governing concern and give it richness. For profound vitality, thought, and conception, and luxuriant, freely flowing diction, I have scarcely seen anything to match this piece. Must not everyone else retreat three marches before it?

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Its style is lofty, its diction antique, its learning broad, and its vitality abundant. Reading it…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
令人灑然佳士佳士
考試官敎諭朱批充迖瑩徹而操縱有法將
不足傳邪
君子會道於身而天下不能外之以為道是故
操之至約而施之則至廣取之至近而推之則
至遠君子豈甞以吾之動於此而持以待天下
後世之人使其必吾信且從也而天下後世之
人亦豈以其道之出於君子有所企焉而求以
不外於其道耶吾知其動之也自其身焉而與
===
斯民共由之而已而人之囿其化守其法者相
率焉以為日用之常而卒不能外乎其道而亦
不知道之出於君子也何也天下之人不同而
其心則君子之心也後世之天下不同而其民
則當時之民也君子以吾心之同而觸其本然
之理備制作之善而盡鼓舞之神則道之行也
固天下後世之所固有者矣民方安於其心之
固有而相忘相比於治化之中雖欲外之以為
道其可得哉甞讀書曰亶聰明作元后元后作
punctuated:
令人灑然，佳士！佳士！

考試官敎諭朱批：充迖瑩徹，而操縱有法，將不足傳邪？

君子會道於身，而天下不能外之以為道。是故操之至約，而施之則至廣；取之至近，而推之則至遠。君子豈甞以吾之動於此，而持以待天下後世之人，使其必吾信且從也？而天下後世之人，亦豈以其道之出於君子，有所企焉，而求以不外於其道耶？吾知其動之也，自其身焉，而與斯民共由之而已。而人之囿其化、守其法者，相率焉以為日用之常，而卒不能外乎其道，而亦不知道之出於君子也。何也？天下之人不同，而其心則君子之心也；後世之天下不同，而其民則當時之民也。君子以吾心之同，而觸其本然之理，備制作之善，而盡鼓舞之神，則道之行也，固天下後世之所固有者矣。民方安於其心之固有，而相忘相比於治化之中，雖欲外之以為道，其可得哉？甞讀《書》曰：「亶聰明作元后，元后作
translation_en:
…leaves the reader refreshed. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Full and expansive, lucid and clear, yet controlled and developed with method: could this fail to deserve transmission?

The gentleman brings the Way together in his own person, and all under Heaven cannot establish a Way outside it. Thus, what he holds to is most concise, yet its application is most extensive; what he draws upon is nearest at hand, yet its extension reaches farthest. Has the gentleman ever taken his actions here as a standard to impose upon people throughout the world and in later generations, requiring them invariably to trust and follow him? And do people throughout the world and in later generations aspire to his Way and seek to remain within it simply because it issues from the gentleman? I know only that his action begins with his own person, and that he follows this Way together with the people. Those who live within his transforming influence and observe his standards lead one another in treating these as the ordinary practices of daily life. In the end they cannot depart from his Way, yet they do not even know that it issues from the gentleman. Why is this? People throughout the world differ, but their hearts are the same as the gentleman’s heart. The world of later generations differs, but its people are like the people of his own time. Drawing upon what his own heart shares with others, the gentleman engages their inherent principles, perfects the excellence of institutions and regulations, and fully exercises the wondrous power of inspiring the people. Thus, the Way put into practice is precisely what people throughout the world and in later generations inherently possess. The people rest content in what is inherent in their hearts and live together in unselfconscious harmony amid good government and moral transformation. Even if they wished to establish a Way outside this, could they do so? I once read in the Book of Documents: “One truly discerning and intelligent becomes the sovereign; the sovereign becomes…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
民父母天命賦予曷甞有所豐嗇哉君子得其
清且厚者天民之先覺也天之所縱者也而覺
民之責不得不任焉天生斯民使之司牧而理
人之責不得不任焉君子當君師之責而勢之
所必趨者天也君子奉天時者也時乘之責不
得不任焉夫君子兼此三者於天下而天下之
生也不能無父子君臣兄弟夫婦朋友之倫焉
斁其倫則相夷不能無飲食衣服器皿貨財之
欲焉從其欲則相逐不能無宫府質劑簿書會
===
期之煩焉任其煩則相爭君子懼民之必底於
過也而思所以一之於是乎議之禮焉制之度
焉考之文焉爲之冠婚喪祭之典郊社朝聘之
儀燕饗射御鄉相見之節升降上下周旋裼襲
之序類不可勝紀而其爲禮則一也所以敦民
行也爲之冓收弁冦之象韠帶佩笏之章輅弧
旂旐之等豆登几筵之則斗斛權衡之信宫室
舟車陶冶之具類不可勝紀而其爲度則一也
所以防民慾也爲之龍文穗書龜字鍾鼎倒薤
punctuated: 民父母。」天命賦予，曷甞有所豐嗇哉？君子得其清且厚者，天民之先覺也，天之所縱者也，而覺民之責不得不任焉。天生斯民，使之司牧，而理人之責不得不任焉。君子當君師之責，而勢之所必趨者，天也。君子奉天時者也，時乘之責不得不任焉。夫君子兼此三者於天下，而天下之生也，不能無父子、君臣、兄弟、夫婦、朋友之倫焉，斁其倫則相夷；不能無飲食、衣服、器皿、貨財之欲焉，從其欲則相逐；不能無宫府、質劑、簿書、會期之煩焉，任其煩則相爭。君子懼民之必底於過也，而思所以一之。於是乎議之禮焉，制之度焉，考之文焉。爲之冠婚喪祭之典，郊社朝聘之儀，燕饗射御鄉相見之節，升降上下、周旋裼襲之序，類不可勝紀，而其爲禮則一也，所以敦民行也。爲之冓收弁冦之象，韠帶佩笏之章，輅弧旂旐之等，豆登几筵之則，斗斛權衡之信，宫室舟車陶冶之具，類不可勝紀，而其爲度則一也，所以防民慾也。爲之龍文穗書龜字鍾鼎倒薤
translation_en:
…the people's father and mother.” In what Heaven ordains and bestows, has there ever been generosity toward some and parsimony toward others? The gentleman receives what is pure and abundant: he is among Heaven's people the first to awaken to understanding, one whom Heaven has endowed generously. Thus he cannot decline the responsibility of awakening the people. Heaven brings forth these people and appoints him to shepherd them; thus he cannot decline the responsibility of governing them. The gentleman bears the responsibilities of ruler and teacher; that toward which circumstances necessarily tend is Heaven's doing. The gentleman follows Heaven's timing; thus he cannot decline the responsibility of acting as the time requires.

The gentleman combines these three responsibilities toward all under Heaven. In their lives, the people cannot be without the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friend and friend. If they corrupt these relationships, they injure one another. They cannot be without desires for food and drink, clothing, utensils, goods, and wealth. If they indulge these desires, they contend with one another. They cannot be without the complications of palaces and government offices, contracts, registers and documents, and appointed meetings. If these complications are left unchecked, they dispute with one another. The gentleman fears that the people will inevitably fall into error and considers how to bring them into unity. Accordingly, he deliberates upon their rites, establishes their standards, and examines their written forms.

He establishes for them the observances of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice; the ceremonies of sacrifices to Heaven and the soil, court audiences, and diplomatic visits; the protocols of banquets, archery, charioteering, and meetings among local people; and the sequences of ascending and descending, taking higher and lower positions, turning and moving about, and baring or covering the outer garment. Their kinds are too numerous to record exhaustively, yet they are one in constituting ritual: their purpose is to strengthen the people's conduct.

He establishes for them the forms of ceremonial headgear [?]; the distinctive adornments of knee coverings, belts, pendants, and audience tablets; the gradations of ceremonial chariots, bows, and banners; the specifications of sacrificial vessels, stands, and mats; reliable measures of capacity and standards of weight; and the equipment for palaces and dwellings, boats and carriages, pottery and metalworking. Their kinds are too numerous to record exhaustively, yet they are one in constituting standards: their purpose is to restrain the people's desires.

He establishes for them dragon-pattern writing, grain-ear script [?], tortoise writing, bell-and-cauldron inscriptions, and hanging-scallion-leaf script…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之文四聲五音六書之義類不可勝紀而其爲
書則一也所以同民心也夫天下之人犁然不
可齊也其事至賾而不可禦而其變至雜而不
可理也持多術以臨馭之猶懼其不可爲也而
謂此足以一之乎吾知斯人之在天下其性之
不可解與分之不可逃者非强焉而致之也有
能外斯五者以自立乎故禮議而天下之人可
盡也相生相養之道缺一不可而患不防則傷
欲不節則流故度制而事可盡也僞之滋繼之
===
不可已也書契作則亂止矣故文立而變可盡
也夫是三者誠足爲一天下之道矣而亦豈君
子任意創制爲之者哉君子膺天命居天位以
治天之民夫亦曰以天之道治之爾天地有卑
高之位在人則爲禮有方員之體在人則爲度
有陰陽之文在人則爲文是禮也度也文也天
之所授也君子與夫人一也其初本一而人自
異之爾是故本其所固有者推而使天下後世
共由之而已也故其議之制之而考之也非曰
punctuated:
之文，四聲五音六書之義，類不可勝紀，而其爲書則一也，所以同民心也。夫天下之人，犁然不可齊也；其事至賾而不可禦，而其變至雜而不可理也。持多術以臨馭之，猶懼其不可爲也，而謂此足以一之乎？吾知斯人之在天下，其性之不可解與分之不可逃者，非强焉而致之也。有能外斯五者以自立乎？故禮議而天下之人可盡也。相生相養之道，缺一不可，而患不防則傷，欲不節則流。故度制而事可盡也。僞之滋，繼之不可已也；書契作則亂止矣。故文立而變可盡也。

夫是三者，誠足爲一天下之道矣，而亦豈君子任意創制爲之者哉？君子膺天命，居天位，以治天之民，夫亦曰以天之道治之爾。天地有卑高之位，在人則爲禮；有方員之體，在人則爲度；有陰陽之文，在人則爲文。是禮也、度也、文也，天之所授也。君子與夫人一也，其初本一，而人自異之爾。是故本其所固有者，推而使天下後世共由之而已也。故其議之、制之而考之也，非曰
translation_en:
…forms of writing, and the principles of the four tones, five sounds, and six categories of written characters: their kinds are too numerous to record, yet as writing they are one. This is how the people's minds are brought into accord. Now, the people of the world differ so greatly that they cannot be made uniform; their affairs are so intricate that they cannot be managed, and their changing circumstances so diverse that they cannot be ordered. Even when employing many methods to govern them, one still fears that the task cannot be accomplished. Can one then say that these suffice to unite them? I know that, for people living in the world, the bonds of their nature that cannot be dissolved and the duties of their station that cannot be escaped are not imposed by force. Can anyone establish himself outside these five relationships? Thus, when ritual is deliberated upon, all the people of the world can be comprehensively provided for. In the ways by which people sustain and nurture one another, not a single element can be omitted. Yet harm results if dangers are not guarded against, and desires run unchecked if they are not restrained. Thus, when standards are established, affairs can be comprehensively provided for. As deceit proliferates, its continuation cannot be stopped [?]; when written records and contracts are created, disorder ceases. Thus, when written forms are established, changing circumstances can be comprehensively provided for.

These three truly suffice as the way to unite the world. But could they be institutions that the gentleman invents at his own pleasure? The gentleman receives Heaven's mandate and occupies Heaven's position in order to govern Heaven's people. This means only that he governs them through Heaven's Way. Heaven and earth have positions of low and high; among human beings, these become ritual. They have square and round forms; among human beings, these become standards. They have the patterns of yin and yang; among human beings, these become written forms. These rituals, standards, and written forms are bestowed by Heaven. The gentleman and other people are alike in this respect. At the beginning they were fundamentally one; people merely made themselves different. Thus, he takes what they inherently possess as his basis and extends it, so that all the world and later generations may follow it together—that is all. Hence, in deliberating upon ritual, establishing standards, and examining written forms, he does not mean to say…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
爲天下作則也自其身之履者而議之則禮矣
自其身之用者而制之則度矣自其身之著者
而考之則文矣人見其倫理中乎節文動容合
乎規矩經緯通乎天地曰道之在於君子之身
者然也而不知其卽天下之道也何也微斯人
則三者曷從生哉人見其司徒之所授冬官之
所裁内史之所掌而行人之所頒曰道之在於
天下者然也而不知其卽君子之身也何也匪
君子則烏與議而制而考之哉故典章文物之
===
著皆精神心思之微綱紀法度之具悉性命天
人之蘊四海千禩之遠卽几席戸庭之近合人
物貫古今而通極於造化者也是故徴之庶民
考之三王質之鬼神而俟之後聖無有乎或間
者至矣哉君子制作之善乎蓋至是而會道之
全矣由是達之朝廷百官則而象之推之邦國
庶人悅而安之垂之後代百王率而由之以之
而顯神謨申話言渙大號則罔不欽焉天下之
不佩服而諷誦之者未之有也以之而陳藝極
punctuated:
爲天下作則也。自其身之履者而議之，則禮矣；自其身之用者而制之，則度矣；自其身之著者而考之，則文矣。人見其倫理中乎節文，動容合乎規矩，經緯通乎天地，曰：「道之在於君子之身者然也。」而不知其卽天下之道也。何也？微斯人，則三者曷從生哉？人見其司徒之所授、冬官之所裁、内史之所掌，而行人之所頒，曰：「道之在於天下者然也。」而不知其卽君子之身也。何也？匪君子，則烏與議而制而考之哉？故典章文物之著，皆精神心思之微；綱紀法度之具，悉性命天人之蘊；四海千禩之遠，卽几席戸庭之近，合人物、貫古今而通極於造化者也。
是故徴之庶民，考之三王，質之鬼神，而俟之後聖，無有乎或間者。至矣哉，君子制作之善乎！蓋至是而會道之全矣。由是達之朝廷，百官則而象之；推之邦國，庶人悅而安之；垂之後代，百王率而由之。以之而顯神謨、申話言、渙大號，則罔不欽焉，天下之不佩服而諷誦之者，未之有也。以之而陳藝極
translation_en:
…establishing standards for all under Heaven. What the gentleman deliberates upon arises from his own conduct: this is ritual. What he institutes arises from his own practice: these are standards. What he examines arises from what he himself manifests: this is cultural form. People see that his ordering of human relationships accords with ritual distinctions, that his movements and bearing conform to the compass and square, and that the organizing principles of his conduct accord with Heaven and Earth. They say, “Such is the Way embodied in the gentleman,” without realizing that it is precisely the Way of all under Heaven. Why? Without such a person, whence could these three arise? People see what the Minister of Education teaches, what the Winter Offices devise, what the Court Scribe administers, and what the Court Usher promulgates. They say, “Such is the Way present throughout all under Heaven,” without realizing that it is precisely the gentleman’s own person. Why? Without the gentleman, who could deliberate upon, institute, and examine these things? Thus, the manifest forms of statutes, institutions, and ceremonial objects are all expressions of the subtleties of his spirit and thought. The full apparatus of governing principles, laws, and standards embodies all the profound meanings of human nature and destiny, Heaven and humanity. The remoteness of the Four Seas and a thousand years is identical with the proximity of his desk and mat, doorway and courtyard. These things unite human beings and all other beings, link antiquity and the present, and penetrate to the utmost workings of creation.
Thus, they are verified among the common people, examined against the Three Kings, tested before ghosts and spirits, and await the sages of later ages: nowhere is there any discrepancy. How consummate is the excellence of the gentleman’s institutions! At this point, indeed, the Way is brought together in its entirety. From here they reach the court, where the hundred officials take them as their standard and model; they extend to the states, where the common people delight in them and find repose; they are handed down to later ages, where the hundred kings follow and observe them. Through them, sagely plans are made manifest, instructive words reiterated, and great proclamations broadcast: none fail to regard them reverently. Never has there been anyone under Heaven who did not embrace and uphold them, reciting them aloud. Through them, the highest standards of accomplishment are set forth…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
樹表儀程大猷則罔不臧焉天下之不駿惠而
承式之者未之有也世不同而禮同貴賤以章
隆殺以辨卑高以陳安於倫矣而孰知其議之
自君子乎世不同而度同小大定其儀方員成
其象長短協其則便於軌矣而孰知其制之自
君子乎世不同而書同結繩以代百官以治萬
民以察習於文矣而孰知其考之自君子乎所
謂不降皇序下堂陛而天下後世之人各得其
願安於其分鼓舞於道化之中而不知誰之所
===
爲嗚呼至矣信乎操之約而施之則博取之近
而及之則遠也巳稽之古昔禮帝嚳祖爲市畫
卦皇之道也親睦徽典輯瑞同律帝之道也敷
土濬川綏猷肇脩列爵分土王之道也維時於
變從欲風動咸和永清之化流被四訖迨今誦
之不衰也抑記有之五帝不襲禮三王不沿樂
禮樂道之大者而曰不相沿襲何也蓋甞聞之
孔子矣曰殷因於夏禮周因於殷禮所損益可
知也夫殷周之君其人則聖神其時則變革而
punctuated: 樹表儀，程大猷，則罔不臧焉，天下之不駿惠而承式之者，未之有也。世不同而禮同，貴賤以章，隆殺以辨，卑高以陳，安於倫矣，而孰知其議之自君子乎？世不同而度同，小大定其儀，方員成其象，長短協其則，便於軌矣，而孰知其制之自君子乎？世不同而書同，結繩以代，百官以治，萬民以察，習於文矣，而孰知其考之自君子乎？所謂不降皇序、下堂陛，而天下後世之人各得其願，安於其分，鼓舞於道化之中，而不知誰之所爲。嗚呼，至矣！信乎操之約而施之則博，取之近而及之則遠也巳！稽之古昔，禮帝嚳祖、爲市畫卦，皇之道也；親睦徽典、輯瑞同律，帝之道也；敷土濬川、綏猷肇脩、列爵分土，王之道也。維時於變從欲，風動咸和，永清之化流被四訖，迨今誦之不衰也。抑《記》有之：「五帝不襲禮，三王不沿樂。」禮樂，道之大者，而曰不相沿襲，何也？蓋甞聞之孔子矣，曰：「殷因於夏禮，周因於殷禮，所損益可知也。」夫殷周之君，其人則聖神，其時則變革，而
translation_en:
…establish exemplary standards and set forth the great Way: then none fails to become good, and there is no one under Heaven who does not wholeheartedly comply and follow their pattern. Though the ages differ, the rites are the same: distinctions between noble and humble are made clear, degrees of elaboration and reduction are distinguished, and positions low and high are set out. People rest content within their proper relationships; yet who knows that the deliberation behind these rites originated with the gentleman? Though the ages differ, the measures are the same: things large and small have their prescribed forms, square and round their shapes, and long and short their corresponding standards. People readily follow these rules; yet who knows that their establishment originated with the gentleman? Though the ages differ, the writing is the same: knotted cords are replaced, the hundred officials conduct their administration, and the myriad people attain understanding. People become accustomed to written forms; yet who knows that their examination and determination originated with the gentleman? This is what is meant by bringing people throughout the world and in later ages to attain their wishes and rest content in their allotted stations, without descending the august stairway or the steps of the hall [?]. They rejoice amid the transforming influence of the Way, unaware of whose work it is. Ah, how consummate! Truly, what he holds to is concise, but its application is broad; what he draws upon is near, but its reach is far!

Examining antiquity, we find the rites of Di Ku and the ancestors [?], the establishment of markets, and the drawing of the trigrams: these were the Way of the August Sovereigns. Bringing kin into harmony, making the canons illustrious, collecting the jade tokens of authority, and unifying the pitch standards: these were the Way of the Emperors. Ordering the land and dredging the rivers, establishing the great plan and beginning its cultivation, and arranging ranks and apportioning territories: these were the Way of the Kings. In those times, the people were transformed and followed the rulers’ wishes; moved as by the wind, all were harmonious. The transforming influence that brought lasting peace spread to the four extremities, and to this day praise of it has not diminished.

Yet the Record of Rites says: “The Five Emperors did not inherit one another’s rites; the Three Kings did not perpetuate one another’s music.” Rites and music are major elements of the Way. Why, then, does it say that they did not inherit and perpetuate them? We have heard Confucius say: “Yin followed the rites of Xia, and Zhou followed the rites of Yin; what they subtracted and added can be known.” Now, the rulers of Yin and Zhou were sagely and divinely discerning, and their times were times of change, while …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其世則千有餘歲矣文質三統不必於同而三
綱五常之大者則未之有改焉記者所稱特禮
樂之具云爾古今之變不同而俗之便習亦異
久之不能無弊者勢則然也變通宜民之道在
堯舜已然而况於三王乎是故值其常也則不
愆不忘君子之所以動於天下者為未弊值其
變也則損益宜時以足君子未盡之意者固不
害其為道也不然田井矣官周矣以秦新行之
而曰道先王之動可乎雖然子思斯言蓋為周
===
之意也自皇王立極三重之道至周而大備宗
廟朝廷之儀方位國野之規九歲頒諭之制詳
在周書綿延至於後世天下之勢久矣而同軌
同倫同文之治猶相與守之無有自用自專以
干先王之典者弁髦之國大不能邾莒尚足以
奔走天下之諸侯陳檜之詩猶或有西方美人
之思原其所自則文武周公之所以動天下後
世者深且遠也然則君子會道於身而天下後
世不能外之以為道不益信也哉
punctuated:
其世則千有餘歲矣。文質三統，不必於同，而三綱五常之大者，則未之有改焉。記者所稱，特禮樂之具云爾。古今之變不同，而俗之便習亦異，久之不能無弊者，勢則然也。變通宜民之道，在堯舜已然，而况於三王乎？是故值其常也，則不愆不忘，君子之所以動於天下者為未弊；值其變也，則損益宜時，以足君子未盡之意者，固不害其為道也。不然，田井矣，官周矣，以秦新行之，而曰道先王之動，可乎？雖然，子思斯言，蓋為周之意也。
自皇王立極，三重之道至周而大備。宗廟朝廷之儀，方位國野之規，九歲頒諭之制，詳在周書。綿延至於後世，天下之勢久矣，而同軌、同倫、同文之治，猶相與守之，無有自用自專以干先王之典者。弁髦之國，大不能邾莒，尚足以奔走天下之諸侯；陳檜之詩，猶或有西方美人之思。原其所自，則文武周公之所以動天下後世者，深且遠也。然則君子會道於身，而天下後世不能外之以為道，不益信也哉？
translation_en:
…and their eras extended over more than a thousand years. Refinement and simplicity, and the three dynastic systems, need not have been identical; yet the great principles of the Three Bonds and Five Constants were never altered. What the author of the Record of Rites describes concerns only the forms of ritual and music. Circumstances differ between ancient and modern times, as do the practices people find convenient and familiar. That abuses inevitably arise over time follows from the course of events. The Way of adapting institutions to benefit the people was already practiced under Yao and Shun; how much more so under the Three Kings! Thus, in ordinary circumstances, one neither errs nor forgets: the means by which the noble man moves the world have not yet become defective. When circumstances change, reductions and additions appropriate to the times fulfill intentions that the noble man had not fully realized; these certainly do not prevent his practice from remaining the Way. Otherwise, merely arranging fields in the well-field system and organizing offices on the Zhou model, while implementing them as did Qin and Xin, could one claim to follow the actions of the former kings? Nevertheless, these words of Zisi were surely spoken with Zhou in mind.
From the time when the august sovereigns and kings established the supreme standard, the Way of the three weighty matters—ritual, institutions, and writing—reached its full development under Zhou. The ceremonies of ancestral temples and the royal court, the rules governing spatial arrangements in the capital and countryside, and the system of promulgating instructions every nine years are set out in detail in the Documents of Zhou. These endured into later ages. Though the configuration of the realm had long persisted, people still jointly upheld the order of uniform carriage tracks, common ethical relationships, and a shared script. None presumed to act on their own judgment or authority in violation of the statutes of the former kings. A state treated like a discarded ceremonial cap and hairpiece, no greater than Zhu or Ju [?], could still make the feudal lords of the realm hasten to its service. Even among the poems of Chen and Kuai, some still express longing for the beautiful person in the west. Tracing these things to their source, we see how profoundly and enduringly Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou moved the world and later generations. Does this not make it all the more credible that the noble man embodies the Way, and that neither the world nor later generations can find a Way outside it?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
表
擬
賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣
謝表永樂十四年
黃星耀
同考試官教諭羅批語意渾成援引精切咀嚼
覺有餘味可以式矣
同考試官教授簡批體裁莊整不徒駢儷而已
是用錄之
===
考試官教諭黃批麗而則廉而不劌且長於
四六者
考試官教諭朱批措詞舂容忠愛藹然得稱
謝體
永樂十四年某月某日臣等伏蒙
聖恩頒
賜歷代名臣奏議者
伏以
聖主採言式廣師資之益
punctuated:
表

擬賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣謝表，永樂十四年。
黃星耀

同考試官教諭羅批：語意渾成，援引精切，咀嚼覺有餘味，可以式矣。

同考試官教授簡批：體裁莊整，不徒駢儷而已，是用錄之。

考試官教諭黃批：麗而則，廉而不劌，且長於四六者。

考試官教諭朱批：措詞舂容，忠愛藹然，得稱謝體。

永樂十四年某月某日，臣等伏蒙聖恩頒賜《歷代名臣奏議》者。
伏以聖主採言，式廣師資之益，
translation_en:
Memorial

A model memorial of thanks from the assembled officials upon being granted Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi), set in the fourteenth year of Yongle (1416).
By Huang Xingyao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The language and meaning form a seamless whole; the citations are precise and apt. Savoring it, one finds a lingering richness. It may serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Jian, Professor: “Its form is dignified and well ordered, and it offers more than merely paired and parallel phrases. For this reason it has been selected.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Ornate yet governed by proper standards, sharply defined yet not cutting; it is also accomplished in four-and-six-character parallel prose.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The phrasing is measured and ample, with loyalty and affection abundantly evident. It fulfills the requirements of a memorial of thanks.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourteenth year of Yongle, we, your servants, humbly received the imperial favor of a gift of Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties.
We humbly consider that the sage sovereign gathers worthy counsel, thereby extending the benefits of instruction and guidance …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
明庭錫類永垂獻納之規慶
嘉帙之告成荷
殊恩之荐及
寵逾三錫喜溢百朋臣等稽首頓首上言脩齊
平治理不間於古今手足腹心義無逃於
天地自開闢之始卽有君有臣以相臨由載籍
所傳皆立德立言之不朽喜起之迹雖遠
謀謨之範猶存能主善以爲師斯與治而
同道故君子尚友往哲而聖人且擇狂夫
况名臣登對之所陳皆忠義精華之所發
善惟主一文不在兹自杞亡文獻之無徴
暨漢興詩書之不事典刑已墜奚取神交
姓字徒存粗同耳食故魏相疏賢良之策
而唐宗錄忠諫之屏蘇軾敷陳疏僅呈於
陸相汝愚採摭編止及於宋臣惜乎未覩
完書信矣難聞要道時將有待事匪偶然
恭惟
皇帝陛下
punctuated:
明庭錫類，永垂獻納之規。慶嘉帙之告成，荷殊恩之荐及。寵逾三錫，喜溢百朋。臣等稽首頓首上言：脩齊平治，理不間於古今；手足腹心，義無逃於天地。自開闢之始，卽有君有臣以相臨；由載籍所傳，皆立德立言之不朽。喜起之迹雖遠，謀謨之範猶存。能主善以爲師，斯與治而同道。故君子尚友往哲，而聖人且擇狂夫。况名臣登對之所陳，皆忠義精華之所發。善惟主一，文不在兹。自杞亡文獻之無徴，暨漢興詩書之不事，典刑已墜，奚取神交？姓字徒存，粗同耳食。故魏相疏賢良之策，而唐宗錄忠諫之屏。蘇軾敷陳疏，僅呈於陸相；汝愚採摭編，止及於宋臣。惜乎未覩完書，信矣難聞要道！時將有待，事匪偶然。
恭惟皇帝陛下：
translation_en:
…The illustrious court extends its bounty to others, establishing for all time a model for presenting counsel. We rejoice at the completion of this fine collection and gratefully receive the extraordinary favor bestowed upon us anew. This honor surpasses three successive grants; our joy exceeds that of receiving a hundred strings of cowries. We, your servants, bow low and knock our heads upon the ground to submit these words:
The principles of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, bringing peace to the world, and governing the state do not differ between antiquity and the present. The obligations binding ruler and ministers as hands and feet, belly and heart, admit no escape anywhere between Heaven and Earth. From the first opening of the world, there have been rulers and ministers standing in relation to one another. What the written records transmit is the imperishable legacy of establishing virtue and establishing worthy words. Though the days when ruler and ministers joyfully roused one another to service are distant, their exemplary counsels remain. Those who take goodness as their teacher thereby follow the same Way as good government. Thus the gentleman seeks friendship with worthy men of the past, and even the sage selects useful words from the rash. How much more valuable, then, are the statements eminent ministers presented at imperial audiences, all issuing from the finest essence of loyalty and righteousness!
Goodness rests solely upon unity of purpose; is not this cultural legacy here [?]? From the lack of verifiable documentary and learned testimony after the fall of Qi [?], to the neglect of the Odes and Documents when the Han arose, the exemplary traditions had already fallen away: through what could one commune in spirit with the ancients? When only their names survive, knowledge of them scarcely differs from hearsay. Thus Wei Xiang submitted in a memorial the policy proposals of worthy men, while the Tang emperor had loyal remonstrances inscribed upon a screen. Su Shi's memorial of exposition concerned only Chief Minister Lu; Ruyu's compilation of selected writings extended only to ministers of the Song. Alas, no complete collection had yet been seen; indeed, it was difficult to learn the essential Way! The proper time awaited its coming; this undertaking is no chance occurrence.
We reverently consider Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
學本誠明
聖兼述作
宣威沙漠長清瀚海之波
凝命幽燕永定鎬京之鼎
堯仁舜智一德以建厥中
武烈文謨重明而麗乎正乾坤奠位華裔歸
心屬治定而功成欲圖艱以保大因時立
政每勤結網之思稽古求賢恒切拊髀之
嘆偶有見於遺直真深契於
===
淵衷如鄧張諸葛之流及董賈更生之輩全效
忠於往代寔垂範於
今時即意氣之相孚豈世代之能隔欲徵激勸
必藉表章
璽書爰賁於
春宮編纂特煩於翰苑因而博采咸以兼收
紀運自周武至宋元幾四千年而未訖條
目自君德至夷狄積三百卷而有奇義例
體裁備諸子百家之旨文章議論採羣書
punctuated:
學本誠明，聖兼述作。宣威沙漠，長清瀚海之波；凝命幽燕，永定鎬京之鼎。堯仁舜智，一德以建厥中；武烈文謨，重明而麗乎正。乾坤奠位，華裔歸心。屬治定而功成，欲圖艱以保大。因時立政，每勤結網之思；稽古求賢，恒切拊髀之嘆。偶有見於遺直，真深契於淵衷。如鄧、張、諸葛之流，及董、賈、更生之輩，全效忠於往代，寔垂範於今時。即意氣之相孚，豈世代之能隔？欲徵激勸，必藉表章。
璽書爰賁於春宮，編纂特煩於翰苑，因而博采，咸以兼收。紀運自周武至宋元，幾四千年而未訖；條目自君德至夷狄，積三百卷而有奇。義例體裁，備諸子百家之旨；文章議論，採羣書
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s learning is rooted in sincerity and enlightenment, and your sagacity embraces both transmitting tradition and creating anew. You proclaim your might across the desert, keeping the waves of the Hanhai forever calm; you consolidate the Mandate in You and Yan, securing forever the dynastic tripods of Haojing. With Yao’s benevolence and Shun’s wisdom, you establish the Mean through undivided virtue; with King Wu’s martial achievements and King Wen’s plans, your successive brilliance adheres to what is correct. Heaven and earth stand securely in their places, and Chinese and foreign peoples alike give you their allegiance. Now that order is established and achievements complete, you seek to anticipate difficulties and preserve your great dominion. Establishing policies suited to the times, you constantly ponder the weaving of a net to secure worthy men; examining antiquity in search of the worthy, you repeatedly sigh and slap your thigh in longing for them. On encountering upright men of the past, you find a profound affinity with your innermost thoughts. Men such as Deng, Zhang, and Zhuge, and such figures as Dong, Jia, and Gengsheng, devoted themselves wholly and loyally to former dynasties and indeed offer models for the present age. When spirit and purpose accord, how can the generations keep them apart? To make their power to inspire and encourage manifest, they must be publicly honored.
An imperial letter bearing the seal accordingly bestowed honor upon the Crown Prince’s palace, and the work of compilation was specially entrusted to the Hanlin Academy. Materials were then gathered broadly and included comprehensively. Its chronological coverage extends from King Wu of Zhou through the Song and Yuan, spanning nearly four thousand years without exhausting its scope. Its headings range from the ruler’s virtue to foreign peoples, filling more than three hundred juan. Its organizing principles and literary forms encompass the purport of the various masters and the hundred schools; its compositions and discussions draw upon the many books…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
列傳之長理本無窮眞展卷而有益事皆
可法若指掌之易明續六經之所未該驗
累朝之所已試豈云小補允也
大成
錫以徽名頓重斯文之價
付之良梓允爲
天府之珍首宣
賜於
二宮隨覃
===
===
恩於庶位視爲臣鵠喜有的之可趨探若知囊
信隨求而各足是何遭逢之有幸而衣被
之無窮也臣等學本面墻無由納約才非
補
袞何以報章毎懷古道之脩深切高山之仰
先知先覺得我心之同然是訓是行惟
君子之所使庶見馳聲
閭閻猶慚學步邯鄲敢不仰體
鴻私勉抒駑鈍爲臣而必欲盡臣道學古而
punctuated:
列傳之長。理本無窮，眞展卷而有益；事皆可法，若指掌之易明。續六經之所未該，驗累朝之所已試，豈云小補？允也大成！錫以徽名，頓重斯文之價；付之良梓，允爲天府之珍。首宣賜於二宮，隨覃恩於庶位。視爲臣鵠，喜有的之可趨；探若知囊，信隨求而各足。是何遭逢之有幸，而衣被之無窮也！

臣等學本面墻，無由納約；才非補袞，何以報章？毎懷古道之脩，深切高山之仰。先知先覺，得我心之同然；是訓是行，惟君子之所使。庶見馳聲閭閻，猶慚學步邯鄲。敢不仰體鴻私，勉抒駑鈍，爲臣而必欲盡臣道，學古而
translation_en:
…the strengths of the collected biographies. Its principles are inexhaustible: truly, opening its pages brings benefit. Its recorded deeds all offer models to follow, as readily understood as the palm of one’s hand. It supplements what the Six Classics did not encompass and verifies what successive dynasties have already put to the test. How could its contribution be called small? Truly, it is a grand synthesis! Bestowing upon it an auspicious title, Your Majesty at once enhanced the worth of this literary work; committing it to fine printing blocks, you truly made it a treasure of the imperial repository. First you proclaimed its bestowal upon the Two Palaces, then extended your favor to officials of every rank. Regarding it as a target for ministerial conduct, we rejoice to have a mark toward which to strive; consulting it as a storehouse of wisdom, we find that it indeed supplies whatever each seeks. How fortunate we are to have encountered such an occasion, and how boundless are the benefits that enfold us!

We, your servants, are in our learning like men facing a wall, unable to offer counsel that reaches your heart. Our talents cannot mend the imperial robes—that is, remedy our sovereign’s shortcomings—so how can we offer words worthy of your gift? Whenever we contemplate the cultivation of the ancient Way, we feel profound admiration, as for a lofty mountain. Those who first attained knowledge and understanding grasped what our hearts alike acknowledge; these teachings we put into practice, acting only as the noble man directs. We hope that our reputation may spread among the common people, yet feel ashamed that we merely imitate others, like the man who learned to walk in Handan. How could we fail reverently to appreciate your immense favor and strive to exert our dull abilities, determined as servants to fulfill the Way of service, and in studying antiquity to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
期不愧古人三復斯言用代韋弦之義再
陳末論聊伸犬馬之忱步亦步趨亦趨程
法期無忘於前烈可曰可否曰否獻替矢
不負於他時伏願
言必見諸躬行
博則歸於守約
任人惟舊
進德圖新
終始惟勤學古訓以有獲
===
緝熙罔懈率舊章而無愆
霈雨露之恩咸歸
大造
擴河海之量不擇細流
治敎萬年
君道與
師道同泰
車書一統文運偕
國運竝升臣無任瞻
punctuated:
期不愧古人。三復斯言，用代韋弦之義；再陳末論，聊伸犬馬之忱。步亦步，趨亦趨，程法期無忘於前烈；可曰可，否曰否，獻替矢不負於他時。
伏願言必見諸躬行，博則歸於守約；任人惟舊，進德圖新；終始惟勤，學古訓以有獲；緝熙罔懈，率舊章而無愆。霈雨露之恩，咸歸大造；擴河海之量，不擇細流。治敎萬年，君道與師道同泰；車書一統，文運偕國運竝升。臣無任瞻
translation_en:
…in the hope of not falling short of the ancients. We repeatedly ponder these words, taking them as admonitory reminders in place of the leather thong and bowstring. Once more we present our humble views, merely to express our devotion as dogs and horses in your service. When you walk, we walk; when you hasten, we hasten: in taking your example as our standard, we hope never to forget the achievements of our predecessors. What is right we shall call right; what is wrong we shall call wrong: in recommending the good and correcting faults, we pledge never to fail you in the days to come.
We humbly wish that your words may always find expression in your own conduct, and that broad learning may culminate in holding fast to the essentials; that you may employ those long known to you, and seek continual renewal in advancing your virtue; that you may remain diligent from beginning to end, learning the teachings of antiquity and thereby gaining benefit; and that you may continue in luminous virtue without flagging, following established precedents without error. May your grace pour down like rain and dew, so that all may partake of your great beneficence; may your magnanimity expand like the rivers and seas, rejecting no small stream. May governance and moral instruction endure for ten thousand years, and may the Way of the ruler and the Way of the teacher flourish together. May carriage tracks and written characters be unified throughout the realm, and may the fortunes of letters rise together with those of the state. Your servant, overcome with emotion, gazes toward…

text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱

聞
第叁場

第一問
楊棐

皇上功德並懋淵源所漸得自傳心誠足以媲美往聖而下視近代是作援
據精確賛述詳明其涵濡治化獨深者與
同考試官教諭張批正道不傳曠矣千載我
聖祖龍興
皇上紹述後先同光要非偶然子能揚厲
閎休而根極要領必俊茂博達之士也用錄以傳
考試官教諭黃批敷揚我

天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場，策，第一問。
楊棐。
同考試官教諭龍批：「我聖祖、皇上功德並懋，淵源所漸，得自傳心，誠足以媲美往聖，而下視近代。是作援據精確，賛述詳明，其涵濡治化獨深者與！」
同考試官教諭張批：「正道不傳，曠矣千載。我聖祖龍興，皇上紹述，後先同光，要非偶然。子能揚厲閎休，而根極要領，必俊茂博達之士也。用錄以傳。」

translation_en:
…looking up to Heaven and reverently admiring Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling awe, I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question.
Yang Fei.
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor, comments: “Our Sagely Founder and His Majesty alike excel in achievement and virtue. The profound source of their formative influence lies in the transmission of the mind. They truly merit comparison with the sages of old and tower above rulers of more recent times. This essay adduces evidence precisely and offers detailed, lucid praise and exposition. Surely its author has been especially deeply imbued with the transforming influence of our governance!”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The true Way went untransmitted for a thousand years. Our Sagely Founder rose like a dragon, and His Majesty carried on his work; predecessor and successor shine with equal brilliance. This is certainly no accident. You can extol their magnificent blessings while tracing the essential principles to their roots. You must be a man of outstanding talent and broad understanding. Accordingly, this essay is selected for preservation and circulation.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖創業之隆
皇上中興之盛犖然當於人心非漫作者
考試官敎諭朱批天人一理古今一心我
聖祖
皇上作述可以推見是作獨能對揚錄之
帝王之所以明聖兼資而作述並隆者無
他焉法天而已矣法祖而已矣天而知所
以法則蘊之爲大德發之爲王道皆盡善
盡美之規而其詒謀也遠祖而知所以法
===
則上以體天心下以奠民命皆善繼善述
之道而其敷治也周不于其文于其實善
法天者也不師其迹師其意善法祖者也
作者之謂聖而善法天其知所以作乎述
者之謂明而善法祖其知所以述乎以淵
懿端純之則而肇駿龐高朗之業以開拓
積累之勤而衍昌明閎遠之緖先後一揆
古今罕儷則我
高祖之創造丕基與
punctuated:
聖祖創業之隆、皇上中興之盛，犖然當於人心，非漫作者。

考試官敎諭朱批：天人一理，古今一心。我聖祖、皇上作述，可以推見。是作獨能對揚，錄之。

帝王之所以明聖兼資而作述並隆者，無他焉，法天而已矣，法祖而已矣。天而知所以法，則蘊之爲大德，發之爲王道，皆盡善盡美之規，而其詒謀也遠；祖而知所以法，則上以體天心，下以奠民命，皆善繼善述之道，而其敷治也周。不于其文，于其實，善法天者也；不師其迹，師其意，善法祖者也。作者之謂聖，而善法天，其知所以作乎？述者之謂明，而善法祖，其知所以述乎？以淵懿端純之則，而肇駿龐高朗之業；以開拓積累之勤，而衍昌明閎遠之緖。先後一揆，古今罕儷，則我高祖之創造丕基與
translation_en:
