而禮樂達於天下乃於文章道德未知其
出於一先儒嘗譏其吟詩飲酒文人自立
矣則所言文與道俱不知果澤於道否也
居士之作後性之說豈君子玩物之戒聖
人敎人之道哉彼蘇之馳騁曾之純正又
不足言矣嗟乎四海之至廣千百年之至
久而專其所長以自名其家者數人而已
punctuated:
者，日光玉潔，周情孔思，詭然而蛟龍翔，鬱然而虎鳳躍，誠一代之宗工也。然其論古人，則以屈、孟、馬、楊爲一等，乃卑孟軻爲伍。先儒嘗譏其無頭學問，徒費精神矣。則所謂因文見道，不知果合於道否也。大顛之比，宰相之書，豈君子居身之珎、儒者衛道之嚴哉？彼柳之峻拔、劉之譎怪，又不足言矣。時丁五代，萎薾甚矣。至宋復興，時則有若歐陽脩者，賦詩似李白，論事似陸贄，有周旋揖讓之態，無局促拘迫之形，誠斯文之隆棟也。觀其言曰：「三代以上，治出於一，而禮樂達於天下。」乃於文章道德，未知其出於一。先儒嘗譏其吟詩飲酒，文人自立矣。則所言文與道俱，不知果澤於道否也。居士之作，後性之說，豈君子玩物之戒、聖人敎人之道哉？彼蘇之馳騁、曾之純正，又不足言矣。

嗟乎！四海之至廣，千百年之至久，而專其所長以自名其家者，數人而已。
translation_en:
…whose radiance was like the sun and whose purity was like jade, whose sentiments were those of the Duke of Zhou and whose thoughts were those of Confucius. In wondrous transformations his writing soared like a dragon; in luxuriant vigor it leapt like tigers and phoenixes. Truly, Han Yu was a master of his age. Yet when discussing the ancients, he ranked Qu Yuan, Meng Ke, Sima Qian, and Yang Xiong together, thus lowering Meng Ke to the company of the others. Earlier Confucian scholars criticized his learning as lacking a guiding principle and merely wasting his mental energies. As for his purported perception of the Way through literature, we cannot know whether it truly accorded with the Way. His association with Dadian and his letters to the chief councilor—did these show the care with which a gentleman treasures his own integrity, or the rigor with which a Confucian defends the Way? As for Liu’s lofty vigor and the other Liu’s strange ingenuity, these hardly merit further discussion.

When the age reached the Five Dynasties, the decline was profound. With the Song came a revival, and there appeared a man such as Ouyang Xiu. In composing poetry he resembled Li Bai; in discussing affairs he resembled Lu Zhi. His writing had the bearing of someone moving gracefully through ceremonial bows and courtesies, with nothing cramped or constrained about it. Truly, he was a great supporting beam of this literary tradition. Consider his statement: “In the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music extended throughout the realm.” Yet he did not understand that literary composition and moral virtue likewise issued from a single source. Earlier Confucian scholars criticized him for reciting poetry and drinking wine, establishing himself merely as a literary man. As for his claim that literature accompanies the Way, we cannot know whether he was truly steeped in the Way. His writings as a ‘Retired Scholar’ and his doctrine of treating human nature as secondary—did these embody the gentleman’s caution against becoming absorbed in things, or the sages’ way of teaching others? As for Su’s unrestrained range and Zeng’s purity and correctness, these hardly merit further discussion.

Alas! Across the immense expanse within the Four Seas and the long course of hundreds and thousands of years, only a few men have distinguished themselves through their particular strengths and established a literary tradition of their own…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
而君子猶病其未能粹然於道德之歸至
於呟議小言或不免於背道者而乃得與
諸子並傳至今如執事所云者蓋其故有
二焉有近理之言而不能粹然澤於道者
彼方溺於末世之習以其見爲學不能反
而歸於正而其爲文直抒發其心之所欲
言故其偏頗之情亦自不可掩至於蕩然
無所近者亦能抉奇怪之言以駭世之耳
目而人皆狃於其習悅其言其入人旣深
===
則雖有反經之君子亦不能盡取而悉禁
之故人亡而響猶存也而執事復究言世
變之趨無乃有感於宋人之言乎曰周爲
上七國次之漢爲下東漢以下無取焉雖
然誠然矣愚聞之語曰文者配序三靈管
攝萬類天地之文吾未聞有改焉豈其在
人獨異歟太極一圖契先聖作易之旨定
性一篇即孔子中和之義愚不敢謂其非
三代之文也是故世變不足繫也已三代
punctuated:
而君子猶病其未能粹然於道德之歸。至於呟議小言，或不免於背道者，而乃得與諸子並傳至今，如執事所云者，蓋其故有二焉。有近理之言而不能粹然澤於道者，彼方溺於末世之習，以其見爲學，不能反而歸於正；而其爲文，直抒發其心之所欲言，故其偏頗之情亦自不可掩。至於蕩然無所近者，亦能抉奇怪之言，以駭世之耳目，而人皆狃於其習，悅其言。其入人旣深，則雖有反經之君子，亦不能盡取而悉禁之，故人亡而響猶存也。
而執事復究言世變之趨，無乃有感於宋人之言乎？曰：「周爲上，七國次之，漢爲下，東漢以下無取焉。」雖然，誠然矣。愚聞之，語曰：「文者，配序三靈，管攝萬類。」天地之文，吾未聞有改焉，豈其在人獨異歟？《太極》一圖，契先聖作《易》之旨；《定性》一篇，即孔子中和之義。愚不敢謂其非三代之文也。是故世變不足繫也已。三代
translation_en:
…Yet the gentleman still finds fault with their failure to attain complete purity in their commitment to the Way and virtue. As for obscure discussions [?] and minor sayings, some of which inevitably depart from the Way, how have they nevertheless been transmitted alongside the writings of the various masters down to the present, as you observe? There are, broadly, two reasons. Some contain statements approaching principle, yet cannot be wholly imbued with the Way. Their authors were immersed in the habits of a declining age, taking their own views for learning and unable to turn back to what is correct. In composing, they simply expressed what their hearts wished to say; consequently, their partial and biased dispositions could not be concealed. As for those utterly unrestrained writings that nowhere approach principle, their authors could nevertheless draw out strange and extraordinary expressions to startle the eyes and ears of the world. People became accustomed to their ways and delighted in their words. Once these had deeply penetrated people’s minds, even gentlemen who returned to the Classics could not gather them all up and prohibit them entirely. Thus, although the authors are gone, their echoes remain.
You further inquire into the direction of change across the ages. Might you have been moved by the words of a Song writer: “The Zhou ranks highest; the Seven States come next; the Han ranks lowest. From the Eastern Han onward, nothing merits adoption”? That said, there is indeed truth in this. Yet I have heard the saying: “Writing matches and orders the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and governs and embraces the myriad kinds of things.” I have never heard that the patterned order of Heaven and Earth has changed. Could it be different in humanity alone? The Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) accords with the intent of the former sages in composing the Book of Changes; the essay Settling the Nature (Dingxing) embodies Confucius’s meaning of equilibrium and harmony. I would not venture to say that these are not writings of the same order as those of the Three Dynasties. Thus, changes across the ages cannot determine the matter. The Three Dynasties…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
而上教化行於上則比屋皆脩其身三代
而下道德明於下則君子自脩其身故脩
身者隨其身之所接物之所至莫非文也
由博約之功而造一貫之妙則出之以聲
為法言著之於身為德容筆之於書為聖
經豈必綴詞抽思操觚展翰而後為文哉
愚也非曰能之願學焉
第五問
廖雲鵬
===
同考試官教諭龍批屯田榷鹽一策正以觀士
子經濟之略往往掇拾迄無定見推究源委而斟酌時宜
可以施諸實政者莫踰此篇
同考試官教授簡批祛弊振法灼有定裁他日
服官必不坐視民瘼錄之以端觀法
考試官教諭黃批條析利弊如指諸掌末篇
慨嘆有深長思焉佳士佳士
考試官教諭朱批論事正而不苛詳而有要
用世之才舍子其誰
punctuated:
而上，教化行於上，則比屋皆脩其身；三代而下，道德明於下，則君子自脩其身。故脩身者，隨其身之所接、物之所至，莫非文也。由博約之功而造一貫之妙，則出之以聲為法言，著之於身為德容，筆之於書為聖經。豈必綴詞抽思、操觚展翰而後為文哉？愚也非曰能之，願學焉。

第五問
廖雲鵬

同考試官教諭龍批：屯田榷鹽一策，正以觀士子經濟之略。往往掇拾，迄無定見。推究源委而斟酌時宜，可以施諸實政者，莫踰此篇。

同考試官教授簡批：祛弊振法，灼有定裁。他日服官，必不坐視民瘼。錄之以端觀法。

考試官教諭黃批：條析利弊，如指諸掌。末篇慨嘆，有深長思焉。佳士！佳士！

考試官教諭朱批：論事正而不苛，詳而有要。用世之才，舍子其誰？
translation_en:
…and earlier, when moral instruction prevailed among those above, every household cultivated personal virtue; from the Three Dynasties onward, when the Way and virtue shone among those below, gentlemen cultivated their own virtue. Thus, for those who cultivate themselves, everything they encounter and every circumstance that comes their way is an expression of cultural refinement. Through the work of broad learning and restraint through ritual, they attain the subtle understanding of a single unifying principle. Expressed in speech, this becomes exemplary words; manifested in the person, it becomes a virtuous bearing; committed to writing, it becomes the sages’ classics. Must one string together phrases, draw forth thoughts, take up writing tablets, and wield a brush before producing such refinement? I do not claim to be capable of this, but I wish to learn.

Fifth Policy Question
Liao Yunpeng

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: This policy question on military agricultural colonies and the salt monopoly was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ grasp of statecraft. They often merely piece together borrowed material, never reaching a firm judgment. For investigating origins and ramifications, weighing what suits present circumstances, and offering proposals applicable to actual government, no essay surpasses this one.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jian, Professor: On eliminating abuses and reinvigorating institutions, he has clear and definite judgments. When he holds office in the future, he will surely not stand idly by in the face of the people’s suffering. I have selected this essay to establish a proper model for study and emulation.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: He analyzes benefits and drawbacks point by point, as clearly as if pointing to something in his own palm. The impassioned lament at the essay’s close contains profound and far-reaching thought. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: His discussion of affairs is upright without being harsh, detailed while grasping the essentials. Who but you possesses the talent to serve the world?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
愚聞之察利病之原者智也然必有貞固
之才而後其智始成酌損益之宜者才也
然必有昭曠之智而後其才始達蓋天下
之事固有法密而弊愈滋名存而實則亡
者非智足以及之則雖弊原之日陳於吾
前亦將忽焉而莫之知旣識矣舉其事而
必有以成其謀非一人之力旦夕焉所可
必也非一人一旦之力可成則將有震訶
至矣不有貞固之才鮮不從中沮者何也
===
人方便於其弊而樂乎吾之能舍吾旣處
其勞而且有隱虞焉則亦何不爲便安之
圖必處羣猜之中任不可期之功耶是故
知之未必行行之未必終也嗚呼天下之
事莫不然也而屯田鹽法尤甚者其在閩地
則屯田居其七八而鹽法特一二耳愚生
有懷欲陳久矣而况明問之及乎夫自漢
文募塞下之民昭帝屯張掖之田而屯田
之制始興行之而効者有之矣若趙充國
punctuated: 愚聞之，察利病之原者，智也；然必有貞固之才，而後其智始成。酌損益之宜者，才也；然必有昭曠之智，而後其才始達。蓋天下之事，固有法密而弊愈滋、名存而實則亡者。非智足以及之，則雖弊原之日陳於吾前，亦將忽焉而莫之知。旣識矣，舉其事而必有以成其謀，非一人之力旦夕焉所可必也。非一人一旦之力可成，則將有震訶至矣。不有貞固之才，鮮不從中沮者。何也？人方便於其弊，而樂乎吾之能舍；吾旣處其勞，而且有隱虞焉，則亦何不爲便安之圖，必處羣猜之中，任不可期之功耶？是故知之未必行，行之未必終也。嗚呼！天下之事莫不然也，而屯田、鹽法尤甚者。其在閩地，則屯田居其七八，而鹽法特一二耳。愚生有懷，欲陳久矣，而况明問之及乎！夫自漢文募塞下之民、昭帝屯張掖之田，而屯田之制始興。行之而効者有之矣，若趙充國
translation_en:
I have heard that discerning the sources of benefits and harms is wisdom; yet only with steadfast ability can that wisdom achieve results. Weighing what should appropriately be curtailed or augmented is ability; yet only with clear and far-ranging wisdom can that ability find full expression. In the affairs of the world, there are indeed cases in which regulations grow more elaborate while abuses proliferate, and institutions survive in name while their substance disappears. Unless our wisdom is sufficient to comprehend them, even when the sources of abuse are displayed before us daily, we will overlook them and remain unaware. Once we have recognized them, undertaking the matter and bringing our plans to fruition is not something that one person's efforts can assuredly accomplish overnight. Since it cannot be accomplished by one person's efforts in a single day, angry reprimands will follow. Without steadfast ability, few will avoid losing heart along the way. Why is this? Others are enjoying the advantages afforded by these abuses and would welcome our abandoning the effort. We, meanwhile, bear the toil and also harbor unspoken apprehensions. Why, then, should we not seek ease and security, instead of insisting on remaining amid widespread suspicion and undertaking work whose success cannot be assured? Thus, understanding does not necessarily lead to action, nor does action necessarily continue to completion.

Alas! This is true of all affairs in the world, but especially of military agricultural colonies and the salt administration. In Fujian, the colonies account for seven or eight tenths of the problem, while the salt administration accounts for only one or two tenths. I, an unworthy scholar, have long wished to set forth my thoughts on these matters; how much more so now that your discerning question addresses them!

The system of military agricultural colonies first arose when Emperor Wen of the Han recruited people to settle along the frontier and Emperor Zhao established agricultural colonies at Zhangye. There have indeed been instances in which its implementation proved effective, such as Zhao Chongguo …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之屯於金城而饟積殷盛卒底擊零之功
諸葛亮之屯於斜谷而民咸安堵用成伐
魏之圖羊祜之屯於襄陽而墾田八百竟
收十年之需自是而鄧艾行之則資食有
儲韓重華行之則收粟省緡何承矩行之
則稻田足食所謂無加賦之名而軍國之
用自足無轉運之勞而倉儲之積自盈非
容民之遺意乎自青州貢鹽之制周官鹽
人之役而鹽之名始起然未聞其有榷也
===
至管仲舉伐菑煑海之利而國大富劉晏
上鹽法輕重之宜而國足用盛度善行義
清課之謀而公私咸賴外此而鹽資船運
而民力寬者李沆也錢鈔請鹽而省般運
者范祥也片言弛禁而惠及一邑者方平
也所謂斂山澤之貨以寬田疇之賦收關
市之稅以助什一之法非經國之急務乎
是故歷代不能外而我
國家亦因之請自閩言屯田之法爲衛者十
punctuated: 之屯於金城，而饟積殷盛，卒底擊零之功；諸葛亮之屯於斜谷，而民咸安堵，用成伐魏之圖；羊祜之屯於襄陽，而墾田八百，竟收十年之需。自是而鄧艾行之，則資食有儲；韓重華行之，則收粟省緡；何承矩行之，則稻田足食。所謂無加賦之名，而軍國之用自足；無轉運之勞，而倉儲之積自盈，非容民之遺意乎？自青州貢鹽之制、周官鹽人之役，而鹽之名始起，然未聞其有榷也。至管仲舉伐菑煑海之利，而國大富；劉晏上鹽法輕重之宜，而國足用；盛度善行義清課之謀，而公私咸賴。外此，而鹽資船運而民力寬者，李沆也；錢鈔請鹽而省般運者，范祥也；片言弛禁而惠及一邑者，方平也。所謂斂山澤之貨，以寬田疇之賦；收關市之稅，以助什一之法，非經國之急務乎？是故歷代不能外，而我國家亦因之。請自閩言屯田之法：爲衛者十
translation_en:
…established agricultural colonies at Jincheng, where military provisions accumulated abundantly, ultimately bringing success in the campaign against the Ling [?]. Zhuge Liang established agricultural colonies at Xiegu, where the people all remained secure in their homes, thereby advancing his plan to attack Wei. Yang Hu established agricultural colonies at Xiangyang, where eight hundred units of farmland were reclaimed, ultimately yielding provisions sufficient for ten years. When Deng Ai implemented this system, supplies and food were held in reserve; when Han Chonghua implemented it, grain was collected and expenditure in strings of cash reduced; when He Chengju implemented it, rice fields provided ample food. This is what is meant by meeting military and state expenses without imposing additional taxes, and filling the granaries without the toil of transporting provisions. Does this not preserve the ancient intent of providing for the people?

Salt first came to prominence with Qingzhou’s tribute of salt and the duties of the Salt Officers in the Offices of Zhou, though we hear of no monopoly at that time. Then Guan Zhong exploited the profits of cutting scrub and boiling seawater, greatly enriching his state. Liu Yan submitted proposals for suitably adjusting the salt administration, providing the state with sufficient revenue. Sheng Du effectively implemented a plan concerning “righteousness and clearing the levies” [?], benefiting both government and people. Besides these, it was Li Hang who used boats to transport salt, easing the burden on the people; it was Fan Xiang who allowed salt to be obtained through cash and certificates, reducing transport burdens; and it was Fangping who, with a few words, secured the relaxation of prohibitions and benefited an entire county. This is what is meant by collecting the wealth of mountains and marshes to lighten taxation on farmland, and collecting duties at passes and markets to supplement the tithe system. Are these not urgent tasks in governing a state?

Thus successive dynasties could not dispense with these measures, and our own dynasty has likewise followed them. Allow me to discuss the agricultural colony system beginning with Fujian: the number of guards is ten…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
有六焉所者九十有九而以籍軍十之二
者守城郭十之七者服田畝焉有二八三
七四六中半之例有新屯舊屯之名而計
其所授之田則二人合四十石量其所入
之粟則一人各十二石蓋以一方之屯而
廩一方之兵無事則荷耜耒遇警則執干
戈勤服則無曠土食力則少惰農其兩利
而無害者乎榷鹽之法爲場者七所輸者
歲二萬有奇而三場餘引僅六千有六百
===
===
餘焉置引而驗之召商而中之而徵納有
本折之異分掣有大小引之殊蓋程之有
時月行之有疆界輸官以粟酬商以鹽在
民則食味在商則取贏其兼濟而不悖者
乎夫閩之屯田非有兗徐草萊荊襄泛濫
之虞也雖多高原而實腴衍額輸之盈縮
田里之多寡未甞不在籍也然名雖存而
實則亡矣言者曰徵餘糧之半正糧聽自
給而屯倉廢因沙尤之寇補種增餘丁而
punctuated:
有六焉，所者九十有九，而以籍軍十之二者守城郭，十之七者服田畝焉。有二八、三七、四六、中半之例，有新屯、舊屯之名。而計其所授之田，則二人合四十石；量其所入之粟，則一人各十二石。蓋以一方之屯，而廩一方之兵，無事則荷耜耒，遇警則執干戈。勤服則無曠土，食力則少惰農，其兩利而無害者乎？榷鹽之法，爲場者七，所輸者歲二萬有奇，而三場餘引僅六千有六百餘焉。置引而驗之，召商而中之，而徵納有本折之異，分掣有大小引之殊。蓋程之有時月，行之有疆界，輸官以粟，酬商以鹽。在民則食味，在商則取贏，其兼濟而不悖者乎？
夫閩之屯田，非有兗徐草萊、荊襄泛濫之虞也。雖多高原，而實腴衍。額輸之盈縮，田里之多寡，未甞不在籍也。然名雖存，而實則亡矣。言者曰：「徵餘糧之半，正糧聽自給，而屯倉廢；因沙尤之寇，補種增餘丁，而
translation_en:
…sixteen in all, with ninety-nine battalion offices. Of the registered soldiers, two-tenths defend the cities and seven-tenths cultivate the fields. There are prescribed allocations of two to eight, three to seven, four to six, and half and half, as well as the categories of new and old military agricultural colonies. Reckoning the land allotted to them, two men together receive land assessed at forty shi of grain; reckoning the grain they deliver, each man supplies twelve shi. Thus the agricultural colonies of a region provision that region’s troops. In quiet times they shoulder their ploughing tools; when danger comes, they take up shields and spears. Diligent cultivation leaves no land idle, and living by one’s own labor reduces the number of indolent farmers. Does this not yield benefits on both sides without harm?
Under the salt monopoly system, there are seven saltworks, whose annual deliveries amount to more than twenty thousand; yet the surplus salt certificates of three saltworks number only a little over six thousand six hundred. Certificates are issued and checked, and merchants are invited to bid for them. Payments collected differ between those made in kind and those commuted, while the allocation and inspection of salt distinguish between large and small certificates. There are prescribed months for these procedures and territorial limits on circulation. Grain is delivered to the government, and merchants are recompensed with salt. The people gain seasoning for their food, and the merchants gain profits. Does this not serve both interests without conflict?
As for Fujian’s military agricultural colonies, they face neither the threat of land reverting to scrub in Yan and Xu nor that of flooding in Jing and Xiang. Although much of the land is upland, it is fertile and extensive. Surpluses and shortfalls in quota deliveries, and the extent of the farmland, have always been recorded in the registers. Yet although the name survives, the substance has disappeared. Critics say: “Half the surplus grain is collected, while the regular grain allotment is left for the soldiers’ own support, and the colony granaries have fallen into disuse. Because of the bandits in Sha and You, supplementary cultivators were assigned and additional military dependents enrolled [?], and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
經略弛更番之法不立則視阡陌爲世守
之恒産專官之禁不除則以衞隷爲私家
之奴役如是而欲屯法之行可乎夫閩之
鹽法非有淮運二萬浙運十萬之多也雖
無專使而有專官其條告之防飭論奏之
陳建未嘗不詳也然法雖密而弊愈滋矣
言者曰私販不禁則課將遏行影射不懲
則法從旁尼夾賣之弊不察則巵而漏者
也捕卒之戒不嚴則關而暴者也如是而
===
欲鹽法之善可乎雖然不識立法之原則
行法之委不可得而言也不明致弊之實
則除弊之方不可得而言也屯田之弊果
如言者乎蓋在閩則有四焉田畝存於版
籍歳入歸於豪右草莽蕪於逃亡耕耨廢
於貧乏則屯法之未可行也鹽法之弊果
如言者乎蓋在閩則有四焉嚴出納之防
杜守支之弊正行鹽之地還鹽額之舊則
鹽法之尚可善也嗟乎鹽法之弊官有常
punctuated:
經略弛。更番之法不立，則視阡陌爲世守之恒産；專官之禁不除，則以衞隷爲私家之奴役。如是而欲屯法之行，可乎？夫閩之鹽法，非有淮運二萬、浙運十萬之多也。雖無專使，而有專官，其條告之防飭、論奏之陳建，未嘗不詳也。然法雖密，而弊愈滋矣。言者曰：「私販不禁，則課將遏行；影射不懲，則法從旁尼；夾賣之弊不察，則巵而漏者也；捕卒之戒不嚴，則關而暴者也。」如是而欲鹽法之善，可乎？
雖然，不識立法之原，則行法之委不可得而言也；不明致弊之實，則除弊之方不可得而言也。屯田之弊，果如言者乎？蓋在閩則有四焉：田畝存於版籍，歳入歸於豪右，草莽蕪於逃亡，耕耨廢於貧乏，則屯法之未可行也。鹽法之弊，果如言者乎？蓋在閩則有四焉：嚴出納之防，杜守支之弊，正行鹽之地，還鹽額之舊，則鹽法之尚可善也。嗟乎！鹽法之弊，官有常
translation_en:
…and administration has grown lax. Unless a system of rotation is established, the fields will be regarded as permanent estates held hereditarily; unless the prohibition concerning specially appointed officials is removed [?], the guards’ personnel will be treated as servants of private households. Under such circumstances, can one expect the military agricultural colony system to function? Fujian’s salt administration does not handle quantities as great as the twenty thousand of the Huai salt administration or the hundred thousand of the Zhe salt administration. Although it has no specially appointed commissioner, it does have officials specifically responsible for the task. The safeguards and injunctions in its regulations and proclamations, and the proposals set forth in its memorials, have invariably been detailed. Yet the more elaborate the regulations, the more abuses proliferate. Critics say: “Unless illicit trading is prohibited, tax collection will be obstructed; unless trading under borrowed cover is punished, the law will be thwarted indirectly; unless the abuse of selling illicit salt alongside lawful salt is investigated, it is like a leaking cup; unless strict discipline is imposed on the arresting soldiers, there will be violence at the barriers [?].” Under such circumstances, can one expect salt administration to be well managed?
Nevertheless, without understanding the original principles behind the laws, one cannot discuss the details of their implementation; without understanding the actual causes of abuses, one cannot discuss how to eliminate them. Are the abuses in the military agricultural colonies really as the critics describe? In Fujian there are four: fields remain on the registers, but their annual proceeds go to powerful local families; land becomes overgrown because its cultivators have fled; and cultivation ceases because of poverty. These are the reasons the colony system cannot yet function properly. Are the abuses in salt administration really as the critics describe? In Fujian there are four corresponding measures: tighten safeguards over receipts and disbursements, eliminate abuses in waiting to receive salt allotments, rectify the designated salt-marketing territories, and restore the former salt quotas. Salt administration can thus still be improved. Alas! As for the abuses in salt administration, the officials have fixed …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
征商有定入但使稍自待者以柄其事則
其艾滌之法通變之方當不煩餘力爾乃
若屯田則大可慨焉請爲執事陳之今夫
戍卒之名不願聽故其避之也若湯火然
此固天下之通情也而此方之人乃夤緣
掛籍未聞有虚伍者何也彼其平居坐食
經歳無劒楯之交似聞籌給則且蟻聚支
廩之司矣稽籍則存待飼則存已而覈其
實則亡矣驕惰脆弱旣不堪爲公府衞一
===
稍逆其意則欲羣起而呼噪夫屯之制久
矣歳所嘗入二十爲率而以其半納屯倉
以其半輸城倉而遞歳轉運之數入于司
農者蓋有其額焉而今則并常數而逋之
所受之田自其祖父已侵而有之而子孫
已忘其爲公家產矣雖左驗甚明卒不肯
少伏焉而其巧於隱避者則又依憑豪右
盜沽而乾沒之嗚呼
國家置屯優戍之法豈誠不可問哉夫利弊
punctuated: 征，商有定入。但使稍自待者以柄其事，則其艾滌之法、通變之方，當不煩餘力爾。乃若屯田，則大可慨焉。請爲執事陳之。今夫戍卒之名，不願聽，故其避之也若湯火然，此固天下之通情也。而此方之人，乃夤緣掛籍，未聞有虚伍者，何也？彼其平居坐食，經歳無劒楯之交，似聞籌給，則且蟻聚支廩之司矣。稽籍則存，待飼則存，已而覈其實則亡矣。驕惰脆弱，旣不堪爲公府衞，一稍逆其意，則欲羣起而呼噪。夫屯之制久矣，歳所嘗入，二十爲率，而以其半納屯倉，以其半輸城倉。而遞歳轉運之數，入于司農者，蓋有其額焉。而今則并常數而逋之。所受之田，自其祖父已侵而有之，而子孫已忘其爲公家產矣。雖左驗甚明，卒不肯少伏焉。而其巧於隱避者，則又依憑豪右，盜沽而乾沒之。嗚呼！國家置屯優戍之法，豈誠不可問哉？夫利弊
translation_en:
…levies, and merchants have fixed receipts. If only someone with a modicum of self-respect were entrusted with these affairs, methods for rooting out abuses and adapting to circumstances should require little further effort. As for the military agricultural colonies, however, their condition is deeply lamentable. Allow me to lay it before you, Sir.

People today are unwilling even to hear the designation “garrison soldier,” and avoid it as they would boiling water or fire. This is surely a feeling common throughout the realm. Yet people here use connections to get themselves entered on the rolls, and one never hears of vacancies in the ranks. Why is this? In ordinary times they draw sustenance without working, passing entire years without any clash of swords and shields. At the mere hint that rations are to be allotted [?], they gather like ants at the office that issues grain. Check the registers, and they are present; when waiting to be fed, they are present. But then investigate the actual situation, and they are gone. Arrogant, indolent, feeble, and weak, they are unfit even to serve as guards for government offices; yet at the slightest affront to their wishes, they are ready to rise in a body and raise an uproar.

The system of military agricultural colonies has existed for a long time. The customary annual payment was reckoned at twenty, half delivered to the colony granary and half to the city granary. There were also established quotas for the amounts transported each year to the fiscal authorities. Now, however, they default even on the regular payments. The fields allotted to them had already been appropriated as private possessions by their fathers and grandfathers, and their descendants have forgotten that these are public property. Even when the corroborating evidence is perfectly clear, they refuse to concede the slightest point. Those adept at concealment and evasion, moreover, rely on powerful local families, illicitly sell the land, and pocket the proceeds.

Alas! Can the state's system of establishing military agricultural colonies and providing generously for garrison troops truly be beyond scrutiny? As for the benefits and abuses…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之在目前也自非大無睹之士鮮不徐徐
察而得之然持之而莫肯議欲有謀焉而
卒中阻者往往也吁於今不察則將至於
必不可究詰之地矣夫才智兼資而損益
合宜非經國者事乎尚其加意焉爾
punctuated: 之在目前也，自非大無睹之士，鮮不徐徐察而得之。然持之而莫肯議，欲有謀焉而卒中阻者，往往也。吁！於今不察，則將至於必不可究詰之地矣。夫才智兼資，而損益合宜，非經國者事乎？尚其加意焉爾！
translation_en: …when these benefits and abuses lie before one’s eyes, few, unless utterly unseeing, would fail to discern them through patient examination. Yet it often happens that those who have the matter in hand are unwilling to discuss it, and that attempts to devise a plan are ultimately obstructed midway. Alas! Unless the matter is investigated now, it will reach a point where it can no longer be thoroughly examined and brought to account. Is it not the task of those who govern the state to draw upon both ability and wisdom, making appropriate reductions and additions? May they give this their particular attention!

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
嘉靖壬子秋福建舉鄉試事
旣竣例有錄以告成將
獻之
上焉巡按御史曾佩謂宏以職事
當序諸末簡乃敢申于多士
曰文章氣運其幾相因而
===
聖君賢輔其道所以相成也歷觀
古今莫不皆然猗與休哉
今日文明之運士以文獲進者何
其遭際之盛而尚忍負於相
成之道哉我
祖宗肇造區宇以來稽古右文道
隆化洽百八十年于兹矣曁
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

嘉靖壬子秋，福建舉鄉試事。旣竣，例有錄以告成，將獻之上焉。巡按御史曾佩謂宏以職事當序諸末簡，乃敢申于多士曰：「文章氣運，其幾相因；而聖君賢輔，其道所以相成也。歷觀古今，莫不皆然。猗與休哉！今日文明之運，士以文獲進者，何其遭際之盛，而尚忍負於相成之道哉！我祖宗肇造區宇以來，稽古右文，道隆化洽，百八十年于兹矣。曁
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renzi year of the Jiajing reign (1552), Fujian held its Provincial Examination. When it was completed, a record was compiled, as customary, to report its successful conclusion and to be presented to the emperor. The Regional Inspector, Zeng Pei, told me, Hong, that my official duties required me to write a postface at the end of the volume. I therefore venture to address these words to the assembled scholars:

“Literary composition and the fortunes of the age are linked in their underlying workings; a sage ruler and worthy ministers likewise fulfill their Way through mutual assistance. Surveying past and present, we find this invariably so. Ah, how splendid! In this age of flourishing literary culture, how fortunate are scholars who gain advancement through their writing! Could they yet bear to betray the Way of mutual assistance?

“Since our imperial ancestors founded the realm, they have examined antiquity and honored letters. The Way has flourished, and their transforming influence has spread everywhere, for one hundred and eighty years now. And coming to …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
我
皇上益光世德豐芑之澤旣厚且
長肆薄海內外熏烝涵沛無
遠弗屆惟玆閩粤去
京師五千餘里爲海隅之邦方
今聲名文物視東南諸郡不
少讓此豈偶然蓋成之者遠
===
也况士之生玆服也連山鉅
海厚儲秀發精英之不可秘
者自鍾爲名世之才且吾道
之南肇自龜山而紫陽因之
結社師友淵源文獻足徴焉
詩稱申甫之生本於崧岳傳
云鄒魯多禮義之俗則諸士
punctuated: 我皇上益光世德，豐芑之澤旣厚且長，肆薄海內外，熏烝涵沛，無遠弗屆。惟玆閩粤，去京師五千餘里，爲海隅之邦，方今聲名文物，視東南諸郡不少讓。此豈偶然？蓋成之者遠也。况士之生玆服也，連山鉅海，厚儲秀發，精英之不可秘者，自鍾爲名世之才。且吾道之南，肇自龜山，而紫陽因之，結社師友，淵源文獻足徴焉。詩稱申甫之生本於崧岳，傳云鄒魯多禮義之俗，則諸士
translation_en:
…our Emperor has further glorified the virtue of his forebears. His bounty in nurturing talent, like luxuriant millet, has been both profound and enduring. Thus, throughout the realm and beyond, his transforming influence permeates and nourishes all; no place is too distant for it to reach. This land of Minyue lies more than five thousand li from the capital, in a corner beside the sea. Yet today its renown, literary culture, and institutions yield little to those of the other prefectures of the southeast. Could this be mere chance? What has brought this about has deep roots.

Moreover, for scholars born in this region, its mountain ranges and vast seas richly store and splendidly manifest their finest essences. These essences cannot remain hidden: they naturally concentrate in talents who win renown in their age. Furthermore, the southward transmission of our Way began with Guishan, and Ziyang carried it forward. They formed scholarly associations as teachers and friends; the lineage of this tradition is amply attested by writings and worthy men. The Book of Odes traces the birth of Shen and Fu to the lofty sacred mountain, while the commentary says that Zou and Lu abound in customs of ritual propriety and righteousness. Thus, these scholars…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之所以鍾靈山海而景行先
哲者又當倍於他邦宏之濫
玆役也獲縱觀諸士之作皆
能以文鳴世悉古今名物之
變嚴義利名實之防發道德
性命之蘊而又隱然有忠
君愛
===
國之思以此措之躬行發揮于
事業夫豈無益於
國者雖然宏猶有懼焉士之仕
也由此其始進臣子之以人
事
君也寔闗効忠之大自鄉舉里選
之法不可復而科目之制興
punctuated: 之所以鍾靈山海而景行先哲者，又當倍於他邦。宏之濫玆役也，獲縱觀諸士之作，皆能以文鳴世，悉古今名物之變，嚴義利名實之防，發道德性命之蘊，而又隱然有忠君愛國之思。以此措之躬行，發揮于事業，夫豈無益於國者？雖然，宏猶有懼焉。士之仕也，由此其始進；臣子之以人事君也，寔闗効忠之大。自鄉舉里選之法不可復，而科目之制興
translation_en:
…their drawing upon the spiritual essence of the mountains and seas and emulating the worthy conduct of earlier sages should thus be doubly evident compared with men of other regions. Having undeservedly undertaken this duty, I, Hong, have been able to survey the candidates’ writings. All are capable of winning renown through their literary accomplishments: they comprehend changes in names and things from antiquity to the present, rigorously maintain the distinctions between righteousness and profit and between name and reality, and bring forth the profound meanings of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny. Moreover, underlying their work is a concern for loyalty to the ruler and love of the realm. If they put this into personal practice and give it expression in their public undertakings, how could it fail to benefit the realm?

Nevertheless, I still have misgivings. It is through this examination that scholars first advance toward official service; and for a subject to serve his ruler by providing him with worthy men is indeed a matter of great consequence in fulfilling his loyalty. Since the system of recommending men from districts and selecting them from villages could no longer be restored, and the system of examinations arose…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
不得已乃求之言語文字之
間以循辨論官材之典但靜
言庸違古聖賢之所深戒有
司者得無以是爲懼乎譬之
種木者求用於數十年之後
其培植長養無所不至固以
其爲梗楩杞梓可以登於用
===
也
國家之所望於士者亦然有司
者持尺寸而度之謂其爲有
用之材也而舉之於是乎宴
之鹿鳴優以計偕貢之
天子之廷方以遠且大者期之也
□□特以言自售矣乃或視
punctuated:
不得已，乃求之言語文字之間，以循辨論官材之典。但靜言庸違，古聖賢之所深戒，有司者得無以是爲懼乎？譬之種木者，求用於數十年之後，其培植長養，無所不至，固以其爲梗楩杞梓，可以登於用也。
國家之所望於士者亦然。有司者持尺寸而度之，謂其爲有用之材也，而舉之。於是乎宴之鹿鳴，優以計偕，貢之天子之廷，方以遠且大者期之也。□□特以言自售矣，乃或視
translation_en:
…With no alternative, one therefore seeks talent through speech and writing, following the established practice of distinguishing and assessing men’s fitness for office. Yet fine words followed by contrary conduct were precisely what the ancient sages and worthies sternly warned against. Can the responsible officials fail to be apprehensive about this? Consider someone planting trees for use several decades later: he spares no effort in cultivating and nurturing them, precisely because he regards them as geng [?], pian, qi, and zi trees that can eventually furnish useful timber.
The state’s expectations of scholars are likewise. The responsible officials measure them against their standards, judge them to be useful timber, and recommend them. They then entertain them at the Deer Cry banquet, honor them by providing for their journey to the capital, and present them at the Son of Heaven’s court, expecting achievements of far-reaching and great consequence. [Two illegible characters] merely to promote oneself through words [?]; yet some may regard …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
□惰而繼焉自廢繩墨舉
平生之所學與今日之所言
者如筌蹄然而甘心棄之則
所求非所望有司者之掄材
是亦罔也已
國家亦何賴於士而若是其崇
重之也亦豈忠義之士所以
===
自處者乎詩曰周王壽考遐
不作人君道也又曰濟濟多
士文王以寧臣道也此君臣
相成之義也我
皇上嗣大歷服方膺
皇天眷命於億萬年之久則作人
□無疆惟休今兹彙征
punctuated:
□惰而繼焉，自廢繩墨，舉平生之所學與今日之所言者，如筌蹄然而甘心棄之，則所求非所望，有司者之掄材，是亦罔也已。國家亦何賴於士，而若是其崇重之也？亦豈忠義之士所以自處者乎？
詩曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」君道也。又曰：「濟濟多士，文王以寧。」臣道也。此君臣相成之義也。我皇上嗣大歷服，方膺皇天眷命於億萬年之久，則作人□無疆惟休。今兹彙征
translation_en:
…and indolence follows [?]. They themselves discard the guiding rules, willingly casting aside everything they have learned throughout their lives and everything they have said today, as though these were fish traps and rabbit snares whose purpose had been served. Then what they seek is not what was expected of them, and the responsible officials’ selection of talent amounts to deception. What reliance could the state place upon such scholars, that it should honor and esteem them so highly? Could this be how scholars of loyalty and righteousness ought to conduct themselves?
The Book of Odes says: “May the king of Zhou enjoy long life; why should he not nurture men of talent?” This is the way of the ruler. It also says: “Numerous were the worthy men; through them King Wen enjoyed tranquility.” This is the way of the minister. Here lies the principle by which ruler and ministers bring one another to fulfillment. Our Emperor has succeeded to the great and enduring imperial charge and now receives August Heaven’s favor and mandate for countless millions of years; thus his nurturing of talent [illegible] brings boundless glory [?]. Now, those advancing together…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
□被於久道之化蓋亦
有年明於服勤之義得無有
感激而思報者乎得無有効
疏附先後奔走禦侮之勞以
爲
國之楨榦者乎由玆道也以勵
臣節以煕庶工以弼成悠久
===
無疆之治則今日諸士之進
豈徒以文名而已
國家養士之意
君臣相須之義均之無負也已而
理學之傳且益徵此邦之有
人有司者不將藉以爲榮乎
望二三子者其相與□
punctuated: □被於久道之化，蓋亦有年。明於服勤之義，得無有感激而思報者乎？得無有効疏附、先後、奔走、禦侮之勞，以爲國之楨榦者乎？由玆道也，以勵臣節，以煕庶工，以弼成悠久無疆之治，則今日諸士之進，豈徒以文名而已？國家養士之意、君臣相須之義，均之無負也已。而理學之傳，且益徵此邦之有人。有司者不將藉以爲榮乎？望二三子者，其相與□
translation_en: …[?] have received the transforming influence of enduring governance for many years. Understanding the duty of diligent service, could they fail to feel grateful and think of repaying it? Could they fail to devote their efforts to drawing others into allegiance, giving guidance and support, carrying out tasks, and resisting affronts, thereby becoming pillars of the state? Following this path, they will strengthen their integrity as ministers, bring distinction to the many offices, and help achieve enduring governance without limit. Would the advancement of these scholars today then amount merely to literary renown? Neither the state's intention in nurturing scholars nor the duty of mutual reliance between ruler and ministers would go unfulfilled. Moreover, the transmission of the Learning of Principle will further attest that this region has men of worth. Will the responsible officials not take pride in this? My hope for you gentlemen is that together you will [?]…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
廣西梧州府蒼梧縣儒學教
諭黃宏謹序
punctuated: 廣西梧州府蒼梧縣儒學教諭黃宏謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully written by Huang Hong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Cangwu County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
國家以經術得人之盛垂百八
十餘年矧我
皇上中興昌運文武徵才功施
社稷猶足多者乃歲壬子又大比
福建巡按御史曾佩寔司監
臨焉乃率稽
===
制典貞肅矩度事事惟謹維時御
史趙孔昭適被
命當代未及至佩乃豫僉謀諸清
戎御史沈寵暨藩臬諸臣左
布政使岑萬等用聘儒官列
司校藝時則以敎諭文暨黃
宏主考試敎授簡嚴莫遺賢
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

國家以經術得人之盛，垂百八十餘年。矧我皇上中興昌運，文武徵才，功施社稷猶足多者。乃歲壬子，又大比。福建巡按御史曾佩寔司監臨焉，乃率稽制典，貞肅矩度，事事惟謹。維時御史趙孔昭適被命當代，未及至，佩乃豫僉謀諸清戎御史沈寵暨藩臬諸臣、左布政使岑萬等，用聘儒官列司校藝。時則以敎諭文暨、黃宏主考試，敎授簡嚴、莫遺賢、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

The state's flourishing recruitment of worthy men through classical learning has continued for over a hundred and eighty years. How much more glorious under our Emperor, whose auspicious reign has brought a restoration: he summons men of talent for civil and military service, and their contributions to the altars of soil and grain are indeed worthy of praise.

In the renzi year [1552], the triennial examination was again held. Zeng Pei, Regional Inspector of Fujian, served as Supervising Official. He consulted the established regulations, maintained strict standards, and attended cautiously to every matter. At this time, Censor Zhao Kongzhao had received orders to replace him but had not yet arrived. Pei therefore consulted in advance with Shen Chong, the Censor responsible for reviewing military affairs, and with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, including Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Cen Wan. They engaged educational officials to serve in the various posts assessing the candidates' compositions. The Instructors Wen Ji and Huang Hong presided as Examiners; the Professors Jian Yan and Mo Yixian …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
學正彭標敎諭鄺夢琰冀藎
臣安憲張邦禮龍慶雲羅見
麟爲同考試提調則右布政
使朱鴻漸右參政丁以忠監
試則按察使范欽僉事黎澄
百執事咸備乃齋惕一心如
期鑰院矢諸神明祈得眞才
===
仰副我
皇上作人盛心內外規畫旣飭乃
合提學副使朱衡所簡士三
千有奇三試之得中式九十
人遵
制額也錄名氏倂文以
獻旣竣事咸謂得人文乃作而
punctuated: 學正彭標，敎諭鄺夢琰、冀藎臣、安憲、張邦禮、龍慶雲、羅見麟，爲同考試。提調則右布政使朱鴻漸、右參政丁以忠；監試則按察使范欽、僉事黎澄。百執事咸備，乃齋惕一心，如期鑰院，矢諸神明，祈得眞才，仰副我皇上作人盛心。內外規畫旣飭，乃合提學副使朱衡所簡士三千有奇，三試之，得中式九十人，遵制額也。錄名氏倂文以獻。旣竣事，咸謂得人，文乃作而
translation_en:
…Peng Biao, a subprefectural school instructor, and Kuang Mengyan, Ji Jinchen, An Xian, Zhang Bangli, Long Qingyun, and Luo Jianlin, county school instructors, served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhu Hongjian and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Ding Yizhong. The examination monitors were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Fan Qin and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Li Cheng. With all the functionaries in place, they purified themselves and, united in reverent vigilance, locked the examination compound on the appointed date. They swore before the deities, praying to obtain men of genuine talent and thereby fulfill His Majesty’s ardent desire to cultivate worthy men.
Once arrangements inside and outside the compound had been put in order, they assembled the more than three thousand candidates selected by Zhu Heng, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner supervising education, and examined them in three sessions. Ninety candidates passed, in accordance with the prescribed quota. Their names, together with their examination essays, were recorded for presentation to the throne. When the work was completed, all agreed that worthy men had been obtained. Wen then rose and…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
言曰猗歟休哉其
聖化之徵乎詩不云乎周王壽考
遐不作人又不云乎勉勉我
王綱紀四方蓋非綱紀無以
成作人之功非壽考無以運
勉勉之化恭惟我
皇上致理作人已逾三紀于茲
===
道久化成所謂壽考作人不於
今日欣逢哉夫天之生材也毓靈
者地際會者時振作裁成者
化閩東南隩區也介在山海
間諦見其山崇巒削璧巉巖
嵯峍厥色蒼蒼厥氣沃沃端
若拱峙若立無幻形無晦象
punctuated: 言曰：「猗歟，休哉！其聖化之徵乎？詩不云乎：『周王壽考，遐不作人。』又不云乎：『勉勉我王，綱紀四方。』蓋非綱紀，無以成作人之功；非壽考，無以運勉勉之化。恭惟我皇上致理作人，已逾三紀于茲，道久化成，所謂壽考作人，不於今日欣逢哉？夫天之生材也，毓靈者地，際會者時，振作裁成者化。閩，東南隩區也，介在山海間。諦見其山，崇巒削璧，巉巖嵯峍，厥色蒼蒼，厥氣沃沃，端若拱峙若立，無幻形，無晦象。
translation_en:
…and said: “Ah, how splendid! Is this not evidence of the sage sovereign’s transforming influence? Does not the Book of Odes say, ‘May the king of Zhou enjoy longevity; does he not nurture men?’ And does it not also say, ‘Diligently our king orders the four quarters’? Without such ordering, the work of nurturing men cannot be accomplished; without longevity, this diligent transforming influence cannot be sustained. We reverently reflect that our Emperor has brought about good government and nurtured men for more than three twelve-year cycles now. His Way has endured, and its transforming influence has reached fruition. Are we not fortunate today to encounter what is meant by ‘longevity and the nurturing of men’?

“When Heaven brings forth talent, the earth nurtures its spiritual potency, the times provide the occasion for its emergence, and moral transformation rouses and shapes it. Min is a sheltered region of the southeast, situated between mountains and sea. Look closely at its mountains: towering peaks, sheer jade-like walls, craggy rocks rising steeply; their hue is deep green, their vital energy abundant. Upright, they seem to stand with hands clasped in reverence, firmly poised; their forms show no deceptive transformations, their appearance no obscurity.…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
維岳降神閩其有焉又見夫
海也瀦之百川洩之尾閭狂
瀾滔滔漫渰萬頃不盈不虚
故觀海者難爲水南越之大
觀以之地靈則人傑况際此
唐虞亨嘉之會濟之
聖化振德之功久之以
===
敬一漸漬之澤則人文丕著又當
何如天下皆爾豈獨閩焉已
哉是故羅之科目試之經術
若不足盡天下士然自
列聖以來迄
今道德功業文章宗工鉅儒所以
彌綸叅賛者世不乏人而後
punctuated: 維岳降神，閩其有焉。又見夫海也，瀦之百川，洩之尾閭，狂瀾滔滔，漫渰萬頃，不盈不虚。故觀海者難爲水，南越之大觀以之。地靈則人傑，况際此唐虞亨嘉之會，濟之聖化振德之功，久之以敬一漸漬之澤，則人文丕著，又當何如？天下皆爾，豈獨閩焉已哉！是故羅之科目，試之經術，若不足盡天下士。然自列聖以來迄今，道德、功業、文章，宗工鉅儒，所以彌綸叅賛者，世不乏人，而後
translation_en:
“The lofty mountains sent down divine spirits”: Fujian surely possesses this blessing. Consider also the sea: the hundred rivers fill it, and the Tail Sluice drains it; its mighty billows surge, spreading over ten thousand qing, yet it neither overflows nor runs empty. Thus, one who has beheld the sea finds other waters wanting; through it, Nanyue possesses a magnificent spectacle. Where the land is numinous, its people are outstanding. Moreover, encountering this auspicious convergence, like the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, aided by the achievements of the sage emperor’s transforming influence in fostering virtue, and long steeped in the beneficence of “reverent single-mindedness” (jingyi), how splendidly must cultural accomplishment flourish! This holds throughout the realm; how could it apply to Fujian alone?
Thus, gathering men through the examination categories and testing them in classical learning might seem insufficient to encompass all the realm’s scholars. Yet from the successive sage emperors down to the present, no age has lacked eminent masters and great Confucian scholars whose moral virtue, achievements, and literary accomplishments have served to order all things and assist the work of transformation. Only then…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
知我
國家經術取人之典超往古獨
隆其得人之盛獨羨今爲尤
烈也夫人
天地之紀也山川之秀也而徵之
文者又治化之象也是故文
等盡得取三試之士之文而
===
覽之于疏通不泥者見其才
于脉絡粲然者見其智于冲
乎虛恢乎有容蘊涵不露者
見其量于嚴以正峭以拔挺
乎不蝓鏘鏘乎若金石聲者
見其節於是又喟然嘆曰美
哉矯乎渢渢乎澤澤乎眞人
punctuated:
知我國家經術取人之典，超往古獨隆，其得人之盛，獨羨今爲尤烈也。
夫人，天地之紀也，山川之秀也，而徵之文者，又治化之象也。是故文等盡得取三試之士之文而覽之：于疏通不泥者見其才，于脉絡粲然者見其智，于冲乎虛、恢乎有容、蘊涵不露者見其量，于嚴以正、峭以拔、挺乎不蝓、鏘鏘乎若金石聲者見其節。於是又喟然嘆曰：「美哉！矯乎！渢渢乎！澤澤乎！眞人
translation_en:
…we recognize that our dynasty’s institution of selecting men through their mastery of the Classics surpasses antiquity in its unique eminence, and that its abundant success in obtaining worthy men is especially outstanding today [?].
Human beings are the ordering thread of Heaven and Earth and the finest essence of mountains and rivers; what manifests itself in their writing is also an image of governance and moral transformation. Thus Wen and his colleagues were able to obtain and examine all the candidates’ writings from the three examination sessions. In writing that was lucid and untrammeled, they perceived talent; in clearly articulated connections, intelligence; in serene openness, expansive receptiveness, and depth held without display, breadth of character; and in stern rectitude, lofty distinction, uprightness without wavering [?], and resonance like that of bronze and stone, moral integrity. Then they sighed in admiration once more: “How beautiful! How vigorous! How rich in resonance! How lustrous! Truly human…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
文也哉蘊之爲道德行之爲
功業發揮之爲文章閩之人
文始信不獨古昔盛而已謂
非日海岳之孕泄也誣乎今
夫南山之石巖巖然有節之
道焉中流之柱琅琅然疏達
以應有才之道焉若納百川
===
而無不容者有量之道焉若
虛明鑒照流動不滓者有智
之道焉合是而毓靈于人斯
弘毅合德任重器也剛大並
用配義功也虛直應物中正
道也則夫秉衷履正知方達
權靜以定躁廣以去隘明以
punctuated: 文也哉！蘊之爲道德，行之爲功業，發揮之爲文章。閩之人文，始信不獨古昔盛而已。謂非日海岳之孕泄也，誣乎！今夫南山之石，巖巖然，有節之道焉；中流之柱，琅琅然，疏達以應，有才之道焉；若納百川而無不容者，有量之道焉；若虛明鑒照，流動不滓者，有智之道焉。合是而毓靈于人，斯弘毅合德，任重器也；剛大並用，配義功也；虛直應物，中正道也。則夫秉衷履正，知方達權，靜以定躁，廣以去隘，明以
translation_en: …cultural brilliance indeed! Held within, it constitutes moral virtue; put into practice, it becomes achievement; expressed fully, it becomes literary composition. Only now do I truly believe that the cultural brilliance of Fujian flourished not merely in antiquity. To deny that it is daily nurtured and brought forth by the seas and mountains [?] would be false indeed! Consider the towering rocks of the southern mountains: in them lies the principle of integrity. The pillar amid the current, resounding clearly and responding freely, embodies the principle of talent. That which receives the hundred rivers, accommodating them all, embodies the principle of magnanimity. That which is empty and luminous, reflecting and illuminating, flowing without becoming sullied, embodies the principle of wisdom. When these qualities unite to nurture spiritual excellence in people, breadth of spirit and resolve combine in virtue, making them vessels capable of bearing heavy responsibilities; strength and greatness operate together, producing achievements consonant with righteousness; openness and uprightness respond to things, constituting the Way of balance and rectitude. Thus, holding fast to their innate moral nature and treading the path of rectitude, knowing fixed principles and understanding judicious adaptation, they use stillness to steady agitation, breadth to dispel narrowness, and illumination to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
疏窒皆文之昭也化之著也
而文武之眞才咸可胥此焉
出矣豈直曰抱藝多士濟濟
然巳乎哉于是見我
聖人綱紀作人之化博以厚矣高
以明矣悠久無疆矣其眞謂
與
===
天無極者乎堯曰放勳光被四表
格于上下禹告成功聲敎訖
于四海於戲此我
國家經術得人于是益盛而爲
我
社稷永賴其有旣哉是舉也提督
軍務右副都御史張烜遹觀
punctuated:
疏窒，皆文之昭也，化之著也，而文武之眞才咸可胥此焉出矣。豈直曰抱藝多士濟濟然巳乎哉？于是見我聖人綱紀作人之化，博以厚矣，高以明矣，悠久無疆矣。其眞謂與天無極者乎！堯曰：「放勳，光被四表，格于上下。」禹告成功，聲敎訖于四海。於戲！此我國家經術得人，于是益盛，而爲我社稷永賴，其有旣哉！
是舉也，提督軍務右副都御史張烜遹觀
translation_en:
…to clear away obstructions—all these manifest cultural refinement and make its transforming influence evident. Genuine talents for both civil and military affairs can all emerge from this. Could it mean merely that numerous accomplished scholars are gathered in impressive ranks? Here we see that our sage sovereign’s transforming work of ordering society and nurturing men is broad and profound, lofty and illuminating, enduring without limit. May it truly be called as boundless as Heaven itself! Of Yao it is said: “His achievement was vast; his radiance extended to the four quarters and reached above and below.” Yu announced the completion of his work, and his civilizing influence reached throughout the Four Seas. Ah! Our state’s recruitment of worthy men through classical learning thus flourishes ever more greatly. Could there be any end to the lasting support they provide for our altars of soil and grain?
For this examination, Zhang Xuan, Superintendent of Military Affairs and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, proceeded to observe…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
厥成左參政汪宗元按察副
使汪俅馮璋僉事張恕汪垍
均範理於外行都司都指揮
僉事張悰署都指揮僉事顧
邦重代都指揮田耕事綜撥
軍士焉副使萬虞愷左參議
熊洛都指揮范德榮行都司
===
都指揮僉事劉敕皆預期入
賀右布政使曾鈞談愷按察使
王昺左參政王璣左參議吳
源俱後先以遷秩行先是刑
部郎中陸穩以訊錄至工部
郎中張祥戶部郎中周載皆
以督賦至咸事事境內樂觀
punctuated: 厥成。左參政汪宗元、按察副使汪俅、馮璋、僉事張恕、汪垍，均範理於外。行都司都指揮僉事張悰、署都指揮僉事顧邦重代都指揮田耕事，綜撥軍士焉。副使萬虞愷、左參議熊洛、都指揮范德榮、行都司都指揮僉事劉敕，皆預期入賀。右布政使曾鈞、談愷、按察使王昺、左參政王璣、左參議吳源，俱後先以遷秩行。先是，刑部郎中陸穩以訊錄至，工部郎中張祥、戶部郎中周載皆以督賦至，咸事事境內，樂觀
translation_en:
…its successful completion. Wang Zongyuan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Wang Qiu and Feng Zhang, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Zhang Shu and Wang Ji, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, all oversaw arrangements outside the examination compound. Zhang Cong, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner of the Branch Regional Military Commission, and Gu Bangzhong, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, who deputized for Regional Military Commissioner Tian Geng, coordinated the deployment of soldiers. Wan Yukai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Xiong Luo, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Fan Derong, Regional Military Commissioner; and Liu Chi, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner of the Branch Regional Military Commission, all came in advance of the appointed date to offer congratulations. Zeng Jun and Tan Kai, Right Provincial Administration Commissioners; Wang Bing, Surveillance Commissioner; Wang Ji, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; and Wu Yuan, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner, departed at various times upon promotion.

Previously, Lu Wen, a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, had arrived to review criminal cases. Zhang Xiang, a bureau director in the Ministry of Works, and Zhou Zai, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, had both arrived to supervise tax collection. All were attending to official business within the province and delighted in witnessing…

text:
人才之盛者亦例得書云
山東兗州府東平州平陰縣
儒學教諭朱文謹序
punctuated:
人才之盛者，亦例得書云。
山東兗州府東平州平陰縣儒學教諭朱文謹序。
translation_en:

Preface by Zhu Wenjin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Pingyin County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之教誠則明矣
明則誠矣
堯舜之道孝弟而已矣
易
文明以健中正而應君子正也唯君子爲
能通天下之志
===
聖人感人心而天下和平
易簡之善配至德
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
慎厥身脩思永惇敘九族庶明勵翼邇可
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。

自誠明謂之性，自明誠謂之教。誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

堯舜之道，孝弟而已矣。

易

文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子爲能通天下之志。

聖人感人心，而天下和平。

易簡之善，配至德。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書

慎厥身，脩思永，惇敘九族，庶明勵翼，邇可
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master skillfully guides people forward step by step. He broadens my learning through culture and restrains me through ritual propriety.

To proceed from sincerity to understanding is called nature; to proceed from understanding to sincerity is called instruction. With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.

The Way of Yao and Shun consists simply in filial piety and respect for elder brothers.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Cultured and enlightened, yet strong; central and correct, with a corresponding response: this is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.

The sage moves people's hearts, and all under Heaven attain peace and harmony.

The goodness of ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.

When the sages of antiquity made the Changes, they intended thereby to follow the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firmness, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin from yang and employed yielding and firm lines alternately; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents (Shu)

Be watchful over your own conduct; in cultivating yourself, consider the long term. Generously maintain the proper order among the nine degrees of kinship, and let the assembled enlightened men diligently assist you. What is near may …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
遠在兹
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
六三德一曰正直二曰剛克三曰柔克平
康正直疆弗友剛克燮友柔克沉潜剛
克高明柔克
我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷歷
年
詩
===
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除
俾爾多益以莫不庶
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽考遐不作人
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四
方
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕公
punctuated:
遠在兹。

若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。

六、三德：一曰正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。平康，正直；疆弗友，剛克；燮友，柔克；沉潜，剛克；高明，柔克。

我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷年。

詩

赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。

天保定爾，亦孔之固。俾爾單厚，何福不除？俾爾多益，以莫不庶。

倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？

追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。

莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王。

春秋

秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕公
translation_en:
…extending to those far away depends upon this.

If I am metal, I shall use you as my whetstone; if I cross a great river, I shall use you as my boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I shall use you as my soaking rain.

Sixth, the three virtues: the first is uprightness, the second mastery through firmness, and the third mastery through gentleness. In peace and tranquility, employ uprightness; against the strong and unfriendly, mastery through firmness; toward the harmonious and friendly, mastery through gentleness. For the retiring and reserved, employ mastery through firmness; for the lofty and assertive, mastery through gentleness.

I have received Heaven’s mandate. May our years grandly match those of Xia, and may they not fall short of those of Yin.

Book of Odes

Valiant are the warriors, the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.

Heaven protects and establishes you, making you exceedingly secure. It grants you abundance: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you ever greater increase, so that nothing fails to flourish.

Brilliant is that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in the heavens. The king of Zhou enjoys long life; does he not nurture men of worth?

Carved and polished is his patterned refinement; gold and jade are his substance. Tirelessly our king orders and governs the four quarters.

None dares fail to come to present offerings; none dares fail to come to acknowledge the king.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The duke…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕
季子來歸〔閔公元年〕公子慶父出奔莒〔閔〕
〔公二年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷齊人來
歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕

沈沈潰〔文公三年〕

孫會自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
===
禮記
善教者使人繼其志其言也約而達微而
臧罕譬而喻可謂繼志矣
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
仁者仁此者也禮者履此者也義者宜此
者也信者信此者也强者强此者也
punctuated:
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
季子來歸。〔閔公元年〕公子慶父出奔莒。〔閔〕〔公二年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔定公十年〕
叔孫得臣會晉人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人伐沈，沈潰。〔文公三年〕
吳子使札來聘。〔襄公二十有九年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕

禮記
善教者使人繼其志，其言也約而達，微而臧，罕譬而喻，可謂繼志矣。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神，如此則四海之內合敬同愛矣。
仁者仁此者也，禮者履此者也，義者宜此者也，信者信此者也，强者强此者也。
translation_en:
… joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
Jizi returned. 〔First year of Duke Min.〕 Prince Qingfu fled to Ju. 〔Second year of Duke Min.〕 In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The people of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Shusun Dechen joined men of Jin, Song, Chen, Wei, and Zheng in attacking Shen. Shen collapsed. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕
The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites
One who teaches well enables others to carry forward his intentions. His words are concise yet convey their meaning, subtle yet excellent; he uses few illustrations yet makes himself understood. This may be called enabling others to carry forward his intentions.
Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares their ordered rhythms. Through harmony, the myriad things retain their proper places; through ordered rhythms, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the visible realm there are ritual and music; in the unseen realm there are ghosts and spirits. Thus, within the Four Seas, all unite in reverence and share in love.
The benevolent are those who express benevolence through this; the ritually proper are those who put this into practice; the righteous are those who accord with this; the trustworthy are those who are faithful to this; the strong are those who persevere in this.

text:
君子力此二者以南面而立夫是以天下
太平也

君子力此二者，以南面而立，夫是以天下太平也。

translation_en:
The gentleman devotes himself to these two things and takes his place facing south as ruler; thus all under Heaven enjoys great peace.

Second Session

Discourse:
“When the gentleman acts, he serves for generations as a guide to all under Heaven.”

One question from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?]:
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor ordering the highest ministers, ministers, and grand masters to follow the Monthly Ordinances for the four seasons. Second year of Yangshuo [23 BCE].
Compose a Tang proclamation conferring on Fang Xuanling, Vice Director of the Left, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Thirteenth year of Zhenguan [639].
Compose a memorial in which the assembled officials give thanks for being granted the Collected Memorials of Famous Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi). Fourteenth year of Yongle [1416].

Five legal judgments:
Rendering judgments and signing official case documents on behalf of fellow officials.
Discarding or destroying implements, crops, and the like.
Marriages involving Mongols and Semu people.
The prohibition against employing persons previously sentenced as palace guards.
False accusations that would entail military exile or compulsory relocation.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第參塲
策五道
問古帝王所以建極敷錫保乂流行者非
可襲取爲之也稽諸堯舜三代典謨訓
誥具有明徵漢以下英君誼辟其所建
立與所表章非不欲法於天下傳之後
世以垂休光然端本善則之要槩乎未
之有聞此所以治安小康視光明俊偉
之業不侔殆亦有由然者我
===
太祖高皇帝
龍飛淮甸汛掃胡元肇建開闢以來所未有
之勳業其
嘉言善行神謀懿範見於日曆之所序載
聖政記之所頌述者旣詳且明不知盡能揄揚
否抑此外別有可言者與我
皇上受
天明命丕振
中興即位以來功德並懋所以經緯天地而
punctuated:
第參塲
策五道

問：古帝王所以建極敷錫、保乂流行者，非可襲取爲之也。稽諸堯舜三代典謨訓誥，具有明徵。漢以下英君誼辟，其所建立與所表章，非不欲法於天下、傳之後世，以垂休光。然端本善則之要，槩乎未之有聞。此所以治安小康，視光明俊偉之業不侔，殆亦有由然者。我太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，汛掃胡元，肇建開闢以來所未有之勳業。其嘉言善行、神謀懿範，見於日曆之所序載、聖政記之所頌述者，旣詳且明，不知盡能揄揚否？抑此外別有可言者與？我皇上受天明命，丕振中興，即位以來，功德並懋，所以經緯天地而
translation_en:
Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The means by which the ancient emperors and kings established the supreme standard and broadly bestowed its blessings, secured orderly government, and extended its influence could not be attained through mere imitation. Examining the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties, we find clear evidence of this throughout. From the Han onward, enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns, in what they established and what they honored and made manifest, certainly wished to provide models for all under Heaven and transmit them to later generations, leaving behind an illustrious legacy. Yet scarcely anything has been heard of their grasping the essentials of rectifying the foundations and making the standards good. There must indeed be reasons why their peaceful government and modest prosperity did not equal those luminous and outstanding achievements.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao rose like a dragon in the lands along the Huai, swept away the alien Yuan, and founded an enterprise unmatched since the beginning of the world. His admirable words and virtuous deeds, inspired plans and exemplary models, are recorded in the Daily Calendar (Rili) and celebrated in the Record of Sagely Government (Shengzheng ji), in accounts both detailed and clear. Have these fully extolled them, or is there more to be said beyond these accounts?

Our reigning emperor received Heaven’s illustrious mandate and brought about a great resurgence. Since his accession, his achievements and virtue have both flourished. The means by which he orders Heaven and Earth and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
昭回日月者誠足以克紹
烈祖而超出百王之上不知於日曆
聖政記諸書有脗合否抑淵源之地別有所自
與諸士子佩服
聖訓蓋已有年果能陳其梗槩而探其本原矣
乎實有司者之所願聞
問同律脩禮肇自舜典而五禮六樂之載
在周禮者尤悉焉自秦滅典籍至漢復
重明經惟樂書遂廢不講學者不過取
===
周官宗伯一篇與二戴所記誦習之而
已然以班固藝文志攷之是禮經非樂
也彼樂自爲六家今散佚不傳矣夫六
經之道如四時相須以成歲乃自漢以
來缺大樂而不求學者亦安之不復疑
豈理也哉宋時和胡阮李范馬劉楊諸
賢之議終不能以相一而其說亦可得
而聞歟迨至蔡元定旁搜冥契積之累
年著爲律呂新書文公稱其明白淵深
punctuated:
昭回日月者，誠足以克紹烈祖，而超出百王之上。不知於日曆、聖政記諸書有脗合否？抑淵源之地別有所自與？諸士子佩服聖訓，蓋已有年，果能陳其梗槩而探其本原矣乎？實有司者之所願聞。

問：同律脩禮，肇自舜典，而五禮六樂之載在周禮者尤悉焉。自秦滅典籍，至漢復重明經，惟樂書遂廢不講。學者不過取周官宗伯一篇與二戴所記，誦習之而已。然以班固藝文志攷之，是禮經，非樂也。彼樂自爲六家，今散佚不傳矣。夫六經之道，如四時相須以成歲，乃自漢以來，缺大樂而不求，學者亦安之，不復疑，豈理也哉？宋時和、胡、阮、李、范、馬、劉、楊諸賢之議，終不能以相一，而其說亦可得而聞歟？迨至蔡元定，旁搜冥契，積之累年，著爲律呂新書，文公稱其明白淵深
translation_en:
…and lend radiance to the sun and moon, truly suffice to carry forward the achievements of his illustrious ancestor and surpass the hundred kings. Do these accord with the accounts in the Daily Records, the Record of Sagely Governance, and other such books? Or do they derive from some other source? You examination candidates have taken the imperial instructions to heart for many years. Can you indeed set forth their broad outlines and explore their fundamental source? This is what we officials wish to hear.

Question: The unification of pitch standards and the ordering of ritual originated in the Canon of Shun; the Rites of Zhou records the five rites and six musical traditions in particular detail. After the Qin destroyed the canonical writings, the Han once again valued mastery of the Classics, yet the writings on music alone fell into neglect and were no longer studied. Scholars did no more than recite and study the section on the Minister of Rites in the Offices of Zhou and the records compiled by the two Dai. Yet if we examine Ban Gu’s Treatise on Literature, these belong to the ritual classics, not to music. Music itself comprised six textual traditions, now scattered and lost, no longer transmitted. The Way of the Six Classics is like the four seasons, which depend upon one another to complete the year. Yet since the Han, the great ceremonial music has been missing and no effort has been made to recover it; scholars, too, have accepted this without further question. Can this be reasonable? The views of the Song worthies He, Hu, Ruan, Li, Fan, Ma, Liu, and Yang never achieved agreement. Can you nevertheless explain their theories? Later, Cai Yuanding searched widely and attained profound insights, accumulating his findings over many years and composing the New Book of Pitch Standards. Lord Wen praised it as clear and profound…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
縝密通暢不爲牽合附會之談元定閩
產也今其書具在諸士子固甞誦說而
講求之可悉言其指要歟抑別有其說
歟夫追韶濩之正聲變鄭衞之餘習使
移風易俗不爲虛語必如之何而可
問氏族之學其來久矣三代以前氏族分
而爲二氏以別貴賤也而曰姓可呼爲
氏氏不可呼爲姓者何歟姓以別婚姻
也而氏曰姓不同姓曰氏不同者何歟
===
司馬子長劉知幾良史也而於姬旦姬
伯猶且昧焉則玆學湮晦可知矣以紀
傳所睹記者漢有官譜氏族篇萬姓譜
魏立九品置中正晉宋以後有百家譜
百官譜姓苑官氏志至唐則尤盛矣氏
族志大唐姓系錄衣冠開元永泰諸譜
而又有韻略韻譜姓纂姓解不知果有
裨於世教否乎叅之三代之法抑或有
同歟乃所稱三十二類四聲複姓之說
punctuated:
縝密通暢，不爲牽合附會之談。元定閩產也，今其書具在，諸士子固甞誦說而講求之，可悉言其指要歟？抑別有其說歟？夫追韶濩之正聲，變鄭衞之餘習，使移風易俗不爲虛語，必如之何而可？

問：氏族之學，其來久矣。三代以前，氏族分而爲二。氏以別貴賤也，而曰姓可呼爲氏，氏不可呼爲姓者，何歟？姓以別婚姻也，而氏曰姓不同，姓曰氏不同者，何歟？司馬子長、劉知幾，良史也，而於姬旦、姬伯猶且昧焉，則玆學湮晦可知矣。以紀傳所睹記者，漢有《官譜》《氏族篇》《萬姓譜》；魏立九品，置中正；晉宋以後，有《百家譜》《百官譜》《姓苑》《官氏志》；至唐則尤盛矣：《氏族志》《大唐姓系錄》，《衣冠》《開元》《永泰》諸譜，而又有《韻略》《韻譜》《姓纂》《姓解》。不知果有裨於世教否乎？叅之三代之法，抑或有同歟？乃所稱三十二類、四聲複姓之說，
translation_en:
…meticulous and coherent, without strained connections or forced interpretations. Yuanding was a native of Fujian. His book survives intact today, and you candidates have surely recited, discussed, and studied it. Can you set out its essential meaning fully? Or do you have some other explanation? How must one proceed to recover the correct sounds of the Shao and Huo music, transform the lingering musical habits of Zheng and Wei, and ensure that changing prevailing customs is more than empty talk?

Question: The study of clans and lineages has a long history. Before the end of the Three Dynasties, clan and lineage designations were divided into two categories. Clan names (shi) distinguished noble from base; why, then, is it said that a surname (xing) may be called a clan name, but a clan name may not be called a surname? Surnames distinguished those eligible to intermarry; what, then, is meant by saying, in relation to clan names, that surnames differ, and in relation to surnames, that clan names differ [?]? Sima Zichang and Liu Zhiji were accomplished historians, yet even they were unclear concerning Ji Dan and Ji Bo. From this we can see how obscure this field of learning had become. Among the works recorded in historical annals and biographies, the Han had Official Genealogies, Chapters on Clans and Lineages, and Genealogies of the Myriad Surnames. The Wei established the nine ranks and appointed Rectifiers. From the Jin and Song onward there were Genealogies of the Hundred Families, Genealogies of the Hundred Officials, Garden of Surnames, and Treatise on Official Clans. In the Tang, such works became especially abundant: the Treatise on Clans and Lineages, Record of Surname Lineages of the Great Tang, the genealogies entitled Caps and Girdles, Kaiyuan, and Yongtai, as well as the Outline Arranged by Rhymes, Genealogies Arranged by Rhymes, Compilation of Surnames, and Explanations of Surnames. Did these truly contribute to moral instruction in society? Compared with the institutions of the Three Dynasties, did they perhaps have something in common? As for the accounts of the so-called thirty-two categories and of compound surnames arranged by the four tones…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
抑又何歟玆欲俾千餘年湮源斷緒之
典燦然在目親上尊祖而安民定志之
道係焉諸士子講之素矣其何以復我
問人有言道勝者文不難而自至文與道
果有二乎六經無文法而天地之至文
歸之孔子曰文不在玆乎子貢稱夫子
之文章可得而聞其所言者何文也戰
國時以操術以騁辨以工言以作賦馳
驟於文苑者不知其幾也可指其人而
===
言之歟漢最盛矣賈陸董劉班馬其著
者嚴徐鄒枚司馬王楊之徒呟議小言
互相雄長抑豈盡無其實耶不然則響
隨人徂何以流傳至今也周情孔思詞
臻其妙然其論古人直以屈孟馬楊爲
一等是不免裂文與道而二之治出於
一之說似矣而其言曰我所謂文必與
道俱不識其文果澤於道耶夫上下數
千年間蓋所稱能文之士如斯而已而
punctuated:
抑又何歟？玆欲俾千餘年湮源斷緒之典燦然在目，親上尊祖而安民定志之道係焉。諸士子講之素矣，其何以復我？

問：人有言：「道勝者，文不難而自至。」文與道果有二乎？六經無文法，而天地之至文歸之。孔子曰：「文不在玆乎？」子貢稱：「夫子之文章，可得而聞。」其所言者何文也？戰國時，以操術、以騁辨、以工言、以作賦，馳驟於文苑者，不知其幾也。可指其人而言之歟？漢最盛矣，賈、陸、董、劉、班、馬，其著者；嚴、徐、鄒、枚、司馬、王、楊之徒，呟議小言，互相雄長，抑豈盡無其實耶？不然，則響隨人徂，何以流傳至今也？周情孔思，詞臻其妙，然其論古人，直以屈、孟、馬、楊爲一等，是不免裂文與道而二之。「治出於一」之說似矣，而其言曰：「我所謂文，必與道俱。」不識其文果澤於道耶？夫上下數千年間，蓋所稱能文之士如斯而已，而
translation_en:
…And what, moreover, were these? We now wish to bring clearly before our eyes the institutions whose sources have been obscured and whose continuity has been broken for more than a thousand years. Bound up with them is the way of cherishing superiors and honoring ancestors, thereby bringing peace to the people and stability to their aspirations. You candidates have long studied these matters; how will you answer me?

Question: Someone has said, “For one in whom the Way prevails, literary accomplishment comes of itself without difficulty.” Are literature and the Way really two separate things? The Six Classics have no rules of composition, yet the finest writing in heaven and earth is attributed to them. Confucius said, “Does not this cultural tradition reside here in me?” Zigong said, “The Master's cultural accomplishments can be heard.” What did they mean by this “culture” or “literature”? In the Warring States period, countless men ranged through the literary world by wielding techniques, displaying their powers of disputation, crafting their language, or composing rhapsodies. Can you identify these men and discuss them? Literature flourished most abundantly under the Han. Jia, Lu, Dong, Liu, Ban, and Ma were its outstanding figures. Men such as Yan, Xu, Zou, Mei, Sima, Wang, and Yang vied for supremacy in resonant discussions [?] and lesser writings. Could they all have been without substance? Otherwise, their echoes would have faded with their deaths: how could their works have been transmitted down to the present?

With the sentiments of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius, his language attained consummate excellence. Yet, in discussing the ancients, he simply placed Qu, Meng, Ma, and Yang in a single rank; this could hardly avoid splitting literature and the Way into two. The assertion that “good government proceeds from unity” seems sound, yet its author said, “What I call literature must always accompany the Way.” I wonder whether his writing was indeed nourished by the Way. Across several thousand years, those acclaimed as accomplished writers have apparently amounted only to men such as these, and…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
或謂宋之文不如唐唐不如漢漢不如
三代豈世變趨下而文亦因之乎不然
於數家之外將別有其人乎幸爲我折
衷其說
問聖人不言兵與利而容民畜衆聚人理
財自易發之然則屯田榷鹽亦經國之
要務也如屯金城而臨羌畏服屯斜谷
而百姓安堵屯襄陽而墾田八百行於
內地者足國安民行於外地者富邊實
===
塞似得寓兵於農之意矣管仲舉之而
齊國富強劉晏舉之而饟祿充裕盛度
舉之而公私咸賴取於海池者利足經
國取於井地者澤足濟民似因天地自
然之利矣行之於古輙有成效今閩之
要害皆有屯田居則爲農出則爲兵立
法非不善也而久則弊生遂失初制謂
之兵歟則非荷戈之士謂之民歟則非
授田之戶因屯興田不爲無實之虛文
punctuated:
或謂宋之文不如唐，唐不如漢，漢不如三代，豈世變趨下而文亦因之乎？不然，於數家之外，將別有其人乎？幸爲我折衷其說。

問：聖人不言兵與利，而容民畜衆、聚人理財，自易發之。然則屯田榷鹽，亦經國之要務也。如屯金城而臨羌畏服，屯斜谷而百姓安堵，屯襄陽而墾田八百，行於內地者足國安民，行於外地者富邊實塞，似得寓兵於農之意矣。管仲舉之而齊國富強，劉晏舉之而饟祿充裕，盛度舉之而公私咸賴，取於海池者利足經國，取於井地者澤足濟民，似因天地自然之利矣。行之於古，輙有成效。今閩之要害皆有屯田，居則爲農，出則爲兵，立法非不善也。而久則弊生，遂失初制。謂之兵歟，則非荷戈之士；謂之民歟，則非授田之戶。因屯興田，不爲無實之虛文
translation_en:
… Some say that the writings of the Song do not equal those of the Tang, those of the Tang do not equal those of the Han, and those of the Han do not equal those of the Three Dynasties. Could it be that, as the world changes and declines, writing follows it downward? If not, might there be other worthy writers beyond these few masters? Please weigh these views and resolve the matter for me.

Question: The sages did not speak of warfare and profit, yet accommodating the people and nurturing the multitude, gathering people together and managing wealth, are principles expounded in the Book of Changes. Thus military agricultural colonies and the salt monopoly are also essential affairs of statecraft. For example, establishing colonies at Jincheng brought the Qiang nearby into fearful submission [?]; establishing them at Xiegu allowed the common people to live securely; and establishing them at Xiangyang brought eight hundred [units of land?] under cultivation. Practiced in the interior, this system supplied the state and secured the people; practiced in outlying regions, it enriched the frontier and strengthened its defenses. It seems to have embodied the intention of integrating soldiers into the farming population.

When Guan Zhong instituted the salt monopoly, the state of Qi became rich and strong; when Liu Yan instituted it, military provisions and official salaries were amply supplied; when Sheng Du instituted it, both public and private interests benefited. Salt obtained from the sea and salt lakes yielded profits sufficient to sustain the state; salt obtained from wells yielded benefits sufficient to support the people. This seems to have made use of the natural bounty of Heaven and Earth. When these measures were implemented in antiquity, they consistently proved effective.

Today, military agricultural colonies exist at all strategic points in Fujian. At home their men are farmers; when they go forth, they are soldiers. The system as established was certainly sound. Over time, however, abuses arose, and its original arrangements were lost. If we call these men soldiers, they are not men who bear arms; if we call them commoners, they are not households allotted land. Has promoting cultivation through military colonies become an empty form without substance …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣乎閩之瀕海利於鹵鹽司之以官鬻
之以商生財非無道也而久則蠹生因
之極敝謂利在官歟則公無羨餘之積
謂利在商歟則市有折閱之憂計口稅
鹽不爲無名之征求乎今欲祛其弊端
得古人立法之意使公私並受其利抱
奇諸士必有能處之者
punctuated: 矣乎？閩之瀕海，利於鹵鹽，司之以官，鬻之以商，生財非無道也。而久則蠹生，因之極敝。謂利在官歟，則公無羨餘之積；謂利在商歟，則市有折閱之憂。計口稅鹽，不爲無名之征求乎？今欲祛其弊端，得古人立法之意，使公私並受其利，抱奇諸士必有能處之者。
translation_en: …has it not? Fujian’s coastal regions profit from salt made from brine. Officials administer it, and merchants sell it: there is certainly a means of generating revenue. Yet over time abuses have arisen, bringing the system into utter disrepair. If one says that the profit goes to the government, the public treasury has no accumulated surplus; if one says that the profit goes to the merchants, they face the prospect of selling at a loss. Does taxing salt according to the number of people not amount to an exaction without justification? We now wish to eliminate these abuses, recover the intent behind the institutions established by the ancients, and ensure that public and private interests alike benefit. Among you gentlemen of exceptional talent, there must be those who can devise a solution.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
黃星耀
同考試官教諭張批夫子平日教人不出乎此
惟顏子能體之子亦善體顏子者
同考試官教諭龔批此作渾然成章得博約致
一之旨錄之
考試官教諭黃批善發聖賢授受之蘊者
===
考試官教諭朱批典雅莊重
大賢嘆聖人之善教必述教之所以善焉夫文
以啟知禮以約行學之序也知博約之序則知
所以入道矣聖教斯所以爲善乎此顏子學旣
有得因嘆聖道之高妙而及其教也蓋曰不可
幾及者聖人之道固非示人以遠矣所可循者
聖人之教蓋確然示人以易矣何也夫道有所
由入强之則難功有所當加悖之則拂吾夫子
之教人也因其材而不强人以難能循其序亦
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。」
黃星耀

同考試官教諭張批：「夫子平日教人不出乎此，惟顏子能體之，子亦善體顏子者。」
同考試官教諭龔批：「此作渾然成章，得博約致一之旨，錄之。」
考試官教諭黃批：「善發聖賢授受之蘊者。」
考試官教諭朱批：「典雅莊重。」

大賢嘆聖人之善教，必述教之所以善焉。夫文以啟知，禮以約行，學之序也。知博約之序，則知所以入道矣。聖教斯所以爲善乎！此顏子學旣有得，因嘆聖道之高妙而及其教也。蓋曰：不可幾及者，聖人之道，固非示人以遠矣；所可循者，聖人之教，蓋確然示人以易矣。何也？夫道有所由入，强之則難；功有所當加，悖之則拂。吾夫子之教人也，因其材而不强人以難能，循其序亦
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The Master skillfully guides people onward step by step. He broadens me through cultural learning and disciplines me through ritual propriety.”
Huang Xingyao

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The Master’s everyday teaching never went beyond this. Only Master Yan could embody it; you, too, are adept at embodying Master Yan’s understanding.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor: “This composition forms a seamless whole and grasps the purport of bringing breadth of learning and discipline through ritual propriety into unity. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “A fine exposition of the profound meaning transmitted by the sage and received by the worthy.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Classically elegant, dignified, and weighty.”

When a great worthy praises the sage’s skill in teaching, he must explain what makes that teaching good. Cultural learning opens up understanding, while ritual propriety disciplines conduct: this is the proper sequence of learning. To understand the sequence of broadening and disciplining is to understand how to enter the Way. Is this not what makes the sage’s teaching good? Here Master Yan, having already gained something through learning, marvels at the loftiness and subtlety of the sage’s Way and then turns to his teaching. It is as though he says: The sage’s Way is something one can scarcely approach, yet he certainly does not present people with something remote. The sage’s teaching is something one can follow, and it assuredly shows people an accessible path. Why is this? There is a route by which to enter the Way; forcing progress makes it difficult. There are points at which effort should be applied; going against them brings obstruction. In teaching people, our Master follows their capacities without forcing upon them what they can hardly accomplish; he follows the proper sequence and also…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
不雜施而不遜何循循善誘如之蓋文以載道
非博知或失則隘矣夫子懼我之未博無以會
道之散殊也而先我以此焉使之或遠稽於文
獻之徵或廣求於事物之故學而知之多識於
前言往行以畜其德也默而識之知周於窮理
盡性求至于命也此則見聞博而所以豫吾入
道之基者在此不有夫子孰知文之當博也如
此哉禮以會道非約行或失則肆矣夫子懼我
之未約無以協道之中正也而繼我以此焉使
===
之或考祥於視履之旋或致審於用動之則範
我于皇極之門隨事觀理率履而不越也飭我
於嘉會之地因物察則範圍而不過也此則中
正履而所以要吾踐道之歸者在此不有夫子
又孰知禮之當約也如此哉夫先之文以始其
知則博文者致知之不可以已者也繼之禮以
約其行則約禮者力行之不可以已者也功以
漸加敎有定序此夫子之敎所以爲善而回之
由敎而入亦因是庶幾矣乎雖然二者之敎固
punctuated: 不雜施而不遜，何循循善誘如之！蓋文以載道，非博知，或失則隘矣。夫子懼我之未博，無以會道之散殊也，而先我以此焉。使之或遠稽於文獻之徵，或廣求於事物之故，學而知之，多識於前言往行，以畜其德也；默而識之，知周於窮理盡性，求至于命也。此則見聞博，而所以豫吾入道之基者在此。不有夫子，孰知文之當博也如此哉！禮以會道，非約行，或失則肆矣。夫子懼我之未約，無以協道之中正也，而繼我以此焉。使之或考祥於視履之旋，或致審於用動之則，範我于皇極之門，隨事觀理，率履而不越也；飭我於嘉會之地，因物察則，範圍而不過也。此則中正履，而所以要吾踐道之歸者在此。不有夫子，又孰知禮之當約也如此哉！夫先之文以始其知，則博文者，致知之不可以已者也；繼之禮以約其行，則約禮者，力行之不可以已者也。功以漸加，敎有定序，此夫子之敎所以爲善，而回之由敎而入，亦因是庶幾矣乎！雖然，二者之敎固
translation_en:
…nor does he impart instruction indiscriminately and out of due order. What could equal such orderly and skillful guidance! Cultural learning carries the Way; without broadening one’s knowledge, one risks falling into narrowness. The Master feared that my learning was not yet broad enough to comprehend the Way in its diverse manifestations, and therefore began my instruction with this. He had me seek evidence far back in writings and worthy men’s testimony, or inquire widely into the reasons underlying affairs and things. By learning and thereby coming to know, I would acquaint myself extensively with the words and deeds of earlier people and thus nurture my virtue. By silently retaining what I learned, I would extend my understanding through investigating principles and fully realizing human nature, seeking ultimately to comprehend Heaven’s mandate. In this way, my experience and learning would become broad: herein lay the foundation prepared for my entry into the Way. Without the Master, who would have known that cultural learning should be broadened in this manner!

Ritual brings the Way together; without restraining one’s conduct, one risks falling into license. The Master feared that I was not yet sufficiently restrained to accord with the Way’s centrality and correctness, and therefore continued my instruction with this. He had me examine auspicious signs by reviewing the course of my conduct, or scrutinize the standards governing my actions. He formed me at the gate of the august ultimate standard, so that I would observe principles in each affair and follow the proper course without transgression. He disciplined me in the realm where excellence converges, so that I would discern standards in each thing and remain within their bounds without excess. In this way, centrality and correctness would be put into practice: herein lay the means of securing the ultimate aim of my practice of the Way. Without the Master, who, again, would have known that ritual should provide restraint in this manner!

He began with cultural learning to initiate understanding: thus, broadening cultural learning means that extending one’s knowledge must never cease. He followed this with ritual to restrain conduct: thus, accepting ritual restraint means that diligent practice must never cease. Effort increases gradually, and instruction follows a fixed sequence. This is what makes the Master’s teaching excellent; and was it not through this, too, that Hui could approach entry into the Way by following his instruction? Nevertheless, these two forms of instruction certainly…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
有先後之序其實功則合一而亦相因者也蓋
博文者博禮之文也而非粗也約禮者約文之
禮也而非隱也夫博約之功卽精一之訓雖聖
賢道學之傳率不外是此固入道心法也要之
博者博此者也約者約此者也過此以往其曾
子一貫之唯顏子心齋坐忘之後乎噫豈惟顏
曾哉進如堯舜道統執中之傳謂非精一之功
基之也不可
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之敎誠則明矣
===
明則誠矣
王墀
同考試官敎諭羅批誠明處說得明盡未有如
此篇者
同考試官敎諭龍批天人之辨直截得明使學
者有下手處
考試官敎諭黃批是有得於誠明之學者
考試官敎諭朱批發揮精切
中庸別言性敎之異而必要其同也夫性命於
punctuated:
有先後之序，其實功則合一而亦相因者也。蓋博文者，博禮之文也，而非粗也；約禮者，約文之禮也，而非隱也。夫博約之功，卽精一之訓，雖聖賢道學之傳，率不外是。此固入道心法也。要之，博者博此者也，約者約此者也。過此以往，其曾子一貫之唯、顏子心齋坐忘之後乎？噫！豈惟顏曾哉？進如堯舜道統執中之傳，謂非精一之功基之也，不可。

自誠明謂之性，自明誠謂之敎。誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

王墀

同考試官敎諭羅批：誠明處說得明盡，未有如此篇者。

同考試官敎諭龍批：天人之辨，直截得明，使學者有下手處。

考試官敎諭黃批：是有得於誠明之學者。

考試官敎諭朱批：發揮精切。

《中庸》別言性敎之異，而必要其同也。夫性命於
translation_en:
…there is an order of precedence, but in their actual practice they form a unity and also depend upon one another. For broad learning in cultural forms means learning broadly the forms of ritual propriety; it is not something coarse. Restraining oneself through ritual propriety means adhering to the ritual principles of those cultural forms; it is not something hidden. The work of broadening learning and exercising restraint is precisely the teaching of refinement and single-mindedness. Even the learning of the Way transmitted by sages and worthies generally goes no further than this. This is indeed the method of cultivating the mind through which one enters the Way. In essence, what one studies broadly is this, and what one adheres to through restraint is this. Beyond this, would one reach the stage following Master Zeng’s assent to the single thread running through the Way, and Master Yan’s fasting of the mind and sitting in forgetfulness? Ah! Why speak only of Yan and Zeng? Going further, to the transmission of holding fast to the Mean in the succession of the Way from Yao and Shun, one cannot deny that the work of refinement and single-mindedness provides its foundation.

“From sincerity to illumination is called nature; from illumination to sincerity is called instruction. With sincerity comes illumination; with illumination comes sincerity.”

Wang Chi 王墀

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: No essay has ever explained sincerity and illumination as clearly and fully as this one.

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: The distinction between Heaven and humanity is made clear in a direct and decisive manner, giving learners a place to begin their efforts.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: This is someone who has gained an understanding of the learning of sincerity and illumination.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The exposition is precise and pertinent.
