title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天敎立於人若異矣然由敎入性以人盡天何
甞不歸於同哉此子思子發明誠明之義者至
矣若謂天人之不能無判者分也而其未始有
間者理也于其分則等異于其理則歸同何也
理備於我精以粹矣至純而無所於雜夫是之
謂誠知發於我靈以瑩矣至照而無所於遺夫
是之謂明夫由誠而明者言之是乃原於帝降
之衷非假人力至者剛柔立本洗心退藏於密
自可酬酢而佑神也易簡成能齋戒神明其德
===
自能知來而藏往也非性而何夫由明而誠者
言之是乃本於吾學之力非由人性生者窮理
盡性見天則於會通之餘冒天下之道也下學
上達合天德於研幾之後立天下之有也非敎
而何此聖賢所由以分似若區以别者然而道
原於一理終歸于同爾蓋誠而明者天人合一
者也德無不實明無不照無所爲而然也明而
誠者以人合天者也先明乎善後實其善必俟
勉而至也誠之至者固無不照矣未至於誠者
punctuated: 天，敎立於人，若異矣。然由敎入性，以人盡天，何甞不歸於同哉？此子思子發明誠明之義者至矣。若謂天人之不能無判者，分也；而其未始有間者，理也。于其分則等異，于其理則歸同，何也？理備於我，精以粹矣，至純而無所於雜，夫是之謂誠；知發於我，靈以瑩矣，至照而無所於遺，夫是之謂明。夫由誠而明者言之，是乃原於帝降之衷，非假人力至者。剛柔立本，洗心退藏於密，自可酬酢而佑神也；易簡成能，齋戒神明其德，自能知來而藏往也。非性而何？夫由明而誠者言之，是乃本於吾學之力，非由人性生者。窮理盡性，見天則於會通之餘，冒天下之道也；下學上達，合天德於研幾之後，立天下之有也。非敎而何？此聖賢所由以分，似若區以别者。然而道原於一，理終歸于同爾。蓋誠而明者，天人合一者也，德無不實，明無不照，無所爲而然也；明而誠者，以人合天者也，先明乎善，後實其善，必俟勉而至也。誠之至者，固無不照矣；未至於誠者，
translation_en:
…Heaven, while teaching is established by human beings: they seem different. Yet by proceeding through teaching to enter into one's nature, and through human effort to fulfill what comes from Heaven, how could they ever fail to converge? Here Master Zisi's elucidation of sincerity and illumination reaches its utmost depth. One might say that what necessarily distinguishes Heaven from humanity is their respective province, while what has never allowed any separation between them is principle. In their respective provinces they differ in degree, but in principle they converge. Why is this? Principle is fully present within me, refined and pure, utterly pure and without admixture: this is what is called sincerity. Understanding issues from within me, numinous and radiant, illuminating all and leaving nothing out: this is what is called illumination.

Speaking of proceeding from sincerity to illumination, this originates in the inner moral norm bestowed by the Lord on High; it is not attained through reliance on human effort. The firm and yielding establish the foundation; one cleanses the heart and withdraws into hidden stillness, naturally able to respond to things and assist the workings of the spirits. Ease and simplicity bring capacity to fulfillment; through purification and abstinence one makes one's virtue numinous and luminous, naturally able to know what is coming and retain what has passed. What is this if not nature?

Speaking of proceeding from illumination to sincerity, this rests upon the effort of one's learning; it does not arise spontaneously from human nature. By investigating principle and fully realizing one's nature, one perceives Heaven's norms after comprehending how things connect, encompassing the Way of all under Heaven. By learning what is below and attaining what is above, one accords with Heaven's virtue after investigating the subtle beginnings of things, establishing all that exists under Heaven. What is this if not teaching?

This is the basis for distinguishing sages from worthies, as though they were divided into separate categories. Yet the Way has a single source, and principle ultimately converges in unity. For those who proceed from sincerity to illumination, Heaven and humanity form a unity: their virtue is wholly real and their illumination leaves nothing unlit; they are so without deliberate action. Those who proceed from illumination to sincerity unite the human with Heaven: first they understand goodness, then they make that goodness real, necessarily awaiting sustained effort before attaining it. Those whose sincerity has reached its utmost assuredly leave nothing unilluminated; as for those who have not yet attained sincerity…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
先之格致之功而誠正豫焉精義入神其寂然
者可以見誠之源也德之實者固無不明矣尚
歉於實者始乎問學之道而德性尊焉大心體
物其澄然者可以見誠之立也謂非明亦可以
至於誠哉是知性教之分聖賢之等也明誠之
同安勉之歸也思誠君子其當知所從事也乎
雖然首言性道教此獨言性教不及道者何也
噫道固在其中也誠明謂者率此性而天道者
也明誠謂者率此性而人道者也天人雖殊其
===
歸實一而已大抵由教者固當知善反矣性之
者奈何亦曰不可無盡性之功焉聖人定之中
正仁義而立人極此則道自我行教自我立而
性自我盡矣故曰惟至誠為能盡性
堯舜之道孝弟而已矣
廖雲鵬
同考試官教諭安批堯舜無窮事業只自孝弟
中推出來此作發揚得盡非用心於內者不能道
同考試官教諭鄺批是寧志於作聖者不徒以
punctuated:
先之格致之功，而誠正豫焉。精義入神，其寂然者，可以見誠之源也。德之實者，固無不明矣；尚歉於實者，始乎問學之道，而德性尊焉。大心體物，其澄然者，可以見誠之立也。謂非明亦可以至於誠哉？是知性教之分，聖賢之等也；明誠之同，安勉之歸也。思誠君子，其當知所從事也乎！雖然，首言性、道、教，此獨言性、教，不及道者，何也？噫！道固在其中也。誠明謂者，率此性而天道者也；明誠謂者，率此性而人道者也。天人雖殊，其歸實一而已。大抵由教者，固當知善反矣；性之者，奈何？亦曰不可無盡性之功焉。聖人定之中正仁義，而立人極，此則道自我行，教自我立，而性自我盡矣。故曰：「惟至誠為能盡性。」
堯舜之道，孝弟而已矣。
廖雲鵬
同考試官教諭安批：「堯舜無窮事業，只自孝弟中推出來。此作發揚得盡，非用心於內者不能道。」
同考試官教諭鄺批：「是寧志於作聖者，不徒以
translation_en:
…one first undertakes the work of investigating things and extending knowledge, with sincerity of intention and rectification of the mind already involved therein. By refining one's understanding of principles and penetrating the spiritual, one can discern the source of sincerity in that stillness. Where virtue is fully realized, illumination is assured. Those whose realization remains incomplete begin with inquiry and learning, thereby honoring their moral nature. By expanding the mind to comprehend all things, one can discern the establishment of sincerity in that clarity. Could one claim that sincerity can be attained without illumination? Thus we know that the distinction between nature and instruction corresponds to the differing levels of sages and worthies, while the convergence of illumination and sincerity is the common destination of those who proceed with ease and those who strive. Surely the gentleman intent upon sincerity should know where to direct his efforts!
Nevertheless, the opening speaks of nature, the Way, and instruction; why does this passage speak only of nature and instruction, without mentioning the Way? Ah! The Way is already contained within them. What is termed proceeding from sincerity to illumination is following this nature as the Way of Heaven; what is termed proceeding from illumination to sincerity is following this nature as the human Way. Though Heaven and humanity differ, their ultimate destination is truly one. In general, those who proceed through instruction must know how to return properly to their nature. But what of those who embody it naturally? They too cannot dispense with the work of fully realizing their nature. The sage establishes centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, thereby setting the ultimate standard for humanity. Thus the Way is practiced through oneself, instruction is established through oneself, and one's nature is fully realized through oneself. Hence it is said: “Only utmost sincerity enables one fully to realize one's nature.”
“The Way of Yao and Shun consists solely in filial devotion and respect for elder brothers.”
Liao Yunpeng
Comment by Associate Examiner An, Instructor: “The boundless achievements of Yao and Shun all grew out of filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. This composition brings out their significance fully. No one who had not applied himself inwardly could express this.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor: “This is surely [?] someone intent upon becoming a sage, who does not merely regard …”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
文而已
考試官教諭黃批文有思致有體認殆無愧
於士矣
考試官教諭朱批精密
大賢言二聖之道不外率性之常而已夫性分
常道莫先孝弟也堯舜所以爲聖不過率此性
已爾聖脩之功何俟他求哉此孟子曉曹交意
蓋如此今夫道不遠人而遠人爲之者失之離
性外無聖而外性求之者幾於罔何則堯大聖
===
人也後世無及焉以放勳則天觀堯堯若有異
行也而不知堯之爲道亦惟從事於此性矣舜
大聖人也後世無及焉以重華協帝觀舜舜若
有絕德也而不知舜之爲道外性亦非所有事
矣親親爲仁吾性之孝形焉夫人同此性則同
此孝而堯舜固亦同夫人爾敬長爲義吾性之
弟著焉夫人同此性則同此弟而堯舜則亦與
人同爾蓋孝弟也者不慮而知吾性良知也堯
舜雖生知亦不過率孝弟之良知以爲知外此
punctuated:
文而已。
考試官教諭黃批：文有思致，有體認，殆無愧於士矣。
考試官教諭朱批：精密。
大賢言二聖之道，不外率性之常而已。夫性分常道，莫先孝弟也。堯舜所以爲聖，不過率此性已爾。聖脩之功，何俟他求哉？此孟子曉曹交意，蓋如此。今夫道不遠人，而遠人爲之者，失之離；性外無聖，而外性求之者，幾於罔。何則？堯，大聖人也，後世無及焉。以放勳則天觀堯，堯若有異行也，而不知堯之爲道，亦惟從事於此性矣。舜，大聖人也，後世無及焉。以重華協帝觀舜，舜若有絕德也，而不知舜之爲道，外性亦非所有事矣。親親爲仁，吾性之孝形焉。夫人同此性，則同此孝，而堯舜固亦同夫人爾。敬長爲義，吾性之弟著焉。夫人同此性，則同此弟，而堯舜則亦與人同爾。蓋孝弟也者，不慮而知，吾性良知也。堯舜雖生知，亦不過率孝弟之良知以爲知，外此
translation_en:
…literary composition alone.
Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: “The composition shows thoughtful conception and personal understanding; its author surely merits the name of scholar.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Refined and precise.”
The great worthy declares that the Way of the two sages extends no further than the constant norms of following one’s nature. Among the constant principles inherent in our nature, none takes precedence over filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. What made Yao and Shun sages was simply their following this nature. Why should the work of cultivating sagehood require seeking elsewhere? Such, in essence, was Mencius’s intention in instructing Cao Jiao. Now, the Way is not remote from human beings; those who pursue it at a distance from humanity err in separating the two. There is no sagehood outside human nature; those who seek it outside that nature approach delusion. Why is this so? Yao was a great sage whom no one in later ages could equal. When we regard Yao in terms of his far-reaching achievements and his emulation of Heaven, he seems to have possessed extraordinary conduct. Yet this overlooks the fact that Yao’s practice of the Way consisted solely in attending to this nature. Shun was a great sage whom no one in later ages could equal. When we regard Shun in terms of his renewed brilliance and his accord with the emperor, he seems to have possessed unparalleled virtue. Yet this overlooks the fact that, in practicing the Way, Shun likewise concerned himself with nothing outside human nature. Loving one’s parents constitutes benevolence: through it, the filial devotion of our nature takes form. Everyone shares this nature and therefore shares this filial devotion; Yao and Shun were certainly just like everyone else in this respect. Respecting one’s elders constitutes righteousness: through it, our nature’s respect for elder brothers becomes manifest. Everyone shares this nature and therefore shares this fraternal respect; Yao and Shun were likewise the same as other people in this respect. Filial devotion and fraternal respect are known without deliberation: they are the innate knowledge of our nature. Although Yao and Shun possessed knowledge from birth, their knowing was simply a matter of following this innate knowledge of filial devotion and fraternal respect. Beyond this…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
良知而有所知非性之知也何庸心焉不學而
能吾性良能也堯舜雖安行亦不過率孝弟之
良能以為能外此良能而有所能非性之能也
何致力焉本之民彝之常而寓聖脩之極其在
堯也猶夫舜也觀其自親睦以至昭明協和皆
舉此措之爾舍孝弟之外無堯矣堯亦更能外
此而他有所為乎始之烝民之則而極作聖之
功其在舜也猶夫堯也觀其自克諧以至慎徽
風動皆推此運之爾舍孝弟之外無舜矣舜又
===
安能遠此而更有所加乎故曰而已矣者真見
孝弟之足以盡堯舜而求堯舜之道者固不必
遠有所慕矣知此則知湯之所以為湯文之所
以為文亦非外性分有他道者昧此而泥於形
體之較不亦陋也與大抵堯舜聖之至者也孝
弟性之至者也蓋性分之中萬善咸備一孝弟
立而萬善固從之矣故始于家邦而終于四海
雖施諸後世而無朝夕者由此其選也若夫遠
人為道外性求聖者其弊也離且罔又何怪哉
punctuated: 良知而有所知，非性之知也，何庸心焉？不學而能，吾性良能也。堯舜雖安行，亦不過率孝弟之良能以為能；外此良能而有所能，非性之能也，何致力焉？本之民彝之常，而寓聖脩之極，其在堯也猶夫舜也。觀其自親睦以至昭明協和，皆舉此措之爾。舍孝弟之外無堯矣，堯亦更能外此而他有所為乎？始之烝民之則，而極作聖之功，其在舜也猶夫堯也。觀其自克諧以至慎徽風動，皆推此運之爾。舍孝弟之外無舜矣，舜又安能遠此而更有所加乎？故曰「而已矣」者，真見孝弟之足以盡堯舜，而求堯舜之道者固不必遠有所慕矣。知此，則知湯之所以為湯、文之所以為文，亦非外性分有他道者。昧此而泥於形體之較，不亦陋也與？大抵堯舜，聖之至者也；孝弟，性之至者也。蓋性分之中，萬善咸備，一孝弟立，而萬善固從之矣。故始于家邦而終于四海，雖施諸後世而無朝夕者，由此其選也。若夫遠人為道、外性求聖者，其弊也離且罔，又何怪哉？
translation_en:
…innate knowledge: to know something beyond this is not knowledge belonging to our nature. Why expend thought upon it? Being able to act without learning is the innate capacity of our nature. Although Yao and Shun acted with effortless ease, their capacity amounted to no more than following the innate capacity for filial devotion and fraternal respect. Any capacity beyond this innate capacity is not a capacity belonging to our nature. Why expend effort upon it? Grounded in the enduring norms of human relationships, yet embodying the utmost achievement of sagely cultivation, Yao was just like Shun. Consider how Yao proceeded from loving his kin and bringing them into harmony to illuminating virtue and harmonizing the myriad states: all this was simply putting these qualities into practice. Apart from filial devotion and fraternal respect, there is no Yao. Could Yao himself have gone beyond these and accomplished anything else?

Beginning with the norms of the common people and culminating in the achievement of sagehood, Shun was just like Yao. Consider how he proceeded from bringing his family into harmony to carefully honoring the cardinal relationships and transforming others as the wind moves them: all this was simply extending these qualities and putting them to work. Apart from filial devotion and fraternal respect, there is no Shun. How, then, could Shun have departed from these and added anything further? Thus, the words “and nothing more” express a true understanding that filial devotion and fraternal respect suffice to encompass all that Yao and Shun were. Those who seek the Way of Yao and Shun certainly need not direct their aspirations toward anything remote. Understanding this, one understands that what made Tang who he was, and King Wen who he was, likewise involved no other Way beyond their inherent nature. To remain blind to this and become mired in comparisons of bodily form—is this not shallow?

Broadly speaking, Yao and Shun represent the utmost of sagehood; filial devotion and fraternal respect represent the utmost of human nature. Within our inherent nature, all goodness is fully present. Once filial devotion and fraternal respect are established, all other goodness naturally follows. Thus, beginning with the family and the state and extending ultimately throughout the realm, their influence reaches even later generations, without distinction of morning or evening. Through this they stand preeminent [?]. As for those who pursue a Way remote from human beings and seek sagehood outside human nature, their failings are estrangement and delusion. What is surprising about that?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
然則有志堯舜之道者如何曰近而取足吾性
分中則蕩蕩巍巍眞堯舜者固自在也
易
文明以健中正而應君子正也唯君子爲
能通天下之志
王徽猷
同考試官敎諭鄺批措詞典雅說理精到可卜
其爲佳士無疑

===
日正己應物者不能作
考試官敎諭黃批理明詞則
考試官敎諭朱批腴而暢
彖傳本卦以釋同人之貞而推其爲大同之道
也蓋天下无正外之同也而君子之所以大同
於天下者胥此矣與人同者而可以不之務乎
今夫同人之道審乎公私邪正之間而已矣卦
之爲同本非不足於公者而文王必重以利貞
之戒夫固欲人擇其正也是故必有明辨之智
punctuated:
然則有志堯舜之道者如何？曰：近而取足吾性分中，則蕩蕩巍巍，眞堯舜者固自在也。

易
文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子爲能通天下之志。

王徽猷

同考試官敎諭鄺批：措詞典雅，說理精到，可卜其爲佳士無疑。
同考試官敎授簡批：發揮大同之道詳盡，非平日正己應物者不能作。
考試官敎諭黃批：理明詞則。
考試官敎諭朱批：腴而暢。

彖傳本卦以釋同人之貞，而推其爲大同之道也。蓋天下无正外之同也，而君子之所以大同於天下者胥此矣。與人同者，而可以不之務乎？今夫同人之道，審乎公私邪正之間而已矣。卦之爲同，本非不足於公者，而文王必重以利貞之戒，夫固欲人擇其正也。是故必有明辨之智
translation_en:
What, then, should one who aspires to the Way of Yao and Shun do? The answer is: seek close at hand and find sufficiency within one's own allotted nature; then, in its vastness and loftiness, the true Yao and Shun are already present within oneself.

Book of Changes
“Cultured and enlightened, yet vigorous; central and correct, and meeting with a response: this is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven.”

Wang Huiyou 王徽猷

Comment by Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor: “The phrasing is classical and elegant, and the exposition of principle precise and thorough. One can confidently predict that he will be an outstanding scholar.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jian, Professor: “His exposition of the Way of great unity is exhaustive. Only someone who habitually rectifies himself and responds appropriately to things could have written this.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The principles are clear and the wording conforms to proper standards.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Rich and fluent.”

The Commentary on the Judgments draws upon the hexagram itself to explain the correctness of Fellowship with Others (Tongren), and extends this to elucidate the Way of great unity. For there is no unity under Heaven apart from correctness, and it is entirely through this that the gentleman achieves great unity with all under Heaven. Can one who seeks fellowship with others fail to devote himself to this?

Now, the Way of Fellowship with Others consists simply in discerning the distinctions between public and private interests, and between perversity and correctness. The fellowship embodied in this hexagram is certainly not deficient in impartiality; yet King Wen nevertheless reinforced it with the admonition that “correctness is beneficial.” His intention was assuredly that people should choose what is correct. Thus, one must possess the wisdom of clear discrimination…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也而後能審於所同而此卦之德則文明以健
者也夫其健也而出於文明也則是可否之辨
預持於翕受之初而諂瀆之幾不昧於泛交之
際其在同人固有求同理而不求同俗者矣必
有中正之守也而後能慎於所從而此卦之體
則中正而應者也夫其應也而本於中正也則
是所挾持者大而不舍己以徇人所篤棐者忠
而非自卑以求幸其事是君固有相知以心而
相濟以道者矣此固君子之正而同人之所尚
===
焉者也如此而不有以通天下之志邪蓋天下
无正外之理而同人以正則盡乎理矣理之所
在勢固不得而限之天下无正外之心而同人
以正則得其心矣心之所在跡又不得而拘之
故自其同之見於處物也不必其可者與之而
後以為同也雖其不可者拒之而天下亦不病
其為隘自其同之見於事君也不必其美者將
順之而後以為同也雖其過焉匡救之而天下
亦不病其為拂信乎天下之志唯君子為能通
punctuated: 也，而後能審於所同，而此卦之德則文明以健者也。夫其健也，而出於文明也，則是可否之辨預持於翕受之初，而諂瀆之幾不昧於泛交之際。其在同人，固有求同理而不求同俗者矣。必有中正之守也，而後能慎於所從，而此卦之體則中正而應者也。夫其應也，而本於中正也，則是所挾持者大，而不舍己以徇人；所篤棐者忠，而非自卑以求幸。其事是君，固有相知以心而相濟以道者矣。此固君子之正，而同人之所尚焉者也。如此，而不有以通天下之志邪？蓋天下无正外之理，而同人以正，則盡乎理矣。理之所在，勢固不得而限之。天下无正外之心，而同人以正，則得其心矣。心之所在，跡又不得而拘之。故自其同之見於處物也，不必其可者與之而後以為同也；雖其不可者拒之，而天下亦不病其為隘。自其同之見於事君也，不必其美者將順之而後以為同也；雖其過焉匡救之，而天下亦不病其為拂。信乎，天下之志唯君子為能通
translation_en:
…and only then can one judge discerningly with whom to unite. The virtue of this hexagram, however, is enlightened clarity joined with strength. Since its strength issues from enlightened clarity, the distinction between what is acceptable and unacceptable is already maintained when one first welcomes others, and the incipient signs of flattery and disrespect remain clearly discernible amid wide-ranging associations. In fellowship with others, one thus seeks unity in principle rather than conformity to prevailing customs. One must hold firmly to centrality and correctness before one can exercise care in deciding whom to follow; the structure of this hexagram is precisely that of centrality and correctness joined with correspondence. Since its correspondence is rooted in centrality and correctness, what one upholds is great, and one does not abandon oneself to accommodate others; the earnest assistance one gives is loyal, and one does not abase oneself to seek favor. In serving this ruler, there is thus mutual understanding through the heart and mutual assistance through the Way. This is indeed the correctness of the noble man and what Fellowship with Others esteems. How could this fail to bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communication?

For there is no principle under Heaven outside correctness. When one unites with others through correctness, one fully realizes principle. Where principle resides, circumstances cannot impose limits upon it. There is no heart under Heaven outside correctness. When one unites with others through correctness, one wins their hearts. Where the heart resides, outward forms likewise cannot constrain it. Thus, when this fellowship manifests itself in dealing with others, it need not be considered fellowship only when one joins with them in what is acceptable. Even when one rejects what is unacceptable in them, no one under Heaven faults one for narrowness. When this fellowship manifests itself in serving the ruler, it need not be considered fellowship only when one supports and advances what is good in him. Even when one corrects and remedies his faults, no one under Heaven faults one for being obstructive. Truly, it is only the noble man who can bring the aspirations of all under Heaven into communication…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之而大同之道亦惟於至正得之耳苟或不擇
可否而一於同則反爲同之累矣而亦何所於
利哉故君子不爲苟同非好異也必天下之是
已則非矣不狥人以同非惡同也必天下之同
已則異矣推之三仁不能易其心而禹稷顏回
可以易其地皆是物也而況與人同者可以弗
之由乎嗚呼公私邪正之辨學易者可以深長
思矣
易簡之善配至德
===
郭培之
同考試官教諭龍 批 製詞朗潤析理精深非
惟秀雅可愛亦足占其體認之學
同考試官教諭安 批 易道配人事處講得透
徹必爲用意密造理深之士
考試官教諭黃 批 詞理俱到
考試官教諭朱 批 敷贍精當
大傳擬易理於人心之德而易之廣大徴矣蓋
人心易理其道本相通也以易簡之善而配之
punctuated:
之，而大同之道亦惟於至正得之耳。苟或不擇可否而一於同，則反爲同之累矣，而亦何所於利哉？故君子不爲苟同，非好異也；必天下之是已，則非矣。不狥人以同，非惡同也；必天下之同已，則異矣。推之，三仁不能易其心，而禹稷顏回可以易其地，皆是物也。而況與人同者，可以弗之由乎？嗚呼！公私邪正之辨，學易者可以深長思矣。
易簡之善配至德
郭培之
同考試官教諭龍批：製詞朗潤，析理精深，非惟秀雅可愛，亦足占其體認之學。
同考試官教諭安批：易道配人事處，講得透徹，必爲用意密、造理深之士。
考試官教諭黃批：詞理俱到。
考試官教諭朱批：敷贍精當。
大傳擬易理於人心之德，而易之廣大徴矣。蓋人心易理，其道本相通也。以易簡之善而配之
translation_en:
…them; and the way of great unity, too, can be attained only through the utmost rectitude. If one makes no distinction between what is acceptable and what is not, pursuing agreement alone, this instead becomes an encumbrance to unity. What benefit could there be in it? Thus the gentleman does not agree indiscriminately, but this is not because he delights in differences. To insist that everyone under Heaven approve of oneself [?] would be wrong. He does not yield to others merely to agree, but this is not because he dislikes agreement. To insist that everyone under Heaven agree with oneself [?] would itself produce divergence. Extending this reasoning, the three humane men could not change their convictions, while Yu, Ji, and Yan Hui could have exchanged places: all exemplify this same principle. How much more, then, must those seeking unity with others follow it! Alas! Those who study the Book of Changes may ponder deeply and at length the distinction between public-mindedness and selfishness, perversity and rectitude.
The Goodness of Ease and Simplicity Matches Supreme Virtue
Guo Peizhi
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor, comments: “The language is lucid and polished, and the analysis of principle precise and profound. Beyond its admirable elegance, it also provides evidence of his learning through personal understanding.”
Associate Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The passage matching the Way of the Changes to human affairs is explained thoroughly. He must be a scholar meticulous in thought and profound in his grasp of principle.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Ample in exposition, precise and apt.”
The Great Commentary compares the principles of the Changes with the virtue of the human mind, thereby demonstrating the breadth and greatness of the Changes. For the human mind and the principles of the Changes are fundamentally interconnected in their Way. Taking the goodness of ease and simplicity and matching it with…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
至德夫何間然之有哉此可見易之廣大也大
傳之意若謂易之爲書也推其廣大之由固天
地以爲本論其廣大之實則天人以爲配是故
不但參諸造化而推之人事亦有脗合焉者矣
何則乾一而實確然示人易者也易之卦爻而
屬乎陽者其善不同同歸於易矣夫坤二而虛
隤然示人簡者也易之卦爻而屬乎陰者其善
不同同歸於簡矣實理昭於法象而善有成名
至道顯於卦爻而用无定在孰不曰此易簡之
===
在書者耳而何以配人之至德也殊不知人之
生也天命之性雖全體而不偏而健順之德則
隨感而異用故廓然太公而一私不撓人有健
之德也而易之言易者與之合焉蓋德行恒易
是亦天下之至健者爲之也而易與人非有二
矣怡然順理而一物无累人有順之德也而易
之言簡者與之準焉蓋德行恒簡亦惟天下之
至順者能之也而理與書合于一矣故默會乎
法象之表則易簡者健順之良能也健順者易
punctuated: 至德，夫何間然之有哉？此可見易之廣大也。大傳之意，若謂易之爲書也，推其廣大之由，固天地以爲本；論其廣大之實，則天人以爲配。是故不但參諸造化，而推之人事，亦有脗合焉者矣。何則？乾一而實，確然示人易者也。易之卦爻而屬乎陽者，其善不同，同歸於易矣。夫坤二而虛，隤然示人簡者也。易之卦爻而屬乎陰者，其善不同，同歸於簡矣。實理昭於法象，而善有成名；至道顯於卦爻，而用无定在。孰不曰：「此易簡之在書者耳，而何以配人之至德也？」殊不知人之生也，天命之性雖全體而不偏，而健順之德則隨感而異用。故廓然太公而一私不撓，人有健之德也，而易之言易者與之合焉。蓋德行恒易，是亦天下之至健者爲之也，而易與人非有二矣。怡然順理而一物无累，人有順之德也，而易之言簡者與之準焉。蓋德行恒簡，亦惟天下之至順者能之也，而理與書合于一矣。故默會乎法象之表，則易簡者，健順之良能也；健順者，易
translation_en:
…with consummate virtue—what discrepancy could there be between them? Here one can see the vastness of the Changes. The meaning of the Great Commentary seems to be this: considering the Changes as a book, if one traces the source of its vastness, Heaven and Earth are indeed its foundation; if one discusses what its vastness consists in, Heaven and humanity stand in correspondence. Thus it not only accords with the workings of creation: when extended to human affairs, it likewise fits them perfectly.

Why is this so? Qian is one and solid; firm and steadfast, it manifests ease to humanity. Those hexagrams and lines of the Changes that belong to yang differ in their excellences, but all converge upon ease. Kun is two and open; yielding, it manifests simplicity to humanity. Those hexagrams and lines of the Changes that belong to yin differ in their excellences, but all converge upon simplicity. Substantial principle shines forth in the patterns and images, and its excellences acquire established names; the highest Way appears in the hexagrams and lines, yet its operation has no fixed locus. Who would not say, “These are merely ease and simplicity as found in the book; how can they correspond to consummate human virtue?”

Yet this overlooks the fact that, when human beings are born, although the nature conferred by Heaven is complete and without partiality, the virtues of vigor and compliance operate differently in response to what moves them. Thus, when people are expansively impartial [?], undisturbed by even a single selfish thought, they possess the virtue of vigor, and what the Changes says of ease accords with it. For constancy in ease in virtuous conduct is also the work of those of utmost vigor in the world: the Changes and humanity are not two separate things. When people gladly follow principle, unburdened by any single thing, they possess the virtue of compliance, and what the Changes says of simplicity corresponds to it. For constancy in simplicity in virtuous conduct is likewise something only those of utmost compliance in the world can achieve: principle and the book unite as one. Thus, through silent apprehension beyond the patterns and images, ease and simplicity are the innate capacities of vigor and compliance; vigor and compliance are ease…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
簡之成德也至德非妙於有而易簡非隱於无
矣其用相發而其理有不足以相當也哉神明
於卦爻之內則易本陰陽之理以為書也人會
陰陽之理以成德也人固天地之心而易亦性
命之奧矣其理相通而其善有不足以相配也
哉由是觀之而易之廣大見矣雖然易書固該
乎人道而人心實備乎易理者也聖人心涵太
極全體動靜而以其理示之易故易作而聖人
之心極昭焉此易簡之所自來也吾人之心孰
===
不有太極乎而往往以自私用智累之所以卒
畔于易也是故易知易從之訓聖人首發於傳
而此復以其相配言之若曰易簡吾心所本有
也而易特與之配焉耳然則自喪其良而不知
求配於易者可不為之動心乎
書
愼厥身脩思永惇敘九族庶明勵翼邇可
遠在兹
黃休泰
punctuated:
簡之成德也。至德非妙於有，而易簡非隱於无矣。其用相發，而其理有不足以相當也哉？神明於卦爻之內，則易本陰陽之理以為書也，人會陰陽之理以成德也。人固天地之心，而易亦性命之奧矣。其理相通，而其善有不足以相配也哉？由是觀之，而易之廣大見矣。雖然，易書固該乎人道，而人心實備乎易理者也。聖人心涵太極，全體動靜，而以其理示之易，故易作而聖人之心極昭焉。此易簡之所自來也。吾人之心孰不有太極乎？而往往以自私用智累之，所以卒畔于易也。是故易知易從之訓，聖人首發於傳，而此復以其相配言之，若曰：「易簡，吾心所本有也，而易特與之配焉耳。」然則自喪其良而不知求配於易者，可不為之動心乎？

書
愼厥身，脩思永，惇敘九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠在兹。
黃休泰
translation_en:
…simplicity brought to perfected virtue. Supreme virtue is not something wondrous beyond tangible existence, nor are ease and simplicity concealed in nonbeing. Their functions bring one another into expression: could their principles fail to correspond? When one apprehends the spiritual illumination within the hexagrams and their lines, one sees that the Changes takes the principles of yin and yang as the basis of its text, while human beings comprehend those principles to perfect their virtue. Human beings are indeed the heart of Heaven and Earth, and the Changes is also the repository of the mysteries of human nature and destiny. Their principles communicate with one another: could their goodness fail to match? Viewed thus, the breadth and greatness of the Changes become apparent.

Nevertheless, while the book of Changes encompasses the human Way, the human heart itself fully possesses the principles of the Changes. The sage’s heart embraces the Supreme Ultimate and embodies movement and stillness in their entirety. He displays their principles in the Changes; thus, with the composition of the Changes, the sage’s heart becomes fully manifest. This is the source of ease and simplicity. Whose heart does not possess the Supreme Ultimate? Yet we repeatedly burden it with selfishness and contrivance, and so ultimately depart from the Changes. Hence the sage first set forth in the Commentary the teaching of being easy to understand and easy to follow, and here again speaks of their correspondence, as though saying: “Ease and simplicity are inherent in my heart; the Changes merely corresponds to them.” Should those who themselves forfeit their innate goodness, yet do not know to seek correspondence with the Changes, not be stirred by this?

Book of Documents
“Be watchful over your person; in cultivating yourself, think of the enduring consequences. Generously maintain the proper ordering of the nine degrees of kinship. Let the many enlightened men exert themselves in assisting you. What is near may be extended afar: herein lies the means.”
Huang Xiutai

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭張批此題似易實難作者不掇
陳言則騁浮詞理渾涵而文醇雅者僅見此篇
同考試官敎授莫批融貫心理思致悠揚疏通知
遠之學不當如是邪取之
考試官敎諭黃批莊重有體
考試官敎諭朱批峻潔
人君知所以脩德則其化大行矣夫君身萬化
之原也德脩于上而天下國家之化有不裕如
矣乎臯陶陳謨而廣之也蓋謂人君之治求之
===
於外者拂而難反之于已者順而易所謂迪德
謨明者亦惟於身焉取之誠使其逸欲是戒敬
脩其可願之善而發號施令之必臧兢業自持
率循於罔愆之度而出入起居之必欽然猶謀
慮深長不以小成而自安言而思世爲天下法
也志意高遠不以近利而自狃行而思世爲天
下則也以此迪德則脩身之外無餘理而思永
之外無餘心吾見氣機感動而道化流行由之
而家焉此心同也此理同也異文以合愛權然
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭張批：「此題似易實難，作者不掇陳言，則騁浮詞。理渾涵而文醇雅者，僅見此篇。」
同考試官敎授莫批：「融貫心理，思致悠揚，疏通知遠之學，不當如是邪？取之。」
考試官敎諭黃批：「莊重有體。」
考試官敎諭朱批：「峻潔。」
人君知所以脩德，則其化大行矣。夫君身，萬化之原也。德脩于上，而天下國家之化有不裕如矣乎？臯陶陳謨而廣之也，蓋謂人君之治，求之於外者拂而難，反之于已者順而易。所謂迪德謨明者，亦惟於身焉取之。誠使其逸欲是戒，敬脩其可願之善，而發號施令之必臧；兢業自持，率循於罔愆之度，而出入起居之必欽。然猶謀慮深長，不以小成而自安，言而思世爲天下法也；志意高遠，不以近利而自狃，行而思世爲天下則也。以此迪德，則脩身之外無餘理，而思永之外無餘心。吾見氣機感動，而道化流行。由之而家焉，此心同也，此理同也，異文以合愛，權然
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “This topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Writers either pick up stale sayings or give free rein to empty rhetoric. Only in this essay have I found principles richly comprehended and prose pure and elegant.”
Associate Examiner Mo, Professor, comments: “It integrates the mind and principle throughout, and its thought unfolds with lingering resonance. Should not learning that achieves broad understanding and knowledge of distant things be like this? Accept it.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Grave and dignified, with proper form.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Elevated and clean.”
When a ruler understands how to cultivate virtue, his transforming influence spreads widely. The ruler’s person is the source of all transformation. When virtue is cultivated above, can the transformation of the realm, the state, and the family fail to proceed with ample ease? Gao Yao set forth his counsels and expanded upon this point. His meaning was that, in governing, what a ruler seeks externally meets resistance and difficulty, while what he seeks by turning back upon himself proceeds smoothly and easily. What is called practicing virtue and being enlightened in counsel is likewise to be sought solely in one’s own person. Let him truly guard against ease and desire, reverently cultivate the goodness worthy of being desired, and ensure that every command and ordinance he issues is good. Let him maintain himself in vigilance and diligence, consistently follow standards free from error, and ensure that his every movement and daily activity is reverent. Yet his deliberations must also be profound and far-reaching: he must not rest content with minor achievements, but, whenever he speaks, consider how his words may serve as a model for the realm for generations. His aspirations must be lofty and far-reaching: he must not become habituated to immediate gains, but, whenever he acts, consider how his conduct may serve as a standard for the realm for generations. If he practices virtue in this way, no principle lies outside the cultivation of his person, and no concern of his mind lies outside taking thought for the long term. I see the vital impulses responding and stirring, and the transforming influence of the Way flowing forth. Extend this to the family: this mind is shared, and this principle is shared. Through differing forms of observance, affection is brought into unity, [the following expression, 權然, is unclear] …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
情意之浹洽殊事以合敬沛然恩義之流通觀
于其家而家無不齊也是不由于脩身乎由之
而國焉此心同也此理同也百僚師師奮庸以
煕帝載庶官濟濟祗慎以亮天工觀于其國而
國無不治也是又不本于脩身乎又由家國而
之天下焉此心同也此理同也舉此加彼有不
疾而速之機篤近舉遠有不行而至之妙萬邦
之協和皆俊德之所昭宣四方之風動皆惠迪
之所衣被觀于天下而天下無不平也又豈能
===
外于此身之脩耶夫脩身則迪德之實可見而
其化蓋不止于謨明弼諧而已非吾君之所當
務歟嗟乎是說也天德王道一以貫之者也其
要在于兢業萬幾蓋幾者動之微善惡之所由
分也察微知著圖大於細而檢身之功益以邃
密其于治也何有此臯陶所以尤致意於終篇
也堯舜執中要不外是序道統者而謂臯陶見
而知之有以哉
我受天命丕若有夏歷年式勿替有殷歷
punctuated:
情意之浹洽，殊事以合敬，沛然恩義之流通。觀于其家，而家無不齊也，是不由于脩身乎？由之而國焉，此心同也，此理同也。百僚師師，奮庸以煕帝載；庶官濟濟，祗慎以亮天工。觀于其國，而國無不治也，是又不本于脩身乎？又由家國而之天下焉，此心同也，此理同也。舉此加彼，有不疾而速之機；篤近舉遠，有不行而至之妙。萬邦之協和，皆俊德之所昭宣；四方之風動，皆惠迪之所衣被。觀于天下，而天下無不平也，又豈能外于此身之脩耶？夫脩身，則迪德之實可見，而其化蓋不止于謨明弼諧而已，非吾君之所當務歟？嗟乎！是說也，天德王道一以貫之者也。其要在于兢業萬幾。蓋幾者，動之微，善惡之所由分也。察微知著，圖大於細，而檢身之功益以邃密，其于治也何有？此臯陶所以尤致意於終篇也。堯舜執中，要不外是。序道統者而謂臯陶見而知之，有以哉！

我受天命，丕若有夏歷年，式勿替有殷歷
translation_en:
…feelings and intentions mingle harmoniously; through differing duties, reverence is united, and kindness and righteousness flow abundantly. Consider his family: it is entirely well ordered. Does this not proceed from cultivating oneself? From there, extend this to the state: the heart is the same, and the principle is the same. The officials encourage one another, exerting themselves in service to advance the emperor’s undertakings; the assembled officers act reverently and cautiously to assist Heaven’s work. Consider his state: it is entirely well governed. Is this not likewise rooted in cultivating oneself? Then extend this from the family and state to all under Heaven: the heart is the same, and the principle is the same. Extending what operates here to what lies there brings about swiftness without haste; treating those nearby generously and extending this to those far away achieves the marvel of arriving without travelling. The concord of the myriad states is entirely the manifestation of illustrious virtue; the responsiveness of the four quarters, as to a passing wind, comes entirely from the encompassing influence of following the Way. Consider all under Heaven: everywhere is at peace. How could this lie outside the cultivation of oneself?

Through cultivating oneself, the substance of practising virtue becomes visible, and its transforming influence surely extends beyond enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance. Is this not what our ruler ought to pursue? Ah! This teaching runs through Heaven’s virtue and the kingly Way as a single thread. Its essential point is to attend with vigilance and reverence to the myriad incipient developments in affairs. Such beginnings are the subtle first stirrings of action, where good and evil diverge. Discern the subtle to understand what will become manifest; plan for the great in its smallest details. As the work of examining oneself grows ever deeper and more exact, what difficulty can there be in governing? This is why Gao Yao gave this matter particular attention at the end of the chapter. The central principle upheld by Yao and Shun ultimately goes no further than this. Those who trace the succession of the Way say that Gao Yao knew it through direct encounter: they have good reason!

We have received Heaven’s mandate; may we fully match the years of the Xia, and may we not fall short of the Shang’s span of…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
年
蔣龍
同考試官教諭張批說君臣同心祈命詞不繁
理意自鬯達可以為文矣
同考試官教授莫批語緒和平想見當時氣象
經義之優者
考試官教諭黃批體裁渾雄
考試官教諭朱批典暢
大臣欲君臣期有周受命之永兼乎二代焉甚
===
矣天命之難諶也然則欲兼二代之永命者不
有望于君臣之相成哉召公陳誥于王而深致
意于此也蓋曰天命之簡畀無常上下之責任
則一我之欲其勤恤者豈有他哉亦相期於無
窮而已誠以我周之命文考之所誕膺締造亦
艱難矣茲欲其中土之乂克配上帝有以衍統
緒於昌明武王之所迪有積累亦憂勤矣茲欲
其初服之慎克享天心有以垂曆數於悠久遠
而稽之於夏歷年四百何其祚之靈長也然祚
punctuated:
年。
蔣龍。
同考試官教諭張批：說君臣同心祈命，詞不繁，理意自鬯達，可以為文矣。
同考試官教授莫批：語緒和平，想見當時氣象，經義之優者。
考試官教諭黃批：體裁渾雄。
考試官教諭朱批：典暢。
大臣欲君臣期有周受命之永，兼乎二代焉。甚矣，天命之難諶也！然則欲兼二代之永命者，不有望于君臣之相成哉？召公陳誥于王，而深致意于此也。蓋曰：天命之簡畀無常，上下之責任則一。我之欲其勤恤者，豈有他哉？亦相期於無窮而已。誠以我周之命，文考之所誕膺，締造亦艱難矣。茲欲其中土之乂，克配上帝，有以衍統緒於昌明。武王之所迪有，積累亦憂勤矣。茲欲其初服之慎，克享天心，有以垂曆數於悠久。遠而稽之於夏，歷年四百，何其祚之靈長也！然祚
translation_en:
…years.

Jiang Long.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “It explains how ruler and ministers, united in purpose, pray for the Mandate. The wording is economical, and the principles and meaning unfold naturally and clearly. This makes a worthy essay.”

Associate Examiner Mo, Professor, comments: “The language is balanced and harmonious, allowing one to envision the atmosphere of that time. An excellent exposition of the Classics.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The composition is rounded and powerful.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and fluent.”

The great minister wished ruler and ministers to aspire to a duration for Zhou’s Heavenly Mandate that would encompass those of the two preceding dynasties. How difficult it is to rely upon Heaven’s Mandate! If they wished their enduring Mandate to encompass the durations of both dynasties, must they not look to ruler and ministers to support one another in their accomplishments? When the Duke of Shao presented his announcement to the king, he placed particular emphasis on this.

His meaning was this: Heaven’s choice of whom to favor with its Mandate is inconstant, but the responsibility of those above and below is one. Could I have any other purpose in wishing them to labor diligently and remain watchful? It is simply that they should encourage one another to aspire to an endless succession. For the Mandate of our Zhou was grandly received by our deceased, cultivated father, King Wen, and its foundation was established with great difficulty. Now we wish that, through good government of the central lands, we may prove worthy of the Lord on High and extend our dynastic succession in flourishing splendor. What King Wu attained likewise rested upon achievements accumulated through anxious toil. Now we wish that, through care at the beginning of this reign, we may win Heaven’s favor and perpetuate the allotted span of our rule far into the future.

Looking far back and examining the Xia, we find that it endured for four hundred years. How enduring was its heavenly blessing! Yet that blessing…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
于有夏亦可以祚于有周將申命而用休近而
觀之於殷歷年六百何其慶之綿延也然慶於
有殷亦可以慶于有周將眷命而用懋並乎夏
而又克兼乎殷天之祐也無已吾受之也亦無
已宜君宜王得以紹休于先烈矣同乎殷而又
克兼乎夏帝之畀也無疆吾承之也亦無疆克
長克君得以媲美于前代矣雖曰周命維新安
知其久而不渝也上下勤恤正以迂滋至之休
可諉曰我周受命止如夏而已乎雖曰多方誕
===
受安保其遠而不替也君臣同心正以凝單厚
之福可諉曰我周受命止如殷而已乎吁召公
之欲君臣祈天永命如此可謂深切著明者矣
雖然帝天之命主于民心而敬德又所以誠小
民故曰王其疾敬德又曰欲王以小民受天永
命人君以德誠民則至和熏烝天心感孚歷年
久長可以馴致宜乎召公反覆致意也厥後成
王爲周令主而卜世卜年皆過其曆然後知老
成謀國之慮非偶然者噫其斯以爲召公歟
punctuated:
于有夏，亦可以祚于有周，將申命而用休。近而觀之於殷，歷年六百，何其慶之綿延也！然慶於有殷，亦可以慶于有周，將眷命而用懋。並乎夏而又克兼乎殷，天之祐也無已，吾受之也亦無已，宜君宜王，得以紹休于先烈矣。同乎殷而又克兼乎夏，帝之畀也無疆，吾承之也亦無疆，克長克君，得以媲美于前代矣。雖曰「周命維新」，安知其久而不渝也？上下勤恤，正以迂滋至之休，可諉曰我周受命止如夏而已乎？雖曰「多方誕受」，安保其遠而不替也？君臣同心，正以凝單厚之福，可諉曰我周受命止如殷而已乎？吁！召公之欲君臣祈天永命如此，可謂深切著明者矣。

雖然，帝天之命主于民心，而敬德又所以誠小民。故曰：「王其疾敬德。」又曰：「欲王以小民受天永命。」人君以德誠民，則至和熏烝，天心感孚，歷年久長，可以馴致，宜乎召公反覆致意也。厥後成王爲周令主，而卜世卜年皆過其曆，然後知老成謀國之慮非偶然者。噫！其斯以爲召公歟！
translation_en:
…upon the Xia, so too could it bestow blessings upon the Zhou, renewing its mandate and thereby granting favor. Looking more recently to the Yin, whose reign lasted six hundred years, how enduring were their blessings! Yet the blessings granted to the Yin could also be granted to the Zhou: Heaven would favor them with its mandate and thereby encourage them. Equaling the Xia and also encompassing the longevity of the Yin, Heaven’s protection would be unceasing, and our reception of it likewise unceasing. Worthy to be rulers and kings, we could carry forward the glory of our illustrious predecessors. Matching the Yin and also encompassing the longevity of the Xia, the Supreme Lord’s gifts would be boundless, and our receipt of them likewise boundless. Capable of being leaders and rulers, we could rival the excellence of former dynasties. Though it is said, “Zhou’s mandate is newly bestowed,” how can we know that it will endure without alteration? Those above and below must labor diligently and show solicitude, precisely to welcome the blessings arriving in abundance [?]. Could we evade our responsibility by saying that our Zhou’s mandate need last only as long as the Xia’s? Though it is said that Zhou “received dominion over the many regions on a grand scale,” how can we ensure that it will endure far into the future without decline? Ruler and ministers must unite their hearts precisely to secure abundant blessings. Could we evade our responsibility by saying that our Zhou’s mandate need last only as long as the Yin’s? Ah! Such was the Duke of Shao’s desire that ruler and ministers pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate. His admonition may indeed be called profound, earnest, and manifestly clear.

Nevertheless, the mandate of the Supreme Lord, Heaven, rests principally upon the hearts of the people, and reverence for virtue is also the means of winning the allegiance of the common people [?]. Thus he said, “Let the king urgently revere virtue.” He also said, “I wish the king, through the common people, to receive Heaven’s enduring mandate.” When a ruler uses virtue to win the people’s allegiance [?], perfect harmony spreads its influence, and Heaven’s heart is moved to respond with trust. A reign of long duration can then gradually be attained. It was fitting that the Duke of Shao should repeatedly impress this upon the king. Thereafter, King Cheng became an excellent ruler of Zhou, and the dynasty’s generations and years both exceeded the span foretold by divination. Only then can we understand that the seasoned elder’s deliberations for the state were no casual matter. Ah! Was this not what made him the Duke of Shao!

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
詩
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除
俾爾多益以莫不庶
陳聯芳
同考試官敎諭箕批題語若重複而其中自有
脉絡此作體貼得精可以式矣
同考試官學正彭批詞意渾成而且有倫得作
詩之義
考試官敎諭黃批是能發揚忠愛之情者
===
考試官敎諭朱批典雅
臣子託天眷君之至而錫福無所不備焉蓋百
順之謂備福莫大焉詩人之祝其君者以之忠
愛之情可見矣且天保臣子有愛君無已之心
故託諸祝頌以致其願望之私若曰吾人受君
之恩渥矣莫知其所以報者亦惟望諸天耳天
之所以眷吾君者何如降鑒不遠所以扶持而
安全之者益篤其仁愛之心使之滿而不溢高
而不危將以奠之磐石之固而承藉之基恃以
punctuated:
詩

天保定爾，亦孔之固。俾爾單厚，何福不除？俾爾多益，以莫不庶。

陳聯芳

同考試官敎諭箕批：題語若重複，而其中自有脉絡。此作體貼得精，可以式矣。

同考試官學正彭批：詞意渾成，而且有倫，得作詩之義。

考試官敎諭黃批：是能發揚忠愛之情者。

考試官敎諭朱批：典雅。

臣子託天眷君之至，而錫福無所不備焉。蓋百順之謂備，福莫大焉。詩人之祝其君者以之，忠愛之情可見矣。且《天保》，臣子有愛君無已之心，故託諸祝頌，以致其願望之私。若曰：吾人受君之恩渥矣，莫知其所以報者，亦惟望諸天耳。天之所以眷吾君者何如？降鑒不遠，所以扶持而安全之者，益篤其仁愛之心，使之滿而不溢，高而不危，將以奠之磐石之固，而承藉之基恃以
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Heaven protects and establishes you, with exceeding firmness. It grants you abundant bounty: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you ever greater increase, so that nothing fails to flourish.”

Chen Lianfang

Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: “The wording of the topic seems repetitive, yet it has an underlying thread. This composition grasps its meaning with precision and may serve as a model.”

Associate Examiner Peng, School Instructor, comments: “Expression and meaning form an integrated whole, and the argument is orderly. It captures the intent behind the composition of the ode.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “This succeeds in bringing forth feelings of loyalty and love.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

The subject expresses through Heaven the utmost solicitude for his ruler, so that the blessings bestowed upon him lack nothing. For completeness means that all things accord with one's wishes; no blessing is greater than this. This is what the poet invokes in blessing his ruler, and his feelings of loyalty and love are evident therein. In “Heaven Protects You” (Tian bao), the subject's love for his ruler knows no end. He therefore entrusts his heartfelt hopes to blessings and praise. It is as though he were saying: “We have received our ruler's abundant favor. Not knowing how to repay it, we can only look to Heaven. How does Heaven cherish our ruler? Its watchful gaze from above is never far away. In supporting him and keeping him secure, Heaven makes its benevolent love ever more profound, allowing him to be full without overflowing and exalted without peril. It will establish him as firmly as a massive rock, while the foundation that supports him may be relied upon to…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
無恐矣臨下有赫所以保右而申命之者益隆
其眷顧之私使之身其用康國其用寧將以措
之泰山之安而帝位之履賴以不疚矣所以保
定之者何其固耶蓋使爾之受福也與時俱積
旣斂之而盡厚矣然厚薄之勢相乗者也所受
者一或不繼則厚者有時而薄非福之全也其
必有秩之祐默運夫循環之端前之所錫方除
其舊而後之所繼已布其新翕受有無方之益
而美利獲厚終之慶是所以成其盡厚者益不
===
可窮矣又何有不除乎又使爾之受福也日進
無疆旣集之而多益矣然損益之機相形者也
所受者一有不繼則益者有時而損非福之備
也其必多助之至引之爲盛大之休在此者惟
見其有餘而在彼者非見其不足天心篤栽培
之理而造化無多取之忌是所以成其多益者
愈不可紀矣又何有不庶乎至是則吾君諸福
之物爲始備而吾人願望之私亦庶乎少慰矣
大抵人君之所奉若者天道也則其所以欽承
punctuated:
無恐矣。臨下有赫，所以保右而申命之者，益隆其眷顧之私，使之身其用康，國其用寧，將以措之泰山之安，而帝位之履賴以不疚矣。所以保定之者，何其固耶！蓋使爾之受福也，與時俱積，旣斂之而盡厚矣。然厚薄之勢相乗者也，所受者一或不繼，則厚者有時而薄，非福之全也。其必有秩之祐，默運夫循環之端，前之所錫方除其舊，而後之所繼已布其新，翕受有無方之益，而美利獲厚終之慶，是所以成其盡厚者，益不可窮矣。又何有不除乎？又使爾之受福也，日進無疆，旣集之而多益矣。然損益之機相形者也，所受者一有不繼，則益者有時而損，非福之備也。其必多助之至，引之爲盛大之休，在此者惟見其有餘，而在彼者非見其不足。天心篤栽培之理，而造化無多取之忌，是所以成其多益者，愈不可紀矣。又何有不庶乎？至是，則吾君諸福之物爲始備，而吾人願望之私亦庶乎少慰矣。
大抵人君之所奉若者，天道也，則其所以欽承
translation_en:
…and thus be free from fear. Heaven looks down upon those below with awe-inspiring majesty. In protecting and aiding our ruler and renewing its mandate, it deepens its particular solicitude for him, granting him personal well-being and his state tranquility. It will establish him in security like that of Mount Tai, so that his occupation of the imperial throne may thereby remain free from harm. How firm is the protection by which Heaven secures him! It causes your blessings to accumulate with time; gathered together, they have already become abundant in every respect. Yet abundance and scarcity succeed one another. If what you receive should ever cease, abundance may in time become scarcity: this would not be the fullness of blessing. Surely Heaven’s ordered assistance must silently set the cycle in motion: just as its earlier gifts pass out of their old state, those that follow are already spread anew. In receiving them all, you gain increase without limit, and these splendid benefits bring the joy of abundance enduring to the end. Thus, what brings their abundance to fulfillment becomes ever more inexhaustible. How, then, could there be any failure of renewal?

Again, Heaven causes the blessings you receive to increase daily without bounds; gathered together, they have already multiplied greatly. Yet the workings of decrease and increase manifest themselves in relation to one another. If what you receive should ever cease, increase may in time turn to decrease: this would not be the completeness of blessing. Surely the utmost abundance of assistance must lead you onward to great and flourishing good fortune. On this side one sees only a surplus, while on the other one sees no deficiency. Heaven’s heart steadfastly upholds the principle of nurturing growth, and the work of creation harbors no resentment at your receiving much. Thus, what brings this manifold increase to fulfillment becomes ever more beyond reckoning. How, then, could there be any failure of abundance? Only at this point are the various blessings of our ruler complete, and our own heartfelt hopes may perhaps find some small consolation.

Generally speaking, what a ruler reverently follows is the Way of Heaven; thus, that which he reverently receives …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之者亦惟天之明命而已天保臣子必備言其
天福之隆得無侈乎噫雖其願望之深媚愛之
至其從諷諫矣乎故召公卷阿之告必本於壽
考福祿之盛而書以斂時五福爲武王告蓋欲
履其盛者思以保其終而以克負荷者當自得
之於言意之表此固詩人之意也其得告君之
體可與言忠愛者與
倬彼雲漢爲章于天周王壽考遐不作人
追琢其章金玉其相勉勉我王綱紀四
===
方
黃星耀
同考試官教諭龔批作人綱紀之義發揮殆
盡錄之
同考試官學正彭批此必有得於
聖化者可與言詩矣
考試官教諭黃批渾然成章可誦
考試官教諭朱批文有典則
詩人兩興美聖人之德自其化人統人者言之
punctuated:
之者，亦惟天之明命而已。《天保》，臣子必備言其天福之隆，得無侈乎？噫！雖其願望之深、媚愛之至，其從諷諫矣乎？故召公《卷阿》之告，必本於壽考福祿之盛，而《書》以斂時五福爲武王告。蓋欲履其盛者思以保其終，而以克負荷者當自得之於言意之表。此固詩人之意也。其得告君之體，可與言忠愛者與！
倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
黃星耀
同考試官教諭龔批：作人綱紀之義，發揮殆盡，錄之。
同考試官學正彭批：此必有得於聖化者，可與言詩矣。
考試官教諭黃批：渾然成章，可誦。
考試官教諭朱批：文有典則。
詩人兩興，美聖人之德，自其化人統人者言之
translation_en:
…what he reverently receives is simply Heaven’s luminous mandate. In “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao), the ministers describe fully the abundance of Heaven’s blessings upon their lord: is this not extravagant? Ah! Profound though their hopes and utmost though their affectionate devotion may be, might they also be offering indirect admonition [?]? Thus, the Duke of Shao’s counsel in “Winding Hills” (Juan’e) necessarily takes as its foundation abundant longevity, blessings, and emoluments; and the Book of Documents counsels King Wu to “gather these five blessings.” The intention is that one enjoying such abundance should consider how to preserve it to the end, while one capable of shouldering the burden should grasp this for himself beyond the explicit words. This was indeed the poet’s intention. Having attained the proper manner of addressing a ruler, he is surely someone with whom one may discuss loyalty and love!
How vast that River of Clouds, forming a pattern in Heaven! Long-lived is the king of Zhou: why would he not nurture men of talent? Chiselled and polished is his pattern; gold and jade are his substance. Diligently our king orders and regulates the four quarters.
Huang Xingyao.
Associate Examiner Gong, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of nurturing men of talent and ordering the realm is developed almost exhaustively. Include this essay.”
Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “This must be someone who has gained an understanding of the sage’s transforming influence. One may discuss the Odes with him.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The composition forms a harmonious whole and merits recitation.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The writing accords with classical standards.”
Through two evocative comparisons, the poet praises the sage’s virtue, speaking of his transformation and governance of the people…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也蓋德者治化之本也周王之德久而且純其
能振作綱紀天下也宜哉此詩人所以歌咏之
也其託興之意若曰在天皆成象也惟玆有取
於雲漢之爲章焉其懸象也倬然其甚大其著
明也煥乎其有章在天之文於斯爲至矣况我
文王之德之久不足以成天下之化乎蓋民風
之所尚恒視乎所感之淺深也我周王至德之
所感召而必得其壽皇天之所眷命而多歷年
所是壽考也者所以運敎思於無窮者也故在
===
上者鼓舞作興有以神其機於無間而在下者
敏德遷善有以翼其進於日新大以成大小以
成小而一代人文之運於是乎開之矣聖人之
所以化人者蓋有所自如此在物皆有文質也
惟玆有取於文質之至者焉追琢以爲章而盡
人之巧也金玉以爲相而渾乎天成也在物之
理於是爲至矣况我文王之德之純而不足以
維天下之治乎蓋人心之所向恒視乎君德之
純貳也惟我周王持自强不息之心而恒以一
punctuated:
也。蓋德者，治化之本也。周王之德，久而且純，其能振作綱紀天下也，宜哉！此詩人所以歌咏之也。其託興之意，若曰：在天皆成象也，惟玆有取於雲漢之爲章焉。其懸象也，倬然其甚大；其著明也，煥乎其有章。在天之文，於斯爲至矣。况我文王之德之久，不足以成天下之化乎？蓋民風之所尚，恒視乎所感之淺深也。我周王至德之所感召，而必得其壽；皇天之所眷命，而多歷年所。是壽考也者，所以運敎思於無窮者也。故在上者鼓舞作興，有以神其機於無間；而在下者敏德遷善，有以翼其進於日新。大以成大，小以成小，而一代人文之運，於是乎開之矣。聖人之所以化人者，蓋有所自如此。
在物皆有文質也，惟玆有取於文質之至者焉。追琢以爲章，而盡人之巧也；金玉以爲相，而渾乎天成也。在物之理，於是爲至矣。况我文王之德之純，而不足以維天下之治乎？蓋人心之所向，恒視乎君德之純貳也。惟我周王持自强不息之心，而恒以一
translation_en:
…Such is the case. Virtue is the foundation of government and moral transformation. The Zhou king’s virtue was both enduring and pure: how fitting that he could rouse the world and bring it into order! This is why the poet sang his praises. The meaning conveyed through his evocative imagery is as if to say: all things in heaven form celestial figures, but here the patterned brilliance of the Milky Way is singled out. Suspended in the heavens, it is lofty and vast; shining forth, it displays a radiant pattern. Here the beauty of heaven reaches its utmost expression. How, then, could the enduring virtue of our King Wen fail to bring about the moral transformation of the world? What the people esteem in their customs always depends upon how deeply they have been moved. The supreme virtue of our Zhou king called forth a response that assured him longevity; august Heaven bestowed its favor and mandate upon him, granting him many years. This longevity was what enabled him to extend his thought for instruction without end. Thus those above inspired and roused the people, exercising the workings of transformation with wondrous and uninterrupted efficacy; those below diligently cultivated virtue and turned toward goodness, advancing with renewed progress each day. Those of great capacity fulfilled their great potential, and those of lesser capacity fulfilled their lesser potential. Thus an era of cultural flourishing began. Such was the source from which the sage’s transformation of the people arose.
All things possess both adornment and substance, but here those in which adornment and substance attain perfection are singled out. Chasing and carving create their patterns, exhausting the resources of human skill; gold and jade form their substance, whole and seemingly fashioned by Heaven. Here the principles embodied in things reach their utmost expression. How, then, could the purity of our King Wen’s virtue fail to sustain order throughout the world? The allegiance of people’s hearts always depends upon whether their ruler’s virtue is pure or divided. Our Zhou king alone maintained a resolve for unceasing self-strengthening and remained constant in a single…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
德操憂勤惕若之念而健以體天是勉勉也者
所以運王道於無外者也是故在上者勵精明
作有以握其機於至一而在下者範圍曲成有
以萃其渙於大同綱則常張紀則常理而天下
一統之盛於是乎基之矣聖人之所以治人者
蓋有所本又如此矣是則舉天下而皆在於綱
紀敎化之中則髦士之趨六師之及其所得於
此者多矣文王之德之盛不亦徵諸是哉抑觀
周道之昌自文王要其成盛德大業後世無以
===
加矣而要其所以自得則自敬始故曰敬止曰
勉勉曰亹亹此純亦不已也惟不已故敎化之
所以成綱紀之所由布而周之興也勃焉自此
而執競之武王勉敬之成王因之以爲祈天永
命之基皆此道也故古今致盛治而爲天下後
世之所不可幾及者未甞不自敬得之豈但文
王爲然
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕公
punctuated:
德，操憂勤惕若之念，而健以體天，是勉勉也者，所以運王道於無外者也。是故在上者勵精明作，有以握其機於至一；而在下者範圍曲成，有以萃其渙於大同。綱則常張，紀則常理，而天下一統之盛於是乎基之矣。聖人之所以治人者，蓋有所本，又如此矣。是則舉天下而皆在於綱紀敎化之中，則髦士之趨、六師之及，其所得於此者多矣。文王之德之盛，不亦徵諸是哉？抑觀周道之昌自文王，要其成，盛德大業，後世無以加矣。而要其所以自得，則自敬始。故曰「敬止」，曰「勉勉」，曰「亹亹」，此純亦不已也。惟不已，故敎化之所以成、綱紀之所由布，而周之興也勃焉。自此而執競之武王、勉敬之成王，因之以爲祈天永命之基，皆此道也。故古今致盛治而爲天下後世之所不可幾及者，未甞不自敬得之，豈但文王爲然？

春秋

秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕公
translation_en:
…in virtue, he maintained a spirit of anxious diligence and vigilance, vigorously embodying Heaven. This unremitting exertion was how he extended the kingly Way everywhere, leaving nothing outside it. Thus those above devoted their energies to enlightened action, grasping the pivotal principle in its utmost unity; those below provided guidance and brought all things to fulfillment according to their circumstances, gathering what was dispersed into great concord. The guiding cords were always stretched taut, the ordering threads always kept straight: here were laid the foundations of the flourishing unity of all under Heaven. Such, again, was the foundation upon which the sage governed others. With all under Heaven encompassed within these ordering principles and moral transformation, both the direction taken by eminent scholars and the reach of the six armies owed much to this. Is not the fullness of King Wen’s virtue demonstrated here?

Moreover, consider how the flourishing of Zhou’s Way began with King Wen. Looking at its consummation, later ages could add nothing to its abundant virtue and great achievements. Yet, tracing how he attained these things within himself, we find that he began with reverence. Hence the expressions “abiding in reverence,” “unremitting in exertion,” and “assiduously diligent”: this purity, too, never ceased. Precisely because it never ceased, moral transformation was accomplished, the principles of order were spread abroad, and Zhou rose vigorously. Thereafter, King Wu, “mighty in strength,” and King Cheng, diligent in reverence, followed this as the foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. All followed this same Way. Thus, in ancient times and today, those who have achieved such flourishing government that none in the world or in later ages could approach it have invariably attained it through reverence. How could King Wen alone have been so?

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The duke…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖公四年〕
林貞相
同考試官教諭羅批齊桓主盟而敢專征他尚
何責焉詞嚴義正無踰此作
考試官教諭黃批得正名本意
考試官教諭朱批簡嚴
春秋兩紀兵事有序外君主兵而見其罪有序
伯主專征而見其罪夫諸侯不得主兵伯主不
===
得專征皆分之所在也郕與楚之伐也而春秋
烏可逭其罪哉且甞攷周官而知有周之所以
制兵矣天子以一人而莅萬邦故有用天下諸
侯以討不庭焉未聞諸侯而主諸侯之兵也方
伯以六服而承天子故有奉天子明命以討不
庭焉未聞方伯而專方伯之兵也春秋而降周
制不存列國用兵恒隨時之所變以為上下蓋
自霸圖之未成也而權無所統則以諸侯而自
用其兵有如宋桓之伐郕郕附庸之小邦伐之
punctuated:
會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
林貞相
同考試官教諭羅批：「齊桓主盟而敢專征，他尚何責焉？詞嚴義正，無踰此作。」
考試官教諭黃批：「得正名本意。」
考試官教諭朱批：「簡嚴。」
春秋兩紀兵事，有序外君主兵而見其罪，有序伯主專征而見其罪。夫諸侯不得主兵，伯主不得專征，皆分之所在也。郕與楚之伐也，而春秋烏可逭其罪哉？且甞攷周官，而知有周之所以制兵矣。天子以一人而莅萬邦，故有用天下諸侯以討不庭焉，未聞諸侯而主諸侯之兵也。方伯以六服而承天子，故有奉天子明命以討不庭焉，未聞方伯而專方伯之兵也。春秋而降，周制不存，列國用兵，恒隨時之所變以為上下。蓋自霸圖之未成也，而權無所統，則以諸侯而自用其兵，有如宋桓之伐郕。郕，附庸之小邦，伐之
translation_en:
…met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to invade Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕
Lin Zhenxiang
Associate Examiner Luo, an Instructor, comments: “Duke Huan of Qi presided over the covenant yet dared to undertake punitive campaigns on his own authority. What further grounds for reproach need one seek? Stern in wording and correct in principle: no composition surpasses this one.”
Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: “Grasps the underlying intent of rectifying names.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Concise and rigorous.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records two military affairs: in one, it relates how rulers of other states commanded troops and thereby reveals their guilt; in the other, it relates how a hegemon undertook a punitive campaign on his own authority and thereby reveals his guilt. That the feudal lords may not assume command of armies, and that a hegemon may not undertake punitive campaigns on his own authority, are both matters of their allotted duties. In the attacks on Cheng [?] and Chu, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals let their guilt pass uncondemned?
I have examined the Offices of Zhou and thus learned how the Zhou regulated military affairs. The Son of Heaven, as one man, presided over the myriad states; hence he employed the feudal lords of the realm to chastise those who failed to appear at his court. Never have I heard that a feudal lord could command the armies of the other feudal lords. A regional chief served the Son of Heaven through the six zones of service; hence he carried out the Son of Heaven’s explicit commands to chastise those who failed to appear at court. Never have I heard that a regional chief could exercise independent control over the forces under his authority.
From the Spring and Autumn period onward, the institutions of Zhou no longer endured. The various states, in employing troops, continually adjusted their conduct to changing circumstances. Before hegemonic rule had taken shape, authority had no unifying center, and feudal lords therefore employed their armies on their own initiative. Such was Duke Huan of Song’s attack on Cheng [?; the examination passage names Ni]. Cheng was a small dependent state; to attack it…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
非也然而宋人所以伐之者一出於已而未甞
有王朝司馬之與聞牙璋無起旅之文虎符無
興兵之制徇其所私而威福自便人臣懷靖共
之心者不爲此矣不然則弊黼九章之器宋之
所以承先王也是皆所以尊王章勵臣節而桓
之專恣至此何有一念本原之思乎春秋於郕
之伐也而以宋爲主兵主兵豈諸侯事哉而桓
之罪自明矣迨霸圖之已就也而權有所歸則
以方伯而并徵其兵有如齊桓之伐楚楚憑陵
===
之大邦伐之宜也然而齊桓所以伐之者一專
於已而未甞有王朝司馬之錫命在庭無弓矢
之賜在廟無鈇鉞之頒犯其所禁而匡合是圖
人臣懷畏抑之心者不爲此矣不然則五侯九
伯之命齊之所以承先王也是正所以尊王靈
肅侯度而桓之專擅至此何甞一念冠履之思
乎春秋於楚之伐也而以齊爲專征專征豈方
伯事哉而桓公之罪又明矣雖然宋之伐郕不
足論也齊之圖霸功也安中夏攘外夷無求以
punctuated:
非也。然而宋人所以伐之者，一出於已，而未甞有王朝司馬之與聞。牙璋無起旅之文，虎符無興兵之制，徇其所私而威福自便，人臣懷靖共之心者不爲此矣。不然，則弊黼九章之器，宋之所以承先王也，是皆所以尊王章、勵臣節，而桓之專恣至此，何有一念本原之思乎？春秋於郕之伐也，而以宋爲主兵，主兵豈諸侯事哉？而桓之罪自明矣。

迨霸圖之已就也，而權有所歸，則以方伯而并徵其兵。有如齊桓之伐楚，楚憑陵之大邦，伐之宜也。然而齊桓所以伐之者，一專於已，而未甞有王朝司馬之錫命。在庭無弓矢之賜，在廟無鈇鉞之頒，犯其所禁而匡合是圖，人臣懷畏抑之心者不爲此矣。不然，則五侯九伯之命，齊之所以承先王也，是正所以尊王靈、肅侯度，而桓之專擅至此，何甞一念冠履之思乎？春秋於楚之伐也，而以齊爲專征，專征豈方伯事哉？而桓公之罪又明矣。

雖然，宋之伐郕不足論也。齊之圖霸，功也，安中夏，攘外夷，無求以
translation_en:
…was wrong. Yet the men of Song undertook this attack entirely on their own initiative, without the Minister of War at the royal court ever being informed. There was no written authorization on a toothed jade tablet to mobilize troops, nor any warrant conveyed by a tiger tally to raise an army. They pursued their private interests and exercised punitive and beneficent power at their own discretion. A subject who cherished a spirit of dutiful respect would not have acted thus. Moreover, the worn axe-patterned regalia bearing nine emblems [?] were what Song had received from the former kings. These all served to honor royal institutions and strengthen a subject’s fidelity. Yet Huan’s arbitrary self-indulgence reached such a point: did he give even a moment’s thought to the source of his authority? In its account of the attack on Cheng, the Spring and Autumn Annals treats Song as assuming command of the army. But is command of the army the business of a feudal lord? Huan’s guilt is thus self-evident.

Once the hegemonic enterprise had been established and authority had acquired a center, a regional overlord would levy the forces of the other lords together with his own. Such was Duke Huan of Qi’s attack on Chu. Chu was a great state that bullied others, and attacking it was appropriate. Yet Duke Huan of Qi undertook the attack entirely on his own authority, without ever receiving a command from the Minister of War at the royal court. No bows and arrows were bestowed upon him in the royal court; no battle-axes were conferred upon him in the ancestral temple. He violated the prohibitions binding him while seeking to set the realm in order and unite the lords. A subject who cherished reverence and restraint would not have acted thus. Moreover, the commission concerning the five ranks of lords and the nine regional chiefs was what Qi had received from the former kings. Its very purpose was to honor royal majesty and enforce the rules governing the lords. Yet Huan’s usurpation of authority reached such a point: did he ever give even a moment’s thought to the distinction between cap and shoes—that is, between superior and subordinate? In its account of the attack on Chu, the Spring and Autumn Annals treats Qi as undertaking a punitive expedition on its own authority. But is an independent punitive expedition the business of a regional overlord? Duke Huan’s guilt is thus also clear.

Nevertheless, Song’s attack on Cheng scarcely merits discussion. Qi’s pursuit of hegemony was an achievement: it brought peace to the central states and repelled the foreign peoples, seeking nothing [?], in order to …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
尊王爲名而陘亭之師徵王貢問王祭焉此尊
王至大也舉天下至大之名而不能仗天下之
大義以大分臨之宜楚之能爲辭也夫苟知春
秋之法諸侯無專兵方伯無專征舉天下之大
而唯一人之命是從天下可大定矣吁此春秋
所以爲經世也
吳子使札來聘襄公二十有九年夏曹公
孫會自鄭出奔宋昭公二十年
陳奎
===
同考試官教諭羅批會傳成文長於褒貶者
考試官教諭黃批開闔有法
考試官教諭朱批莊重
春秋以過中貶辭國之賢以世類進去國之士
此見季札爲賢者之過故責之備公孫會爲賢
者之後故善之長也其春秋因事褒貶之教乎
且札吳之公子也聞樂知德吾嘗聞其賢矣賢
而特書春秋之法經於札之來聘獨以名紀者
何蓋君子遇變而能通故道行而無弊札之在
punctuated:
尊王爲名，而陘亭之師，徵王貢，問王祭焉，此尊王至大也。舉天下至大之名，而不能仗天下之大義以大分臨之，宜楚之能爲辭也。夫苟知春秋之法，諸侯無專兵，方伯無專征，舉天下之大，而唯一人之命是從，天下可大定矣。吁！此春秋所以爲經世也。
「吳子使札來聘。」襄公二十有九年夏。「曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。」昭公二十年。
陳奎
同考試官教諭羅批：「會傳成文，長於褒貶者。」
考試官教諭黃批：「開闔有法。」
考試官教諭朱批：「莊重。」
春秋以過中貶辭國之賢，以世類進去國之士。此見季札爲賢者之過，故責之備；公孫會爲賢者之後，故善之長也。其春秋因事褒貶之教乎？且札，吳之公子也，聞樂知德，吾嘗聞其賢矣。賢而特書，春秋之法。經於札之來聘，獨以名紀者，何？蓋君子遇變而能通，故道行而無弊。札之在
translation_en:
…with “honoring the king” as his avowed purpose. In the campaign at Xingting, he demanded the tribute owed to the king and questioned Chu about the royal sacrifices: these were matters of the greatest importance in honoring the king. Yet while invoking the greatest cause under Heaven, he could not uphold the great righteousness of the realm and confront Chu on the basis of the fundamental distinctions of rank. It is therefore understandable that Chu could offer a rebuttal. If only the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals were understood—that the feudal lords may not independently deploy armies, and regional overlords may not independently undertake punitive campaigns—then throughout the vast realm, only the commands of the One Man, the king, would be obeyed, and all under Heaven could enjoy lasting peace. Ah! This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals serves to order the world.
“The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit to our court.” Summer, the twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang. “Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng to Song.” The twentieth year of Duke Zhao.
Chen Kui.
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “He brings together the commentaries to form his essay and excels at praise and blame.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The unfolding and gathering of the argument follow a method.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Dignified and grave.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals censures a worthy man who declined rulership for exceeding the mean, while according favorable treatment to a man who left his state on account of his lineage. This shows that Ji Zha committed the error of a worthy man, and so was held to the highest standard; Gongsun Hui was a descendant of a worthy man, and so the favorable judgment was extended to him. Is this not the teaching of praise and blame that the Spring and Autumn Annals applies according to circumstances?
Now Zha was a prince of Wu. By hearing music, he understood virtue; I have indeed heard of his worthiness. To give a worthy man special mention is a principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, when recording Zha’s diplomatic visit, does the classic identify him solely by his personal name? A gentleman can adapt when confronted with changed circumstances; thus the Way is put into practice without harmful consequences. As for Zha’s position in…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
吳非猶泰伯之於周夷齊之於孤竹也札非壽
夢之所賢者乎使札也承父兄之志以慰其付
託之重則邦其永孚於休胡乃徇狷介之節而
昧大中之道效匹夫之爲而陷賢智之過則延
陵之逃不免爲於陵之操而專諸之禍兆矣噫
以札而非賢也則固無足責矣札而誠賢也其
可使之有過中之行也哉故因其來聘而特以
名稱所謂責賢之備者以此若會者曹之大夫
也待放而奔是亦人臣之常耳常事不書而春
===
秋之法經於會之出奔賢以公孫者何蓋君子
節立而不毀故名遠而彌光曹之有子臧猶唐
之有巢許虞之有務光也會非子臧之後裔乎
使會也懷利祿之榮有忝於箕裘之紹則世德
弗能作求今也自鄭而待深得察罪之宜賜玦
而奔尤協去國之禮則守道不失適光於守節
無求而甘棠之愛永矣噫以會而匪臧也則亦
無足錄矣會而有臧也其可使之泯滅無聞也
哉故因其出奔而特稱公孫所謂善善之長者
punctuated:
吳，非猶泰伯之於周、夷齊之於孤竹也。札非壽夢之所賢者乎？使札也承父兄之志，以慰其付託之重，則邦其永孚於休。胡乃徇狷介之節，而昧大中之道，效匹夫之爲，而陷賢智之過？則延陵之逃，不免爲於陵之操，而專諸之禍兆矣。噫！以札而非賢也，則固無足責矣；札而誠賢也，其可使之有過中之行也哉？故因其來聘而特以名稱，所謂責賢之備者以此。
若會者，曹之大夫也。待放而奔，是亦人臣之常耳。常事不書，而春秋之法，經於會之出奔，賢以公孫者何？蓋君子節立而不毀，故名遠而彌光。曹之有子臧，猶唐之有巢許、虞之有務光也。會非子臧之後裔乎？使會也懷利祿之榮，有忝於箕裘之紹，則世德弗能作求。今也自鄭而待，深得察罪之宜；賜玦而奔，尤協去國之禮。則守道不失，適光於守節無求，而甘棠之愛永矣。噫！以會而匪臧也，則亦無足錄矣；會而有臧也，其可使之泯滅無聞也哉？故因其出奔而特稱公孫，所謂善善之長者
translation_en:
…in Wu, [Ji Zha’s position] was unlike that of Taibo in Zhou or Boyi and Shuqi in Guzhu. Was Zha not the one whom Shoumeng deemed worthy? Had Zha carried on the intentions of his father and elder brothers, fulfilling the weighty trust they placed in him, the state might have enjoyed enduring prosperity. Why, then, did he cling to an aloof integrity while failing to understand the great way of the Mean, imitate the conduct of a private individual, and fall into the error of the worthy and wise who go too far? Thus the flight of the lord of Yanling inevitably became like the scrupulous withdrawal of the recluse of Yuling, and already foreshadowed the calamity wrought by Zhuan Zhu. Alas! If Zha were not worthy, there would indeed be no reason to reproach him. But if Zha truly was worthy, could he be allowed conduct that transgressed the Mean? Hence, on the occasion of his diplomatic visit, the text pointedly calls him by his personal name. This is what is meant by demanding completeness of virtue from the worthy.
As for Hui, he was a grand master of Cao. To await dismissal and then flee was simply ordinary conduct for a minister. Ordinary events are not recorded; why, then, under the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, does the Classic honor Hui by calling him “ducal grandson” when recording his flight? When a gentleman establishes his integrity and does not compromise it, his reputation travels far and shines ever brighter. Cao’s possession of Zizang was like Tang’s possession of Chao Fu and Xu You, or Yu’s possession of Wu Guang [?]. Was Hui not a descendant of Zizang? Had Hui cherished the glory of profit and official emoluments, disgracing his inherited calling, he could not have carried forward his family’s ancestral virtue. Now, however, he waited in Zheng [?], fully observing the proper course of awaiting judgment upon his offense; when given a jade ring with a break in it, signaling dismissal, he fled, conforming especially well to the ritual proprieties of leaving one’s state. By holding to the Way without deviation, he brought further glory to the integrity that seeks no reward, perpetuating the affection for ancestral virtue evoked by the sweet pear tree. Alas! If Hui were not good, there would likewise be no reason to record him. But if Hui possessed goodness, could he be allowed to disappear without being heard of? Hence, on the occasion of his flight, the text specifically calls him “ducal grandson.” This is what is meant by extending the honoring of goodness to later generations…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
以此是則均一辭國也在季札則責諸其身在
子臧則錄諸其後聖人豈有厚薄於其間哉無
亦以中道防之耳雖然臧固無議矣札其可少
乎當勢利喧豗之時而能砥礪名節誠足以廉
頑立懦觀其掛劔示信退師全名其所見者甚
定也豈與利疚勢回盛衰改節者比哉使國人
能成其志則亦可以垂名於不替矣惜乎所值
之非不得以遂其附於子臧之志也然則君子
責人固所當備而取人尤可不恕也哉
===
禮記
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
楊棐
同考試官教諭羅 批 聖人心通天地故禮序樂
和功用隆懋此作根極理要而辭復昌達錄之以式
考試官教諭黃 批 精醇明鬯非苟作者
punctuated:
以此。是則均一辭國也，在季札則責諸其身，在子臧則錄諸其後，聖人豈有厚薄於其間哉？無亦以中道防之耳。雖然，臧固無議矣，札其可少乎？當勢利喧豗之時，而能砥礪名節，誠足以廉頑立懦。觀其掛劔示信，退師全名，其所見者甚定也，豈與利疚勢回、盛衰改節者比哉？使國人能成其志，則亦可以垂名於不替矣。惜乎所值之非，不得以遂其附於子臧之志也。然則君子責人固所當備，而取人尤可不恕也哉？

禮記
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神，如此則四海之內合敬同愛矣。
楊棐

同考試官教諭羅批：聖人心通天地，故禮序樂和，功用隆懋。此作根極理要，而辭復昌達，錄之以式。
考試官教諭黃批：精醇明鬯，非苟作者。
translation_en:
…is for this reason. Thus, although both alike declined rulership, in Ji Zha’s case the Sage held the man himself accountable, whereas in Zizang’s case he accorded recognition to his descendant. Could the Sage have favored one over the other? Surely he was merely establishing safeguards through the middle way. Nevertheless, although Zizang is beyond criticism, can Zha be belittled? Amid the clamor for power and profit, he could temper and preserve his reputation and integrity: this was indeed enough to make the avaricious honest and the irresolute firm. Consider how he hung up his sword to demonstrate his faithfulness and withdrew his army to preserve his good name. His convictions were deeply settled. How could he be compared with those whom profit corrupts and power deflects, who change their principles as fortunes rise and fall? Had the people of his state enabled him to fulfill his purpose, he too could have left an enduring name. Alas, the adverse circumstances he encountered prevented him from fulfilling his aspiration to follow Zizang’s example. Thus, although a gentleman should demand completeness in others, when recognizing their merits, must he not be especially understanding?

Record of Rites
“Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the measured order of Heaven and Earth. Through harmony, the myriad things suffer no loss; through measured order, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the visible realm there are rites and music; in the unseen realm there are ghosts and spirits. Thus, all within the Four Seas are united in reverence and share in love.”
Yang Fei

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The sage’s mind communicates with Heaven and Earth; hence ritual brings order and music brings harmony, with magnificent and abundant effects. This composition reaches to the roots of essential principles, and its language is also rich and fluent. It is selected to serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Refined, pure, clear, and lucid: this is no carelessly composed work.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭朱批〔整雅〕
論禮樂之成功合造化而感人心也蓋聖人之
禮樂與天地相為流通者也則其感人心也豈
容已哉且夫不觀禮樂之功用極其隆無以見
聖人之制作極其善何以言之樂一也謂之大
樂者和之至而非徒假於聲容之末者也欣喜
歡愛之情脗合乎絪縕化醇之妙即天地自然
之和焉禮一也謂之大禮者序之至而非徒事
乎器數之煩者也親疎貴賤之制默契乎高下
===
散殊之理即天地自然之節焉夫惟其和之同
也故能以和召和昭宣化育而百物為之咸若
無或失者矣夫惟其節之同也故能以序賛序
節事天地而百神為之受職無弗享者矣是則
禮樂鬼神其致一也自其明而在聖人之制作
言之則有禮樂禮樂者有迹之鬼神也自其幽
而在天地之功用言之則有鬼神鬼神者無形
之禮樂也其合造化如此是天地且弗違而況
於人乎吾見大禮之所感召興起其退讓之風
punctuated:
考試官教諭朱批〔整雅〕。

論禮樂之成功，合造化而感人心也。蓋聖人之禮樂，與天地相為流通者也，則其感人心也，豈容已哉？且夫不觀禮樂之功用極其隆，無以見聖人之制作極其善。何以言之？樂一也，謂之大樂者，和之至，而非徒假於聲容之末者也。欣喜歡愛之情，脗合乎絪縕化醇之妙，即天地自然之和焉。禮一也，謂之大禮者，序之至，而非徒事乎器數之煩者也。親疎貴賤之制，默契乎高下散殊之理，即天地自然之節焉。夫惟其和之同也，故能以和召和，昭宣化育，而百物為之咸若，無或失者矣。夫惟其節之同也，故能以序賛序，節事天地，而百神為之受職，無弗享者矣。是則禮樂鬼神，其致一也。自其明而在聖人之制作言之，則有禮樂；禮樂者，有迹之鬼神也。自其幽而在天地之功用言之，則有鬼神；鬼神者，無形之禮樂也。其合造化如此，是天地且弗違，而況於人乎？吾見大禮之所感召，興起其退讓之風
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔Orderly and elegant.〕

In considering the achievements of ritual and music, we find that they accord with the processes of creation and transformation and move human hearts. The sages’ ritual and music circulate in mutual communion with Heaven and Earth; how, then, could their influence on human hearts ever cease? Moreover, unless we observe the utmost grandeur of the workings of ritual and music, we cannot perceive the utmost excellence of the sages’ institutions. How may this be explained? Music is one, yet what is called great music is harmony brought to perfection, not merely something dependent on the outward details of sound and appearance. The feelings of delight, joy, gladness, and love accord precisely with the marvelous intermingling of cosmic forces that transforms things into their full substance: this is the spontaneous harmony of Heaven and Earth. Ritual is one, yet what is called great ritual is order brought to perfection, not merely an occupation with the complexities of vessels and prescribed quantities. Its regulations distinguishing close from distant relations and noble from humble tacitly accord with the principle by which things are differentiated as high and low: this is the spontaneous articulation of Heaven and Earth. Precisely because its harmony is the same as theirs, it can summon harmony through harmony, manifesting and extending transformation and nurture, so that all things flourish accordingly and none goes astray. Precisely because its articulation is the same as theirs, it can assist order through order and regulate service to Heaven and Earth, so that the many spirits receive their duties and none fails to partake of the offerings. Thus ritual, music, and the spirits all have a single ultimate operation. Viewed in their manifest aspect, embodied in the sages’ institutions, there are ritual and music: ritual and music are the spirits with perceptible traces. Viewed in their hidden aspect, embodied in the workings of Heaven and Earth, there are the spirits: the spirits are ritual and music without visible form. Such is their accord with creation and transformation. If even Heaven and Earth do not run counter to them, how much less could human beings? I see that great ritual, through its power to move and summon people, brings forth a custom of yielding and deference …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
四海雖大莫不有序有等而相接一於敬矣大
樂之所潛孚敦尚其仁厚之俗四海雖遠莫不
和親和順而相與一於愛矣由是言之禮樂成
功之大自有不可誣者謂非達天德之聖人其
孰能當之雖然要之皆出於吾心耳蓋聖人之
心與天地本同一理其始也法天地以為禮樂
終則以禮樂而賛天地至於天地官萬物育則
其功化之極固有不期然而然者故曰吾之心
正則天地之心亦正吾之氣順則天地之氣亦
===
順兩間之妙用莫有出於此心之外者此其所
以與天地參也嗚呼先王之道禮樂可謂盛矣
君子力此二者以南面而立夫是以天下
太平也
李遇春
同考試官教諭羅批〔由身達治天人合一之學〕
〔正如此發明透徹無踰此作〕
考試官教諭黃批〔峻潔得體〕
考試官教諭朱批〔淵朗〕
punctuated:
四海雖大，莫不有序有等，而相接一於敬矣。大樂之所潛孚，敦尚其仁厚之俗，四海雖遠，莫不和親和順，而相與一於愛矣。由是言之，禮樂成功之大，自有不可誣者。謂非達天德之聖人，其孰能當之？雖然，要之皆出於吾心耳。蓋聖人之心與天地本同一理，其始也，法天地以為禮樂；終則以禮樂而賛天地。至於天地官、萬物育，則其功化之極，固有不期然而然者。故曰：「吾之心正，則天地之心亦正；吾之氣順，則天地之氣亦順。」兩間之妙用，莫有出於此心之外者，此其所以與天地參也。嗚呼！先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣！君子力此二者，以南面而立，夫是以天下太平也。
李遇春
同考試官教諭羅批〔由身達治，天人合一之學，〕〔正如此發明，透徹無踰此作。〕
考試官教諭黃批〔峻潔得體。〕
考試官教諭朱批〔淵朗。〕
translation_en:
… Vast though all within the Four Seas may be, none fail to observe order and rank, and all meet one another in reverence. Wherever great music silently wins people's trust, it fosters customs of benevolence and generosity. Distant though the lands within the Four Seas may be, none fail to live in harmony, affection, and concord, and all deal with one another in love. Viewed thus, the greatness of what rites and music accomplish is undeniable. Who but a sage who comprehends Heaven's virtue could be equal to this? Yet ultimately all this issues from our own hearts. The sage's heart and Heaven and Earth fundamentally share a single principle. At first, he models rites and music upon Heaven and Earth; ultimately, through rites and music, he assists Heaven and Earth. When Heaven and Earth take their proper stations [?] and the myriad things are nourished, the consummation of his transformative achievement comes about without being deliberately sought. Thus it is said: “When my heart is rectified, the heart of Heaven and Earth is also rectified; when my vital energy is harmonious, the vital energy of Heaven and Earth is also harmonious.” None of the wondrous workings between Heaven and Earth lies outside this heart. This is how the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Ah! In the Way of the former kings, rites and music may indeed be called magnificent! The noble man devotes himself to these two and takes his place facing south as ruler; thereby all under Heaven enjoys great peace.

Li Yuchun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “The learning that proceeds from one's own person to governance and unites Heaven and humanity should be elucidated precisely in this way. No composition surpasses this one in thoroughness and clarity.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Rigorous and polished, befitting the form.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Profound and lucid.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
君子以禮樂而爲治則天下化成矣夫禮樂出
於吾身致治之本也君子舉而措諸天下而有
不化成者哉夫子告子張問政至此謂夫禮樂
之道其用雖達諸天下而其本不外於吾身是
故君子蓋甞言而履之矣匪以自淑也舉而施
之於有政吾身之序達之爲天下之序蓋甞行
而樂之矣匪以自豫也推而見之於臨民吾身
之和達之爲天下之和向明涖治之餘有以立
大中至正之矩出乎身者加乎民者也正位凝
===
命之際有以妙體信達順之機發乎邇者見乎
遠者也是雖無心於天下之化也然禮達而分
自定作則自我也人莫不順其則聲教所及自
四達而不悖樂行而民鄉方建極於上也下莫
不歸其極德化所被殆充周而不窮篤恭之妙
徵至治於有象内外寧謐之休可坐而致矣而
天下之人有不得其所者乎平中之盛昭大化
於無爲遠近乂安之治不勞而定矣而天下之
事有不得其理者乎此天下之治必以有本而
punctuated: 君子以禮樂而爲治，則天下化成矣。夫禮樂出於吾身，致治之本也。君子舉而措諸天下，而有不化成者哉？夫子告子張問政，至此謂夫禮樂之道，其用雖達諸天下，而其本不外於吾身。是故君子蓋甞言而履之矣，匪以自淑也；舉而施之於有政，吾身之序，達之爲天下之序。蓋甞行而樂之矣，匪以自豫也；推而見之於臨民，吾身之和，達之爲天下之和。向明涖治之餘，有以立大中至正之矩，出乎身者，加乎民者也；正位凝命之際，有以妙體信達順之機，發乎邇者，見乎遠者也。是雖無心於天下之化也，然禮達而分自定，作則自我也，人莫不順其則，聲教所及，自四達而不悖；樂行而民鄉方，建極於上也，下莫不歸其極，德化所被，殆充周而不窮。篤恭之妙，徵至治於有象，内外寧謐之休，可坐而致矣，而天下之人有不得其所者乎？平中之盛，昭大化於無爲，遠近乂安之治，不勞而定矣，而天下之事有不得其理者乎？此天下之治必以有本而
translation_en:
When the gentleman governs through ritual and music, all under Heaven are transformed and brought to perfection. Ritual and music issue from his own person: they are the foundation of good government. If the gentleman puts them into practice throughout the realm, how could transformation and perfection fail to follow? At this point in the Master's reply to Zizhang's question about government, he means that although the operation of the Way of ritual and music extends throughout the realm, its foundation lies nowhere outside one's own person.

Thus the gentleman has indeed spoken of it and put it into practice, but not merely to improve himself. He takes it up and applies it to government, extending the order within himself to become the order of all under Heaven. He has indeed practised it and taken delight in it, but not merely for his own enjoyment. He extends it and manifests it in governing the people, so that the harmony within himself becomes the harmony of all under Heaven. As he faces the light and administers government, he establishes a standard of perfect centrality and utmost correctness: what issues from his person is applied to the people. As he takes his rightful position and secures Heaven's mandate, he gives subtle effect to the workings of embodying trustworthiness and extending concord: what originates nearby becomes manifest afar.

Though he has no deliberate intention of transforming all under Heaven, once ritual extends everywhere, distinctions settle into place of themselves. The standard originates with him, and none fail to follow it; wherever his proclamations and instruction reach, they naturally spread in all directions without meeting opposition. When music is practised, the people turn toward the proper course. He establishes the supreme standard above, and all below turn to it; the transforming influence of his virtue spreads everywhere without exhaustion.

The subtle efficacy of earnest reverence manifests perfect government in visible forms. The blessing of tranquillity within and without can be attained while seated at ease: could anyone under Heaven then fail to find a proper place? The fullness of equilibrium and centrality makes great transformation manifest through nonaction. Order and peace, far and near, become established without toil: could any affair under Heaven then fail to accord with its proper principle? Thus the government of all under Heaven must have a foundation upon which …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
立也爲政者烏可不知所從事哉抑此卽王天
下之道力此者德也南面者位也有其德有其
位而致天下之治無難矣是之謂天德王道聖
人履中正而樂和平之明驗也匪獨告子張爲
然他日語爲邦之問斟酌四代禮樂則夫子之
爲政可槩見者如此苟得邦家綏來動和之化
固其所必致也哉故曰作禮樂者必聖人在天
子之位
第貳塲
===
論
君子動而世爲天下道
林茂勛
同考試官學正彭批〔士人輙事套括以炫藝能要於理道無當此作根究本始開闔無端如入武庫而百物森具閱良驥而冀北羣空雄偉奇雋於是微笑〕
同考試官教授莫批〔文章多技惟在主理而澤氣思致淵深詞華鬯茂者僅見此篇人其退避三舍乎〕
考試官教諭黃批〔格高詞古學博氣昌讀之〕
punctuated:
立也，爲政者烏可不知所從事哉？抑此卽王天下之道，力此者德也，南面者位也。有其德，有其位，而致天下之治無難矣。是之謂天德王道，聖人履中正而樂和平之明驗也。匪獨告子張爲然，他日語「爲邦」之問，斟酌四代禮樂，則夫子之爲政可槩見者如此。苟得邦家，「綏來動和」之化，固其所必致也哉！故曰：「作禮樂者，必聖人在天子之位。」

第貳塲

論

君子動而世爲天下道

林茂勛
同考試官學正彭批〔士人輙事套括以炫藝能，要於理道無當。此作根究本始，開闔無端，如入武庫而百物森具，閱良驥而冀北羣空，雄偉奇雋，於是微笑。〕
同考試官教授莫批〔文章多技，惟在主理而澤氣。思致淵深、詞華鬯茂者，僅見此篇。人其退避三舍乎！〕
考試官教諭黃批〔格高詞古，學博氣昌，讀之〕
translation_en:
… is established. How can one who governs fail to know what to devote himself to? Moreover, this is none other than the Way of ruling the world as a true king: devoting oneself to this is virtue, and facing south as ruler is the position. Having the virtue and having the position, there is no difficulty in bringing about order in the world. This is what is called heavenly virtue and the Kingly Way, the clear proof of the sage treading in centrality and correctness and delighting in harmony and peace. Not only was this so when instructing Zizhang; on another day, when answering the question about "governing a state," he weighed and selected from the rites and music of the four dynasties—thus what can be generally seen of the Master's approach to governance is like this. If he had gained a state or ruling family, the transforming influence by which "he comforts them and they come, he stirs them and they are harmonious" would surely have been brought about by him! Therefore it is said: "He who creates rites and music must be a sage in the position of the Son of Heaven."

Second Session

Discourse
