"The gentleman moves and for generations is a Way for the world."

By Lin Maoxun 林茂勛.
Associate Examiner Peng, Subprefectural Director of Studies, comments: [Scholars constantly resort to formulaic conventions to show off their literary skill, which in the end misses the mark of principle and the Way. This essay investigates the fundamental origins, opening and closing with boundless versatility—like entering an armory where all kinds of weapons are arrayed in abundance, or inspecting fine steeds until the herds of northern Ji are emptied. Grand, extraordinary, and incisive; at this one smiles in appreciation [? 於是微笑, likely a graphic error for 於斯為盛 "reaches its height here"].]
Associate Examiner Mo, Prefectural Director of Studies, comments: [Writing has many techniques, but it lies solely in taking principle as the master and enriching the vital breath. One whose thought is profound and whose literary flourishes are luxuriant and flourishing is seen only in this piece. Should others not retreat three marches before him!]
Examiner Huang, County Director of Studies, comments: [Its style is lofty and its diction ancient, its learning broad and its vital breath flourishing; reading it…]

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
令人灑然佳士佳士
考試官教諭朱批充𠉀瑩徹而操縱有法將
不足傳邪
君子會道於身而天下不能外之以為道是故
操之至約而施之則至廣取之至近而推之則
至遠君子豈嘗以吾之動於此而持以待天下
後世之人使其必吾信且從也而天下後世之
人亦豈以其道之出於君子有所企焉而求以
不外於其道耶吾知其動之也自其身焉而與
===
斯民共由之而已而人之囿其化守其法者相
率焉以為日用之常而卒不能外乎其道而亦
不知道之出於君子也何也天下之人不同而
其心則君子之心也後世之天下不同而其民
則當時之民也君子以吾心之同而觸其本然
之理備制作之善而盡鼓舞之神則道之行也
固天下後世之所固有者矣民方安於其心之
固有而相忘相比於治化之中雖欲外之以為
道其可得哉嘗讀書曰亶聰明作元后元后作
punctuated:
令人灑然，佳士！佳士！
考試官教諭朱批：充𠉀瑩徹，而操縱有法，將不足傳邪？
君子會道於身，而天下不能外之以為道。是故操之至約，而施之則至廣；取之至近，而推之則至遠。君子豈嘗以吾之動於此，而持以待天下後世之人，使其必吾信且從也？而天下後世之人，亦豈以其道之出於君子，有所企焉而求以不外於其道耶？吾知其動之也，自其身焉，而與斯民共由之而已。而人之囿其化、守其法者，相率焉以為日用之常，而卒不能外乎其道，而亦不知道之出於君子也。何也？天下之人不同，而其心則君子之心也；後世之天下不同，而其民則當時之民也。君子以吾心之同，而觸其本然之理，備制作之善，而盡鼓舞之神，則道之行也，固天下後世之所固有者矣。民方安於其心之固有，而相忘相比於治化之中，雖欲外之以為道，其可得哉？嘗讀《書》曰：「亶聰明作元后，元后作
translation_en:
…leaves one feeling refreshed. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: "It is full, luminous, and pellucid [?], and its handling of the argument follows a clear method. Shall it not be worthy of transmission?"

The gentleman embodies the Way within his own person, and the world cannot depart from him to fashion a Way of its own. Therefore, what he holds fast to is most concise, yet its application is most broad; what he draws from is most near at hand, yet its extension is most far-reaching. Did the gentleman ever act in a certain manner here and hold it up to await the people of the world and future ages, compelling them to trust and follow him? And did the people of the world and future ages ever tiptoe in expectation just because the Way came from the gentleman, seeking not to depart from his Way? I know that when he acts, it begins from his own person, and he simply follows it together with the people. Those who are encompassed by his transforming influence and who abide by his laws follow one another in taking it as the constant norm of daily life; in the end, they cannot depart from his Way, nor do they even know that the Way originated with the gentleman. Why is this? The people of the world differ, yet their minds are the mind of the gentleman; the world of later ages differs, yet its people are the same as the people of that time. When the gentleman uses the commonality of his own mind to touch upon their inherent principle, perfecting the goodness of institutions and exhausting the miraculous power of inspiring them, then the practice of the Way is indeed something already inherent in the world and in future ages. Since the people are content with what is inherent in their own minds, forgetting themselves and joining together within his ordering and transforming influence, even if they wished to depart from it to fashion another Way, how could they do so? I have read in the Book of Documents (Shu): "Truly perceptive and intelligent, he becomes the great sovereign; the great sovereign becomes…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
民父母天命賦予曷嘗有所豐嗇哉君子得其
清且厚者天民之先覺也天之所縱者也而覺
民之責不得不任焉天生斯民使之司牧而理
人之責不得不任焉君子當君師之責而勢之
所必趨者天也君子奉天時者也時乘之責不
得不任焉夫君子兼此三者於天下而天下之
生也不能無父子君臣兄弟夫婦朋友之倫焉
斁其倫則相夷不能無飲食衣服器皿貨財之
欲焉從其欲則相逐不能無宮府質劑簿書會
===
期之煩焉任其煩則相爭君子懼民之必底於
過也而思所以一之於是乎議之禮焉制之度
焉考之文焉爲之冠婚喪祭之典郊社朝聘之
儀燕饗射御鄉相見之節升降上下周旋裼襲
之序類不可勝紀而其爲禮則一也所以敦民
行也爲之辱收弁冠之象韠帶佩笏之章輅弧
旟旐之等豆登几筵之則斗斛權衡之信宮室
舟車陶冶之具類不可勝紀而其爲度則一也
所以防民慾也爲之龍文穗書龜字鍾鼎倒薤
punctuated: 民父母。」天命賦予，曷嘗有所豐嗇哉？君子得其清且厚者，天民之先覺也，天之所縱者也，而覺民之責不得不任焉；天生斯民，使之司牧，而理人之責不得不任焉；君子當君師之責，而勢之所必趨者天也，君子奉天時者也，時乘之責不得不任焉。夫君子兼此三者於天下，而天下之生也，不能無父子、君臣、兄弟、夫婦、朋友之倫焉，斁其倫則相夷；不能無飲食、衣服、器皿、貨財之欲焉，從其欲則相逐；不能無宮府、質劑、簿書、會期之煩焉，任其煩則相爭。君子懼民之必底於過也，而思所以一之。於是乎議之禮焉，制之度焉，考之文焉。爲之冠、婚、喪、祭之典，郊、社、朝、聘之儀，燕、饗、射、御、鄉、相見之節，升降、上下、周旋、裼襲之序，類不可勝紀，而其爲禮則一也，所以敦民行也。爲之辱收、弁冠之象，韠帶、佩笏之章，輅弧、旟旐之等，豆登、几筵之則，斗斛、權衡之信，宮室、舟車、陶冶之具，類不可勝紀，而其爲度則一也，所以防民慾也。爲之龍文、穗書、龜字、鍾鼎、倒薤…
translation_en:
… the father and mother of the people." In the endowments of the Mandate of Heaven, when has there ever been any partiality in generosity or stinginess? The noble man receives that which is pure and thick: he is the first among Heaven's people to be awakened, the one whom Heaven lets flourish, and so he cannot but take up the responsibility of awakening the people. Heaven gives birth to these people and causes him to shepherd them, and so he cannot but take up the responsibility of governing others. The noble man bears the responsibilities of ruler and teacher, and that toward which the trend of circumstances must incline is Heaven; the noble man is one who reverently follows Heaven's timing, and so he cannot but take up the responsibility of riding the timely moment.

Now, when the noble man combines these three responsibilities over all under Heaven, in the life of the world there cannot fail to be the human relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friend and friend—yet if these relationships are ruined, people will destroy one another. There cannot fail to be desires for food and drink, clothing, vessels, and wealth—yet if these desires are indulged, people will chase after one another in contention. There cannot fail to be the complexities of palace and government offices, contracts and tallies, registers and account books, and appointed meetings—yet if these complexities are left to themselves, people will quarrel with one another. The noble man, fearing that the people will inevitably end up in transgression, seeks the means to unify them. Thereupon he deliberates on ritual propriety, establishes regulations and measures, and examines the written scripts.

He institutes for them the canons of capping, wedding, mourning, and sacrifice; the ceremonies of suburban and altar sacrifices, court audiences, and diplomatic missions; the etiquette of banquets, feasts, archery, charioteering, district symposia, and formal interviews; and the sequences of ascending and descending, moving up and down, turning about, and baring or covering the upper garment. Such categories are too numerous to record in full, yet as ritual propriety they are one—the means by which to make the people's conduct earnest.

He institutes for them the forms of the Xushou [? 辱收, for 母追] and ceremonial caps and crowns; the insignia of knee-covers, sashes, pendants, and tablets; the grades of state carriages, bows, and falcon- and tortoise-banners; the standards for wooden and pottery sacrificial platters, stools, and mats; the trustworthy measures of pecks, bushels, weights, and scales; and the implements of palaces and houses, boats and carriages, and pottery and metallurgy. Such categories are too numerous to record in full, yet as regulations and measures they are one—the means by which to curb the people's desires.

He institutes for them dragon script, grain-ear script, tortoise characters, bell-and-tripod inscriptions, hanging-leek script…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之文四聲五音六書之義類不可勝紀而其爲
書則一也所以同民心也夫天下之人羣然不
可齊也其事至賾而不可禦也其變至雜而不
可理也持多術以臨馭之猶懼其不可爲也而
謂此足以一之乎吾知斯人之在天下其性之
不可解與分之不可逃者非強焉而致之也有
能外斯五者以自立乎故禮議而天下之人可
盡也相生相養之道缺一不可而患不防則傷
欲不節則流故度制而事可盡也僞之滋變之
===
不可巳也書契作則亂止矣故文立而變可盡
也夫是三者誠足爲一天下之道矣而亦豈君
子任意創制爲之者哉君子膺天命居天位以
治天之民夫亦曰以天之道治之爾天地有卑
高之位在人則爲禮有方員之體在人則爲度
有陰陽之文在人則爲文是禮也度也文也天
之所授也君子與夫人一也其初本一而人自
異之爾是故本其所固有者推而使天下後世
共由之而巳也故其議之制之而考之也非曰
punctuated: 之文，四聲、五音、六書之義，類不可勝紀，而其爲書則一也，所以同民心也。夫天下之人羣然不可齊也，其事至賾而不可禦也，其變至雜而不可理也。持多術以臨馭之，猶懼其不可爲也，而謂此足以一之乎？吾知斯人之在天下，其性之不可解與分之不可逃者，非強焉而致之也。有能外斯五者以自立乎？故禮議而天下之人可盡也。相生相養之道，缺一不可，而患不防則傷，欲不節則流，故度制而事可盡也。僞之滋，變之不可巳也，書契作則亂止矣，故文立而變可盡也。夫是三者，誠足爲一天下之道矣，而亦豈君子任意創制爲之者哉？君子膺天命、居天位以治天之民，夫亦曰以天之道治之爾。天地有卑高之位，在人則爲禮；有方員之體，在人則爲度；有陰陽之文，在人則爲文。是禮也，度也，文也，天之所授也，君子與夫人一也。其初本一，而人自異之爾。是故本其所固有者，推而使天下後世共由之而巳也。故其議之、制之而考之也，非曰
translation_en:
… graphs, as well as the principles of the four tones, the five musical notes, and the six classes of character formation—their varieties are too numerous to record, yet as writing they are one, which is how the minds of the people are unified.

Now, the people of the world gather in multitudes and cannot be made uniform; their affairs are utterly intricate and cannot be warded off; their permutations are utterly variegated and cannot be put in order. Even if one employs a multitude of techniques to govern and control them, one still fears it cannot be done—how then can one say that these [three] alone suffice to unify them? I know that as people exist in the world, the nature from which they cannot be untethered and the lot from which they cannot escape are not brought about by coercion. Is there anyone who can stand on their own outside the five cardinal relationships? Therefore, once ritual is deliberated, all the people in the world can be encompassed. In the ways of mutual generation and mutual nourishment, not a single one can be lacking; yet if harms are not guarded against, there is injury, and if desires are not moderated, there is dissipation. Therefore, once standards and measures are established, all affairs can be encompassed. As artifice proliferates, permutations become unstoppable; yet once written tallies and documents are created, disorder ceases. Therefore, once written characters are established, all permutations can be encompassed.

Now, these three are truly sufficient to serve as the Way for unifying the world. Yet how could they be things that the noble man arbitrarily invents and establishes at will? The noble man receives the Mandate of Heaven and occupies the position of Heaven in order to govern the people of Heaven; this simply means governing them by the Way of Heaven. Heaven and Earth have the positions of low and high, which among human beings become ritual; they have the forms of square and round, which among human beings become standards and measures; they have the patterns of yin and yang, which among human beings become writing. These—ritual, standards and measures, and writing—are bestowed by Heaven, and in this the noble man and the common person are one. In the beginning they are originally one, and people merely differentiate them on their own. For this reason, he simply grounds himself in what is inherently present, extending it so that all the world and later generations may follow it together. Therefore, in deliberating rituals, establishing standards, and examining writing, it is not that…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
爲天下作則也自其身之履者而議之則禮矣
自其身之用者而制之則度矣自其身之著者
而考之則文矣人見其倫理中乎節文動容合
乎規矩經緯通乎天地曰道之在於君子之身
者然也而不知其卽天下之道也何也微斯人
則三者曷從生哉人見其司徒之所授冬官之
所裁內史之所掌而行人之所頒曰道之在於
天下者然也而不知其卽君子之身也何也匪
君子則烏與議而制而考之哉故典章文物之
===
著皆精神心思之微綱紀法度之具悉性命天
人之蘊四海千祺之遠卽几席戶庭之近合人
物貫古今而通極於造化者也是故徵之庶民
考之三王質之鬼神而俟之後聖無有乎或間
者至矣哉君子制作之善乎蓋至是而會道之
全矣由是達之朝廷百官則而象之推之邦國
庶人悅而安之垂之後代百王率而由之以之
而顯神謨申話言渙大號則罔不欽焉天下之
不佩服而諷誦之者未之有也以之而陳藝極
punctuated: 爲天下作則也。自其身之履者而議之，則禮矣；自其身之用者而制之，則度矣；自其身之著者而考之，則文矣。人見其倫理中乎節文，動容合乎規矩，經緯通乎天地，曰：「道之在於君子之身者然也。」而不知其卽天下之道也。何也？微斯人，則三者曷從生哉？人見其司徒之所授、冬官之所裁、內史之所掌，而行人之所頒，曰：「道之在於天下者然也。」而不知其卽君子之身也。何也？匪君子，則烏與議而制而考之哉？故典章文物之著，皆精神心思之微；綱紀法度之具，悉性命天人之蘊。四海千祺之遠，卽几席戶庭之近，合人物、貫古今而通極於造化者也。是故徵之庶民，考之三王，質之鬼神，而俟之後聖，無有乎或間者。至矣哉，君子制作之善乎！蓋至是而會道之全矣。由是達之朝廷，百官則而象之；推之邦國，庶人悅而安之；垂之後代，百王率而由之。以之而顯神謨、申話言、渙大號，則罔不欽焉，天下之不佩服而諷誦之者，未之有也。以之而陳藝極
translation_en:
…to establish standards for All-under-Heaven. What he deliberates upon, taking his own conduct as the basis, becomes ritual; what he institutes, taking his own practice as the basis, becomes measures; what he examines, taking his own outward expression as the basis, becomes cultural forms. People see that his ordering of human relationships accords with ritual articulations, that his movements and bearing conform to rules and standards, and that the organizing principles of his conduct communicate with Heaven and Earth. They say, “Such is the Way embodied in the gentleman,” yet do not know that this is precisely the Way of All-under-Heaven. Why? Without such a person, from where could these three arise? People see what the Minister of Education imparts, what the Minister of Works fashions, what the Interior Scribe administers, and what the Messenger promulgates. They say, “Such is the Way as it exists in All-under-Heaven,” yet do not know that it is precisely the gentleman’s own person. Why? Without the gentleman, who could deliberate upon, institute, and examine these things?

Thus, the manifest forms of statutes, institutions, and cultural objects are all the subtle workings of spirit and thought; the concrete apparatus of governing principles, laws, and measures consists entirely of the profound contents of human nature and destiny, Heaven and humanity. The remoteness of the Four Seas and “a thousand blessings” [?] is none other than the proximity of one’s mat, table, doorway, and courtyard. These unite people and things, link antiquity with the present, and penetrate to the utmost workings of creation. Accordingly, they may be verified among the common people, examined against the Three Kings, tested before ghosts and spirits, and left to await later sages, without any discrepancy. How consummate is the excellence of the gentleman’s establishment of institutions! At this point, indeed, he comprehends the Way in its entirety.

When these are extended to the court, the hundred officials take them as their standard and emulate them; when they are propagated throughout the states, the common people delight in them and find repose in them; when they are handed down to later generations, the hundred kings follow and abide by them. Through them, sagely plans are made manifest, instructive words are reiterated, and great proclamations are disseminated: none fail to revere them. There has never been anyone in All-under-Heaven who did not embrace and observe them, recite and chant them. Through them, standards of excellence are set forth…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
樹表儀程大猷則罔不臧焉天下之不駿惠而
承式之者未之有也世不同而禮同貴賤以章
隆殺以辨卑高以陳安於倫矣而孰知其議之
自君子乎世不同而度同小大定其儀方員成
其象長短協其則便於軌矣而孰知其制之自
君子乎世不同而書同結繩以代百官以治萬
民以察習於文矣而孰知其考之自君子乎所
謂不降皇序下堂陛而天下後世之人各得其
願安於其分鼓舞於道化之中而不知誰之所
===
爲嗚呼至矣信乎操之約而施之則博取之近
而及之則遠也巳稽之古昔禮帝饗祖爲市畫
卦皇之道也親睦徽典輯瑞同律帝之道也敷
土濬川綏猷肇脩列爵分土王之道也維時於
變從欲風動咸和永清之化流被四訖迨今誦
之不衰也抑記有之五帝不襲禮三王不沿樂
禮樂道之大者而曰不相沿襲何也蓋甞聞之
孔子矣曰殷因於夏禮周因於殷禮所損益可
知也夫殷周之君其人則聖神其時則變革而
punctuated: 樹表儀，程大猷，則罔不臧焉，天下之不駿惠而承式之者，未之有也。世不同而禮同，貴賤以章，隆殺以辨，卑高以陳，安於倫矣，而孰知其議之自君子乎？世不同而度同，小大定其儀，方員成其象，長短協其則，便於軌矣，而孰知其制之自君子乎？世不同而書同，結繩以代，百官以治，萬民以察，習於文矣，而孰知其考之自君子乎？所謂不降皇序，下堂陛，而天下後世之人各得其願，安於其分，鼓舞於道化之中，而不知誰之所爲。嗚呼，至矣！信乎操之約而施之則博，取之近而及之則遠也巳！稽之古昔，禮帝饗祖，爲市畫卦，皇之道也；親睦徽典，輯瑞同律，帝之道也；敷土濬川，綏猷肇脩，列爵分土，王之道也。維時於變，從欲風動，咸和永清之化，流被四訖，迨今誦之不衰也。抑記有之：「五帝不襲禮，三王不沿樂。」禮樂，道之大者，而曰不相沿襲，何也？蓋甞聞之孔子矣，曰：「殷因於夏禮，周因於殷禮，所損益可知也。」夫殷周之君，其人則聖神，其時則變革，而
translation_en: …establish exemplary standards and take the great Way as their model: then all is good, and none under Heaven fails to follow it devotedly and adopt it as a rule. Though ages differ, the rites are the same: noble and humble ranks are made clear, greater and lesser degrees of ceremony distinguished, and lower and higher positions set forth. People rest content within their proper relationships, yet who knows that the deliberation on these rites originated with the gentleman? Though ages differ, the measures are the same: large and small have fixed standards, square and round take their proper shapes, and long and short conform to their rules. People find these standards convenient, yet who knows that their establishment originated with the gentleman? Though ages differ, writing is the same: knotted cords are replaced, the hundred officials conduct their administration, and the myriad people gain understanding. People become accustomed to the written forms, yet who knows that their examination originated with the gentleman? This is what is meant by remaining above the august steps, without descending from the hall [?], while people throughout the world and in later generations each attain their wishes, rest content with their allotted station, and rejoice amid the transforming influence of the Way, unaware of whose doing it is. Ah, how consummate! Truly, what he holds to is simple, yet its application is broad; what he draws upon is near, yet its reach is far! Looking back to antiquity, offering rites to the Supreme Deity and sacrifices to ancestors, establishing markets and drawing the trigrams: these were the Way of the August Sovereigns. Bringing kin into harmony and honoring the established ordinances, collecting jade credentials and unifying pitch standards: these were the Way of the Emperors. Ordering the land and dredging rivers, establishing sound principles and beginning their cultivation, assigning ranks and apportioning territories: these were the Way of the Kings. In those times, people were transformed; they followed their rulers’ wishes and moved as though stirred by the wind. The transforming influence that brought universal harmony and enduring peace spread to the four extremities [?], and its praises continue unabated to this day. Yet the Record of Rites says: “The Five Emperors did not inherit one another’s rites; the Three Kings did not follow one another’s music.” Rites and music are great constituents of the Way: why, then, does it say that they did not follow or inherit one another’s practices? We have heard Confucius say: “Yin followed the rites of Xia, and Zhou followed the rites of Yin; what they diminished and added can be known.” Now, the rulers of Yin and Zhou were sage and divinely perceptive in their persons, and their times were times of change, while…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其世則千有餘歲矣文質三統不必於同而三
綱五常之大者則未之有改焉記者所稱特禮
樂之具云爾古今之變不同而俗之便習亦異
久之不能無弊者勢則然也變通宜民之道在
堯舜已然而況於三王乎是故值其常也則不
愆不忘君子之所以動於天下者為未弊值其
變也則損益宜時以足君子未盡之意者固不
害其為道也不然田井矣官周矣以秦新行之
而曰道先王之動可乎雖然子思斯言蓋會于周
===
之意也自皇王立極三重之道至周而大備宗
廟朝廷之儀方位國野之規九歲頒諭之制詳
在周書綿延至於後世天下之勢久矣而同軌
同倫同文之治猶相與守之無有自用自專以
干先王之典者弁髦之國大不能邾莒尚足以
奔走天下之諸侯陳檜之詩猶或有西方美人
之思原其所自則文武周公之所以動天下後
世者深且遠也然則君子會道於身而天下後
世不能外之以為道不益信也哉
punctuated: 其世則千有餘歲矣。文質三統不必於同，而三綱五常之大者則未之有改焉。記者所稱，特禮樂之具云爾。古今之變不同，而俗之便習亦異，久之不能無弊者，勢則然也。變通宜民之道，在堯舜已然，而況於三王乎？是故值其常也，則不愆不忘，君子之所以動於天下者為未弊；值其變也，則損益宜時，以足君子未盡之意者，固不害其為道也。不然，田井矣，官周矣，以秦新行之，而曰道先王之動，可乎？雖然，子思斯言，蓋會于周之意也。自皇王立極，三重之道至周而大備。宗廟朝廷之儀，方位國野之規，九歲頒諭之制，詳在周書。綿延至於後世，天下之勢久矣，而同軌同倫同文之治，猶相與守之，無有自用自專以干先王之典者。弁髦之國，大不能邾莒，尚足以奔走天下之諸侯；陳檜之詩，猶或有西方美人之思。原其所自，則文武周公之所以動天下後世者深且遠也。然則君子會道於身，而天下後世不能外之以為道，不益信也哉？
translation_en:
…and their eras spanned more than a thousand years. Refinement and simplicity, and the three dynastic systems, need not have been identical; yet the great principles of the Three Bonds and Five Constants were never altered. What the author of the Record referred to was merely the outward apparatus of rites and music. Circumstances change between antiquity and the present, and what people find convenient and customary also differs. That abuses should inevitably arise over time follows from the nature of things. The way of adapting institutions to benefit the people was already practiced under Yao and Shun; how much more so under the Three Kings!

Thus, in ordinary circumstances, one neither errs nor forgets: the means by which the noble man moves the world have not yet become defective. When circumstances change, however, making reductions and additions suited to the times, thereby fulfilling intentions that the noble man had not fully realized, certainly does not impair their conformity to the Way. Otherwise, if fields were arranged in the well-field system and offices modeled on those of Zhou, but these were implemented by Qin or Xin, could one say that they followed the Way embodied in the former kings’ actions? Nevertheless, these words of Zisi were, presumably, intended to find their culmination in Zhou.

From the time the ancient sovereigns and kings established the supreme standard, the Way of the three weighty matters reached its full development under Zhou. The ceremonies of ancestral temples and the royal court, the rules governing orientation and the arrangement of the capital and countryside, and the system of promulgating instructions every nine years are set out in detail in the Documents of Zhou. These continued into later ages. The prevailing order of the world endured for a long time, and people still jointly maintained a government characterized by uniform carriage tracks, common ethical relationships, and a shared script. None presumed to act on their own judgment or authority in violation of the former kings’ statutes. Even a state treated as a discarded ceremonial cap and hairpiece, no larger than Zhu or Ju [?], could still command the attendance of the feudal lords of the realm. Even among the poems of Chen and Kuai, some still expressed longing for the fair person of the west. Tracing this to its source, we find that the influence through which Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou moved the world and later generations was profound and far-reaching. Does this not further confirm that the noble man embodies the Way in his own person, and that neither the world nor later generations can seek a Way outside it?

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
表
擬
賜歷代名臣奏議羣臣
謝表永樂十四年
黃星耀
同考試官教諭羅批語意渾成援引精切咀嚼
覺有餘味可以式矣
同考試官教授簡批體裁莊整不徒駢儷而已
是用錄之
===
考試官教諭黃批麗而則廉而不劌足長於
四六者
考試官教諭朱批措詞舂容忠愛藹然得稱
謝體
永樂十四年某月某日臣等伏蒙
聖恩頒
賜歷代名臣奏議者
伏以
聖主採言式廣師資之益
punctuated:
表
擬賜《歷代名臣奏議》羣臣謝表，永樂十四年。
黃星耀

同考試官教諭羅批：語意渾成，援引精切，咀嚼覺有餘味，可以式矣。
同考試官教授簡批：體裁莊整，不徒駢儷而已，是用錄之。

考試官教諭朱批：措詞舂容，忠愛藹然，得稱謝體。

永樂十四年某月某日，臣等伏蒙聖恩頒賜《歷代名臣奏議》者。
伏以：聖主採言，式廣師資之益，
translation_en:
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks from the assembled officials upon receiving Memorials Submitted to the Throne by Eminent Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai mingchen zouyi), set in the fourteenth year of Yongle (1416).
By Huang Xingyao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “Expression and meaning form a seamless whole. The citations are apt and precise; savoring them leaves a lingering flavor. This may serve as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jian, Professor: “The composition is dignified and orderly, more than merely an exercise in parallel prose. For this reason, it has been selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Elegant yet conforming to proper standards, sharply defined yet not cutting: it merits a leading place among compositions in four-and-six prose.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The phrasing is measured and ample, suffused with loyalty and affection. It accords with the proper form of a memorial of thanks.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourteenth year of Yongle, we, your servants, humbly received, through Your Majesty’s gracious favor, the imperially bestowed Memorials Submitted to the Throne by Eminent Ministers of Successive Dynasties.

We humbly reflect: the sagely sovereign gathers counsels, thereby extending the benefits of learning from worthy exemplars…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
明庭錫類永垂獻納之規慶
嘉帙之告成荷
殊恩之荐及
寵逾三錫喜溢百朋臣等稽首頓首上言竊齊
平治理不間於古今手足腹心義無逃於
天地自開闢之始卽有君有臣以相臨由載籍
所傳皆立德立言之不朽喜起之迹雖遠
謀謨之範猶存能主善以為師斯與治而
同道故君子尚友往哲而聖人且擇狂夫
===
況名臣登對之所陳皆忠義精華之所發
善惟主一文不在茲自杞亡文獻之無徵
曁漢興詩書之不事典刑已墜奚取神交
姓字徒存粗同耳食故魏相疏賢良之策
而唐宗錄忠諫之屏蘇軾敷陳疏僅呈於
陸相汝愚採摭編止及於宋臣惜乎未覩
完書信矣難聞要道時將有待事匪偶然
恭惟
皇帝陛下
punctuated:
明庭錫類，永垂獻納之規。慶嘉帙之告成，荷殊恩之荐及。寵逾三錫，喜溢百朋。臣等稽首頓首上言：竊齊平治理，不間於古今；手足腹心，義無逃於天地。自開闢之始，卽有君有臣以相臨；由載籍所傳，皆立德立言之不朽。喜起之迹雖遠，謀謨之範猶存。能主善以為師，斯與治而同道。故君子尚友往哲，而聖人且擇狂夫。
況名臣登對之所陳，皆忠義精華之所發。善惟主一，文不在茲？自杞亡文獻之無徵，曁漢興詩書之不事，典刑已墜，奚取神交？姓字徒存，粗同耳食。故魏相疏賢良之策，而唐宗錄忠諫之屏。蘇軾敷陳疏，僅呈於陸相；汝愚採摭編，止及於宋臣。惜乎未覩完書，信矣難聞要道。時將有待，事匪偶然。
恭惟皇帝陛下，
translation_en:
…The enlightened court extends its beneficence to others of like kind, bequeathing forever a standard for offering counsel. We celebrate the completion of this fine collection and gratefully receive the special favor bestowed upon us once again. This honor surpasses three successive grants; our joy exceeds that of receiving a hundred strings of cowries. We, your servants, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words: we humbly consider [?] that the principles of orderly and peaceful government do not differ between antiquity and the present. The bond between ruler and ministers, like that between hands and feet and belly and heart, cannot be escaped anywhere between Heaven and Earth. From the beginning of creation there have been rulers and ministers in their respective relationships; those whose deeds the written records transmit achieved immortality through establishing virtue and enduring words. Though the days when ruler and ministers joyfully roused one another to action are distant, their exemplary counsels still survive. Whoever takes goodness as his guide and teacher thereby follows the same Way as good government. Thus the gentleman befriends worthy men of the past, and even the sage selects useful words from the rash.
Moreover, what eminent ministers set forth when received in audience all issued from the finest essence of loyalty and righteousness. Goodness alone is the constant guide: is not this cultural inheritance embodied here? Since the loss of documentary and worthy human testimony in Qi [?], and the neglect of the Odes and Documents at the rise of the Han, the exemplary standards have fallen away. How, then, can one commune in spirit with the ancients? When only their names survive, this amounts to little more than feeding on hearsay. Thus Wei Xiang submitted a memorial presenting the policy proposals of worthy men, while an emperor of the Tang had loyal remonstrances inscribed on a screen. Su Shi's memorial setting forth such counsel was confined to Minister Lu [?]; the compilation assembled by Ruyu extended only to ministers of the Song. Alas, no complete collection had yet been seen; indeed, it was difficult to learn the essential Way. The proper time still awaited its arrival; this undertaking is no mere accident.
We reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
學本誠明
聖兼述作
宣威沙漠長清瀚海之波
凝命幽燕永定鎬京之鼎
堯仁舜智一德以建厥中
武烈文謨重明而麗乎正乾坤奠位華裔歸
心屬治定而功成欲圖艱以保大因時立
政每勤結網之思稽古求賢恒切拊髀之
嘆偶有見於遺直真深契於
===
淵衷如鄧張諸葛之流及董賈更生之輩今日效
忠於往代寔垂範於
今時即意氣之相孚豈世代之能隔欲徵激勸
必藉表章
璽書爰賁於
春宮編纂特煩於翰苑因而博采咸以兼收
紀運自周武至宋元幾四千年而未訖條
目自君德至夷狄積三百卷而有奇義例
體裁備諸子百家之旨文章議論採羣書
punctuated: 學本誠明，聖兼述作。宣威沙漠，長清瀚海之波；凝命幽燕，永定鎬京之鼎。堯仁舜智，一德以建厥中；武烈文謨，重明而麗乎正。乾坤奠位，華裔歸心。屬治定而功成，欲圖艱以保大。因時立政，每勤結網之思；稽古求賢，恒切拊髀之嘆。偶有見於遺直，真深契於淵衷。如鄧、張、諸葛之流，及董、賈、更生之輩，今日效忠於往代，寔垂範於今時。即意氣之相孚，豈世代之能隔？欲徵激勸，必藉表章。璽書爰賁於春宮，編纂特煩於翰苑。因而博采，咸以兼收。紀運自周武至宋元，幾四千年而未訖；條目自君德至夷狄，積三百卷而有奇。義例體裁，備諸子百家之旨；文章議論，採羣書
translation_en:
…Your learning is rooted in sincerity and illumination; your sageliness embraces both transmitting and creating. You proclaim your might across the deserts, keeping the waves of the vast northern wastes forever calm; you consolidate the Mandate in You and Yan, securing forever the dynastic cauldrons of Haojing. With Yao’s benevolence and Shun’s wisdom, you establish the mean through undivided virtue; with King Wu’s martial achievements and King Wen’s wise plans, your redoubled brilliance accords with rectitude. Heaven and earth take their appointed places; Chinese and foreign peoples turn their hearts to you. Now that order is established and achievements complete, you seek to anticipate difficulties and preserve your great enterprise. Establishing government suited to the times, you continually ponder the weaving of nets to secure worthy men; examining antiquity and seeking the worthy, you often sigh and slap your thigh in longing for such men. When you happen upon upright men of the past, they find a profound response in your innermost heart. Such figures as Deng, Zhang, and Zhuge, and such men as Dong, Jia, and Gengsheng, ‘today rendered loyal service in former ages’ [?], and indeed provide models for the present. When spirit and purpose accord, how could the generations keep them apart? To bring about encouragement and exhortation, their deeds must be made manifest.
An imperial letter bearing your seal thereupon graced the heir apparent’s palace, and the work of compilation was specially entrusted to the Hanlin Academy. Materials were accordingly gathered widely and comprehensively included. Its chronological coverage extends from King Wu of Zhou to the Song and Yuan, spanning nearly four thousand years without exhausting the record; its categories range from the ruler’s virtue to foreign peoples, filling more than three hundred juan. Its organizing principles and literary forms encompass the purport of the various masters and hundred schools; its prose and discussions draw upon the many books…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
列傳之長理本無窮真展卷而有益事皆
可法若指掌之易明續六經之所未該驗
累朝之所已試豈云小補允也
大成
錫以徽名頓重斯文之價
付之良梓允為
天府之珍首宣
賜於
二宮隨覃
===
恩於庶位視為臣鵠喜有的之可趨探若知囊
信隨求而各足是何遭逢之有幸而衣被
之無窮也臣等學本面牆無由納約才非
補
袞何以報章毎懷古道之脩深切高山之仰
先知先覺得我心之同然是訓是行惟
君子之所使庶見馳聲
閭閻猶慚學步邯鄲敢不仰體
鴻私勉抒駑鈍為臣而必欲盡臣道學古而
punctuated:
列傳之長。理本無窮，真展卷而有益；事皆可法，若指掌之易明。續六經之所未該，驗累朝之所已試，豈云小補，允也大成。錫以徽名，頓重斯文之價；付之良梓，允為天府之珍。首宣賜於二宮，隨覃恩於庶位。視為臣鵠，喜有的之可趨；探若知囊，信隨求而各足。是何遭逢之有幸，而衣被之無窮也！
臣等學本面牆，無由納約；才非補袞，何以報章？毎懷古道之脩，深切高山之仰。先知先覺，得我心之同然；是訓是行，惟君子之所使。庶見馳聲閭閻，猶慚學步邯鄲。敢不仰體鴻私，勉抒駑鈍，為臣而必欲盡臣道，學古而
translation_en:
…the strengths of the collected biographies. Its principles are inexhaustible: truly, opening its volumes brings benefit. Its precedents all offer models to follow, as clear as looking at one’s own palm. It supplements what the Six Classics did not encompass and verifies what successive dynasties have already put to the test. How could its contribution be called slight? Truly, it is a grand synthesis. Bestowed with an illustrious title, this work’s worth was at once enhanced; entrusted to fine printing blocks, it has indeed become a treasure of the imperial repository. First, its bestowal upon the Two Palaces was proclaimed; then this favor was extended to officials of every rank. Regarding it as a target for ministerial conduct, we rejoice to have a mark toward which to strive. Consulting it as a storehouse of wisdom, we find that it supplies whatever each seeks. How fortunate we are to encounter such an age, and how boundless are the benefits that enfold us!
We, your servants, are so deficient in learning that we stand as if facing a wall, unable to offer counsel that reaches your understanding. Our talents cannot mend the imperial robes—that is, remedy our sovereign’s shortcomings—so how can we respond worthily to this splendid gift? Whenever we reflect upon the lofty way of antiquity, we feel profound reverence, as though gazing up at a high mountain. Those who knew and understood before us have grasped what our own hearts likewise recognize. We follow these teachings and put them into practice, acting only as the noble man directs. We may hope to win renown among the village lanes, yet remain ashamed of resembling the man who tried to learn the gait of Handan and lost his own. How could we fail reverently to embody your munificent favor and strive to exert our dull abilities, determined as ministers to fulfill the minister’s way, and in studying antiquity to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
期不愧古人三復斯言用代韋弦之義再
陳末論聊伸犬馬之忱步亦步趨亦趨程
法期無忘於前烈可曰可否曰否獻替矢
不負於他時伏願
言必見諸躬行
博則歸於守約
任人惟舊
進德圖新
終始惟勤學古訓以有獲
===
緝熈罔懈率舊章而無愆
霈雨露之恩咸歸
大造
擴河海之量不擇細流
治敎萬年
君道與
師道同泰
車書一統文運偕
國運並升臣無任瞻
punctuated: 期不愧古人。三復斯言，用代韋弦之義；再陳末論，聊伸犬馬之忱。步亦步，趨亦趨，程法期無忘於前烈；可曰可，否曰否，獻替矢不負於他時。伏願言必見諸躬行，博則歸於守約；任人惟舊，進德圖新；終始惟勤，學古訓以有獲；緝熈罔懈，率舊章而無愆。霈雨露之恩，咸歸大造；擴河海之量，不擇細流。治敎萬年，君道與師道同泰；車書一統，文運偕國運並升。臣無任瞻
translation_en:
…hoping not to fall short of the ancients. We repeatedly ponder these words, taking them as admonitions like the leather thong and bowstring; once more we offer our humble views, to express our devoted loyalty. When you walk, we walk; when you hasten, we hasten: in following your example, we hope never to forget the illustrious achievements of our predecessors. What is right we shall call right, and what is wrong we shall call wrong: in advancing worthy counsel and opposing errors, we vow not to fail you in days to come.
We humbly pray that your words will always find expression in your own conduct, and that broad learning will culminate in holding fast to essential principles; that in employing men you will rely on those long trusted, and in advancing virtue seek renewal; that you will remain diligent from beginning to end, gaining benefit through studying ancient teachings; and that you will continue to cultivate luminous virtue without respite, following established institutions without error. May your grace pour down like rain and dew, so that all may share in your great nurturing beneficence; may your magnanimity expand like rivers and seas, rejecting no small stream. May your governance and moral instruction endure for ten thousand years, with the Way of the ruler and the Way of the teacher flourishing together; may carriage gauges and written script be unified throughout the realm, and the fortunes of letters rise together with those of the state. Your servant cannot contain his feelings as he gazes upward…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
楊棐
===
同考試官教諭龍批我
聖祖
皇上功德竝懋淵源所漸得自傳心誠足以媲美往聖而下視近代是作援
據精確賛述詳明其涵濡治化獨深者與
同考試官教諭張批正道不傳曠矣千載我
聖祖龍興
皇上紹述後先同光要非偶然子能揚厲
閎休而根極要領必俊茂博達之士也用錄以傳
考試官教諭黃批敷揚我
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策
第一問
楊棐

同考試官教諭龍批：我聖祖、皇上功德竝懋，淵源所漸，得自傳心，誠足以媲美往聖而下視近代。是作援據精確，賛述詳明，其涵濡治化獨深者與！

同考試官教諭張批：正道不傳，曠矣千載。我聖祖龍興，皇上紹述，後先同光，要非偶然。子能揚厲閎休，而根極要領，必俊茂博達之士也。用錄以傳。

考試官教諭黃批：敷揚我
translation_en:
…looking up to Heaven and reverently toward Your Majesty, your servant is overcome with fervent emotion and profound trepidation, and respectfully submits this memorial to express his thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Yang Fei 楊棐

Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: Our sagely founding ancestor and His Majesty alike excel in achievement and virtue. The profound source of their nurturing influence lies in the transmission of the mind. They truly merit comparison with the sages of antiquity and surpass the rulers of more recent times. This composition adduces precise evidence and offers detailed, lucid praise. Surely its author has been exceptionally deeply imbued with the transforming influence of imperial governance!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The true Way went untransmitted—a void lasting a thousand years! Our sagely founding ancestor rose like a dragon, and His Majesty carried on his work. Predecessor and successor shine with equal brilliance; this can hardly be accidental. You have been able to extol their magnificent achievements while tracing the essential principles to their roots. You must be a man of outstanding talent and broad understanding. Accordingly, this composition is selected for preservation and circulation.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Expounding and extolling our…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖創業之隆
皇上中興之盛犖然當於人心非漫作者
考試官教諭朱批天人一理古今一心我
聖祖
皇上作述可以推見是作獨能對揚錄之
帝王之所以明聖兼資而作述並隆者無
他焉法天而已矣法祖而已矣天而知所
以法則蘊之為天德發之為王道皆盡善
盡美之規而其詒謀也遠祖而知所以法
===
則上以體天心下以奠民命皆善繼善述
之道而其敷治也周不于其文于其實善
法天者也不師其迹師其意善法祖者也
作者之謂聖而善法天其知所以作乎述
者之謂明而善法祖其知所以述乎以淵
懿端純之則而肇駿龐高朗之業以開拓
積累之勤而衍昌明閎遠之緒先後一揆
古今罕儷則我
高祖之創造丕基與
punctuated:
聖祖創業之隆、皇上中興之盛，犖然當於人心，非漫作者。
考試官教諭朱批：「天人一理，古今一心。我聖祖、皇上作述，可以推見。是作獨能對揚，錄之。」
帝王之所以明聖兼資而作述並隆者，無他焉，法天而已矣，法祖而已矣。天而知所以法，則蘊之為天德，發之為王道，皆盡善盡美之規，而其詒謀也遠。祖而知所以法，則上以體天心，下以奠民命，皆善繼善述之道，而其敷治也周。不于其文，于其實，善法天者也；不師其迹，師其意，善法祖者也。作者之謂聖，而善法天，其知所以作乎？述者之謂明，而善法祖，其知所以述乎？以淵懿端純之則，而肇駿龐高朗之業；以開拓積累之勤，而衍昌明閎遠之緒。先後一揆，古今罕儷，則我高祖之創造丕基與
translation_en:
…the grandeur of the Sagely Founder's establishment of the dynasty and the splendor of His Majesty's restoration. It strikingly accords with people's hearts; this is no casually composed work.
Examiner Zhu, a School Instructor, comments: “Heaven and humanity share one principle; past and present share one mind. This can be discerned from the founding achievements of our Sagely Founder and His Majesty's continuation of them. This composition is uniquely able to acclaim those achievements in fitting terms. Let it be recorded.”
The reason emperors and kings possess both enlightened discernment and sagely wisdom, and achieve greatness both in founding and in carrying forward, is nothing other than this: they model themselves on Heaven and on their ancestors. If they know how to model themselves on Heaven, what they nurture within becomes Heavenly virtue, and what they express in action becomes the Kingly Way. Both embody standards of perfect goodness and beauty, and their plans for posterity reach far into the future. If they know how to model themselves on their ancestors, above they embody Heaven's mind, and below they secure the people's livelihood. Both are ways of skillfully inheriting and carrying forward, and their administration extends everywhere. Attending to substance rather than outward form is skillful emulation of Heaven; taking ancestral intentions rather than mere traces of ancestral deeds as one's guide is skillful emulation of the ancestors. One who originates is called a sage: does someone who skillfully emulates Heaven not understand how to originate? One who carries forward is called enlightened: does someone who skillfully emulates the ancestors not understand how to carry forward? Through standards of profound excellence, rectitude, and purity, they inaugurate a mighty, expansive, lofty, and brilliant enterprise; through the labor of opening new ground and building upon accumulated achievements, they extend a flourishing, enlightened, far-reaching succession. Earlier and later rulers follow the same standard, rarely matched in either antiquity or the present. Thus, our Gaozu's establishment of the great dynastic foundation and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上之赫然中興者可得而颺言矣夫天與祖
之所當法者何也豈不曰人君之有天下
受之於天受之於祖宗乎受之於天則君
曰天子民曰天民位曰天位祿曰天祿政
曰天工國曰天邑典禮曰天敘天秩賞罰
曰天命天討自念慮以至猷爲燕居以至
大廷孰非天之所照臨者而可不奉若乎
受之於祖宗則對其神祇奉其宗廟臨其
人民統其子姓握其大寶守其宗器主其
===
===
社稷山川若其草木鳥獸自一身以至四
海旦夕以至永年孰非祖宗之所付畀者
而可不敬承邪稽之於古若堯舜禹湯文
武憲天立極夏啓太甲高宗成王皆以繼
述擅稱載諸典謨訓誥可得而睹已漢唐
宋諸君創之者乏靈承之素而欲守之者
盡效法之能難矣宜乎雜霸雜夷而微弱
不振也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝起自淮甸天與人歸
punctuated:
皇上之赫然中興者，可得而颺言矣。夫天與祖之所當法者何也？豈不曰人君之有天下，受之於天，受之於祖宗乎？受之於天，則君曰天子，民曰天民，位曰天位，祿曰天祿，政曰天工，國曰天邑，典禮曰天敘天秩，賞罰曰天命天討。自念慮以至猷爲，燕居以至大廷，孰非天之所照臨者，而可不奉若乎？受之於祖宗，則對其神祇，奉其宗廟，臨其人民，統其子姓，握其大寶，守其宗器，主其社稷山川，若其草木鳥獸。自一身以至四海，旦夕以至永年，孰非祖宗之所付畀者，而可不敬承邪？稽之於古，若堯舜禹湯文武，憲天立極；夏啓太甲高宗成王，皆以繼述擅稱。載諸典謨訓誥，可得而睹已。漢唐宋諸君，創之者乏靈承之素，而欲守之者盡效法之能，難矣！宜乎雜霸雜夷，而微弱不振也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，起自淮甸，天與人歸
translation_en:
…and His Majesty’s glorious restoration may be celebrated aloud. What, then, is it about Heaven and the ancestors that must be emulated? Is it not that a ruler receives possession of all under Heaven from Heaven and from his ancestors? Since he receives it from Heaven, the ruler is called the Son of Heaven; the people, Heaven’s people; his position, Heaven’s position; his emoluments, Heaven’s emoluments; government, Heaven’s work; and the realm, Heaven’s domain. Canonical institutions and rites are called Heaven’s ordering and ranking; rewards and punishments, Heaven’s commands and chastisements. From thoughts to plans and actions, from private repose to the great court, what is there that Heaven does not illuminate and oversee? How could he fail to obey it reverently?
Since he receives it from his ancestors, he faces their spirits, serves their ancestral temples, governs their people, presides over their descendants, holds their supreme treasure—the throne—guards their ancestral vessels, and presides over their altars of soil and grain, their mountains and rivers, and their plants, trees, birds, and beasts. From his own person to all within the Four Seas, from each morning and evening to the years stretching far ahead, what has not been entrusted to him by his ancestors? How could he fail to receive it reverently?
Examining antiquity, we find that Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu modeled themselves on Heaven and established the supreme standard. Qi of Xia, Tai Jia, Gaozong, and King Cheng all won distinction for continuing and carrying forward their predecessors’ work. These things are recorded in the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents, where they may be seen. Among the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song, the founders lacked a foundation of reverent reception of Heaven’s mandate [?]; to expect those who preserved their dynasties to exercise fully the capacity to emulate them was difficult indeed! No wonder their rule mingled the ways of hegemonic rulers and foreign peoples, becoming weak and failing to revive.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, Emperor Gao, rose from the Huai region; Heaven favored him, and the people rallied to him…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
豐功偉烈震燿今古所謂
嘉言善行神謀懿範蓋甞得於故老之所傳
聞學士之所闡繹其見於日曆者自興臨
濠迄於洪武六年凡戒敕之諄複征伐之
次第禮樂之沿革刑政之設施羣臣之功
過四夷之朝貢率多登載乃宋濂敬序之
曰功高萬古也得國之正也獨稟全智也
敬天勤民也家法之嚴也兵政有統也揭
其大要於簡端矣其見於
===
聖政記者起甲辰以至洪武三十一年凡攻守
之機宜中外之政令人才之用舍制度之
損益
詔命之敷宣災祥之著見頗已條列乃夏原
吉略論之曰制禮作樂脩明典章定郊祀
而定學校尊孔子而育賢才黜異端而表
章典籍正神號而嚴秩祀典察天文推曆
數定封建謹法律慎賞罰撫四夷總其大
端於末篇也此特其梗槩而已他如日曆
punctuated: 豐功偉烈，震燿今古。所謂嘉言善行、神謀懿範，蓋甞得於故老之所傳聞、學士之所闡繹。其見於《日曆》者，自興臨濠迄於洪武六年，凡戒敕之諄複、征伐之次第、禮樂之沿革、刑政之設施、羣臣之功過、四夷之朝貢，率多登載。乃宋濂敬序之曰：「功高萬古也，得國之正也，獨稟全智也，敬天勤民也，家法之嚴也，兵政有統也。」揭其大要於簡端矣。其見於《聖政記》者，起甲辰以至洪武三十一年，凡攻守之機宜、中外之政令、人才之用舍、制度之損益、詔命之敷宣、災祥之著見，頗已條列。乃夏原吉略論之曰：「制禮作樂，脩明典章，定郊祀而定學校，尊孔子而育賢才，黜異端而表章典籍，正神號而嚴秩祀典，察天文，推曆數，定封建，謹法律，慎賞罰，撫四夷。」總其大端於末篇也。此特其梗槩而已。他如《日曆》
translation_en:
…His magnificent achievements and mighty deeds shone through past and present. What are called his admirable words and good conduct, his inspired plans and exemplary standards, we have learned from accounts transmitted by elders and elucidated by scholars. Those recorded in the Daily Record (Rili) extend from his rise in Linhao to the sixth year of Hongwu. His earnest and repeated admonitions and commands, the sequence of his campaigns, continuities and changes in rites and music, the implementation of punishments and government, the merits and faults of his ministers, and tribute missions from the peoples of the four quarters were, for the most part, recorded therein. Song Lian reverently supplied a preface, saying: “His achievements surpass those of all ages; he acquired the realm with perfect legitimacy; he alone was endowed with complete wisdom; he revered Heaven and labored for the people; his rules for the imperial household were strict; his military administration had a unified order.” Thus he set out its principal themes at the beginning of the volume.

Those recorded in the Record of Sagely Government (Shengzheng ji) extend from the jiachen year to the thirty-first year of Hongwu. Strategic considerations in attack and defense, administrative orders at court and in the provinces, the employment and dismissal of men of talent, modifications to institutions, the promulgation of imperial edicts, and manifestations of calamities and auspicious signs were set out in considerable detail. Xia Yuanji then briefly discussed them, saying: “He established rites and created music, perfected and clarified statutes and regulations, settled the suburban sacrifices and established schools, honored Confucius and nurtured worthy talent, rejected heterodox teachings and exalted the canonical writings, rectified the titles of deities and strictly ordered the prescribed sacrifices, observed celestial phenomena, calculated the calendar, settled the system of enfeoffment, attended carefully to laws, exercised caution in rewards and punishments, and pacified the peoples of the four quarters.” Thus he summarized its main points in the concluding section. These are merely the broad outlines. Other works, such as the Daily Record…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
續編之所紀注五倫書之所採摭政要之
所裒次事蹟之所綜述未易殫數眞與典
謨訓誥相爲表裏而謂足以盡之乎迨我
皇上曆運中興德業並懋如
四郊分而陰陽位
九廟列而功德敘
玄極建而
烈祖歆
明堂立而
===
嚴父饗體玄象則
皇穹有宇倣金匱則
皇史有宬謹時巡則
大狩龍飛有錄重農事則無逸豳風有頌廣
聖謨則表尚書之三要揚
先德則疏遺治之五事明
大典以立人極毀土像以崇師道正祀儀以黜
虜族斥異端以銷佛像
七陵有述達精禋也
punctuated: 續編之所紀注，《五倫書》之所採摭，《政要》之所裒次，《事蹟》之所綜述，未易殫數，眞與典謨訓誥相爲表裏，而謂足以盡之乎？迨我皇上曆運中興，德業並懋，如四郊分而陰陽位，九廟列而功德敘，玄極建而烈祖歆，明堂立而嚴父饗。體玄象則皇穹有宇，倣金匱則皇史有宬；謹時巡則大狩龍飛有錄，重農事則無逸豳風有頌；廣聖謨則表《尚書》之三要，揚先德則疏遺治之五事；明大典以立人極，毀土像以崇師道，正祀儀以黜虜族，斥異端以銷佛像。七陵有述，達精禋也。
translation_en:
…what is recorded in the continuation, gathered in the Book of the Five Human Relationships, compiled in Essentials of Government, and comprehensively recounted in the Accounts of Deeds cannot readily be enumerated in full. These truly complement the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of antiquity. Could one claim that the foregoing suffices to exhaust them?

When our present emperor brought about a restoration in the course of dynastic destiny, his virtue and achievements flourished together. Thus, the four suburban altars were separately established, giving yin and yang their proper positions; the nine ancestral temples were arrayed, ordering the recognition of merit and virtue; the Palace of the Mysterious Ultimate was built, and the illustrious ancestors accepted its offerings; the Hall of Light was established, and his revered father received sacrifice. To embody the celestial configurations, a vault was provided for August Heaven; to imitate the metal coffer, a repository was provided for the imperial historical records. His care for seasonal inspection tours found expression in records of the Great Hunt and the Dragon’s Ascent; his concern for agriculture, in eulogies on Against Idleness and the Airs of Bin. To extend sagely counsel, he set forth three essentials of the Book of Documents; to exalt his predecessors’ virtue, he expounded five matters concerning their legacy of government. He clarified the great rites to establish the supreme standard for humanity, destroyed clay images to honor the Way of the Teacher, corrected sacrificial observances to exclude the barbarian lineage, and rejected heterodox teachings by melting down Buddhist images. There is an account of the seven imperial mausoleums, giving expression to the purity of his sacrificial devotion.…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
感雨有吟恤民隱也
平臺有詩敕時幾也
重華有籍端尚友也通
懿親之好則使
問時行杜倖門之入則爵賞日愼受交南之
欵則功收干羽絕塞北之請則
慮周帷幄
乾剛振而政令出於
朝廷人心順而敎化達於天下諸如此類眞
===
有非漢唐宋諸君所能彷咈萬一者何哉
亦曰
皇祖善於法
天而
皇上又善於法
祖耳夫言法天者莫著乎詩言法祖者莫辨於
春秋詩曰敬天之怒無敢戲豫又曰畏天
之威于時保之篇中陳述不一而足春秋
明王道黜伯功而於初稅畝作丘甲諸事
punctuated:
感雨有吟，恤民隱也；平臺有詩，敕時幾也；重華有籍，端尚友也。通懿親之好，則使問時行；杜倖門之入，則爵賞日愼；受交南之欵，則功收干羽；絕塞北之請，則慮周帷幄。乾剛振而政令出於朝廷，人心順而敎化達於天下。諸如此類，眞有非漢唐宋諸君所能彷咈萬一者，何哉？亦曰：皇祖善於法天，而皇上又善於法祖耳。
夫言法天者莫著乎詩，言法祖者莫辨於春秋。詩曰：「敬天之怒，無敢戲豫。」又曰：「畏天之威，于時保之。」篇中陳述，不一而足。春秋明王道，黜伯功，而於初稅畝、作丘甲諸事
translation_en:
…There are verses on being moved by rain, expressing concern for the people’s sufferings; poems on the Platform, urging vigilance over the first stirrings of affairs; and writings on Chonghua [?], rectifying the practice of taking the ancients as friends. To cultivate affection among imperial kinsmen, envoys regularly convey inquiries after their welfare. To close the avenues of advancement through undue favor, ranks and rewards are bestowed with ever greater care. In accepting Jiaonan’s submission, he achieves success through shields and plumes—the civilizing rites of peace. In rejecting requests from beyond the northern frontier, his deliberations within the command tent encompass every contingency. His firm, Heaven-like resolve is roused, and governmental commands issue from the imperial court; the people’s hearts submit, and moral instruction reaches all under Heaven. In matters such as these, his achievements truly exceed anything the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song could remotely approach. Why is this? It is simply that the Imperial Ancestor excelled at modeling himself on Heaven, and His Majesty in turn excels at modeling himself on his ancestor.
Now, nothing sets forth the principle of modeling oneself on Heaven more clearly than the Book of Odes, and nothing distinguishes the principle of modeling oneself on one’s ancestors more precisely than the Spring and Autumn Annals. The Odes says: “Respect Heaven’s anger; dare not indulge in frivolity or ease.” It also says: “Fear Heaven’s might, and thereby preserve yourself.” Its poems contain more statements of this kind than can readily be enumerated. The Spring and Autumn Annals elucidates the Way of the true king and disparages the achievements of hegemons; as for such matters as the first imposition of a tax on land by the mu and the establishment of military levies by the qiu …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
悉筆於書以垂鑒戒其維持法守何緫緫
也試觀我
皇祖端莊誠慎動稽天則甞曰人君一言一行
皆上通於天必敬以將之而後行無不善又
曰朕為人主惟思脩德致和以契天地之心
故見之實政不尚彌文蓋不特
郊祀而
面加戒諭
禱雨而躬執露曝也我
===
皇上則又恪遵
祖訓稽求實典觀述
祖德之詩可以推見緒餘諸所行事雖不規規
擬議而意自融貫誠所謂善繼善述矣然
且
欽天而形之記頌
畏星變而見之勅文夙夜兢業罔非對越是
其法天者正所以法
祖也與詩春秋所稱何異焉乃執事猶曰探其
punctuated: 悉筆於書，以垂鑒戒。其維持法守，何緫緫也！試觀我皇祖，端莊誠慎，動稽天則。甞曰：「人君一言一行，皆上通於天，必敬以將之，而後行無不善。」又曰：「朕為人主，惟思脩德致和，以契天地之心。」故見之實政，不尚彌文，蓋不特郊祀而面加戒諭、禱雨而躬執露曝也。我皇上則又恪遵祖訓，稽求實典。觀述祖德之詩，可以推見緒餘。諸所行事，雖不規規擬議，而意自融貫，誠所謂善繼善述矣。然且欽天而形之記頌，畏星變而見之勅文，夙夜兢業，罔非對越。是其法天者，正所以法祖也，與《詩》《春秋》所稱何異焉？乃執事猶曰：「探其
translation_en:
…all were recorded in the text to furnish examples and warnings for posterity. How manifold its efforts to uphold established standards! Consider our Imperial Ancestor: dignified, sincere, and circumspect, he measured his every action against Heaven’s rules. He once said: “Every word and deed of a ruler reaches Heaven above. Only when reverence guides them will all his actions be good.” He also said: “As ruler, I think only of cultivating virtue and bringing about harmony, so as to accord with the heart of Heaven and Earth.” Thus he expressed this in substantive governance, without prizing elaborate formalities. It was by no means only at the suburban sacrifices that he personally delivered admonitions, or when praying for rain that he himself stood exposed to the elements [?].

Our present Emperor, in turn, scrupulously follows the ancestral instructions and investigates precedents for substantive action. From his poems recounting the Ancestor’s virtue, one can infer further manifestations of this spirit. In all his actions, although he does not narrowly imitate and deliberate over every detail, his intentions naturally form a coherent whole. Truly, this is what is meant by skillfully carrying forward a predecessor’s intentions and deeds. Moreover, he expresses his reverence for Heaven in records and eulogies, and his awe at celestial anomalies in imperial edicts. Vigilant and conscientious morning and night, he acts always as though in the presence of Heaven. His emulation of Heaven is precisely his means of emulating the Ancestor. How does this differ from what the Book of Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals commend? Yet you, honored examiners, still say: “Investigate its…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
本原豈以
聖道難爲形容庸衆未易窺測乎夫亦求之心
而已蓋天下之治本于道而道本于心心
以體道則道純道以出治則治裕千聖授
受端不外此伏誦我
高皇諭曰此心如止水明鏡無分毫私意累之
然後揆事度物廓然無滯又曰人心虛靈乘
氣機出入操而存之爲難罔敢自暇自逸大
哉
===
聖言乎我
皇上敬一有箴五箴有註夫敬所以存其心而
不忽一所以純乎理而無雜也而又嚴
郊廟謹燕居孚言行貫終始則所以直乎內者
益密視聽言動皆聽命于心者也由之辨
是非察忠邪一政令端舉止則所以方乎
外者益慎蓋嘗論之
高祖之學舉其大而
皇上之學會其精同條共貫眞有互相發明者
punctuated:
本原，豈以聖道難爲形容，庸衆未易窺測乎？夫亦求之心而已。蓋天下之治本于道，而道本于心。心以體道，則道純；道以出治，則治裕。千聖授受，端不外此。伏誦我高皇諭曰：「此心如止水明鏡，無分毫私意累之，然後揆事度物，廓然無滯。」又曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難，罔敢自暇自逸。」大哉，聖言乎！
我皇上《敬一》有箴，五箴有註。夫敬所以存其心而不忽，一所以純乎理而無雜也。而又嚴郊廟，謹燕居，孚言行，貫終始，則所以直乎內者益密，視聽言動皆聽命于心者也。由之辨是非，察忠邪，一政令，端舉止，則所以方乎外者益慎。蓋嘗論之：高祖之學舉其大，而皇上之學會其精，同條共貫，眞有互相發明者。
translation_en:
…its fundamental source—is this because the Way of the sage is difficult to describe, and ordinary people cannot readily fathom it? One need only seek it in the mind. For the governance of all under Heaven is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in the mind. When the mind embodies the Way, the Way is pure; when the Way issues in governance, governance is ample. What the myriad sages have transmitted and received lies entirely within this. I reverently recite an instruction of our Emperor Gao: “This mind should be like still water and a bright mirror, unburdened by the slightest selfish intention. Only then can it assess affairs and weigh things, open and unobstructed.” He also said: “The human mind is empty and numinous, coming and going with the workings of vital energy. To hold fast to it and preserve it is difficult; one dares not indulge in leisure or ease.” How great are these sagely words!
Our present Emperor has composed an admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi), and commentaries on the Five Admonitions. Reverence preserves the mind from neglect; oneness keeps it pure in accordance with principle, without admixture. Moreover, he solemnly attends to the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple rites, exercises care in private life, makes his words and deeds accord, and remains consistent from beginning to end. Thus his means of making the inner self upright become ever more exacting: seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting all obey the mind. Through this he distinguishes right from wrong, discerns loyalty and wickedness, unifies governmental commands, and rectifies his conduct. Thus his means of making his outward actions square become ever more circumspect. I have considered this: the learning of Gaozu sets forth the essentials, while the learning of our present Emperor brings together their subtlest significance. They share the same branches and a common thread, truly illuminating one another.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
故本原澄徹探之無際氣機充溢施之不
匱以是法天則天心合以二氣爲端以五
行爲綏以萬化爲委者在是矣以是法
祖則
祖德孚以仁義爲榦以事功爲標以文章爲葩
者在是矣然裁成輔相範圍彌綸則有以
賛化育之不及而長養培植開廣流衍者
又有以増創造之舊而俾之維新其極也
天下一心萬類一氣太和凝溢道化融暢
===
可以貞日月可以奠山川可以擯鬼神可
以綏百物可以膺五福可以協庶徵可以
畜四靈可以召諸瑞
鴻休
玄化淳曜充溢其始也法
天而旣則與天參且配天矣始也法
祖而旣則與
祖光且紹
祖矣要亦不過自此心推之信乎
punctuated: 故本原澄徹，探之無際；氣機充溢，施之不匱。以是法天，則天心合，以二氣爲端，以五行爲綏，以萬化爲委者，在是矣。以是法祖，則祖德孚，以仁義爲榦，以事功爲標，以文章爲葩者，在是矣。然裁成輔相，範圍彌綸，則有以賛化育之不及；而長養培植，開廣流衍者，又有以増創造之舊，而俾之維新。其極也，天下一心，萬類一氣，太和凝溢，道化融暢，可以貞日月，可以奠山川，可以擯鬼神，可以綏百物，可以膺五福，可以協庶徵，可以畜四靈，可以召諸瑞。鴻休玄化，淳曜充溢。其始也法天，而旣則與天參，且配天矣；始也法祖，而旣則與祖光，且紹祖矣。要亦不過自此心推之，信乎，
translation_en: Thus the fundamental source is clear and limpid, its depths boundless to exploration; the animating force is abundant, inexhaustible in its application. Taking Heaven as the model through this, one accords with Heaven’s heart: herein lie the two forces of yin and yang as the beginning, the Five Phases as the ordering principle [?], and the myriad transformations as the outcome. Taking the ancestors as the model through this, one realizes their virtue: herein lie benevolence and righteousness as the trunk, practical achievements as the branches, and literary expression as the blossoms. Yet by shaping and assisting, encompassing and comprehensively ordering, one can supplement what the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth leave unaccomplished. Through nurturing and cultivating, expanding and extending, one can also augment the foundations already established and make them anew. At its culmination, all under Heaven share one heart, and the myriad kinds of beings share one vital force. Supreme harmony gathers and overflows; the transforming influence of the Way pervades all freely. It can establish the constancy of the sun and moon, secure the mountains and rivers, ward off ghosts and spirits [?], bring peace to all beings, receive the Five Blessings, bring the various signs into accord, nurture the Four Numinous Creatures, and summon every auspicious portent. Vast blessings and mysterious transforming power, pure and radiant, fill all things to overflowing. At first one takes Heaven as the model; ultimately one stands alongside Heaven and even becomes its match. At first one takes the ancestors as the model; ultimately one shares their glory and carries on their legacy. In essence, this is no more than extending what proceeds from this heart. Truly, …

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
作述之隆先後一揆
盛德大業充塞天地而超越今古殆猶聞簫
韶而知舜之難名覩河洛而知禹之莫及
矣書曰維天聰明惟聖時憲
皇祖以之又曰以覲耿光以揚大烈
皇上有焉敢以是爲
聖明頌
第二問
朱成文
===
同考試官教諭安 批 樂書亡佚久矣季通獨持
新見駁正前聞一時學士宗之然猶有遺論此作考據精
詳而擴所未發其有見之言乎
同考試官教諭冀 批 上下古今是非朗朗在目
賛明曠典以還虞氏之隆端有望於子矣
考試官教諭黃 批 考據詳明品裁精當是
嘗究心於樂律者取之不徒以文而已
考試官教諭朱 批 理核而詞足以達錄之以
式多士
punctuated:
作述之隆，先後一揆。盛德大業，充塞天地而超越今古，殆猶聞簫韶而知舜之難名，覩河洛而知禹之莫及矣。《書》曰：「維天聰明，惟聖時憲。」皇祖以之。又曰：「以覲耿光，以揚大烈。」皇上有焉。敢以是爲聖明頌。

第二問
朱成文

同考試官教諭安批：樂書亡佚久矣，季通獨持新見，駁正前聞，一時學士宗之。然猶有遺論，此作考據精詳，而擴所未發，其有見之言乎！

同考試官教諭冀批：上下古今，是非朗朗在目。賛明曠典，以還虞氏之隆，端有望於子矣。

考試官教諭黃批：考據詳明，品裁精當，是嘗究心於樂律者。取之不徒以文而已。

考試官教諭朱批：理核而詞足以達，錄之以式多士。
translation_en:
…In the grandeur of founding and carrying forward, predecessor and successor follow a single standard. Their abundant virtue and great achievements fill Heaven and Earth and surpass ancient and modern times. It is much like hearing the Shao music and realizing how difficult it is to describe Shun’s greatness, or beholding the He and Luo rivers and realizing that Yu cannot be equaled. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven is perceptive and discerning; the sage takes this as his model.” Your Imperial Ancestor followed this. It also says: “To display his brilliant radiance and proclaim his great achievements.” Your Majesty embodies this. I venture to offer these words in praise of Your sagely wisdom.

Second Question
Zhu Chengwen

Comment by Associate Examiner An, Instructor: The writings on music have long been lost. Jitong alone advanced fresh insights, refuting and correcting earlier accounts, and the scholars of his time took him as their authority. Yet matters remained undiscussed. This essay is meticulous and detailed in its examination of evidence and develops what had not yet been elucidated. Surely these are words of genuine insight!

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: Ranging across antiquity and the present, this essay sets right and wrong clearly before our eyes. In assisting the elucidation of grand rites so as to restore the splendor of the age of Yu Shun, we assuredly place our hopes in you.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The examination of evidence is detailed and clear, and the assessments are precise and sound. This is someone who has devoted serious thought to musical pitch standards. I select this essay for more than its literary merits alone.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The reasoning is sound, and the language adequately conveys it. I include it as a model for the many candidates.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
樂之用必有數也欲精其義者自辨數始
矣樂之體必有義也欲辨其數者自精義
始矣故本氣以定律因律以審音可語數
矣而其義寓焉義也者數之適其正者也
反情以和志緣志以定官可語義已而其
數寓焉數也者義之成其文者也是故絲
竹金石樂之器也高下清濁樂之音也論
倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也夫
器尚象而音尚聲聞睹之所及也非數耶
===
記曰其數可陳是也情惟危而官惟微中
和之所基也非義耶記曰其義難知是也
通極於人心之原而達乎造化之蘊者然
後可以幾精義之學貫徹乎聲氣之元而
底乎道律之妙者然後可以與辨數之識
夫是以施於金石越於聲音用於宗廟社
稷事乎山川鬼神而與民同者也惟樂不
可以偽為而可易言乎哉執事策問禮樂
於正樂獨有感焉而專究律吕之說誠探
punctuated: 樂之用必有數也，欲精其義者，自辨數始矣。樂之體必有義也，欲辨其數者，自精義始矣。故本氣以定律，因律以審音，可語數矣，而其義寓焉。義也者，數之適其正者也。反情以和志，緣志以定官，可語義已，而其數寓焉。數也者，義之成其文者也。是故絲竹金石，樂之器也；高下清濁，樂之音也；論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。夫器尚象，而音尚聲，聞睹之所及也，非數耶？《記》曰：「其數可陳。」是也。情惟危，而官惟微，中和之所基也，非義耶？《記》曰：「其義難知。」是也。通極於人心之原，而達乎造化之蘊者，然後可以幾精義之學；貫徹乎聲氣之元，而底乎道律之妙者，然後可以與辨數之識。夫是以施於金石，越於聲音，用於宗廟社稷，事乎山川鬼神，而與民同者也。惟樂不可以偽為，而可易言乎哉？執事策問禮樂，於正樂獨有感焉，而專究律吕之說，誠探
translation_en:
The functioning of music necessarily involves numerical relations. Those who wish to grasp its principles precisely must begin by distinguishing these relations. The essential constitution of music necessarily involves principles. Those who wish to distinguish its numerical relations must begin by grasping its principles precisely. Thus, by grounding pitch standards in qi and using those standards to examine tones, one can discuss numerical relations; yet principles reside within them. Principles are numerical relations attaining their proper measure. By returning to the feelings to harmonize the intentions, and following the intentions to determine music’s functions, one can discuss principles; yet numerical relations reside within them. Numerical relations are the patterned expression of principles.

Thus, silk strings, bamboo pipes, metal bells, and stone chimes are music’s instruments; high and low, clear and turbid are music’s tones; ordered relationships free from trouble are music’s true character; delight, joy, pleasure, and affection are music’s functions. Instruments give priority to form, and tones to sound: these lie within the reach of hearing and sight. Are they not matters of numerical relations? The Record of Rites says, “Its numerical relations can be set forth.” This is what it means. Feelings are precarious, while music’s functions are subtle; they provide the foundation for equilibrium and harmony. Are they not matters of principle? The Record of Rites says, “Its principles are difficult to know.” This is what it means.

Only those who penetrate to the very source of the human heart and comprehend the hidden workings of creation can approach the learning that grasps principles precisely. Only those who thoroughly understand the origin of sound and qi and reach the subtleties of the Way and pitch standards [?] can possess the discernment needed to distinguish numerical relations. Through this, music is imparted to bells and chimes, issues forth in sounds, is employed in the ancestral temples and at the altars of soil and grain, serves the spirits of mountains and rivers, and is shared with the people. Music cannot be made through pretense: how, then, could it be discussed lightly?

In your policy question on ritual and music, you show particular concern for putting music in order and investigate specifically the theory of the pitch standards, lü and lü. You are indeed probing…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
本矣愚生閩產也誦說前哲間有所疑請
先窮其法而後質之可乎夫律呂何昉也
黃帝使伶倫取嶰谷之竹制十二之管吹
陽律以應鳳鳴者六曰律律以言乎法也
以統氣類物也吹陰律以應凰鳴者六曰
呂呂以言乎侶也以助陽宣氣也故律之
屬六曰黃鐘太簇姑洗蕤賓夷則無射是
也呂之屬六曰大呂夾鐘仲呂林鐘南呂
應鐘是也此律呂之所由起也究其義焉
===
則所假之物九成數也故管之寸九也黃
鐘之聲樂之端也半之清聲也倍之緩聲
也三分其一以損益之相生之聲也十二
變而復黃鐘聲之總數也乃命之曰十二
律旋迭爲均均有七調合八十四調播之
於八音著之於歌頌以奉天地事祖考和
君臣接賓旅恢政敎而厚風俗此樂之所
由起也三五神聖莫不有樂而文武之積
樂始大備考其官則大司樂大師典同也
punctuated:
本矣。愚生閩產也，誦說前哲，間有所疑，請先窮其法而後質之，可乎？夫律呂何昉也？黃帝使伶倫取嶰谷之竹，制十二之管。吹陽律以應鳳鳴者六，曰律。律以言乎法也，以統氣類物也。吹陰律以應凰鳴者六，曰呂。呂以言乎侶也，以助陽宣氣也。故律之屬六，曰黃鐘、太簇、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射，是也。呂之屬六，曰大呂、夾鐘、仲呂、林鐘、南呂、應鐘，是也。此律呂之所由起也。

究其義焉，則所假之物，九成數也，故管之寸九也。黃鐘之聲，樂之端也；半之，清聲也；倍之，緩聲也；三分其一以損益之，相生之聲也；十二變而復黃鐘，聲之總數也。乃命之曰十二律，旋迭爲均，均有七調，合八十四調。播之於八音，著之於歌頌，以奉天地、事祖考、和君臣、接賓旅、恢政敎而厚風俗。此樂之所由起也。三五神聖莫不有樂，而文武之積，樂始大備。考其官，則大司樂、大師、典同也。
translation_en:
…the root indeed. I, an unworthy student, am a native of Min. In reciting and discussing the teachings of earlier sages, I sometimes have doubts. May I first examine the methods thoroughly and then submit these doubts for your judgment? Where did the yang and yin pitch standards originate? Huangdi had Ling Lun take bamboo from Xiegu and fashion twelve pipes. The six yang pitches blown to correspond to the calls of the male phoenix were called lü 律. Here lü means a rule: they regulate qi and classify things. The six yin pitches blown to correspond to the calls of the female phoenix were called lü 呂. Here lü means a companion: they assist yang and disseminate qi. Thus the six yang pitch standards are Huangzhong, Taicu, Guxian, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi. The six yin pitch standards are Dalu, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong. This is how the yang and yin pitch standards originated.

Examining their significance, we find that, in the material objects employed, nine is the number of completion; hence the pipe measures nine cun. The sound of Huangzhong is the starting point of music. Halving its length produces a higher sound; doubling it produces a lower sound. Subtracting or adding one-third produces pitches that generate one another. Twelve transformations return to Huangzhong, completing the full cycle of pitches. These were therefore named the twelve pitch standards. Each serves in turn as the tonal basis, with seven modes for each, making eighty-four modes in all. These are sounded through the eight classes of musical instruments and expressed in songs and hymns, to honor Heaven and Earth, serve the ancestors, bring ruler and ministers into harmony, receive guests and travelers, extend government and moral instruction, and enrich social customs. This is how music originated. The divine sages—the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—all had music, but only through the accumulated achievements of Kings Wen and Wu did music become fully developed. Examining its officials, we find the Musician-in-Chief, the Music Master, and the Director of Pitch Standards.

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其器則不越乎五音十二律而已由周而
下鐘律聲廢司馬遷攬三代遺文以著律
書其所載十二律分寸之數相生之法雖
合而未詳劉歆推曆律之委折以明五事
其所言十二辰積算之數職掌之官雖詳
而未盡蔡邕劉安舉其器而鐘律之議無
定說萬寶常王朴得其末而製尺之法多
互見杜夔荀勗徒誇平生穎敏之資而阮
咸夙號神解竟阻正變之悟錢樂之陳仲
===
儒雖擅一時音雅之名而信都芳世稱知
音竟守輪扇之曲自秦至漢數百年惟太
子丞鮑興之庶幾斯學爾而人祖音息未
聞嗣其響者由漢至隋垂十代所存者鐘
宮一調及七聲爾而餘爲啞鐘不復睹其
全者迨於有宋則研神音器者阮逸李照
范鎮也而空談鮮精索之功號稱名儒者
司馬光胡瑗楊時也而考究多拘攣之見
蓋易竹爲銅取同天下之風俗其言則繆
punctuated: 其器則不越乎五音十二律而已。由周而下，鐘律聲廢。司馬遷攬三代遺文以著《律書》，其所載十二律分寸之數、相生之法，雖合而未詳。劉歆推曆律之委折以明五事，其所言十二辰積算之數、職掌之官，雖詳而未盡。蔡邕、劉安舉其器，而鐘律之議無定說；萬寶常、王朴得其末，而製尺之法多互見。杜夔、荀勗徒誇平生穎敏之資，而阮咸夙號神解，竟阻正變之悟；錢樂之、陳仲儒雖擅一時音雅之名，而信都芳世稱知音，竟守輪扇之曲。自秦至漢數百年，惟太子丞鮑興之庶幾斯學爾，而人祖音息，未聞嗣其響者。由漢至隋垂十代，所存者鐘宮一調及七聲爾，而餘爲啞鐘，不復睹其全者。迨於有宋，則研神音器者阮逸、李照、范鎮也，而空談鮮精索之功；號稱名儒者司馬光、胡瑗、楊時也，而考究多拘攣之見。蓋易竹爲銅，取同天下之風俗，其言則繆；
translation_en:
…As for its instruments, they encompassed no more than the five notes and twelve pitch standards. After the Zhou, the sounds of bells and pitch standards fell into disuse. Sima Qian gathered surviving writings of the Three Dynasties to compose his Treatise on Pitch Standards. Its measurements of the twelve pitch standards in inches and tenths of an inch, and its methods for generating them successively, were consistent but insufficiently detailed. Liu Xin traced the intricacies of calendrical and pitch calculations to elucidate the five matters. His accounts of accumulated numerical calculations for the twelve earthly branches and of the officials responsible were detailed but incomplete. Cai Yong and Liu An brought forward their instruments, yet discussions of bells and pitch standards reached no settled conclusion. Wan Baochang and Wang Pu grasped only the peripheral details, while their methods of making measuring rules frequently overlapped. Du Kui and Xun Xu merely boasted of their lifelong gifts of quick intelligence; Ruan Xian, long reputed to possess inspired understanding, ultimately failed to comprehend the principal and altered tones. Although Qian Lezhi and Chen Zhongru enjoyed contemporary renown for musical refinement, Xindu Fang, celebrated as a connoisseur of music, ultimately remained confined to the wheel-and-fan device [?].

In the several centuries from the Qin through the Han, only Bao Xing, Assistant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, came close to mastering this learning. Yet with his passing the sound ceased [?], and no successor was heard to carry on its resonance. From the Han to the Sui, through nearly ten dynasties, only the single bell mode of gong and its seven notes survived; the rest were mute bells, and the complete system could no longer be seen. When the Song arrived, those who devoted their minds to musical instruments included Ruan Yi, Li Zhao, and Fan Zhen, but their empty discussions yielded little rigorous investigation. Those acclaimed as eminent Confucian scholars included Sima Guang, Hu Yuan, and Yang Shi, but their inquiries were often constrained by narrow views. As for replacing bamboo with bronze in order to make customs uniform throughout the realm, that argument was mistaken…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
以準代竹取其審聲音之易達其法則悖
或以律求黍而用黍之法未定或以尺求
律而辨尺之智多爽文公朱子謂諸賢之
說終不能以相一也信哉時則有若蔡季
通旁搜遠取竭半生探討之功冥契深造
資師友淵源之力獨究心於律呂之學而
豁然貫通於是新書作焉自今觀之明律
呂之本原則揭黃鐘以灼聲氣之元始而
自黃鐘之實以至於謹權量凡十有三章
===
===
焉詳律呂之證辨則提造律以彰萬事之
根本而自律長短圍徑之數以至於度量
權衡凡十章焉舉其凡則黃鐘十一律之
本也吹之而聲和候之而氣應而後數始
形焉黃鐘得則以生十一正律十一正律
各自爲宮以生五聲二變之律合十二正
律旋宮各生五聲二變之律合之爲八十
四律也約其要則黃鐘者其始也十二律
者其末也旋宮十二律者其始也八十四
punctuated: 以準代竹，取其審聲音之易達，其法則悖。或以律求黍，而用黍之法未定；或以尺求律，而辨尺之智多爽。文公朱子謂諸賢之說終不能以相一也，信哉！時則有若蔡季通，旁搜遠取，竭半生探討之功；冥契深造，資師友淵源之力。獨究心於律呂之學，而豁然貫通，於是新書作焉。自今觀之，明律呂之本原，則揭黃鐘以灼聲氣之元始，而自黃鐘之實以至於謹權量，凡十有三章焉；詳律呂之證辨，則提造律以彰萬事之根本，而自律長短圍徑之數以至於度量權衡，凡十章焉。舉其凡，則黃鐘，十一律之本也。吹之而聲和，候之而氣應，而後數始形焉。黃鐘得，則以生十一正律；十一正律各自爲宮，以生五聲二變之律。合十二正律，旋宮各生五聲二變之律，合之爲八十四律也。約其要，則黃鐘者，其始也；十二律者，其末也。旋宮，十二律者，其始也；八十四
translation_en:
…To replace bamboo pitch pipes with the zhun tuning instrument, on the grounds that it makes the assessment of musical sounds readily intelligible, is a misguided method. Some sought to determine the millet grain standard from the pitch standards, although the method of using millet grains remained unsettled; others sought to determine pitch standards from measuring rods, yet their judgments in distinguishing the rods were often mistaken. Master Zhu Xi, honored with the posthumous title Wengong, said that the explanations of these worthy scholars could never ultimately be reconciled. How true!

At that time there was Cai Jitong, who searched widely and drew on distant sources, devoting half his life to investigation. Through profound understanding and advanced study, he drew upon the intellectual lineage transmitted by his teachers and friends. He applied himself especially to the study of pitch standards and attained a sudden, comprehensive understanding. Thus his New Treatise came to be written.

Viewed today, its elucidation of the origins of pitch standards sets forth Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch, to illuminate the beginnings of sound and qi. From the capacity of the Huangzhong pipe through the careful regulation of weights and measures, there are thirteen chapters in all. Its detailed examination of evidence and disputed points concerning pitch standards foregrounds the construction of pitch pipes to reveal the foundation of all things. From the numerical specifications for the lengths, circumferences, and diameters of pitch pipes through measures of length and capacity, weights, and balances, there are ten chapters in all.

To state its general principles: Huangzhong is the foundation of the other eleven pitch standards. When its pipe is blown, its sound must be harmonious; when used to observe seasonal qi, it must respond to that qi. Only then do the numerical relationships begin to take form. Once Huangzhong has been established, it generates the eleven other standard pitches. Each of these eleven in turn serves as gong, the tonic, to generate the pitches of the five notes and the two altered notes. Taking all twelve standard pitches together and rotating the tonic, each generates the pitches of the five notes and two altered notes, making eighty-four pitches in all. To summarize the essentials: Huangzhong is the starting point, and the twelve pitch standards are the endpoint. In rotating the tonic, the twelve pitch standards are the starting point, and the eighty-four…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
調者其末也而十二大調則黃鐘第一大
調其始也而終於應鐘第十二大調其末
也至於十二律大調莫不有始末之節焉
証以上生下生之說則以十二辰生十二
律而以陽律起數陰律減之三分損益八
位相生得比次降殺之序非陰陽消長之
機乎取諸旋相為宮之旨則以十二律配
十二日而以正變相運減半節之黃鐘常
尊不為諸役合尊卑先後之法非天地自
===
然之分乎言乎候氣則密室閉戶實葭覆
緹桉律候之以驗十二月之氣而時序正
矣言乎審度則黃鐘之管長九十黍之廣
積九寸積寸至引而五度審矣言乎嘉量
則容千二百黍積八百一十分積龠至斛
而五量嘉矣言乎謹權衡則重十有二銖
積銖至石而五權謹矣夫制律者必先求
聲氣之元以定黃鐘之管然後十二律定
而和氣可道此正樂之法不可易者而漢
punctuated:
調者其末也。而十二大調，則黃鐘第一大調其始也，而終於應鐘第十二大調，其末也。至於十二律大調，莫不有始末之節焉。証以上生下生之說，則以十二辰生十二律，而以陽律起數，陰律減之，三分損益，八位相生，得比次降殺之序，非陰陽消長之機乎？取諸旋相為宮之旨，則以十二律配十二日，而以正變相運，減半節之，黃鐘常尊，不為諸役，合尊卑先後之法，非天地自然之分乎？

言乎候氣，則密室閉戶，實葭覆緹，桉律候之，以驗十二月之氣，而時序正矣。言乎審度，則黃鐘之管長九十黍之廣，積九寸，積寸至引，而五度審矣。言乎嘉量，則容千二百黍，積八百一十分，積龠至斛，而五量嘉矣。言乎謹權衡，則重十有二銖，積銖至石，而五權謹矣。

夫制律者，必先求聲氣之元，以定黃鐘之管，然後十二律定，而和氣可道。此正樂之法不可易者，而漢
translation_en:
…modes are its culmination. As for the twelve major modal groups, the first, Huangzhong (Yellow Bell), is their beginning, and they conclude with the twelfth, Yingzhong (Responding Bell), their culmination. Each of the major modal groups of the twelve pitch standards thus has its ordered beginning and end. If we verify this through the theory of upward and downward generation, the twelve earthly branches generate the twelve pitch standards. The calculation begins with the yang pitch standards and reduces the yin standards; through subtracting or adding one-third and generating successive pitches eight positions apart, it obtains an ordered sequence of progressive diminution. Is this not the mechanism by which yin and yang wane and wax? If we draw upon the principle of rotating the pitches so that each serves as gong, the twelve pitch standards are matched with twelve days. The regular and altered pitches operate in succession, and their lengths are regulated by halving. Huangzhong always occupies the position of honor and does not serve the others. This accords with the rules governing higher and lower rank, precedence and succession. Is this not the natural ordering of Heaven and Earth?

As for observing the qi, one closes the doors of a sealed chamber, fills the pitch pipes with reed-membrane ashes, covers them with red silk, and observes them according to their pitch standards to test the qi of the twelve months. The sequence of the seasons is thereby correctly established. As for determining measures of length, the Huangzhong pipe is ninety millet-grain widths long, amounting to nine cun. By accumulating cun up to yin, the five measures of length are determined. As for standardizing measures of capacity, it holds twelve hundred millet grains, amounting to eight hundred and ten cubic fen. By accumulating yue up to hu, the five measures of capacity are standardized. As for ensuring precision in weighing, its contents weigh twelve zhu. By accumulating zhu up to shi, the five measures of weight are made precise.

Those who establish pitch standards must first seek the source of sound and qi in order to fix the Huangzhong pipe. Only then can the twelve pitch standards be established and harmonious qi be guided. This method of rectifying music cannot be altered. Yet the History of the Han…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
書隋志及房庶之徒乃拘拘於尺黍開爲
縱橫長短之說其謬益甚矣不有元定之
書則羣言日殽何時巳哉朱子稱其明白
淵深縝密通暢可以補樂書之缺誠非虛
美也元定以攷聲候氣爲得古人制作之
本而截竹候氣之說當時號爲卓然者雖
然愚生竊有疑焉嘗自其候氣之法推之
黃鐘候子月之氣其律九寸大呂候丑月
倍律八寸三分有奇計一月而氣之上升
===
不過五分一釐三毫而林鐘南呂乃僅三
分奇耳信如其說則九寸之下地極深厚
何能遽升以應黃鐘之律乎且十二月之
氣百里之內隨高下而一時並應耶此則
可疑也自配月之說推之王者居常如食
舉登車則用當月之律故子月奏黃鐘之
均寅月奏太簇之均至於大祀享始合樂
而六律迭奏禮王者宮縣四面備十二辰
之方位故樂縣之後亦依之律之配月爲
punctuated: 書、隋志及房庶之徒，乃拘拘於尺黍，開爲縱橫長短之說，其謬益甚矣。不有元定之書，則羣言日殽，何時巳哉？朱子稱其明白淵深，縝密通暢，可以補樂書之缺，誠非虛美也。元定以攷聲候氣爲得古人制作之本，而截竹候氣之說，當時號爲卓然者。雖然，愚生竊有疑焉。嘗自其候氣之法推之：黃鐘候子月之氣，其律九寸；大呂候丑月，倍律八寸三分有奇。計一月而氣之上升，不過五分一釐三毫，而林鐘、南呂乃僅三分奇耳。信如其說，則九寸之下，地極深厚，何能遽升以應黃鐘之律乎？且十二月之氣，百里之內，隨高下而一時並應耶？此則可疑也。自配月之說推之：王者居常，如食舉、登車，則用當月之律，故子月奏黃鐘之均，寅月奏太簇之均。至於大祀享，始合樂，而六律迭奏。禮，王者宮縣，四面備十二辰之方位，故樂縣之後亦依之。律之配月爲
translation_en:
…the Book of Han, the musical treatise in the Book of Sui, and men such as Fang Shu cling narrowly to rulers and millet grains, elaborating theories of longitudinal and transverse measurement, length and shortness; their errors grow ever more serious. Without Yuanding’s book, the various accounts would become more confused by the day: when would this ever cease? Master Zhu praised it as lucid and profound, meticulous and coherent, capable of filling the gaps in writings on music. This was certainly no empty praise. Yuanding held that investigating sounds and observing qi recovered the foundations of the ancients’ institutions, and his theory of cutting bamboo pipes to observe qi was regarded at the time as outstanding. Nevertheless, I, an ignorant student, privately have doubts.

Consider first his method of observing qi. The Huangzhong pitch pipe observes the qi of the zi month and is nine cun long; Dalu observes that of the chou month, its doubled pipe [?] measuring eight cun and three fen, with a remainder. Calculated over one month, the upward rise of qi amounts to no more than five fen, one li, and three hao; between Linzhong and Nanlü, it is only a little over three fen. If his account is indeed correct, the earth below those nine cun is exceedingly deep and thick: how could qi rise so abruptly to respond to the Huangzhong pipe? Moreover, within an area of a hundred li, would the qi of the twelve months respond simultaneously at every elevation? This is doubtful.

Consider next the explanation for matching pitches with months. In his ordinary activities, such as taking a meal or mounting his carriage, the king used the pitch appropriate to the current month. Thus, in the zi month, music was played in the Huangzhong scale, and in the yin month, in the Taicu scale. Only at great sacrificial offerings was the full musical ensemble brought together, with the six yang pitches played in turn. According to ritual practice, the king’s instruments were suspended on all four sides, encompassing the positions of the twelve earthly branches. Thus, what followed the suspension of the instruments [?] also conformed to this arrangement. The matching of pitches with months was for…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
是耳豈謂候氣哉此則可疑也自製律之
說推之謂以律之分寸爲樂器等差而後
聲不相奪是曰從律和聲儒者失其本旨
廼欲以竹管之聲與人聲相比是以求聲
於律謂竹管卽律也虞書以律與度量衡
並稱以其皆度物之器也故竹管非律律
之准也此則可疑也自累黍之法言之黃
鐘之長九十分空徑三分必千二百黍而
後滿耳共以九十黍爲黃鐘之長則儒者
===
一黍爲分之誤也夫一黍果可以爲分而
又必用千二百之數則所謂欲得其廣以
求聲者似矣今累九十黍而不合則夫千
二百之數乃所以求長而非求廣也此則
可疑也夫微言奧旨豈淺陋所能窺識而
先儒亦有以新書爲蔡氏未試之方故不
敢自已其疑也雖然此所謂數也抑末矣
不曰有義乎官者性也情者情也中和致
而禮樂出焉故曰知樂則幾於禮其原一
punctuated:
是耳，豈謂候氣哉？此則可疑也。自製律之說推之，謂以律之分寸爲樂器等差，而後聲不相奪，是曰從律和聲。儒者失其本旨，廼欲以竹管之聲與人聲相比，是以求聲於律，謂竹管卽律也。《虞書》以律與度量衡並稱，以其皆度物之器也。故竹管非律，律之准也。此則可疑也。自累黍之法言之，黃鐘之長九十分，空徑三分，必千二百黍而後滿耳。共以九十黍爲黃鐘之長，則儒者一黍爲分之誤也。夫一黍果可以爲分，而又必用千二百之數，則所謂欲得其廣以求聲者似矣。今累九十黍而不合，則夫千二百之數乃所以求長，而非求廣也。此則可疑也。
夫微言奧旨，豈淺陋所能窺識？而先儒亦有以《新書》爲蔡氏未試之方，故不敢自已其疑也。雖然，此所謂數也，抑末矣。不曰有義乎？官者性也，情者情也。中和致而禮樂出焉，故曰：「知樂則幾於禮。」其原一
translation_en:
…this alone; how could it mean watching for the arrival of qi? This, then, is open to doubt. Reasoning from the account of how pitch standards were made, one uses their measurements in fen and cun to establish gradations among musical instruments, so that their sounds do not overpower one another. This is called harmonizing sounds by following pitch standards. Confucian scholars have lost sight of the original intent and instead seek to compare the sounds of bamboo pipes with the human voice. Thus they seek sound in the pitch standards, taking bamboo pipes themselves to be those standards. The Book of Yu mentions pitch standards alongside measures of length, capacity, and weight because all are instruments for measuring things. Thus bamboo pipes are not the pitch standards themselves, but gauges for them. This, then, is open to doubt. Speaking of the method of lining up millet grains, the Huangzhong pitch pipe is ninety fen long, with an internal diameter of three fen, and requires twelve hundred grains to fill it. To take ninety grains as the length of Huangzhong is the scholars’ error of treating one grain as one fen. If one grain could indeed serve as one fen, and the number twelve hundred must also be used, then the claim that one seeks its breadth in order to obtain the sound would seem plausible. Yet lining up ninety grains does not yield agreement; therefore, the number twelve hundred serves to determine the length, not the breadth. This, then, is open to doubt.
How could someone of my shallow learning discern these subtle words and profound meanings? Yet earlier scholars have also regarded the New Book as Master Cai’s untested method, so I dare not suppress my doubts. Nevertheless, these are what are called numerical calculations, and are, after all, secondary matters. Is it not said that there is also underlying meaning? “Office” is human nature, and “feeling” is emotion [?]. When equilibrium and harmony are fully attained, ritual and music emerge from them. Hence it is said: “To understand music is to come close to ritual.” Their source is one…

title: 嘉靖三十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也執事幸禮書之存而致感於正樂愚則
曰正樂與禮而俱存也皇帝之律豈假諸
數者哉蓋其垂衣而治至和浹洽鳳鳥來
鳴是爲和氣之應故聽之以制律爾恭惟
聖天子在上合天地之德建中和之極和氣流
行熏烝於宇宙間魯兩生所謂禮樂百年
而後興維其時也必有鳳凰來儀以應太
和之運恊至治之聲愚生何幸躬逢其盛
第三問
===
王墀
同考試官教諭鄺批氏族之學先王所以統攝
人心章明教化事若迂緩所繫實重學士蓋難言之此作
考據精詳末復歸之立宗法正學術尤爲有見
同考試官學正彭批問學宏博而品評不爽
古稱胥臣多聞張華博物當不過是矣三復欽袵
考試官教諭黃批考據精詳卓有定裁是
蓋博而能精其應世之士乎
考試官教諭朱批學博而辭復鬯達錄之
punctuated:
也。執事幸禮書之存，而致感於正樂，愚則曰：正樂與禮而俱存也。皇帝之律，豈假諸數者哉？蓋其垂衣而治，至和浹洽，鳳鳥來鳴，是爲和氣之應，故聽之以制律爾。恭惟聖天子在上，合天地之德，建中和之極，和氣流行，熏烝於宇宙間。魯兩生所謂禮樂百年而後興，維其時也。必有鳳凰來儀，以應太和之運，恊至治之聲。愚生何幸，躬逢其盛！
第三問
王墀
同考試官教諭鄺批：氏族之學，先王所以統攝人心、章明教化，事若迂緩，所繫實重，學士蓋難言之。此作考據精詳，末復歸之立宗法、正學術，尤爲有見。
同考試官學正彭批：問學宏博，而品評不爽。古稱胥臣多聞、張華博物，當不過是矣。三復欽袵。
考試官教諭黃批：考據精詳，卓有定裁，是蓋博而能精，其應世之士乎！
考試官教諭朱批：學博而辭復鬯達，錄之。
translation_en:
…are one. You, sir, rejoice that the books on ritual survive and express concern for rectifying music. I would humbly say that correct music survives together with ritual. Did the Emperor’s pitch standards [Huangdi’s?] really depend upon these numbers? He ruled with his robes hanging down, and perfect harmony spread everywhere. Phoenixes came and sang in response to this harmonious influence; he therefore listened to them to establish the pitch standards.
